# China's Alibaba wins injunction against Pentagon contract restrictions

E-commence company can retain US lobbyists who represent defense contractors

Alibaba continues to fight its inclusion on a U.S. blacklist of companies accused of aiding China's military. © Reuters

October 27, 2026 22:41 JST

[](https://twitter.com/share?text=China%27s+Alibaba+wins+injunction+against+Pentagon+contract+restrictions&url=https%3A%2F%2Fasia.nikkei.com%2Fpolitics%2Finternational-relations%2Fus-china-tensions%2Fchina-s-alibaba-wins-injunction-against-pentagon-contract-restrictions&via=NikkeiAsia)[](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fasia.nikkei.com%2Fpolitics%2Finternational-relations%2Fus-china-tensions%2Fchina-s-alibaba-wins-injunction-against-pentagon-contract-restrictions)[](https://api.whatsapp.com/send?text=China%27s+Alibaba+wins+injunction+against+Pentagon+contract+restrictions+https%3A%2F%2Fasia.nikkei.com%2Fpolitics%2Finternational-relations%2Fus-china-tensions%2Fchina-s-alibaba-wins-injunction-against-pentagon-contract-restrictions)[](https://t.me/share/url?text=China%27s+Alibaba+wins+injunction+against+Pentagon+contract+restrictions&url=https%3A%2F%2Fasia.nikkei.com%2Fpolitics%2Finternational-relations%2Fus-china-tensions%2Fchina-s-alibaba-wins-injunction-against-pentagon-contract-restrictions)[](mailto:?subject=China%27s%20Alibaba%20wins%20injunction%20against%20Pentagon%20contract%20restrictions&body=https%3A%2F%2Fasia.nikkei.com%2Fpolitics%2Finternational-relations%2Fus-china-tensions%2Fchina-s-alibaba-wins-injunction-against-pentagon-contract-restrictions)

(Reuters) -- A U.S. federal judge on Monday granted Alibaba Group Holding's request for a preliminary injunction, ordering the U.S. government not to deny Pentagon contracts to companies because they, their parent companies or subsidiaries do business with firms that engage in lobbying activities for the e-commerce giant.

Alibaba sued the U.S. government in June after the Pentagon added it to a list of companies allegedly aiding China's military, alongside internet search provider Baidu, EV maker BYD and other major Chinese manufacturing and technology firms.

Monday's ruling means Alibaba will be able to retain U.S. lobbyists who also represent Pentagon contractors, removing a potential obstacle to the company's efforts to challenge its designation as a Chinese military company.

Advertisement

Alibaba fired dozens of its Washington lobbyists after the Pentagon action in June, according to a source with direct knowledge of the matter who was not authorized to speak to the media.

The designation does not impose formal sanctions, but restricts Pentagon contracts with listed companies and, from 2027, purchases of their products or services through third parties.

Other listed Chinese tech firms were also concerned about the designation's impact on international lobbying activities as well as the indirect procurement ban, which would completely remove Chinese products from US defense contractors' supply chains, the source added.

Alibaba has denied any military ties, saying its products and services are built for retail, logistics and enterprise technology rather than defense or intelligence.

"The determinations have no basis in fact or law," Alibaba said in its lawsuit in June, seeking its removal from the list.

Monday's injunction does not remove Alibaba from the Pentagon list, which the company is continuing to challenge in court.

Alibaba did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the injunction.

Alibaba is one of several Chinese firms taking legal action to challenge their placement on the Pentagon's list.

Last month, two subsidiaries of the world's largest electric vehicle maker, BYD, sued the U.S. Department of Defense over a federal law banning any Pentagon contractors from hiring lobbyists that also work with blacklisted firms, arguing that it breached BYD's First Amendment rights.

In August, DJI, the world's largest drone maker, appealed its inclusion on the blacklist with the court finding merit in its argument that unclassified records did not support the conclusion that the company contributed to the Chinese defense industrial base.

The appeals court ordered the lower court to reconsider its decision to reject DJI's bid to be removed from the Pentagon list, and the case is ongoing.

The same month, biotech firm WuXi AppTec also won a preliminary injunction from a U.S. federal court, which blocked its inclusion on the list. WuXi said the Pentagon designation was politically motivated.

title: 馮睎乾：麥巴比和毛澤東都說了真話
summary: 馮睎乾十三維度 :2026年10月27日週二 麥巴比和毛澤東都說了真話 今年4月初，效力皇家馬德里的法國球星麥巴比（Kylian Mbappé）出席清談節目《The Bridge》，主持人是他的隊友曹亞文尼。麥巴比被問及哪張有關他的迷因圖最爆笑，他答是有人把他的臉放到「一個傢伙的影片（une vidéo d’un mec）」，「我想那是個中国獨裁者（j’crois c’est un dictateur chinois）」，並表示和朋友玩遊戲時，自己也常常用這迷因（注1）。 事
content: 馮睎乾十三維度 :2026年10月27日週二 麥巴比和毛澤東都說了真話 今年4月初，效力皇家馬德里的法國球星麥巴比（Kylian Mbappé）出席清談節目《The Bridge》，主持人是他的隊友曹亞文尼。麥巴比被問及哪張有關他的迷因圖最爆笑，他答是有人把他的臉放到「一個傢伙的影片（une vidéo d’un mec）」，「我想那是個中国獨裁者（j’crois c’est un dictateur chinois）」，並表示和朋友玩遊戲時，自己也常常用這迷因（注1）。 事隔半年，麥巴比這個法語短訪（似乎只是《The Bridge》花絮片段）一直沒多少人留意。豈料到了前天（10月26日），中国足球資訊網站《懂球帝》忽然發聲明，說：「近日，效力於皇家馬德里的法國球員姆巴佩（即麥巴比）在接受採訪時發表涉中国的不當言論。由於他的發言涉及對中国和中国人民的傷害，我們不能進行翻譯，不管怎樣，他的言論都已經傷害了中国球迷和中国人民的感情。」 這份語焉不詳的聲明發布後，中国人民雖然不大清楚自己的感情怎樣被傷害，但依然無阻他們群情洶湧同仇敵愾，一致把矛頭指向外國勢力皇馬及「吃中国飯砸中国鍋」的麥巴比。三家中国贊助商跟麥巴比光速割席，中共外交部發言人也疾言厲色譴責。全賴麥巴比的一條過期短片，中国許多人已順利完成本月「爱国工作」額度，夠交功課有餘了。 不過在這齣「辱華」鬧劇中，我留意到兩個盲點和一大問題。盲點一：麥巴比由始至終沒提及毛澤東的名字，《懂球帝》也根本沒明言他的「不當言論」跟哪個獨裁者有關，為什麼全世界媒體都一面倒報道那是毛澤東，而小粉紅又毫不猶豫地接受和相信呢？這又讓我想起那個老掉牙的笑話。 一戰時期，某天柏林街頭有人大喊：「皇帝是個白癡。」他馬上被德意志帝國的警察拘捕。那人自辯：「我罵的是奧地利皇帝啊。」警察答道：「不必說謊，我們都知道誰是白癡。」試想一下，如果小粉紅們及中共外交部心底裏不認為毛澤東是獨裁者，又憑什麼斷定麥巴比指的是毛澤東而非秦始皇，從而冒犯到今日的中国人民呢？ 事實上，多個法國媒體已指出「失言」訪問是半年前做的。《懂球帝》聲明所說的「近日」，根本完全對不上毛澤東。麥巴比在9月接受《法國足球（France Football）》訪問，確曾談及迷因圖和獨裁者，但當時他明確回應的迷因，是扎伊爾共和國的獨裁者莫布杜（Mobutu），不是毛澤東。換言之，《懂球帝》聲明的「近日」兩字，本身就是虛假訊息，甚至刻意張冠李戴，以圖挑起民族情緒。 盲點二：就算麥巴比真的把毛澤東稱為「獨裁者」，也只是重申毛澤東表達過的觀點而已，何罪之有？1958年八大二次會議，毛澤東曾揚言：「秦始皇算什麼？他只坑了四百六十八個儒，我們坑了四萬六千個儒……我們與民主人士辯論過，你罵我們是秦始皇，不對，我們超過了秦始皇一百倍；罵我們是秦始皇，是獨裁者，我們一概承認。可惜的是你們說得不夠，往往要我們加以補充。」 為了香噴噴的人民幣，麥巴比和皇馬當然想也不想就秒跪，急急發聲明向「被傷害了的中国人」道歉。但如果麥巴比需要道歉，那麼自認獨裁者的毛澤東本人，又要不要被小粉紅和外交部鞭屍呢？如果麥巴比和毛澤東是對的，那麼小粉紅和外交部就應該向麥巴比道歉了。 最後我想指出一個「大問題」：為什麼《懂球帝》不早不晚，偏偏趁着五中全會，忽然翻出半年前的舊訪問呢？你不說，根本就無人問津。好了，如今你煽風點火，客觀效果就是：全世界都在熱烈討論「中国獨裁者」是誰？若你用英文、法文或其他外語搜查這個關鍵詞，Google就會告訴你，除了毛澤東以外，當今的中国獨裁者叫什麼名字。當「中国獨裁者」議題被挑起後，十四億人民就難免作出「不當聯想」，真正受傷害的人是誰，應該不言而喻吧。《懂球帝》射這一球，絕了。 注 1 https://x.com/ladsbanterfooty/status/2115101805856325770?s=46 相關文章 AI沒辱華，只是說了真話 https://www.patreon.com/sefirot/posts/11807855

title: Lockheed Martin Showcases 1000 km PrSM Inc 4 Prototype
zh_title: 洛克希德·马丁公司展示 1000 公里 PrSM Inc 4 原型机
summary: 洛克希德·马丁公司的精确打击导弹 (PrSM) Increment 4 原型机将使用冲压发动机技术和先进的传感器套件来打击 1000 公里外的移动船只。 “随着威胁在全球战区不断演变，陆军需要一种现代化的精确导弹，其射程远远超出当前能力。当从 HIMARS 发射器发射时，PrSM Increment 4 预计将击中至少 1,000 公里外的移动海上和可重新定位的陆地目标，”洛克希德·马丁公司的新闻稿中写道。根据周一发布的消息，洛克希德·马丁公司提交的 PrSM Inc 4 原型机将
content:
洛克希德·马丁公司的精确打击导弹 (PrSM) Increment 4 原型机将使用冲压发动机技术和先进的传感器套件来打击 1000 公里外的移动船只。 “随着威胁在全球战区不断演变，陆军需要一种现代化的精确导弹，其射程远远超出当前能力。当从 HIMARS 发射器发射时，PrSM Increment 4 预计将击中至少 1,000 公里外的移动海上和可重新定位的陆地目标，”洛克希德·马丁公司的新闻稿中写道。根据周一发布的消息，洛克希德·马丁公司提交的 PrSM Inc 4 原型机将使用 L3Harris 的推进系统和现有的制导系统。该公司的Strigo产品中心是一个专门开发数据链、频率传感器和导弹导引头的部门，其工作将为该弹药的制导套件提供信息。该声明强调了 PrSM Inc 1 的“经过战斗验证”的制导和控制系统。这是指该导弹在史诗愤怒行动中针对伊朗目标的交战。洛克希德·马丁公司目前位于阿肯色州卡姆登的 PrSM Inc 1 和 2 导弹生产线可以支持该公司 Inc 4 产品的生产。根据新闻稿，使用现有生产线将实现“所有版本导弹的规模经济”。这家美国防务公司是美国陆军选择参与远程海上打击计划的五家公司之一。
洛克希德·马丁公司的原型机将与 Anduril、Castelion、Mach Industries 和 RTX 提交的材料进行对比。2027 年和 2028 年的测试将为陆军的最终裁决提供依据。源自地面部队的作战需求，PrSM Inc 4将成为华盛顿针对中国的地面反舰能力的关键组成部分。美军计划通过 M142 高机动火箭炮系统等发射器使中国军队受到来自第一岛链群岛的威胁。加拿大和澳大利亚还计划在其 HIMARS 发射器上部署海上打击 PrSM 变体。洛克希德·马丁公司展示 1000 公里 PrSM Inc 4 原型机的帖子首先出现在《海军新闻》上。

【原文 English Original】
Lockheed Martin’s Precision Strike Missile (PrSM) Increment 4 prototype will use ramjet technology and an advanced sensor suite to strike moving ships over 1,000 kilometers away. “As threats evolve throughout the global theater, the Army needs a modernized precision missile that can perform at ranges far beyond current capabilities. When fired from a HIMARS launcher, PrSM Increment 4 is expected to hit both moving maritime and relocatable land targets at least 1,000 km away,” reads the Lockheed Martin release. According to a Monday release, Lockheed Martin’s PrSM Inc 4 prototype submission will use a propulsion system from L3Harris and existing guidance systems. Work from company’s Strigo Product Center, a department specializing in the development of data links, frequency sensors and missile seekers, will inform the munition’s guidance suite. The statement highlighted the “battle-proven” guidance and control systems from PrSM Inc 1. This is in reference to the missile’s engagements during Operation Epic Fury against Iranian targets. Lockheed Martin’s current PrSM Inc 1 and 2 missile production line at Camden, Arkansas, can support the production of the firm’s Inc 4 offering. According to the release, the use of existing lines will achieve “economies of scale for all versions of the missile.” The American defense firm is one of five companies down selected by the U.S. Army for the extended-range maritime strike program. Lockheed Martin’s prototype will go against submissions from Anduril, Castelion, Mach Industries and RTX. Tests in 2027 and 2028 will inform the Army’s final award. Derived from the ground branch’s operational needs , PrSM Inc 4 will form a key component of Washington’s ground-based anti-shipping capabilities against China. From launchers such as the M142 High Mobility Rocket Artillery System, U.S. forces plan to hold Chinese forces under threat from archipelagos in the First Island Chain. Canada and Australia also plan to field maritime strike PrSM variants on their HIMARS launchers. The post Lockheed Martin Showcases 1000 km PrSM Inc 4 Prototype appeared first on Naval News .

title: 5 things to watch out for in 2027 US defence bill aimed at countering China

source: 南华早报SCMP（中国社会/科技/舆情）
summary: 这些措施可能会影响明年的印太安全平衡和美中关系。尽管习近平最近访问了特朗普，但他拒绝与中国在人工智能方面合作。在选举结果的不确定性和地缘政治局势的变化中，立法者必须在[美国国会](https://www.scmp.com/topics/us-congress?pgtype=search?module=inline&pgtype=article)年底休会之前通过该法案，并在将其发送给特朗普签署之前调和两个版本之间的差异。
content:
这些措施可能会影响明年的印太安全平衡和美中关系。

尽管习近平最近访问，特朗普仍拒绝与中国在人工智能领域合作

由于选举结果的不确定性和地缘政治环境的变化，立法者必须在[美国国会](https://www.scmp.com/topics/us-congress?pgtype=search?module=inline&pgtype=article)年底休会之前通过该法案，并在将其发送给特朗普签署之前协调两个版本之间的差异。

以下是五个最值得关注和最具挑衅性的条款，所有这些条款都可能引起北京的反对。

### 1. 支持台湾

尽管特朗普最近发表言论，将对台军售描述为北京的“谈判筹码”，但参众两院正在讨论的法案版本将保持资金流向台湾的国防。

众议院版本将授权为台湾安全合作计划（美国的一项国防援助计划）提供高达 10 亿美元的资金，维持上一财年的水平，并在国防工业优先事项上建立美台伙伴关系。

它还将建立一个开发和测试无人机和反无人机系统的联合计划，并要求台湾海军计划在2028年之前参加环太平洋演习——这一条款在去年的最终妥协法案中被删除。
众议院的进一步条款要求就台湾的能力提交年度报告，并制定通过五眼协调支持其网络防御的战略。

参议院版本将授权从美国战争储备库存向台湾转移武器。它还将台湾安全合作倡议更名为“第一岛链安全合作倡议”。

特朗普在中国谈判中淡化台湾争端

中国驻华盛顿大使馆向《南华早报》表示，对法案中涉台条款“粗暴干涉”中国内政“强烈不满和坚决反对”，任何武装台湾的企图都将面临“严重后果”。

北京将台湾视为中国的一部分，必要时可以使用武力与大陆重新统一。包括美国在内的大多数国家都不承认台湾是一个独立国家，但华盛顿反对任何以武力改变现状的企图，并致力于向台湾提供防御性武器。

### 2. 应对南海危机
参议院版本更多地关注第一岛链，即从[日本](https://www.scmp.com/topics/japan?pgtype=search?module=inline&pgtype=article)穿过台湾和[菲律宾](https://www.scmp.com/topics/philippines?pgtype=search?module=inline&pgtype=article)到婆罗洲的岛屿弧，包围着南中国海。

这将要求五角大楼在一年内起草一份海洋危机管理战略，确定战争之外可能的爆发点，并概述与合作伙伴协调的分阶段应对措施。

其宣称的目的是“否认人民的目的”

【原文 English Original】
The measures could shape the Indo-Pacific security balance and [US-China relations](https://www.scmp.com/topics/us-china-relations?pgtype=search?module=inline&pgtype=article) well into next year.

Trump rejects working with China on AI despite Xi’s recent visit

Lawmakers must pass the bill before the [US Congress](https://www.scmp.com/topics/us-congress?pgtype=search?module=inline&pgtype=article) adjourns at the end of the year and reconcile differences between the two versions before sending it to Trump for his signature, amid uncertainty over the election results and a shifting geopolitical environment.

Here are five of the most notable and provocative provisions to watch, all likely to draw opposition from Beijing.

### 1. Support for Taiwan

Despite Trump’s recent remarks describing arms sales to Taiwan as “negotiating chips” to Beijing, the versions of the bill under discussion in both chambers would keep money flowing to Taiwan’s defence.

The House version would authorise up to US$1 billion for the Taiwan Security Cooperation Initiative – a US defence assistance programme – maintaining the previous financial year’s level, and create a US-Taiwan partnership on defence industrial priorities.

It would also establish a joint programme to develop and test drones and counter-drone systems, and require a plan for Taiwan’s navy to take part in the Rim of the Pacific Exercise by 2028 – a clause that was dropped in last year’s final compromise bill.

Further House provisions call for an annual report on Taiwan’s capabilities and a strategy to support its cyber defence through Five Eyes coordination.

The Senate version would authorise arms transfers to [Taiwan](https://www.scmp.com/topics/taiwan?pgtype=search?module=inline&pgtype=article) from the US War Reserve Stockpile. It would also rename the Taiwan Security Cooperation Initiative the “First Island Chain Security Cooperation Initiative”.

Trump downplays Taiwan dispute in China talks

The Chinese embassy in Washington has told the South China Morning Post that it “strongly deplores and firmly opposes” Taiwan-related provisions in the bill that “grossly interfere” in China’s internal affairs, and that any attempt to arm Taiwan will face “grave consequences”.

Beijing views Taiwan as part of China to be reunited with the mainland, by force if necessary. Most countries, including the US, do not recognise Taiwan as an independent state, but Washington opposes any attempt to change the status quo by force and is committed to supplying the island with defensive weapons.

### 2. Planning for a South China Sea crisis

The Senate version focuses far more on the first island chain, the arc of islands from [Japan](https://www.scmp.com/topics/japan?pgtype=search?module=inline&pgtype=article) through Taiwan and [the Philippines](https://www.scmp.com/topics/philippines?pgtype=search?module=inline&pgtype=article) to Borneo that encloses the South China Sea.

It would require the [Pentagon](https://www.scmp.com/topics/pentagon-us-department-defence?pgtype=search?module=inline&pgtype=article) to draft a crisis-management strategy for the sea within a year, identify likely flashpoints short of war, and outline phased responses coordinated with partners.

The stated aim is to “deny the aim of the People’s Republic of China and deter further [PRC] provocation or actions that expand the crisis.” It would also order facilities planning for rotating US forces in the Philippines, which has clashed with Chinese vessels, and seek a report on Japan’s counterstrike capabilities.

The House version did not mention the South China Sea or the first island chain.

### 3. Countering China’s shipbuilding dominance

The Trump administration has been attempting to increase cooperation with allies with shipbuilding capacities, such as [South Korea](https://www.scmp.com/topics/south-korea?pgtype=search?module=inline&pgtype=article) and Japan, to help revitalise depleted US naval shipbuilding capabilities.

Ships under construction at a shipyard in Taicang, China. Photo: AFP

However, the House and Senate versions take contrasting approaches to foreign shipyard involvement in US Navy shipbuilding.

The House version prohibits using any funds to contract for or procure battle force or combat ships in a foreign shipyard, completely barring overseas construction for the combat fleet.

The Senate version amends the current law by allowing the Pentagon to procure up to two bulk fuel vessels and two strategic sealift/auxiliary non-combat ships from treaty-ally shipyards.

### 4. Tightening of tech restrictions

Both bills would prohibit the Pentagon from using Chinese-manufactured optical fibre and restrict purchases of certain used vessels built in China.

The House would also bar the procurement and use of humanoid robotic systems produced, developed or controlled by foreign adversaries, and restrict purchases of photovoltaic cells, modules and inverters from foreign entities of concern.

A worker processes chips in the workshop of Aoyang Shunchang Optoelectronics Technology in Huai’an, Jiangsu province, China. Photo: CFOTO/Future Publishing via Getty Images

Tougher chip export controls, including the AI OVERWATCH Act, the Chip Security Act and the MATCH Act, could be added before final passage. Zack Cooper, a China expert and senior fellow of the American Enterprise Institute, said the three measures were “perhaps the most important portions related to China right now”.

Beijing has condemned plans, warning chip curbs would cause “arbitrary disruption and damage” to global supply chains.

### 5. Reducing reliance on China for critical minerals

Responding to China’s global dominance in critical mineral supplies that are essential for advanced military technology, the Senate bill would prohibit the Pentagon from buying certain minerals from non-allied nations and set up a pilot programme to restart antimony and copper production in the US.

It also orders an assessment of the Pentagon’s phosphate supply chain, including its dependence on China.

The House bill is broader. It would cap the share of metals the Pentagon can source from abroad and set up tiered sourcing restrictions for critical minerals from China and [North Korea](https://www.scmp.com/topics/north-korea?pgtype=search?module=inline&pgtype=article).

It would also ban silicon-carbide semiconductors made in China and order studies on reliance on Chinese processing and on aluminium and synthetic diamond supplies.

One report would examine whether US scrap exports are feeding [rare-earth refining and magnet production in China](https://www.scmp.com/economy/global-economy/article/3371522/chinas-rare-earth-magnet-exports-eu-and-us-rebound-september?pgtype=search?module=inline&pgtype=article). Another study would assess whether combatant commands should be able to buy critical minerals on their own.

content:
2026 年 7 月 25 日，在澳大利亚北领地邦迪山训练区举行的大规模伤亡训练活动中，美国海军陆战队轮换部队 - 达尔文 26 的水兵正在治疗模拟伤员。美国海军陆战队照片 海军陆战队轮换部队 - 达尔文 26.3 完成了在澳大利亚和印度-太平洋地区为期六个月的轮换部署，美国海军陆战队周五宣布。海军陆战队新闻稿称，MRF-D 部署的结束标志着第 15 次轮换。在部署期间，这支轮换部队被认证为特种目的海军陆战队空地特遣部队——这是 MRF-D 首次获得特殊认证。新闻稿称，MRF-D由海军陆战队第一师第五海军陆战团领导，将来自第一和第三海军陆战队远征军的2000名海军陆战队员和水兵合并成一支能够汇集指挥和控制、航空、地面作战和后勤能力的部队。 3月至10月，这支轮换部队与澳大利亚国防军以及地区盟友和伙伴一起在澳大利亚、菲律宾、新喀里多尼亚、巴布亚新几内亚、法属波利尼西亚和印度尼西亚进行训练。作为一支经过认证的特种海军陆战队空地特遣部队，MRF-D 在该地区充当前沿后备部队，能够从分散的地点开展行动并对危机做出快速反应。 “这第 15 次轮换证明了美国和澳大利亚在并肩训练时能够取得的成就，”美国
MRF-D 26.3 SPMAGT 指挥官、海军陆战队上校乔治·弗林在新闻稿中表示。 “我要向我们的澳大利亚国防军同行和全国各地的主办方表示最深切的谢意，感谢他们坚定不移的支持。通过在 Render Safe、Predators Run、Southern Jackaroo 和 Capital Reach 等演习中共同突破极限，我们从彼此身上学到了很多东西。我们已经建立了无与伦比的互操作性，证明我们可以快速有效地共同行动，以确保自由开放的印度太平洋地区。”一架美国海军陆战队 MV-22B 鱼鹰被分配到第 16 海军陆战队第 165 中型倾转旋翼机中队 (VMM)，第 3 海军陆战队飞机联队，在加利福尼亚州彭德尔顿海军陆战队基地营进行了“钢铁骑士 25”演习的模拟袭击后，准备与第 1 海军陆战师第 5 海军团第 1 营黑脚连一起接载海军陆战队员。 2025 年 12 月 12 日。美国海军陆战队照片 在该部队抵达澳大利亚参加“钢铁骑士 2025”演习之前，在美国开始了部署准备工作。这支仍在组建的部队于 2025 年 12 月 1 日至 14 日在南加州进行了演习，建立了地理上分布的指挥和控制节点，并演练了使用 MV-22B 鱼鹰倾转旋翼机和 C-130J 超级飞机进行人员和装备的长距离移动大力士飞机。
海军陆战队和水兵还接受了对大使馆增援、疏散行动、伤员疏散、远征医疗支援、航空节点行动和远征先进基地行动能力的评估。抵达达尔文后，MRF-D 26.3 开始了其区域训练活动，即 4 月 20 日至 5 月 8 日在菲律宾举行的“肩并肩 2026”演习。此次演习为 MRF-D 26.3 完成 SPMAGTF 认证提供了最终的操作环境。并肩作战期间，海军陆战队和水兵验证了他们救援飞机和人员、进行航空外部运输、运送物资的能力

【原文 English Original】
U.S. Navy sailors with Marine Rotational Force – Darwin 26 treat a simulated casualty during a mass casualty training event at Mount Bundy Training Area in Northern Territory, Australia, July 25, 2026. US Marine Corps photo Marine Rotational Force-Darwin 26.3 completed its six month rotational deployment to Australia and the Indo-Pacific, the service announced on Friday. The conclusion of the MRF-D’s deployment marks the 15th rotation, reads a Marine Corps news release . During the deployment, the rotational force was certified as a Special Purpose Marine Air-Ground Task Force – the first time a MRF-D has received the special certification. The MRF-D, led by 5th Marine Regiment, 1st Marine Division, combined 2,000 Marines and sailors from I and III Marine Expeditionary forces into a force capable of bringing together command and control, aviation, ground combat and logistics capabilities, reads the release. The rotational force trained alongside the Australian Defence Force and regional allies and partners from March to October throughout Australia, the Philippines, New Caledonia, Papua New Guinea, French Polynesia and Indonesia. As a certified Special Purpose Marine Air-Ground Task Force, the MRF-D acted as a forward-postured stand-in force in the region and was capable of operating from dispersed locations and responding quickly to crises. “This 15th rotation stands as a testament to what the U.S. and Australia can achieve when we train shoulder-to-shoulder,” U.S. Marine Corps Col. George Flynn, commanding officer of MRF-D 26.3 SPMAGT, said in the release. “I want to extend my deepest gratitude to our ADF counterparts and our hosts across the country for their unwavering support. By pushing our limits together during exercises like Render Safe, Predators Run, Southern Jackaroo and Capital Reach, we have learned immensely from one another. We have forged an unparalleled level of interoperability, proving that we can move together rapidly and effectively to ensure a free and open Indo-Pacific.” A U.S. Marine Corps MV-22B Osprey assigned to Marine Medium Tiltrotor Squadron (VMM) 165, Marine Aircraft Group 16, 3rd Marine Aircraft Wing, prepare to pick up Marines with Blackfoot Company, 1st Battalion, 5th Marine Regiment, 1st Marine Division, after a simulated raid as part of Exercise Steel Knight 25 at Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton, California, Dec. 12, 2025. US Marine Corps photo Preparations for the deployment began in the U.S. before the unit arrived in Australia with participation in Exercise Steel Knight 2025. Conducted across Southern California from Dec. 1-14, 2025, the still-forming force established geographically distributed command-and-control nodes and rehearsed long-distance movement of personnel and equipment using MV-22B Osprey tiltrotor aircraft and C-130J Super Hercules aircraft. Marines and sailors also underwent evaluations on their ability to conduct embassy reinforcement, evacuation operations, casualty evacuation, expeditionary medical support, aviation-node operations and expeditionary advanced base operations. Following its arrival in Darwin, MRF-D 26.3 began its regional training campaign with Exercise Balikatan 2026, held from April 20 to May 8 in the Philippines. The exercise provided the final operational environment for MRF-D 26.3 to complete its SPMAGTF certification . During Balikatan, Marines and sailors validated their ability to recover aircraft and personnel, conduct aviation external lift, deliver supplies by air to a notional civilian population and establish expeditionary advanced bases in austere, dispersed locations. In Aporawan, Palawan, as part of Balikatan, MRF-D’s ground combat element trained alongside the Armed Forces of the Philippines, Australian Defense Force, New Zealand Defense Force and U.S. joint forces during a counter-landing live-fire exercise. The combined force synchronized Philippine Marine Corps artillery, High Mobility Artillery Rocket Systems, mortars, crew-served weapons, anti-armor systems and air-defense capabilities against simulated amphibious threats. Balikatan culminated on May 3 at Balabac Island, where multinational reconnaissance teams from the Philippine Marine Corps, Australian Army and 1st Reconnaissance Battalion shaped the operational environment before U.S., Philippine and Australian forces conducted an air assault to secure Balabac Airfield. Marine Medium Tiltrotor Squadron 268 (Reinforced) transported personnel and equipment from Antonio Bautista Air Base, while U.S. Army watercraft moved HIMARS into the austere maritime environment. The combined force then integrated air mobility, reconnaissance, ground maneuver and fires during a live-fire demonstration against simulated maritime targets. Coinciding with Balikatan, elements of the force deployed to New Caledonia for Exercise Tagata Toa, a multinational combined-arms exercise hosted by the French Armed Forces from April 27 to May 10. The deployment to New Caledonia also demonstrated the importance of partner-enabled mobility, reads the release. The Royal New Zealand Air Force provided a Boeing 757 and two C-130 Hercules aircraft to move Marines and equipment between Darwin, New Caledonia and Townsville. “By drawing on allied capacity, access and professional relationships, MRF-D moved personnel and equipment across international boundaries faster than it could have through unilateral means. That ability to leverage partner capabilities expanded the combined force’s reach and resilience across the Indo-Pacific,” reads the release. U.S. Marines with Fox Battery, 2nd Battalion, 11th Marine Regiment, Marine Rotational Force – Darwin 26, adjust the trajectory of an M777A2 lightweight 155mm howitzer while conducting a fire mission during Exercise Predator’s Walk at Mount Bundey Training Area, Northern Territory, Australia, May 21, 2026. US Marine Corps photo The special purpose MAGTF then returned its focus to northern Australia on May 18 with Exercise Predators Walk, which continued through June 12 and built tactical familiarity between Marines and Australian counterparts. Then, from May 29 to July 3 in Townsville, Marines trained alongside Australian and Japanese forces during Exercise Southern Jackaroo. The exercise included joint operations and live-fire training designed to strengthen combined readiness and interoperability in complex terrain. Other elements of the units deployed to the Philippines for Exercise KAMANDAG 10, held June 15 to July 1. The MRF-D then participated in a month-long deployment as part of participation in Operation Render Safe, the multinational effort to remove World War II-era unexploded ordnance and reduce risks to communities in East New Britain. From July 1-31, Marines of the MRF-D 26.3 explosive ordnance disposal element disposed of 732 munitions totalling 16,041 pounds of net explosive weight. From July 20 to Aug. 7, MRF-D 26 joined the Australian Army’s 1st Brigade and the Philippine Army’s 1st Brigade Combat Team for Exercise Predators Run 26, in the Townsville Field Training Area. The trilateral exercise integrated U.S., Australian and Philippine forces under a unified command structure for platoon-level training, force-on-force maneuvers and a combined defensive live-fire scenario. The unit employed multiple organic unmanned aircraft systems to expand logistics, medical support and ground-combat capabilities during the exercise U.S. Marines with Combat Logistics Battalion 5, Marine Rotational Force – Darwin 26, guide and stage tactical vehicles in preparation to embark aboard the Royal Australian Navy HMAS Canberra at the Port of Townsville in Queensland, Australia, August 2, 2026. US Marine Corps photo An embarked deployment took place in early August with Royal Australian Navy amphibious assault ship HMAS Canberra (L02). VMM-268 (Rein.) conducted MV-22B Osprey deck landing qualifications, while the Royal Australian Navy mechanized landing craft transported Marine Corps Joint Light Tactical Vehicles (JLTV) and Medium Tactical Vehicle Replacements from Canberra’s well deck to shore. In Indonesia from Aug. 12-28, Alpha Company, 1st Battalion, 5th Marines conducted an annual platoon exchange with Indonesian marines from 7th Infantry Battalion, 4th Brigade near Lampung. Then, from Aug. 31 toSept.11, 230 Marines and sailors joined Indonesian and multinational partners for combined-arms live fire, jungle operations, small-unit tactics, force-on-force training and subject-matter expert exchange as part of Exercise Super Garuda Shield 2026. The rotational force is scheduled to return to the Northern Territory in early 2027 for the 16th MRF-D rotation, according to an Australian Defense Department news release . I MEF deploys two rotational forces to the Indo-Pacific – MRF-D and Marine Rotational Force-South East Asia (MRF-SEA). In previous years, MRF-SEA would deploy from October to March with MRF-D entering the region in April. However, since April this year, MRF-SEA has maintained its command element on a continuous basis in the Philippines with the unit’s recent activity being a bilateral planning exercise with Philippine Joint Task Force personnel from Oct. 5-9. “For MRF-SEA, the planning exercise represents the progression of a rotation built around persistent engagement with Philippine partners,” reads a MRF-SEA news release .

title: Taiwan vows vigilance as Beijing releases satellite imagery of island landmarks
zh_title: 北京发布岛屿地标卫星图像，台湾发誓保持警惕
source: 南华早报SCMP（中国社会/科技/舆情）
summary: 在北京发布该岛的高分辨率卫星图像后，[台湾](https://www.scmp.com/topics/taiwan?module=inline&pgtype=article)军方誓言对中国大陆的情报收集活动保持警惕，引发对其日益增长的[监视](https://www.scmp.com/topics/surveillance?module=inline&pgtype=article)能力的担忧。国防部长辜立雄周二对记者表示：“对于所有针对台湾的此类卫星图像和相关情报收集，国防部任何时候都不会放松警惕。”
content:
在北京发布该岛的高分辨率卫星图像后，[台湾](https://www.scmp.com/topics/taiwan?module=inline&pgtype=article)军方誓言对中国大陆的情报收集活动保持警惕，引发对其日益增长的[监视](https://www.scmp.com/topics/surveillance?module=inline&pgtype=article)能力的担忧。

国防部长辜立雄周二对记者表示：“对于所有针对台湾的此类卫星图像和相关情报收集，国防部任何时候都不会放松警惕。”

“我们还将采取适当的预警和应对措施，包括必要的隐蔽、机动和疏散措施，以确保武装部队的行动安全。”

在他发表上述言论之前，中国大陆国家广播机构 [CCTV](https://www.scmp.com/topics/cctv?module=inline&pgtype=article) 于周日发布了一段 42 秒的视频，其中包含商业吉林一号遥感卫星星座捕获的台湾高分辨率图像。

标有“这是中国的台湾省”的镜头从整个岛屿的景色转移到中正纪念堂、国立故宫博物院、台北巨蛋和台北港以及日月潭和玉山等地标建筑。

“（从太空）每条街道都清晰可见，”它说。

10 月 12 日，人们在台北中正纪念堂外走过台湾国旗。照片：EPA
这次发布标志着吉林一号图像连续第二年在北京 10 月 25 日左右发布的信息中占据显着位置，以纪念 1945 年日本对台湾殖民统治的结束。

北京去年正式将这一天定为“台湾光复日”，吉林一号图像成为将技术能力与台湾主权主张联系起来的更广泛活动的一部分。

北京将台湾视为中国的一部分，必要时可以用武力统一台湾。包括美国在内的大多数国家都不承认台湾是一个独立国家，但华盛顿反对任何以武力夺取这个自治岛屿的企图，并致力于向其提供武器。

去年10月，高分辨率图像显示了台湾各地的地点，包括日月潭、阿里山、台北港和新竹科学园区，街道、建筑物和其他结构清晰可辨。

这一消息的发布当时引起了北京国防部的公开回应。

当被问及如果商业星座能够如此详细地显示台湾街道时，军用卫星可以产生更清晰的图像时，发言人张晓刚说：“中国卫星看到中国台湾的壮丽景观是完全正常的。没有什么值得惊讶的。”

内地报道称，公开发布的图像分辨率一般为亚米级，可以区分街道布局和其他特征。
据其运营商长光卫星技术公司称，吉林一号星座由 141 颗卫星组成，在距地球约 500 公里（311 英里）的地方运行。

在周二的立法会议上，执政的民进党议员吴思耀表示，北京“故意突出了台湾的著名地标，以强化其对台湾的主权主张”，同时利用这些图像来表明其有能力密切监视台湾。

02:20

美国指责中国大陆针对台湾领导人

【原文 English Original】
[Taiwan](https://www.scmp.com/topics/taiwan?module=inline&pgtype=article)’s military has vowed to remain vigilant against mainland Chinese intelligence-gathering activities after Beijing released high-resolution satellite images of the island, raising concerns about its growing [surveillance](https://www.scmp.com/topics/surveillance?module=inline&pgtype=article) capabilities.

“The defence ministry will not lower its vigilance at any time regarding all such satellite imagery and related intelligence collection directed at Taiwan,” Defence Minister Wellington Koo Li-hsiung told reporters on Tuesday.

“We will also take appropriate early-warning and response measures, including the necessary concealment, mobility and dispersal measures, to ensure the operational security of the armed forces.”

His comments followed mainland Chinese state broadcaster [CCTV](https://www.scmp.com/topics/cctv?module=inline&pgtype=article)’s release on Sunday of a 42-second video featuring high-resolution imagery of Taiwan captured by the commercial Jilin-1 remote-sensing satellite constellation.

Labelled “This is China’s Taiwan Province”, the footage moved from views of the entire island to landmarks including Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall, the National Palace Museum, Taipei Dome and Taipei Port, as well as Sun Moon Lake and Mount Jade.

“Every street is clearly visible [from space],” it said.

People walk past Taiwan flags outside Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall in Taipei on October 12. Photo: EPA

The release marked the second consecutive year that Jilin-1 imagery featured prominently in Beijing’s messaging around October 25, which commemorates the end of Japanese colonial rule over Taiwan in 1945.

Beijing last year formally designated the date as “Taiwan Restoration Day”, with Jilin-1 imagery becoming part of a broader campaign linking technological capability with its claim over the island.

Beijing regards Taiwan as part of China to be reunited by force if necessary. Most countries, including the United States, do not recognise Taiwan as an independent state, but Washington is opposed to any attempt to take the self-ruled island by force and is committed to supplying it with weapons.

Last October, high-resolution images showed locations across Taiwan including Sun Moon Lake, Alishan, Taipei Port and Hsinchu Science Park, with streets, buildings and other structures clearly discernible.

The release prompted a public response at the time from Beijing’s defence ministry.

Asked about suggestions that military satellites could produce even clearer images if a commercial constellation could show Taiwan’s streets in such detail, spokesman Zhang Xiaogang said: “It is perfectly normal for Chinese satellites to take a look at the magnificent landscape of China’s Taiwan. There is nothing to be surprised about.”

Mainland reports said the publicly released images were generally at sub-metre resolution, allowing street layouts and other features to be distinguished.

The Jilin-1 constellation then comprised 141 satellites operating about 500km (311 miles) above Earth, according to its operator, Chang Guang Satellite Technology.

At a legislative meeting on Tuesday, ruling Democratic Progressive Party lawmaker Wu Szu-yao said Beijing had “deliberately highlighted prominent Taiwanese landmarks to reinforce its claim” over the island while using the imagery to signal its ability to closely monitor Taiwan.

02:20

US accuses mainland China of targeting Taiwan leader’s family in surveillance case

Premier Cho Jung-tai said in response that Taipei was strengthening its defences through regular and special budgets, and responding to external threats through legal and technological measures.

Analysts said the imagery carried both political and military implications.

Joseph Wen, an adjunct research fellow at Taiwan’s government-funded Institute for National Defence and Security Research, said Jilin-1 illustrated Beijing’s “ability to conduct high-resolution observation of virtually any part of Taiwan”.

Whether mainland China could maintain continuous and real-time surveillance depended on the number and orbital configuration of its satellites, the mix of optical and radar sensors, and the speed at which imagery could be transmitted and processed, he added.

But publicly available information suggested Beijing was probably already capable of near-real-time satellite observation of Taiwan or would be in the foreseeable future, Wen said.

“Persistent observation could reveal militarily useful information from seemingly mundane details, such as changes in the number of vehicles parked at military bases,” he warned.

Analysts also said the releases combined a display of technological prowess with political messaging, as part of a broader pressure campaign involving military exercises, legal warfare and public-opinion operations.

“Through the images, Beijing sent the message that under its satellites, Taiwan is effectively transparent and can be observed in considerable detail,” political commentator Chiu Yi said, adding that this was intended to reinforce the impression that the island was within Beijing’s reach.

Retired Major General Li Cheng-chieh said the imagery carried more than symbolic significance because satellite intelligence could expose troop movements and other military activities.

“Mainland China’s growing constellation could also make surveillance increasingly persistent,” he said, arguing that the pressure created by showing such capabilities could rival that of [People’s Liberation Army](https://www.scmp.com/topics/peoples-liberation-army-pla?module=inline&pgtype=article) exercises around Taiwan.

title: US, Japan rehearse strikes to challenge PLA control of waters near Taiwan
zh_title: 美日演习打击解放军对台湾附近海域的控制
source: 南华早报SCMP（中国社会/科技/舆情）
summary: 美国和日本军队已经演练了在九州和日本西南岛屿上进行协调反舰打击和机动导弹部署，测试旨在挑战北京在台湾冲突中控制周边水域的能力的战术。现在已进入第二周，为期 11 天的【利剑 27 演习】(https://www.scmp.com/news/china/military/article/3370210/how-expanded-japan-us-military-exercises-could-complicate-pla-planning-over-taiwan?module=inline&pgtype=article) 已经测试了盟友如何威胁中国
content:
美国和日本军队已经演练了在九州和日本西南岛屿上进行协调反舰打击和机动导弹部署，测试旨在挑战北京在台湾冲突中控制周边水域的能力的战术。

为期 11 天的【利刃 27 演习】(https://www.scmp.com/news/china/military/article/3370210/how-expanded-japan-us-military-exercises-could-complicate-pla-planning-over-taiwan?module=inline&pgtype=article) 已经进入第二周，测试了盟国如何从多个方向威胁中国军舰，同时让自己的军力更加强大目标。

据美国和日本双方的声明称，他们还进行了修复跑道和维护海上补给线的练习，以便在基地遭受袭击和补给线中断时维持行动。

09:58

巴丹群岛会成为下一个南海爆发点吗？

分析人士表示，所采用的战术可能会使解放军在冲突期间更难定位和压制美国和日本军队，从而可能迫使中国指挥官投入更多资源进行侦察和瞄准。

然而，他们表示，盟军在攻击下维持分散行动的能力将取决于可靠的通信、补给和基础设施。
在 10 月 23 日至 24 日的训练中，美国海军 F/A-18 和 F-35 飞机以及海军陆战队陆基发射器模拟了对日本海（又称东海）的充气海上目标进行协调导弹打击。

两艘配备宙斯盾的日本导弹驱逐舰刚果号和玛雅号充当敌方力量，而美国太空军则帮助保护通信。

盟国还测试了他们在岛屿上移动主要武器和监视系统的速度。

日本C-2和C-130运输机用于移动美国[NMESIS反舰导弹发射器](https://www.scmp.com/news/china/diplomacy/article/3369666/us-deploy-nmesis-anti-ship-system-japanese-island-closest-taiwan-first-time?module=inline&pgtype=article)、MADIS防空车辆和TPS-80监视雷达探测到冲绳西南部的先岛群岛。

演习计划要求将 NMESIS 和 MADIS 系统部署在台湾以东约 110 公里（70 英里）的与那国岛和更东北的石垣岛，监视雷达也部署在宫古岛。

东京大学副教授塞巴斯蒂安·马斯洛表示，正在测试的部署可能要求解放军“在第一岛链上建立更强大的防线”，而美国和日本军队的行动更靠近台湾。
日本陆上自卫队还将其新型25型反舰导弹系统从九州中部熊本基地转移到该岛西北部的一个训练区，这是自3月份部署在那里以来的首次大规模演习。 10月25日，工作人员在大约两分钟内将发射器置于发射位置。

据报道，这种导弹的射程约为 1000 公里，可以威胁到东海大部分地区的解放军海军军舰，包括接近台湾的通道，同时也可以到达中国大陆部分海岸线。

北京将台湾视为中国的一部分，必要时可以通过武力统一。包括美国在内的大多数国家都不承认台湾是一个独立国家，但华盛顿反对任何尝试

【原文 English Original】
US and Japanese forces have rehearsed coordinated anti-ship strikes and mobile missile deployments across Kyushu and Japan’s southwestern islands, testing tactics designed to challenge Beijing’s ability to control surrounding waters in a conflict over [Taiwan](https://www.scmp.com/topics/taiwan?module=inline&pgtype=article).

Now in its second week, the 11-day [Keen Sword 27 exercise](https://www.scmp.com/news/china/military/article/3370210/how-expanded-japan-us-military-exercises-could-complicate-pla-planning-over-taiwan?module=inline&pgtype=article) has tested how the allies could threaten Chinese warships from multiple directions while keeping their own forces harder to target.

They have also practised repairing runways and maintaining maritime supply routes to sustain operations in the event of attacks on bases and disruptions to supply lines, according to statements from both the US and Japanese sides.

09:58

Will Batanes become the next South China Sea flashpoint?

Analysts said the tactics employed could make it harder for the People’s Liberation Army to locate and neutralise US and Japanese forces during a conflict, potentially forcing Chinese commanders to devote more resources to reconnaissance and targeting.

However, the allies’ ability to sustain dispersed operations under attack would depend on reliable communications, supplies and infrastructure, they said.

During training on October 23-24, US Navy F/A-18 and F-35 aircraft and Marine Corps ground-based launchers simulated coordinated missile strikes against an inflatable maritime target in the Sea of Japan, also known as the East Sea.

Two Japanese Aegis-equipped guided-missile destroyers, Kongo and Maya, played the opposing force, while the US Space Force helped protect communications.

The allies also tested how quickly they could move major weapons and surveillance systems across the islands.

Japanese C-2 and C-130 transport aircraft were used to move American [NMESIS anti-ship missile launchers](https://www.scmp.com/news/china/diplomacy/article/3369666/us-deploy-nmesis-anti-ship-system-japanese-island-closest-taiwan-first-time?module=inline&pgtype=article), MADIS air-defence vehicles and TPS-80 surveillance radars to the Sakishima Islands, southwest of Okinawa.

Exercise plans called for the NMESIS and MADIS systems to be positioned on Yonaguni, about 110km (70 miles) east of Taiwan, and Ishigaki, further northeast, with surveillance radars also assigned to Miyako.

Sebastian Maslow, an associate professor at the University of Tokyo, said the deployments being tested could require the PLA to account for “a more robust defence line along the first island chain”, with American and Japanese forces operating closer to Taiwan.

Japan’s Ground Self-Defence Force also moved its new Type 25 anti-ship missile system from its base in Kumamoto, central Kyushu, to a training area further northwest on the island for its first large-scale exercise since being deployed there in March. On October 25, personnel brought a launcher into firing position in about two minutes.

With a reported range of about 1,000km, the missile could threaten PLA Navy warships across much of the East China Sea, including approaches to Taiwan, while placing parts of mainland China’s coastline within reach.

Beijing sees Taiwan as part of China to be reunited by force if necessary. Most countries, including the US, do not recognise Taiwan as an independent state, but Washington is opposed to any attempt to take the self-governed island by force and is committed to supplying it with weapons.

Keen Sword 27, which runs until Thursday, has involved about 45,000 Japanese personnel and 11,000 American troops, along with forces from Australia, Canada, France, Germany, the Netherlands, New Zealand and the Philippines. Britain and South Korea are attending as observers.

It is the biennial exercise’s first iteration since Japan [established its permanent Joint Operations Command in March last year](https://www.scmp.com/news/china/military/article/3304057/japan-goes-offensive-joint-operations-command-chinas-pla-daily-says?module=inline&pgtype=article). The command was created to coordinate Japan’s ground, maritime and air forces under a single operational headquarters to enable faster, more coherent joint responses during crises.

This growing coordination was visible during the drills when Japanese units used targeting information from US forces and higher headquarters to simulate anti-ship attacks. Although no live missiles were fired, the exercise pointed to allied efforts to integrate their targeting and strike operations.

At the exercise’s opening, Lieutenant General George Rowell, deputy commander of the US Pacific Command, said the allies aimed to identify weaknesses in their military cooperation, including how they communicate, share information and coordinate operations before a conflict.

The allies also conducted runway-repair drills at four airbases across Japan, including Kadena on Okinawa, where engineers practised restoring damaged airfields to keep aircraft operating after simulated attacks.

Misato Matsuoka, an associate professor at Teikyo University, said “dispersal can improve survivability, but it does not guarantee it”, pointing to the vulnerability of airfields, ports and supply networks needed to sustain operations under attack.

Even if individual missile launchers remained operational, their effectiveness “may be reduced” if surveillance networks, communications or supply routes were “disrupted”, Matsuoka said.

A statement issued by Kagoshima prefecture on October 7, before the exercise started, said a planned American uncrewed maritime resupply operation was cancelled and a commercial vessel had been substituted for a US Army landing craft, without specifying the reasons.

Trump praises Takaichi ahead of Xi’s US visit

Other training on Tanegashima, about 40km south of Kyushu, was reduced for reasons including transport difficulties, while [Typhoon Champi](https://www.scmp.com/news/china/politics/article/3372015/thousands-evacuated-and-flights-grounded-typhoon-champi-hits-eastern-china?module=inline&pgtype=article) separately disrupted military flights and amphibious training.

Maslow said the disruptions had provided “valuable data points” for military planners, particularly on the use of commercial vessels to sustain operations. He cautioned against interpreting the changes as evidence of inadequate American or Japanese deployment capabilities.

He said that beyond its military objectives, the exercise had helped to “normalise” American and Japanese military presence across Japan’s southern islands, despite opposition from some local communities.

The key to “sustaining deterrence” would be closer allied integration of military and civilian infrastructure, he said.

title: Alibaba wins preliminary injunction against Pentagon lobbying rule
zh_title: 阿里巴巴赢得针对五角大楼游说规则的初步禁令
source: 南华早报SCMP（中国社会/科技/舆情）
summary: 一名联邦法官发现，这家中国科技巨头可能会以言论自由为由成功挑战该措施，随后阿里巴巴赢得了一项初步法院命令，阻止美国一项限制措施赶走了其华盛顿游说者。美国地区法官 Eumi K. Lee 周一裁定，政府未能提供足够的证据来证明这一限制的合理性，这实际上迫使游说公司在代表阿里巴巴和寻求五角大楼合同的客户之间做出选择。阿里巴巴拥有《南华早报》。这一决定使阿里巴巴得以保留也代表阿里巴巴的游说者。
content:
一名联邦法官发现，这家中国科技巨头可能会以言论自由为由成功挑战该措施，随后阿里巴巴赢得了一项初步法院命令，阻止美国一项限制措施赶走了其华盛顿游说者。

美国地区法官 Eumi K. Lee 周一裁定，政府未能提供足够的证据来证明这一限制的合理性，这实际上迫使游说公司在代表阿里巴巴和寻求五角大楼合同的客户之间做出选择。

阿里巴巴拥有《南华早报》。

该决定允许阿里巴巴在诉讼进行期间保留同时代表国防承包商的游说者。它不会将该公司从五角大楼所谓的中国军事公司名单中删除，也不会解决其[对该指定的挑战](https://www.scmp.com/tech/big-tech/article/3365751/cxmt-joins-forming-list-chinese-tech-firms-suing-us-pentagon-over-blacklists?module=inline&pgtype=article)。

“通过限制阿里巴巴保留说客的能力，第 4663 条在功能上限制了其政治言论，”李在加州北区发布的 26 页命令中写道。
该法律于 6 月 30 日生效，禁止五角大楼与那些保留为其[第 1260H 条中国军方名单”上的企业工作的说客的公司（或其母公司或子公司）签订合同。公司](https://www.scmp.com/news/china/diplomacy/article/3356419/us-adds-alibaba-byd-and-other-chinese-tech-champions-military-company-list?module=inline&pgtype=article)。

00:44

中央情报局在新的招募视频中针对中国军官

6月份更新的1260H名单已大幅扩展至互联网、新能源、生物技术和半导体等领域。与阿里巴巴并列的其他知名公司包括百度、比亚迪、蔚来、宇树机器人和药明康德。

裁决中引用的证据显示，尽管这一限制是通过国防合同实施的，但它对阿里巴巴接触美国政策制定者的影响却是巨大的。

在被指定之前，阿里巴巴已聘请了两打游说者和多家游说公司，在国会和行政部门代表其利益。截至 6 月 30 日，该组织已没有注册游说者。

根据该命令，多家公司告诉阿里巴巴，他们因法律原因而退出。有些人代表该公司工作了近十年。
阿里巴巴辩称，失去这些代表使其被边缘化，因为华盛顿正在考虑影响其业务的政策，包括人工智能、消费品进口和设备授权。

政府辩解称，这一限制是一项国家安全措施，称指定公司可以通过共同的游说者获取敏感军事信息，或利用这些关系影响五角大楼的决策。

五角大楼没有立即回应置评请求。

李承认国家安全的重要性，但发现政府没有充分证实这些风险，以证明限制言论的合理性。

它唯一的支持证据是国会的解释性声明，呼吁对涉及与五角大楼和中国政府合作的咨询公司的风险进行研究。

【原文 English Original】
Alibaba has won a preliminary court order blocking a US restriction that drove away its Washington lobbyists, after a federal judge found the Chinese technology giant was likely to succeed in challenging the measure on free-speech grounds.

US District Judge Eumi K. Lee ruled on Monday that the government had failed to provide sufficient evidence to justify the restriction, which effectively forces lobbying firms to choose between representing Alibaba and clients seeking Pentagon contracts.

Alibaba owns the South China Morning Post.

The decision allows Alibaba to retain lobbyists who also represent defence contractors while its lawsuit proceeds. It does not remove the company from the Pentagon’s list of alleged Chinese military companies or resolve its [challenge to that designation](https://www.scmp.com/tech/big-tech/article/3365751/cxmt-joins-growing-list-chinese-tech-firms-suing-us-pentagon-over-blacklists?module=inline&pgtype=article).

“By restricting Alibaba’s ability to retain lobbyists, Section 4663 functionally restricts its political speech,” Lee wrote in the 26-page order issued in the Northern District of California.

The law, which took effect on June 30, bars the Pentagon from entering into contracts with companies – or their parents or subsidiaries – that retain lobbyists working for businesses on its [Section 1260H list of Chinese military companies](https://www.scmp.com/news/china/diplomacy/article/3356419/us-adds-alibaba-byd-and-other-chinese-tech-champions-military-company-list?module=inline&pgtype=article).

00:44

CIA targets Chinese military officers in new recruitment video

The 1260H list updated in June has expanded significantly into sectors such as the internet, new energy, biotechnology and semiconductors. Other prominent companies included alongside Alibaba in the same cohort feature Baidu, BYD, Nio, Unitree Robotics and WuXi AppTec.

Although the restriction operates through defence contracts, its consequences for Alibaba’s access to US policymakers were substantial, according to evidence cited in the ruling.

Before its designation, Alibaba had retained more than two dozen lobbyists and multiple lobbying firms to represent its interests before Congress and the executive branch. By June 30, it had no registered lobbyists.

Several firms told Alibaba they were withdrawing because of the law, according to the order. Some had represented the company for almost a decade.

Alibaba argued that losing those representatives left it sidelined as Washington considered policies affecting its business, including artificial intelligence, consumer product imports and device authorisations.

The government defended the restriction as a national security measure, arguing that designated companies could obtain sensitive military information through shared lobbyists or use those relationships to influence Pentagon decisions.

The Pentagon did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Lee acknowledged the importance of national security but found that the government had not substantiated those risks sufficiently to justify restricting speech.

Its sole supporting exhibit was a congressional explanatory statement that called for a study of risks involving consulting firms working with both the Pentagon and the Chinese government or its affiliates.

The statement contained no findings about the risks posed by lobbyists representing designated companies, she wrote.

The government also failed to demonstrate why less restrictive alternatives, such as disclosure requirements, would be inadequate, the judge found.

Alibaba [sued on June 23](https://www.scmp.com/news/us/article/3358113/alibaba-sues-pentagon-over-china-military-blacklist?module=inline&pgtype=article) after the Pentagon included it in a June update to the military-company list. The department had also named Alibaba in a [February notice that was withdrawn](https://www.scmp.com/news/us/article/3343540/pentagon-adds-chinese-firms-military-list-then-withdraws-filing?module=inline&pgtype=article) shortly after being posted.

The Pentagon cited Alibaba’s alleged affiliations with China’s state assets regulator and the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology as grounds for its designation, according to the order.

Alibaba disputes those grounds. In submissions described by the court, the company said it did not have a close relationship with the state assets regulator and characterised its relationship with the ministry as that of a regulated company dealing with its regulator.

Monday’s preliminary injunction follows an [earlier temporary restraining order](https://www.scmp.com/tech/big-tech/article/3359638/alibaba-wins-reprieve-us-lobbying-after-pentagon-blacklisted-companies?module=inline&pgtype=article) that was due to expire that day. The relief applies specifically to the lobbying-related restriction concerning Alibaba; the judge declined at this stage to block the law across the board or remove the company’s military designation.

The company did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

title: 3 Questions on Lula's victory in Brazil to Regine Schönenberg | Heinrich Böll Stiftung | Brussels office - European Union
summary: Lula has won a historic fourth term, a hopeful signal that the far right can be defeated at the ballot box. Young voters, grassroots activists and more than 10 million members of “Lula’s Army” turned the tide in three weeks. Regine Schönenb
content:
Lula has won a historic fourth term, a hopeful signal that the far right can be defeated at the ballot box. Young voters, grassroots activists and more than 10 million members of “Lula’s Army” turned the tide in three weeks. Regine Schönenberg, Director of the Heinrich-Böll-Stiftung office in Rio de Janeiro, explains what drove this comeback, how civil society can defend social justice, climate and Indigenous rights against a conservative Congress, and what Europe should prioritise now.

### 1. What proved decisive in securing Lula’s re-election, and what does the close result tell us about the continued appeal of Bolsonarism in Brazilian society?

The historic switch to the leading position between the first and second turn of the Brazilian elections demonstrated the vitality of the Brazilian democracy. Within three weeks of intensive campaigning of “Lula's Army” on the streets and within cyberspace the election spirit changed completely. Especially, the mass mobilisation of young people energised the campaign. The most significant factor, however, was the online and on-the-ground mobilisation led by André Janones, a pro-Lula federal congressman, whose WhatsApp channel, known as “Lula's Army,” grew to more than 10 million members who followed his daily instructions to spread pro-Lula content. Over several weeks, rallies also brought supporters to the streets, many organised outside formal party structures. The result: About 3 million voters that abstained in the first turn participated in the runoff, and Lula gained about 4,4 million votes more than Flávio Bolsonaro, and about 10 million votes more than in the first round, whereas his opponent gained less than 4 million additional votes.

However, almost 60 million Brazilians voted for the candidate of the extreme-right due to a strong rejection of the person, Lula da Silva, the worker`s party (PT), an endless flood of fake news and Flavio’s aggressive promises of crime-combat in Bukele's style. Also, the fact, that Flávio Bolsonaro served as a substitute for his imprisoned father further weakened his campaign. Just as the far right fostered anti-PT sentiment within society, anti-Bolsonaro sentiment was a key factor in this election, leading people to reject Flávio Bolsonaro.

### 2. Where do you see the greatest opportunities – and political obstacles – for Lula to advance social justice, climate protection and Indigenous rights? What role can civil society play in pushing for progress?

Lula retaining the Presidency has a major impact on federal policy areas, such as social policies, environmental policy and various multilateral partnerships. In part, this election was not about Lula or the PT; it was about ensuring the continuation of social programmes and strengthening democracy. What must not be forgotten, however, is that from February 2027 on, Lula will have to deal with a Senate and Parliament that are considerably more conservative than at present. Traditionally, elections for governors, senators and members of parliament are heavily regional in nature and linked to numerous clientelist relationships. The fact that Brazil has a first-past-the-post electoral system does not help in this regard.

Lula's most important policy fields such as social justice, climate protection and Indigenous rights are in serious danger to be torpedoed by both chambers of Congress. Draft bills on all critical questions in those policy fields are already prepared and often ready for voting. To prevent them to get implemented is a complicated process of vetoing and counter-vetoing that, together with a lot of negotiation might take years. Unfortunately, the latter is true for constructive legislative projects of the government, too.

The extent to which Lula will be able to prevent the centre-right faction from adopting an obstructionist stance will depend on the composition and communication skills of his government team. During his first speech following his victory on Sunday evening, he was flanked by his loyal Vice-President, Geraldo Alckmin, and surrounded by young politicians and activists. He explicitly highlighted the issues of cybersecurity and the regulation of platforms, his learning process regarding political communication in the virtual sphere, and his plans for greater political participation. It spoke of a new beginning, innovation and the inclusion of civil society, which had made his victory possible in the first place.

It is therefore no surprise that Flávio Bolsonaro immediately declared that he would not recognise the election victory. The extension of polling station opening hours until 7 pm, due to rain and bus cancellations, is now being used as a pretext for this all too obvious manoeuvre, which is not expected to meet with much success. Flavio’s claim is controversial, given that his own campaign had also requested an extension of voting hours. In fact, people here are waiting for Flávio, just like his brother Eduardo Bolsonaro, to leave the country for the US to escape prosecution over numerous corruption scandals.

### 3. What does Lula’s victory mean for Brazil’s relations with the EU, and what should European partners prioritise to support democracy and a socially just ecological transition?

The most important outcome for Europe is that Lula can now continue his role as an important player – entirely in the spirit of traditional Brazilian foreign policy – within forums such as the G20, BRICS and also in the EU-Mercosur agreement, and that Brazil will not bow to pressure to join Trump’s ‘Shield of the Americas’.

As a democrat, one can only hope that the shift in Brazil – and, at the same time, in Serbia – signals a reversal of a global trend towards greater democratic representation.

Chinese President Xi Jinping on Tuesday ⁠extended condolences to the family of former Japanese Prime Minister Yasuo Fukuda, who died last week, while calling on Japan’s current leadership to “safeguard the political foundation” of ties that have been ​strained since late last year.

Fukuda, who died on Thursday ‌from heart ‌failure at the age of 90, used ​his brief period in office to seek closer ties with Asian neighbors, particularly China, with which relations have periodically ⁠been tense.

Fukuda was a Japanese politician of integrity and responsibility, as well ⁠as an old friend of the Chinese people, Xi said in his message, according to ​the state-run Xinhua news agency. ⁠Fukuda “upheld a correct view of history,” Xi said.

The comments were a rare direct ⁠reference by ​the Chinese leader to the relationship between ​the two countries since it deteriorated late last year.

Ties ​between ‌China and Japan sank to their worst levels in years after current Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi angered Beijing in November 2025 by suggesting that Japan ‌could deploy its military if a Chinese move against neighboring Taiwan also threatened its territory.

Beijing called Takaichi’s remarks “egregious” and demanded that she retract them. China has advised its citizens against travel to ​Japan, ​while also banning exports to Japan of ​items that can have a military application, including some ⁠rare earths.

In his message on Tuesday, Xi said he “hopes Japan’s current leaders to cherish the hard work and efforts made by the older generation of politicians, abide by ​the four political documents between China and Japan, and earnestly safeguard the political foundation of bilateral relations.”

China would remember Fukuda’s contributions to China-Japan relations and to Asia’s development, Xi added.

content:
[五角大楼](https://www.scmp.com/topics/pentagon-us-department-defence?module=inline&pgtype=article)已指定科罗拉多号作为第一艘[美国](https://www.scmp.com/topics/united-states?module=inline&pgtype=article)核动力攻击潜艇加入驻扎在西澳大利亚的轮换部队。

官员周二表示，这艘长 115 米（380 英尺）的弗吉尼亚级潜艇配备对地攻击导弹和先进鱼雷，将于 2027 年底驶往新的[澳大利亚](https://www.scmp.com/topics/australia?module=inline&pgtype=article)基地。

盟国在一份联合声明中表示，此次部署是美国、澳大利亚和英国根据其《Aukus》防御协议在太平洋建立联合威慑力量的一个“重要里程碑”。

该防务协议被视为对中国在该地区军事集结的回应，旨在为澳大利亚海军配备一支隐形核动力潜艇舰队，并扩大这三个盟国之间的军事合作。

澳大利亚不允许外国军事基地在其领土上建立，但每年在北部城市达尔文接待美国海军陆战队为期六个月的演习。

2025 年 2 月 26 日，美国海军军官在停靠在西澳大利亚州罗金厄姆的斯特林号海军舰艇上的弗吉尼亚级快速攻击潜艇明尼苏达号上站岗。照片：法新社
核动力潜艇轮换部队——被称为“西潜艇轮换部队”——将驻扎在西澳大利亚的斯特灵海军基地。

该基地预计将轮流容纳多达五艘快速攻击潜艇——四艘来自美国，一艘来自[英国](https://www.scmp.com/topics/britain?module=inline&pgtype=article)。这三个国家表示，这将帮助澳大利亚为操作和维护自己的核动力潜艇做好准备，同时支持其盟友的部署和维护。

澳大利亚国防部长理查德·马勒斯告诉新闻频道 News24，轮换潜艇部队是奥库斯协议下的第一个“真正重大的里程碑”。

“一切都步入正轨，”马尔斯说。 “斯特林号航空母舰上有美国人员正在为此做准备。”

根据政府预测，奥库斯潜艇计划是澳大利亚国防战略的核心，30 年内的耗资可能高达 2350 亿美元。

法国国防集团泰雷兹周一表示，它已在悉尼西郊的赖德尔米尔开设了一个声纳设施，为澳大利亚军方的潜艇、舰艇和海上平台生产和维护拖曳阵列声纳系统。
该站点由泰雷兹澳大利亚公司和英联邦共同资助，将为猎人级护卫舰、柯林斯级潜艇和 BlueSentry 自主系统提供声纳。据描述，投资额为数百万澳元，但没有透露具体数字。

本地保障旨在缩短海上维护周期并延长澳大利亚情报、监视和侦察行动的部署时间。

泰雷兹拥有 ⁠Naval Group 约 35% 的股份，该集团于 2021 年失去了与澳大利亚的潜艇合同，当时堪培拉取消了该计划，转而支持 Aukus 协议，引发了法国与澳大利亚之间的外交争端。

_路透社的补充报道_

【原文 English Original】
[The Pentagon](https://www.scmp.com/topics/pentagon-us-department-defence?module=inline&pgtype=article) has assigned the USS Colorado as the first [US](https://www.scmp.com/topics/united-states?module=inline&pgtype=article) nuclear-powered attack submarine to join a rotating force to be based in Western Australia.

The 115-metre (380-foot) Virginia-class submarine, armed with land-attack missiles and sophisticated torpedoes, would sail to the new [Australian](https://www.scmp.com/topics/australia?module=inline&pgtype=article) base in late 2027, officials said on Tuesday.

The deployment was a “significant milestone” in building up a joint US-Australia-UK deterrence in the Pacific under their [Aukus](https://www.scmp.com/topics/aukus-alliance?module=inline&pgtype=article) defence pact, the allies said in a joint statement.

The defence agreement, seen as a response to China’s military build-up in the region, aims to equip Australia’s navy with a fleet of stealthy nuclear-powered submarines and expand military cooperation between the three allies.

Australia does not permit foreign military bases on its soil, but hosts US Marines for exercises for six months a year in the northern city of Darwin.

US Navy officers stand guard aboard the Virginia-class fast-attack submarine USS Minnesota docked at HMAS Stirling in Rockingham, Western Australia, on February 26, 2025. Photo: AFP

The rotating force of nuclear-powered submarines – known as Submarine Rotational Force-West – is to be hosted at a naval base in Western Australia, HMAS Stirling.

The base is projected to host up to five fast-attack submarines – four from the United States and one from the [UK](https://www.scmp.com/topics/britain?module=inline&pgtype=article) – on a rotational basis. It would help Australia prepare for operating and maintaining its own nuclear-powered submarines while supporting its allies’ deployments and maintenance, the three countries said.

The rotating submarine force was the first “really big milestone” under the Aukus agreement, Australian Defence Minister Richard Marles told news channel News24.

“It’s on track,” Marles said. “There are American personnel at HMAS Stirling right now readying the site for this.”

The Aukus submarine programme lies at the heart of Australia’s defence strategy and could cost up to US$235 billion over 30 years, according to government forecasts.

French defence ⁠group Thales said ⁠on Monday ⁠it had opened a sonar facility in the Western Sydney suburb of Rydalmere to produce ‌and maintain towed array sonar systems for the Australian military’s submarines, ships and maritime platforms.

The site, co-funded by Thales Australia and ⁠the Commonwealth, will supply sonar for Hunter-class ‌frigates, Collins-class submarines and the BlueSentry autonomous system. Investment is ‌described as multimillion Australian dollars but no ⁠specific ⁠figure was disclosed.

Local sustainment is intended ‌to cut offshore maintenance periods and extend deployment ‌times for ‌Australian intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance operations.

Thales owns about 35 per cent of ⁠Naval Group, which lost a submarine contract ⁠with Australia in 2021 when Canberra cancelled the programme in favour ‌of the ‌Aukus pact, triggering a diplomatic dispute between [France](https://www.scmp.com/topics/france?module=inline&pgtype=article) and Australia.

# 中国希望遏制与人工智能相关的裁员：那么法国在这方面对员工有何计划？

面对人工智能带来的就业威胁，中国刚公布了18项措施，旨在预防失业并支持受影响的劳动者。这一举措让一法国高科技新闻网站提出了一个与法国人自身息息相关的问题：面对自动化，法国将如何保障其员工的就业？

发表时间： 27/10/2026 - 22:07 更改时间： 27/10/2026 - 22:15

 9 分钟 浏览时间

 在这张创作于2026年9月23日的示意图中，展示了拼写出“AI”字样的字母、一个键盘以及一只机器手。路透社/Dado Ruvic/示意图/资料照片 REUTERS - Reuters

 作者： [珍妮特](https://rfi.fr/cn/%E4%BD%9C%E8%80%85/%E7%8F%8D%E5%A6%AE%E7%89%B9/ "珍妮特")

广告

继续浏览后续

去年五月，一家领先的法国高科技新闻网站“**Clubic”**重新审视了杭州法院的一项裁决，该裁决认定，因一名员工拒绝与其职位自动化相关的降职而将其解雇是非法的。

如今，这一问题已上升到国家层面。10月23日，中国国务院办公厅发布了18项措施，分为六大领域，涵盖创造就业、社会保障（包括培训和失业预防）等多个方面。

法国也提出了其在工作场所应用人工智能的计划。然而，两国的方案存在显著差异。

**中国旨在提早预防失业问题**

最重要的措施是评估就业风险。某些可能导致大量失业的人工智能项目，尤其是在市场准入受限的行业，将从这一角度进行审查。对于其他项目，有关部门计划根据具体情况进行评估。

北京方面也呼吁劳动密集型行业保持谨慎。政府鼓励企业优先考虑在劳动力短缺或安全风险较高的岗位上实现自动化。也鼓励雇主考虑在任何潜在的裁员之前设置过渡期，事先向员工提供信息和再培训机会。

该文本还规定要监测失业风险，并打击人力资源领域算法的滥用，尤其是在算法导致歧视或侵犯隐私权和休息权的情况下。然而，这些指导原则并非全面禁止基于人工智能的解雇。其适用范围将取决于具体的实施方式。

在法国，培训仍然是重中之重。 法国政府于9月22日公布了“人工智能2027加速计划”，该计划包含12项措施，并在未来一年投入超过8000万欧元。其重点显然有所不同：培训员工和求职者，扶持企业，并预测职业发展趋势。

该计划包括一个名为“探索人工智能”（Explore AI）的免费公共平台、一项国家技能认证，以及一个隶属于研究、调查和统计局（DARES）的观察站，该观察站负责研究人工智能对就业和工作条件的影响。政府同样地希望能加强社会对话。

但这些措施的主要目的是帮助工人适应技术变革。它们本身并不构成一套新的旨在对抗解雇的保护体系。

**在法国，法院也可以介入。**

不过，法国法律确实提供了一些保护措施。对于拥有至少 50 名员工的公司，引入影响工作条件的新技术可能需要与企业内的社会经济委员会 (CSE) 进行磋商。

9月15日，克雷泰伊法院下令停止GISI（Infopro Digital新闻集团旗下子公司）的重组计划，该计划涉及裁减8名编辑秘书职位。GISI出版包括《新工厂》（L'Usine Nouvelle）、《LSA》和《保险评论》（L'Argus de l'assurance）在内的多家刊物，此次重组是更大规模的19个裁员计划的一部分。该公司估计，其人工智能生成系统可以承担约70%的工作。然而，法官认为，这一估计在实际条件下未经充分验证，不足以排除对其他员工的健康和工作量造成的风险。

因此，该项目已暂停，等待进一步测试。这项临时决定本身并不构成人工智能相关解雇的违法行为；它旨在提醒雇主注意其在职业风险预防方面的义务。

该框架将由《欧洲人工智能法》规定的某些义务加以补充。而这项法案将人力资源中使用的AI系统归类为高风险系统，并将相关法规的实施日期推迟至2027年12月2日，这将进一步强化上述框架。

显然，中法两国劳动力市场和工具都不尽相同。但GISI的案例凸显了问题的关键所在。在裁减八个职位之前，该公司曾指望人工智能能够处理其70%的工作量。法官只是要求他们在实际环境中证明这一点。 因为人工智能所承诺的生产力提升往往只是估计值。然而，裁员却绝非是个假想。

summary: 摘要： Statista 的新研究和专家对如何构建现实世界供应链灵活性的见解。您的物流计划最后一次真正按计划进行是什么时候？在物流方面，预计会出现中断。然而，尽管许多运营商正在抓住东南亚更多航线选择和模式带来的机遇，但新的研究表明，物流系统并没有跟上。 **更多选择、更多航线，但并非更强弹性** 去年，中国与东南亚国家联盟 (ASEAN) 之间的贸易额超过 1.05 万亿美元。制造中心正在蔓延
content:
摘要： Statista 的新研究和专家对如何构建现实世界供应链灵活性的见解。您的物流计划最后一次真正按计划进行是什么时候？在物流方面，预计会出现中断。然而，尽管许多运营商正在抓住东南亚更多航线选择和模式带来的机遇，但新的研究表明，物流系统并没有跟上。

**更多选择，更多路线，但不是更多弹性**
 去年，中国与东盟贸易额突破1.05万亿美元。制造中心正在整个地区蔓延，需要更多的货运选择，所有这一切都是在几乎持续中断的背景下进行的。每一次转变都迫使公司重新思考如何（有时是在哪里）转移库存。

该地区 87% 的物流决策者表示，他们的应对措施是增加多式联运路线的使用。然而，92% 的受访者表示，多样化路由仅在其网络中部分实施。

在我们研究的四项单独衡量标准中，只有 0-2% 的受访者选择了最高级别的路由实施、合作伙伴连接、公共机构集成或端到端可见性。
多样化的路线选择只是第一步。还必须有可用的容量。商业安排需要做好准备。交接工作需要发挥作用。并且需要有人有权拨打电话。如果没有这些要素，纸面上看起来具有弹性的路径在实际发生中断时几乎无法提供灵活性。

> 自新冠疫情爆发以来，供应链出现了巨大的波动……每年我们都会遇到一些中断。”
> _Kevin Burrell，马士基 – 湄公河董事总经理_

[![图片2](https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/08796.jpg)](https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/08796.jpg)

**对破坏的下意识反应**
 在过去 12-24 个月中，69% 的物流领导者表示，阻塞点对其运营产生了显着或非常显着的影响。大多数人都会对每次危机做出反应，而不是为危机做好计划——将安全库存增加 50% 或转向最后一刻的空运选择。在这两种情况下，运营商都需要支付更多费用来适应不可预测的网络。

发现更多

航运新闻订阅

每日航运新闻

货运服务

**真正的弹性构建者：充分利用路线选项的系统、数据、合作伙伴和移交**
从中国通过东南亚运输货物可能涉及一长串组织：货运代理、卡车运输公司、码头、海关机构、经纪人、港口、航空公司、航运公司和仓库都可能接触同一批货物。

就个体而言，其中许多组织都装备精良，但每次移交都会造成信息黑洞，而每一种额外的模式都会造成另一次移交。

因此，虽然额外的模式和网关为您提供了更多解决中断的方法，但它们也为您提供了更多信息和责任消失的点。这些弱点在不同地区之间也不一致——研究发现，两个受访者群体的交付时间差异很大，但背后存在不同的问题。这说明了为什么相同的解决方案不能简单地应用于每个走廊。

缺乏数字化也不是问题——例如，91% 的组织已经使用数字文档，但 51% 的组织还报告称集成有限
