title: China has tripled its satellite fleet since 2018 as expansion continues: DIA
zh_title: DIA：自 2018 年以来，随着扩张的继续，中国的卫星数量已增加两倍
summary: 华盛顿——国防情报局 (DIA) 的一份[新报告](https://www.dia.mil/Articles/Press-Release/Article/4633953/dia-releases-challenges-to-security-in-space/) 发现，自 2018 年以来，中国的情报、监视和侦察 (ISR) 卫星数量增加了两倍，并继续扩大探测、跟踪和瞄准美国及其盟国地面部队的能力和在海上。 “中国采用强大的天基情监侦能力，旨在增强其全球态势感知并实现远程打击”，包括电光（EO）和合成孔径雷达
content:
华盛顿——国防情报局 (DIA) 的一份[新报告](https://www.dia.mil/Articles/Press-Release/Article/4633953/dia-releases-challenges-to-security-in-space/) 发现，自 2018 年以来，中国的情报、监视和侦察 (ISR) 卫星数量增加了两倍，并继续扩大探测、跟踪和瞄准美国及其盟国地面部队的能力和在海上。

根据国防情报局周一发布的 2026 年太空安全挑战报告，“中国采用了强大的天基情监侦能力，旨在增强其全球态势感知能力并实现远程打击”，其中包括电光 (EO) 和合成孔径雷达 (SAR) 图像卫星以及其他提供电子和信号情报数据的卫星。

报告称，中国的情监侦卫星网络可以帮助解放军监视和瞄准世界各地的美国及其盟军，特别是整个印度-太平洋地区，包括朝鲜半岛、台湾、菲律宾、印度洋和南海。

DIA 的报告呼应了美国太空部队和太空司令部对解放军日益增强的构建[“杀伤链”](https://breakingdefense.com/2025/06/us-space-commands-gen-whiting-talks-golden-dome-ew-and-chinas-space-based-kill-chain/)以针对美国国内外联合部队的能力的担忧。
美国战略与国际研究中心航空航天安全项目副主任克莱顿·斯沃普表示，中国正在大力投资天基传感器，以监测地球并识别、跟踪和瞄准印度-太平洋地区的物体。

“美国和盟国决策者应该担心的是，解放军的传感器网络会如何削弱美国在空中和海底领域的隐形优势。未来我们是否能够在空中和海底领域进行不被发现的行动？”他告诉《突破防御》。

DIA 报告呼应了 [2026 年 7 月](https://www.spaceforce.mil/About-Us/Fact-Sheets/Fact-Sheet-Display/article/4297159/space-threat-fact-sheet/)太空部队关于太空威胁的情况说明书，指出截至 7 月，中国在轨道上拥有超过 510 颗 ISR 卫星。然而，与太空部队文件不同的是，DIA 报告承认其数量包括中华人民共和国和中国商业公司拥有的卫星。

报告称：“虽然许多ISR卫星表面上与商业和民用任务有关，但它们能力的双重用途性质以及可能的中国军民融合政策意味着它们收集的数据或图像可以被解放军使用。”

国防情报局还表示，中国商业公司正在向“因支持武器扩散而被西方供应商禁止的国家行为者”提供图像。
国防情报局的报告强调，中国的情监侦机群不断扩大并在技术上不断改进，特别是通过北京日益增长的近地轨道卫星群。

然而，美国企业研究所 (AEI) 高级研究员托德·哈里森 (Todd Harrison) 表示，DIA 的数据并不清楚其统计中包含哪些卫星，也缺乏重要的背景信息。

他告诉《Breaking Defense》，中国的作战监视和气象卫星数量已从 2018 年的 141 颗增加到今天的 541 颗，而仅用于监视的卫星数量已从 124 颗增加到 453 颗。“这些数字并没有告诉你的是，近年来曲线的斜率已经趋于平稳，卫星数量的增长速度没有那么快，”哈里森说。

与此同时，美国有 643 个正在进行的调查

【原文 English Original】
WASHINGTON — A [new report](https://www.dia.mil/Articles/Press-Release/Article/4633953/dia-releases-challenges-to-security-in-space/) by the Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) finds that China has tripled its fleet of intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR) satellites since 2018 and continues to expand capabilities to detect, track and target US and allied forces on the ground and at sea.

“China employs a robust space-based ISR capability designed to enhance its worldwide situational awareness and enable long-range strikes,” including electro-optical (EO) and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery satellites and others that provide electronic and signals intelligence data, according to the DIA’s 2026 _Challenges to Space Security_ report, released Monday.

The report says China’s ISR satellite network can help the PLA monitor and target US and allied forces worldwide, particularly across the Indo-Pacific — including the Korean Peninsula, Taiwan, the Philippines, the Indian Ocean and the South China Sea.

The DIA report echoes concerns from US Space Force and Space Command about the PLA’s growing ability to build [“kill chains”](https://breakingdefense.com/2025/06/us-space-commands-gen-whiting-talks-golden-dome-ew-and-chinas-space-based-kill-chain/) to target US joint forces abroad and at home.

Clayton Swope, deputy director of the Center for Strategic and International Studies’ Aerospace Security Project, said China is investing heavily in space-based sensors to monitor Earth and identify, track and target objects in the Indo-Pacific.

“A concern on the minds of US and allied decision makers should be how PLA sensor webs could erode US advantages derived from stealth in the air and undersea domains. Will we be able to operate undetected in the air and undersea domains in the future?” he told Breaking Defense.

Echoing a [July 2026](https://www.spaceforce.mil/About-Us/Fact-Sheets/Fact-Sheet-Display/article/4297159/space-threat-fact-sheet/)Space Force fact sheet on space threats, the DIA report states that China had more than 510 ISR satellites in orbit as of July.Unlike the Space Force document, however, the DIA report acknowledges that its count includes satellites owned by both the People’s Republic of China and Chinese commercial firms.

“While many of these ISR satellites are ostensibly affiliated with commercial and civil missions, the dual-use nature of their capabilities and possibly the Chinese military-civil fusion policies means the data or imagery they collect can be used by the PLA,” the report says.

The DIA also says Chinese commercial firms are supplying imagery “to state actors banned by Western providers for supporting weapons proliferation.”

China’s ISR fleet continues to expand and improve technologically, the DIA report stresses, particularly through Beijing’s growing constellation of satellites in low Earth orbit.

However, American Enterprise Institute’s (AEI) Senior Fellow Todd Harrison said the DIA’s data is unclear about which satellites are included in its count and also lacks important context.

He told Breaking Defense that China’s operational surveillance and weather satellite fleet has grown from 141 in 2018 to 541 today, while its surveillance-only fleet has increased from 124 to 453.“What those numbers don’t tell you is that the slope of the curve has leveled off in recent years — the number of satellites is not increasing as fast,” Harrison said.

Meanwhile, the US has 643 operational surveillance and weather satellites — up from 298 in 2018 — and is expanding its ISR fleet faster than China, he said.

The following chart, created for Breaking Defense from AEI’s [Space Data Navigator](https://spacedata.aei.org/space/satellites?s=sVyo34KeBY), shows that trend.

The DIA report is the third in a series of unclassified reports examining US concerns about adversary advancements in military space, with the first version published in 2019.

The new report covers space threats emanating from China, Russia and “emerging” space powers.

It also looks at developments expected to exacerbate future challenges to US interests in space. Among those listed in the 2026 report: reusable space systems, such as rockets and spaceplanes; increasing use of artificial intelligence; orbital congestion; the collision risk posed by the many non-maneuverable spacecraft that will remain on orbit long after becoming inoperable; and the growing interest in satellites stationed in very low Earth orbit.

Intriguingly, the report includes what appears to be the first public image of China’s reusable [spaceplane](https://breakingdefense.com/tag/chinese-spaceplane/), most recently launched [in February](https://en.people.cn/n3/2026/0207/c90000-20423647.html). The spaceplane is widely believed to be modeled after the US X-37B. Victoria Samson, chief director of space security and stability at the Secure World Foundation, said the image appears to support that assessment.

“It looks a lot like the X-37B!” she told Breaking Defense.

The DIA concludes by predicting that space will become increasingly congested and competitive as capabilities advance and more countries expand their presence in the domain.

“The increase of Chinese, Russian, Iranian, and North Korean counterspace capabilities, rapid growth in the number of space objects, and the proliferation of requirements for space-enabled services will all complicate operations in space in the coming decade,” the report adds.

title: 爆王小洪患癌将卸职 缅北电诈资金流向公安部个人(图)  -  动向 -
summary: 2026年3月5日，中共公安部长王小洪和中央军委副主席张升民（右）在北京人民大会堂出席中共全国人大会议开幕式。（图片来源：FLORENCE LO/POOL/AFP via Getty Images） 【看中国2026年10月28日讯】（看中国记者李德言综合报导）日前，据知情人爆料，[王小洪](https://www.secretchina.com/news/gb/tag/%E7%8E%8B%E5%B0%8F%E6%B4%AA)患癌将卸任公安部部长职务，关于他的接班人选也成为中
content:
2026年3月5日，中共公安部长王小洪和中央军委副主席张升民（右）在北京人民大会堂出席中共全国人大会议开幕式。（图片来源：FLORENCE LO/POOL/AFP via Getty Images）

【看中国2026年10月28日讯】（看中国记者李德言综合报导）日前，据知情人爆料，[王小洪](https://www.secretchina.com/news/gb/tag/%E7%8E%8B%E5%B0%8F%E6%B4%AA)患癌将卸任公安部部长职务，关于他的接班人选也成为中共不同派系角力的焦点。而且中共公安系统处理缅北电信诈骗案件的资金去向，王小洪涉及的巨额贪污腐败都需要收拾。而美起诉书指出，中共公安部参与受贿保护太子集团。

## **爆王小洪患癌 性命可能难保**

近日，中共体制内知情人士对海外中文媒体《大纪元》爆料说，中共[公安部](https://www.secretchina.com/news/gb/tag/%E5%85%AC%E5%AE%89%E9%83%A8)长王小洪因患癌，病灶在上呼吸道或是喉部，病情已发展一年时间。中共高层子女都知道这个情况。因王小洪性命可能难保，他将卸下公安部部长之职。

知情人说，“病情实在挺不了，他要能挺一点，他都不退下来。这么多电诈工作都在收尾，缅北还有那么多人在那里输血，一年几百亿美金，这种人能放弃这个吗？实在没办法了。”

[![Image 2](https://img6.secretchina.com/pic/2025/7-29/p3676411a560438137.jpg)](https://www.naturenergy.us/)

该消息人士说，王小洪卸下公安部部长后不排除继续保留中共国务委员的身份，或是转任全国政协，弄个闲职，实际上基本属于退休。

知情人披露，已经有几任中共公安部长的身体都出现问题了，包括前中共政法委书记、前公安部部长孟建柱也患癌，认为这是“报应”。“癌症这个东西，再好的医疗治不好。”“他（王小洪）和这么多电诈集团有关，主要是他报应了。几任公安部长都身体有问题，包括孟建柱都是癌症。”知情人说，这个东西中共太子党内部研究，都觉得“挺邪”。

据悉，中共公安部是中共用于迫害法轮功和[中国](https://www.secretchina.com/)人权的主要打手。

2026年3月18日至4月14日，没有关于王小洪出席公开活动的报导，引发诸多猜测，例如他是否遭到清洗等。

同年4月，旅澳自媒体人蒋罔正在X平台披露说，王小洪没问题，只是咽喉癌，身体不好。他只是不舍得放权（钱）而已，他是所有中共干部中最懂数字货币的，他要处理大量的比特币和USDT，从中可以提取12%∼15%利益。这是王小洪不肯放权的真实原因。

## **爆中共高层正考虑王小洪接班人选**

今年4月，海外社媒突然流传关于王小洪患咽喉癌的消息，当时海外有多个自媒体账号爆料王小洪将卸职，包括时任湖南省委书记沈晓明、江西省委书记尹弘、时任湖北省委书记王忠林等人或将接替他出任公安部长。

知情人说，“王小洪身体要没问题，他整天要干他的事，他跟[习近平](https://www.secretchina.com/news/gb/tag/%E4%B9%A0%E8%BF%91%E5%B9%B3)这种铁杆，他的年龄还够，他肯定还要再干一届，但他干不了。已经确定了，现在正在选人，选他接班人。”

知情人表示，中共高层正考虑王小洪的接班人选，但习近平未必能接受王的推荐，因为相关的人事安排背后可能涉及到不同派系的角力。“大家都在博弈这个位置，看看习近平能选谁上（出任公安部长）。”

2026年10月24日，中共官宣沈晓明不再担任湖南省委书记、常委委员职务。关于他下一步的走向，也引发关注。

## **公安部新调任官员不是习派系**

2026年9月9日，据中共公安部官网领导栏目更新后显示，原新疆伊犁哈萨克自治州公安局长高琪目前已出任中共公安部党委委员、反恐专员（副部长级）。

高琪是江派官员王乐泉、张春贤的的旧部，且在他们主政新疆期间不断升职，被认为有江派色彩。

2026年9月9日，中共党媒新华社在报导中共国务院的任免名单时提到，任命秦运彪为中共公安部副部长。

秦运彪长期在广西公安系统任职，是前中共政治局常委郭声琨与现任全国人大副委员长彭清华的广西旧部。

秦运彪和高琪被指没有明显的习近平派系背景，他们与[江泽民](https://www.secretchina.com/news/gb/tag/%E6%B1%9F%E6%B3%BD%E6%B0%91)、曾庆红派系的势力关联密切。

这也对应到该知情人所披露的“相关的人事安排背后可能涉及到不同派系的角力。”

## **王小洪的亲信、旧部接连离开公安部**

王小洪是习近平的重要亲信，也是他在福建任职时的旧部，据说两人在福建时私交很好。

近年来，王小洪的公安部亲信接连被调离和免职。

2026年7月16日，谭权被免去“公安部部长助理”职务，他于7月31日出任重庆市副市长、重庆市公安局局长。

2026年6月26日，中共公安部副部长级反恐专员岳修虎调任为国家发改委副主任。

2026年9月初，中共中央港澳办官网“办领导”栏目更新后显示，公安部二局（经济犯罪侦查局）党委书记、局长华列兵出任中纪委国家监委驻港澳办纪检监察组组长。华列兵跟随王小洪在河南省公安厅、北京市公安局、公安部一路担任其下属并升职。

2025年7月，原公安部副部长陈思源、孙茂利被免职。同年5月，公安部部长助理、公安部办公厅主任胡彬郴调任为江苏省副省长、公安厅长。同年4月，许甘露被免去公安部副部长、国家移民管理局（国家出入境管理局）局长职务，现任中共第十四届全国人大外事委员会副主任委员，中国警察学会会长。

岳修虎、陈思源、孙茂利、胡彬郴、许甘露、谭权都是王小洪的嫡系亲信与旧部。

## **[缅北电诈](https://www.secretchina.com/news/gb/tag/%E7%BC%85%E5%8C%97%E7%94%B5%E8%AF%88)案资金被指很多款项流向个人**

据知情人披露，中共公安系统处理缅北电信诈骗案件的资金去向，王小洪涉及到的巨额贪污腐败，这些“烂尾”都需要收拾。而且缅北电诈案涉及资金规模庞大，很多款项都流向了个人。知情人表示，“五百亿美金，两百亿进国家财政了，三百亿都进个人兜了。你拿这些钱，虚拟货币包括比特币，虚拟资产这些钱国家是看不到的，你也查不到。”

从2023年开始，中共公安部进行所谓打击缅北涉中国电信网络诈骗的工作。王小洪也参与到中缅打击电诈的高层协调。

## **王小洪与缅甸对“10．20”枪击案进行交涉**

2026年10月5日，由中共公安部和中共喉舌央视联合摄制的记录片《缅北电诈覆灭纪实》播出第一集《利剑出鞘》。

据央视报导称，2023年10月20日，由缅北果敢明学昌家族控制的电诈园发生“10．20”枪击案，中国公民4死4伤。

报导称，果敢“迫于中共警方压力”，对电诈园区进行检查。2023年10月19日，明家假称要送涉诈人员回国，实际是把卧虎山庄园区内人员转移。电诈人员发现明家并不想把他们送回中国，想趁机逃跑。10月20日凌晨，明家控制的两个园区民兵队镇压逃亡人员，出现4死4伤。

2023年10月31日，时任缅甸国家管理委员会主席敏昂莱在缅甸首都内比都会见王小洪。王小洪与缅甸内政部部长对“10．20”枪击案进行交涉。同年11月12日，中共警方对明学昌、明国平、明菊兰和明珍珍发出通缉令。在4天后，明国平、明菊兰、明珍珍3人被抓捕并移交中方，明学昌自杀。

2024年6月，《华盛顿邮报》调查报导指出，缅北果敢白、魏、刘等家族经营的犯罪网络，长期和中共官员保持密切的关系。报导根据联合国官员、官方网站资料、法院记录、照片和多个知情者的访谈，追查上述家族与中共官员之间的合作及经济往来等情况。上述一些家族首脑在犯罪案件持续发生期间，仍和中共官员有联系。

2026年1月29日，浙江省温州市中级法院依法对明国平、明珍珍、周卫昌、巫鸿明、吴森龙、傅雨彬等11人宣判并执行死刑。

中共当局对此进行宣传，但王小洪在东南亚电诈园区究竟扮演什么角色，目前还无法完全确定，而美国政府的起诉书则给出一些答案。

## **美起诉书：中共公安部、国安部保护太重集团**

2025年10月，美国、英国联手把东南亚诈骗集团“太子集团”定性为跨国犯罪组织，并对包括陈志与胡晓伟（“太子集团”二号人物）在内的146个个人和公司实施制裁，查扣大约12万7000枚比特币，按当时市价是150亿美元。

2026年1月7日，据《柬中时报》报导称，“太子控股集团”创始人兼董事长陈志在柬埔寨被捕，并被遣送回中国接受调查。

2026年6月23日，美国财政部宣布对太子集团9名高层和26个实体实施进一步制裁，包括太子集团领导层、诈骗集团投资者和幌子公司。

2026年7月5日，胡晓伟再次因涉嫌违反日本《出入国管理及难民认定法》被捕。日本媒体引述消息人士称，胡小伟在同年7月29日被送往美国，其后调查工作在美国进行。

2025年10月14日，美国纽约东区联邦法院的文件披露，太子集团在中共眼皮底下是如何安稳做十年的过程。

起诉书说，太子集团高管利用在多个国家的政治影响力保护这个犯罪集团，向公职人员行贿来躲避执法打击。而受贿保护他们的是中共公安部和国安部。其中提到，陈志专门安排一个负责人主管集团的“风险控制”职能，即盯住各国执法机关的调查动向，跟执法官员做“腐败交易”。这表明行贿买通官员是太子集团的“常规业务”。

起诉书披露这个运作过程，首先是“买预警”。每次警方要去诈骗园区突袭抓人之前，集团都能提前得到“风声”，赶在警察上门前转移人员、销毁证据。陈志曾向人炫耀说，他与中共国安部的这套安排，用行贿换取执法行动的事前通报，这使得每次打击行动，“我们都毫发无伤”。

其次，买“摆平”。2023年5月，太子集团一个负责人与一名中共公安部官员谈话。该官员说，他能让太子集团的人“脱身”。作为交换，集团那边的人提出可以“照顾”这名官员的儿子。目前还不清楚这名官员的具体身份。

第三，把警察变成太子集团的打手。

起诉书提到，2023年7月，集团一个负责人指示一名中国执法人员，让地方警察去对“竞争对手”下手，让警察去把“那些地方”“抢了”。然后他们再以集团公司的名义与他们谈“保护”。即太子集团可以调动警察上门去抢、砸，把人先吓住，再由太子集团出面“摆平”。从此这家店就得向太子集团交“保护费”。自媒体时评人李沐阳指出，警察成了太子集团开拓地盘、收保护费的“马前卒”。

起诉书里还有一句话提到，大约在2024年7月，集团的一名“共谋者”对一名“财务人员携款潜逃”向陈志报告，并表示可调动“黑帮与政府”资源，即黑道与政府都成了该集团随时能调动的力量。

有观点认为，太子集团能买通中共公安部且在十年内毫发无伤，背后没有一个够份量的“保护伞”是不可能的。而主管中共公安系统的王小洪在几个月前出现头衔异常，这二者是否存在关联，目前还无法证实，但也耐人寻味。

2026年6月18日，据中共官媒报导称，中共中央书记处书记、国务委员王小洪于6月17日至18日在河北雄安新区、保定市和石家庄市等调研。

王小洪的头衔中，竟然公开缺少最有实权的“公安部部长”一职，而他主要是靠这个职务为人所熟知。党媒这样报导的背后动机引人注意。

## **爆中共高层亲属涉及东南亚电信诈骗洗钱**

2026年10月22日，北京市常务副市长夏林茂被中共官宣调查，他是中共政治局常委、中办主任蔡奇担任北京市委书记期间的旧部。

10月20日，《大纪元》获得消息人士A独家爆料称，“夏林茂相关涉案件，涉及政治局常委蔡奇之子蔡尔津”。

据A披露说，10月19日夜间，中纪委办案人员从北京丽思卡尔顿酒店把已故前中共总理李鹏家族的一名成员带走，并在北京金宝街香港马会俱乐部把中共前国家副主席李源潮的儿子李海进带走。

爆料说，中纪委已掌握证据，这名李鹏家族成员涉及多个案件，其中一个是之前中国大陆发生的诈骗案；李海进涉及到的案件包括，涉及前中共公安部副部长孙力军在东南亚国家参与电信诈骗园区投资建设，以及相关资金转移和洗钱活动；涉及缅甸KK园区佘志江案；涉及老挝特区电诈园区开力公司的洗钱案，涉案金额17亿元人民币左右。

时评人语茗指出，在五中全会召开前，中共高层家属突然被带走，并被爆出涉及到东南亚电信诈骗园区洗钱等案件，而王小洪所在的公安部也被美国政府指出，参与受贿保护太子集团。现在五中全会召开期间，王小洪被爆出患癌而不得不卸任，中共公安系统处理缅北电信诈骗案件的资金去向，王小洪涉及巨额贪污腐败目前也被曝光。王小洪相当于习近平的左膀右臂，如今他不光本身涉及巨额贪腐，且身体状况几乎难以再工作下去，对习近平来说绝非好事。在中共内斗愈发激烈的当下，中共各派系的角力中，习近平高喊反腐多年，要如何对待涉贪腐的王小洪才能让各派系服气，也是一个摆在面前且难以回避的问题。

title: Full, rigorous party self-governance: How the CPC holds itself accountable
summary: _Editor's note: CGTN has launched a new season of its Ask China campaign. We've invited experts, editors, reporters and other professionals to answer insightful questions about China and the CPC sent to CGTN by our viewers from around the w
content:
_Editor's note: CGTN has launched a new season of its Ask China campaign. We've invited experts, editors, reporters and other professionals to answer insightful questions about China and the CPC sent to CGTN by our viewers from around the world. Rimas Ma is a reporter for CGTN Arabic._

In 2012, the Communist Party of China (CPC) introduced a set of rules governing officials' conduct. The document was just over 600 Chinese characters long, and its provisions might have sounded trivial: no floral arrangements at meetings, no lavish dishes at official receptions, no luxury hotels on business trips, and no road closures or traffic restrictions to clear the way for officials.

The rules had a straightforward name: the Party's eight-point frugality code.

Some people initially thought it would be just another short-lived campaign. Yet more than a decade later, it is still going strong.

Behind these rules lies a broader concept: full, rigorous Party self-governance. The idea is that a party that has governed for an extended period cannot rely solely on external oversight to maintain its integrity. It must also hold itself to higher standards and impose stricter internal discipline. Its underlying logic is simple: regulate the exercise of power through rules and constrain conduct through institutions.

**Why does a meal matter?**

You might ask: Does it really matter if an official enjoys a meal at someone else's expense?

The answer can be found in the numbers, without any need for abstract theory. In 2025, China's discipline inspection and supervision authorities investigated more than 290,000 cases involving violations of the spirit of the Party's eight-point frugality code, with more than 370,000 people receiving criticism, education or disciplinary or administrative action.

Many such problems begin with something as seemingly minor as a meal.

In many corruption cases in China, serious misconduct follows a similar path: first, an official accepts a dinner invitation; then gifts; then money in exchange for favors; and eventually, large-scale corruption. A meal may seem insignificant, but it can be the first link in a chain that pulls people into increasingly serious wrongdoing.

That is why these rules target the first link in the chain. By addressing seemingly minor violations, they seek to stop problems before they escalate.

**The story behind an elderly person's allowance**

But keeping officials in check is only half of the picture. The other half is ensuring that ordinary people are not deprived of their rightful benefits.

In Qinghai Province, more than 400,000 people are aged 70 or above. Under government policy, they are eligible for elderly allowances. For a period, however, some did not receive them. Some were unaware of the policy, some found the application procedures too complicated, and some had not been properly informed by local officials.

Local discipline inspection and supervision authorities identified the problem and launched a targeted campaign to address it. The result? All 404,000 elderly people eventually received the allowances to which they were entitled, bringing coverage to 97.6%.

The phrase "full, rigorous Party self-governance" may sound remote from everyday life. But its practical implications can be very concrete: ensuring that an elderly person in a remote village receives a few hundred yuan in annual assistance on time. The amount may be modest, but it is a benefit she is entitled to receive.

In Jiujiang, east China's Jiangxi Province, discipline inspection and supervision authorities discovered that some medical institutions had obtained medical insurance funds through practices such as inflating reimbursement claims, falsifying accounting documents and manipulating billing items.

Medical insurance funds help ordinary people pay for healthcare. Every yuan fraudulently taken from these funds means fewer resources available to those who genuinely need medical treatment. After investigating the cases, the authorities issued recommendations to the medical insurance authorities, prompting the establishment of stricter fund supervision mechanisms and measures to close regulatory loopholes. This gave ordinary people an additional safeguard when seeking reimbursement for medical expenses.

These cases may not have made national headlines. Yet together, they illustrate the most basic purpose of governance: not grand political narratives, but ensuring that ordinary people are treated fairly, one case at a time.

**Can corrupt officials escape accountability by fleeing abroad?**

Corrupt officials in many countries may share one assumption: once they flee abroad, they will be safe.

China's answer is no.

From January to November 2025, China recovered 782 fugitives from overseas and retrieved more than 23.6 billion yuan in illicit funds through its "Sky Net" operation. The operation has continued for more than a decade and involved law enforcement cooperation with multiple countries.

Behind these figures lies a clear message: fleeing to another country or obtaining new passports does not make the matter disappear.

But the significance of pursuing fugitives and recovering illicit assets goes beyond bringing individuals back. It reaffirms a more fundamental principle: the exercise of power carries responsibility.

Officials who violate people's rights, fail to fulfill their duties or abuse their positions for personal gain should face the consequences prescribed by law, wherever they may flee. This is not simply about pursuing particular individuals. It is about upholding a rule: within this system, those who exercise power cannot enjoy its benefits while evading responsibility.

**Corruption is not a challenge unique to China**

Corruption is not unique to any one country.

A World Bank study has pointed out that corruption significantly raises business costs, discourages investment and undermines economic growth. This is not merely theoretical. When businesses no longer have to spend time and money dealing with demands for improper payments or other forms of official misconduct, they can devote more resources to products and technology. When ordinary people can access public services without relying on personal connections, the costs of social and economic activity fall and efficiency improves.

Countries have chosen different approaches to tackling corruption. China has opted for a sustained, institutionalized system of internal oversight: using rules to constrain power, data to identify irregularities, and international cooperation in fugitive repatriation and asset recovery to prevent those accused of corruption from evading accountability abroad.

At the heart of this approach is the logic of full, rigorous Party self-governance. Rather than relying on a single campaign to solve the problem, it seeks to keep the exercise of power under continuous constraint through institutions that operate over time.

**There is no finish line, but there is a clear direction**

This system is not static. Corruption cases continue to emerge, and new problems continue to arise. That is precisely why the system must remain in operation and adapt over time. New cases are investigated every year, and new loopholes are addressed.

In 2025, the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and the National Commission of Supervision continued publishing monthly figures on cases involving violations of the spirit of the Party's eight-point frugality code for the 148th consecutive month. This monthly reporting, sustained for more than 12 years, sends a message in itself: this is not a campaign launched for a limited period or a one-off crackdown, but an ongoing effort.

For ordinary people, these figures may seem distant. But when an official is publicly disciplined for accepting a banquet, when an institution is investigated for improperly distributing benefits, or when an official is penalized for using a government vehicle for private purposes, these individual cases add up to something important: the rules contained in that document of just over 600 Chinese characters are not merely words on paper.

Nor is full, rigorous Party self-governance simply an abstract political slogan. It means that a party with more than 100 million members is using an ongoing institutional framework to address a question faced by countries around the world: How can those entrusted with power be held accountable for their actions?

That is why full, rigorous Party self-governance must be pursued with perseverance and sustained effort. Not because the system is already perfect, but because problems will continue to arise; not because a single campaign can solve everything, but because only sustained efforts can keep the exercise of power under continuous constraint.

## 12th BRICS parliamentary forum concludes in New Delhi, with adoption of joint declaration

### The 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum, which was inaugurated by Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla yesterday, concluded today with the adoption of a Joint Declaration.

[ANI](https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/international/3998041-tibet-uyghur-rights-concerns-raised-in-geneva-with-china-amid-fears-over-minority-freedoms?amp)

Updated:27-10-2026 17:11IST | Created:27-10-2026 17:11IST

Image Credit: ANI

The 12th [BRICS](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=BRICS) Parliamentary Forum, which was inaugurated by [Lok Sabha](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Lok%20Sabha) Speaker Om [Birla](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Birla) yesterday, concluded on Tuesday with the adoption of a Joint Declaration. According to a press release, the declaration formally reiterates member nations' dedication to the principles of the United Nations Charter, sovereign equality, mutual respect, non-interference in internal affairs, and the peaceful settlement of international disputes.

Demonstrating India’s growing diplomatic footprint under its ongoing chairship, the Joint Declaration seamlessly aligned with New Delhi’s core strategic priorities. Reaffirming the consensus of the [New Delhi](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=New%20Delhi) Declaration (NDD), member parliaments issued an explicit endorsement of UN Security Council reform—referencing NDD Paragraph 13—to make global governance more representative of the Global South. India’s firm stance on national security scored a major victory through robust, uncompromised counter-terrorism language; building on NDD Paragraph 40, the declaration condemned cross-border terrorism, terror financing, and safe havens while demanding zero tolerance and an end to double standards.

As per the release, the final text also strongly embedded India-led developmental and climate agendas, including the expansion of Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) repositories, ethical Artificial Intelligence governance, adherence to Common but Differentiated Responsibilities (CBDR-RC), and unanimous support for India’s [BRICS](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=BRICS) Chairship. Delivering the valedictory address, [Lok Sabha](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Lok%20Sabha) Speaker emphasised that global challenges can only be resolved through steadfast dialogue, mutual peace, and collaborative action rather than conflict.

Addressing presiding officers, distinguished delegates, and international parliamentarians from [BRICS](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=BRICS) member and partner nations, [Birla](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Birla) reflected on two days of profound discussions. He noted that while participating nations possess diverse backgrounds, circumstances, and challenges, their shared commitment to humanity's welfare, peace, and prosperity remains the ultimate strength of the [BRICS](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=BRICS) coalition. Highlighting the current global climate of instability, economic uncertainty, and regional conflicts, [Birla](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Birla) reiterated India’s core philosophy: permanent solutions are forged in dialogue, not war; in peace, not conflict; and in collaboration, rather than competition.

He called for a global framework built on absolute respect for national sovereignty, peaceful resolution of international disputes, and equitable development opportunities for all. "Global peace truly means security, respect, justice, and the assurance of a better future for everyone—especially the younger generation,” he stated, noting that coming generations will judge current leaders by the safety and prosperity of the world they leave behind.

Underscoring the evolving responsibilities of democratic institutions, the [Lok Sabha](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Lok%20Sabha) Speaker emphasised that [Parliaments](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Parliaments) are not merely law-making bodies but vital centres of dialogue, consensus, accountability, and public trust. As per the release, he urged global legislatures to adapt to changing times by becoming more effective, transparent, and citizen-centric. Addressing the integration of modern tools, [Birla](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Birla) noted that the adoption of Artificial Intelligence and digital technology can heavily optimise parliamentary workflows and deepen citizen participation, provided its development aligns strictly with human values, ethics, transparency, and accountability.

Birla stressed that the success of [BRICS](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=BRICS) must extend far beyond the progress of its individual member [States](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=States) to benefit the wider international community, granting proper representation to the aspirations of the Global South in global decision-making processes. As the 12th [BRICS](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=BRICS)[Parliamentary Forum](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Parliamentary%20Forum) successfully concluded, [Birla](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Birla) extended warm congratulations and best wishes to China, which assumes the [BRICS](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=BRICS) chair for the year 2027, expressing full confidence that cooperation will continue to flourish under its leadership.

The forum concluded with a resounding call to action for [Parliaments](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Parliaments) worldwide to serve as powerful voices for peace, cooperation, and shared prosperity. (ANI)

(This story has not been edited by Devdiscourse staff and is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

### Imran Khan’s petition in the Bombay High Court challenging the 'Leave India Notice' has been adjourned till November 2.

[ANI](https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/international/3998041-tibet-uyghur-rights-concerns-raised-in-geneva-with-china-amid-fears-over-minority-freedoms?amp)

Updated:27-10-2026 16:35IST | Created:27-10-2026 16:35IST

Image Credit: ANI

Imran Khan’s petition in the [Bombay](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Bombay) High Court challenging the 'Leave [India](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=India) Notice' has been adjourned till November 2. [Imran](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Imran)[Khan](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Khan) was asked to leave [India](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=India) by October 28. ASG appearing for the central government has given oral assurance to the court that no action against [Imran](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Imran)[Khan](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Khan) will be taken till the next hearing.

The challenge shall be kept in abeyance till the next date. Earlier, [Khan](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Khan) filed a writ petition before the [Bombay](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Bombay) High Court challenging a Leave [India](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=India)[Notice](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Notice) (LIN) dated October 14, 2026, issued by the [Foreigners Regional Registration Officer](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Foreigners%20Regional%20Registration%20Officer) (FRRO), Mumbai, directing him to leave [India](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=India) on or before October 28.

Imran Khan's PR team issued a statement, "Mr [Imran](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Imran)[Khan](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Khan) Pal, actor and Overseas Citizen of [India](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=India) (OCI) Cardholder residing in [India](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=India) since the age of 2 years, has filed a [Writ Petition](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Writ%20Petition) before the Hon'ble [Bombay](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Bombay) High Court challenging the Leave [India](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=India)[Notice](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Notice) dated 14.10.2026 (“LIN”) issued by the [Foreigners Regional Registration Officer](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Foreigners%20Regional%20Registration%20Officer) (FRRO), Mumbai, which directs him to leave [India](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=India) on or before 28.10.2026. The petition challenges the procedure the [FRRO](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=FRRO) adopted. The [FRRO](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=FRRO) concluded that Imran, a US National, had taken part in a protest, and on that basis ordered him to leave India. It did so without giving him any opportunity of being heard." The actor’s petition argues that the notice does not specify the provisions of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025, that he allegedly violated. It also contends that the notice was issued without a show-cause notice or an opportunity to be heard.

According to the petition, [Khan](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Khan) has held Overseas Citizen of [India](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=India) (OCI) status since 2006 and has lived in [India](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=India) since he was about two years old. He has cited his education, professional work and family ties in the country to underline his longstanding association with India. The actor has linked the notice to an incident on October 10 near August [Kranti Maidan](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Kranti%20Maidan) and [Nana Chowk](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Nana%20Chowk) in Mumbai, where he says he was briefly detained by police. According to his account, he was returning to his vehicle when he was surrounded by media personnel and apprehended by the police.

He has denied entering any restricted or barricaded area or disobeying police directions to leave. His team said, "After the petition was filed, the [FRRO](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=FRRO) issued a detailed show cause notice (“SCN”). The notice asks [Imran](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Imran) to explain why his OCI registration should not be cancelled because of his presence at the gathering of 10.10.2026, where he was briefly detained by the [Mumbai](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Mumbai) Police. [Imran](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Imran) was neither an organiser of nor a participant in the protest. He had gone to see what was happening. Before he could reach the site, he was surrounded by the media and detained by the police."

The petition further states that [Khan](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Khan) was taken to the Yellow Gate Police Station along with family members and was subsequently released. It refers to an FIR registered at [Gamdevi Police Station](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Gamdevi%20Police%20Station) on October 10 under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). [Khan](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Khan) has contended that the notice appears to have been issued in connection with the FIR, despite the allegations remaining unproven.

The petition also points out that, according to him, no chargesheet had been filed and no charges framed when the notice was issued. Arguing that the direction to leave [India](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=India) has serious consequences for him, [Khan](https://www.devdiscourse.com/news?tag=Khan) has challenged the action as disproportionate and in violation of the legal safeguards he claims are applicable in his case. title: Why Critical Mineral Shortages Are a CEO Issue
summary: CEOs at industrial companies are well aware of potential shortages in critical minerals, and many think they have a plan in place to mitigate those risks. But we consistently find that companies are still underestimating their true vulnerab
content:
CEOs at industrial companies are well aware of potential shortages in critical minerals, and many think they have a plan in place to mitigate those risks. But we consistently find that companies are still underestimating their true vulnerability. Most industrials track their exposure to critical minerals using high-level metrics like spending, information from tier one suppliers, or country-of-origin data. However, true exposure is larger than those metrics suggest. This is because mineral risk often sits deep inside [supply chains](https://www.bcg.com/capabilities/operations/supply-chain-management)—inside the components that companies buy, and inside the tools and processes used to make those components. Concentration risks require looking at processing and ownership, not just mineral production at the mine.

A more comprehensive approach can give companies an accurate view of the vulnerabilities in their supply chain. From that baseline, companies can take a range of steps to reduce their exposure. Critically, this approach also helps companies tap into pools of public capital that many countries have allocated. In 2025, public finance commitments to critical minerals in advanced economies reached around$65 billion, more than four times the 2023 level, and most of that money is not yet spent. When companies have a clear sense of their financial exposure, they can build a case to access these funds.

In that way, industrial companies can stop treating critical minerals as a cost item and start treating them as a source of strategic advantage.

## Three Blind Spots Understate the Risk

Potential shortages of critical minerals are not new, but the scale of the looming shortfall is striking. In our proprietary model, the demand for key inputs—including [rare-earth elements](https://www.bcg.com/industries/industrial-goods/metals-mining) (REEs) and more common products like graphite, copper, and lithium—will be roughly 120% to 250% of forecast supply through 2040. New demand is coming primarily from batteries and electrification (which together are projected to increase the demand for critical minerals 20-fold by 2040), but also from the AI buildout and increased defense spending (segments that are projected to cause demand to triple and quadruple, respectively).

In response, the conventional move is to turn to procurement teams to fix the exposure. But this analysis will not give CEOs the full picture. Leaders need to be aware that the broadly prevailing metrics will lead to three critical blind spots.

**Blind Spot 1: Overweighting Dollars Spent.**Companies often start their risk assessment by looking at their bill of materials, leading them to worry about materials like copper and lithium that are large in tonnage and in procurement dollars. But the more dangerous exposures are often in “mosquito minerals” that are so small by traded value that they never reach the risk register, yet so essential that entire high-value chains stop without them. (See Exhibit 1.)

For example, REEs comprise roughly 40% of the cost of a magnet but less than 1% of the total value of an electric vehicle that requires the magnet. That is too cheap to appear in any cost review that would flag it as a risk, yet a shortage of these elements can stop a production line.

Similarly, a fighter jet uses about 20 kilograms of REEs, which are worth less in total than the paint that coats the plane. Those minerals are a rounding error in percent of unit cost, yet the aircraft does not fly without them.

Rare-earth elements have been getting a lot of attention lately, but the list of “mosquito minerals” is much longer. Consider the following examples:

*   **Gallium.** The entire global market for gallium is worth less than $350 million a year, with annual production of only about 900 tons—making it negligible compared to most other commodities. Yet we estimate that approximately $3.5 trillion worth of final products depend on gallium, including high-speed logic and power chips, AI GPUs, and 5G and satellite communications components. For many of these applications, substitutes are either not available or are technically challenging, with long lead times.
*   **Germanium.**Global sales of germanium each year only total about $260 million, but it is an essential component of electronics and fiber optics, and AI is hungry for both. A recent series of events—export licensing in 2023 followed by an outright ban on exports to the US in 2024 and a cut-off of Japan in early 2026—created severe market turmoil. Germanium prices during this period roughly quadrupled in western markets, trading at a substantial premium to Chinese volumes.
*   **Arsenic.** Virtually no companies list arsenic as a strategic risk, yet in ultra-high-purity form it is indispensable to the gallium-arsenide (GaAs) semiconductors in 5G/6G telecom infrastructure, along with AI data-center optics, radar systems, and defense electronics. The upstream market is minuscule (about $50 million worldwide), and producing semiconductor-grade arsenic (99.999995% pure, also known as 7N5) takes years of accumulated process know-how, with supply chains highly concentrated. China controls about 90% of refining volume, and a single Japanese producer supplies roughly 60% of the world’s ultra-high-purity arsenic. One facility, in one of the most seismically active countries on earth, and no credible alternatives. That is the problem in its purest form: negligible spend by companies, no risk-register entry, and an entire class of advanced and defense electronics that stops without it.

The economics of “mosquito” minerals has an additional wrinkle: they are often recovered as byproducts from other mining and industrial processes. Their supply is therefore set by the market dynamics of the host metal, not their own. So even a sharp price spike does not reliably call forth new production the way it would for a primary commodity.

**Blind Spot 2: Looking Solely at Tier One Suppliers**. Companies tend to look at critical minerals in the products and components they buy from their direct suppliers. Yet a company that buys almost no critical minerals directly can still be acutely exposed, because minerals arrive embedded in components. A motor, magnet, power module, laser, or sensor carries upstream mineral content, leading to dependencies that may not appear on a raw-materials line.

Another reason that companies understate risk is that minerals are not only in the product. They are in the processes required to create products: the crucibles, sputtering targets, furnace internals, catalysts, dies and consumables of suppliers’ production lines, and in the capital equipment itself.

For example, turbine blades, engine blocks, and structural aerospace components are machined with cutting tools made of tungsten carbide bonded with cobalt, chosen because no other material holds an edge at the temperatures and speeds that modern precision machining requires. The cutting tools wear down and need to be replaced. Tungsten mining and refining are heavily concentrated in China, which has in recent years tightened export licensing on tungsten products. Cobalt carries its own concentration risk through the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), where production is dominated by a small number of foreign operators. A manufacturer that has never bought a gram of tungsten or cobalt directly can still find its production line stopped by a shortage of the tooling that cuts its parts—a dependency that does not show up on any bill of materials.

**Blind Spot 3: Focusing on Mineral Production Rather Than Processing and Ownership.**Companies map their exposure to where critical minerals are mined. But processing—not production—is the bottleneck for some minerals. For example, China refines roughly 90% of rare earths and holds the know-how to turn ore into usable magnets. Similarly, it processes some 65% to 70% of lithium and cobalt and around 70% of graphite. Australia produces lithium and ships more than 90% of its spodumene to China to be processed.

Some industrial companies are beginning to factor processing concentration into their risk calculus. But another aspect that few companies measure is ownership of those assets. A map of where assets sit and a map of who owns them can look radically different. Consider cobalt and nickel. (See Exhibit 2.)

*   Cobalt shows concentration at the mining stage. The DRC accounts for roughly two-thirds of global mined cobalt production, with major operations majority-owned by Chinese companies.
*   Nickel shows concentration at the refining stage. Indonesia hosts close to 70% of upstream nickel capacity, while Chinese companies and shareholders account for a majority of Indonesia’s nickel-refining capacity. Moving a supply contract from a Chinese refinery to an Indonesian one may not change a company’s geopolitical risk exposure.

## A Missed Opportunity to Access Public Funds

On their own, the three blind spots are bad enough. But they also mean that companies are missing out on valuable capital from public sector vehicles. If organizations don’t know the full scope of their risk, they don’t realize the opportunities they might have to tap into these resources.

In 2025, public finance commitments to critical minerals in advanced economies reached around$65 billion, more than four times the 2023 level. These structures are not free money; they carry conditions—typically reporting obligations, governance rights, localization requirements, and screening. They are also not a full solution. Instead, they’re meant to be a catalyst, reflecting about one-tenth of the overall capital required to meet the demand for critical minerals through 2040. But they are funds that the private sector can tap into to build a competitive advantage.

Thus far, the vast majority of this capital has been committed but not yet spent. Our review of government-backed vehicles as of mid-2026 found that the flagship instruments are in the early stages of deployment. Some countries have spent less than 10% of their allocated capital; others have spent nothing yet. (See Exhibit 3.)

These vehicles are explicitly designed to draw private capital through measures such as co-investment, guarantees, and—in particular—offtake requirements, which are typically the primary eligibility gate. This is where the three blind spots above are holding companies back. Without a clear sense of their own exposure and a diligent framing of the opportunity, companies cannot make a credible commitment.

That said, there already are encouraging success stories. Several of the companies that have managed to reframe their critical minerals approach and take advantage of these pools of public capital are not mining companies; they are industrial companies and trading firms:

*   **Siemens Gamesa,** the wind-turbine manufacturer, signed a binding five-year supply contract with Arafura Rare Earths, an Australian company building a roughly $1 billion REE mine and processing plant in Australia’s Northern Territory. The contract locks in supply of neodymium and praseodymium—two REEs refined into the magnets inside wind-turbine generators—starting at 200 metric tons a year in 2026 and rising to 400 metric tons a year by year three, for use in turbines assembled at Siemens Gamesa’s factory in Cuxhaven, Germany. Beyond supply, the deal offered other advantages. Germany’s economics ministry had said it would consider backing Arafura’s mine with an export-credit guarantee of up to $600 million on one condition: that Arafura sign offtake contracts with German companies that would process the material domestically. Siemens Gamesa’s contract was structured to satisfy exactly that condition, and Germany’s development bank has since added its own direct investment in the project. title: Exiled Russian dissident Navalnaya warns dictators becoming 'more cunning'
summary: The widow of Russian opposition leader Alexei Navalny warned Tuesday that dictators are becoming "more cunning", as she helped launch a report revealing deepening global ties between autocrats and authoritarian-leaning parties. Yulia Navaln
content:
The widow of Russian opposition leader Alexei Navalny warned Tuesday that dictators are becoming "more cunning", as she helped launch a report revealing deepening global ties between autocrats and authoritarian-leaning parties.

Yulia Navalnaya, who heads the US-based Human Rights Foundation (HRF), urged people not to underestimate the threat that "very dangerous" dictators and their networks pose, arguing they can "only be defeated if those who fight for freedom cooperate too".

"They learn from one another, they work together," she told journalists in London at the launch of the new report, which finds European far-right parties are increasingly coordinating with authoritarian regimes beyond the continent.

"They turn to their own advantage the tools that free and democratic countries give them," she said.

"They know how to exploit the financial and legal systems of Western countries, how to get around restrictions and sanctions."

Navalnaya's husband Navalny, a staunch critic of Russian President Vladimir Putin, died in prison in 2024 while serving a 19-year sentence.

Five European countries, including Britain, France and Germany, concluded earlier this year that he was killed by a "rare toxin" from a dart frog and that the Russian state was the prime suspect.

Navalnaya, 50, has become Russia's leading exiled opposition figure, touring the world to meet foreign leaders, organising opposition rallies and publishing investigations into the alleged corruption of Putin's inner circle.

Asked about US special envoy Steve Witkoff recently telling Putin he was a humanitarian, she called the comment "nonsense" and "a pity".

- 'Crush dissent' -

The HRF collaborated with another US-based non-profit, Action for Democracy, to produce its latest "Authoritarian Collaboration Index" trends report.

It relies on data from HRF's "Tyranny Tracker", a real-time monitoring tool of ties between autocratic regimes, authoritarian-leaning governments and far-right parties.

The paper reported that such parties in Europe, such as Nigel Farage's Reform UK, Marine Le Pen's National Rally in France and Alice Weidel's Alternative for Germany (AfD), are now formalising links to "legitimise" each other.

The study said the AfD had this year "deepened its relations with Russia" beyond financial support towards more "dialogue and engagement".

The warnings come ahead of imminent elections in a host of European countries, including Spain, Germany and France, when far-right parties could make unprecedented gains.

The report found that while China and Russia remain the "primary anchors of a global axis of autocracy", media and technological cooperation has become "institutionalised" between similarly minded countries and parties, particularly across Africa and southeast Asia.

Domonkos Kovacs, project lead for the index, said that, amid "global democratic backsliding", the index aimed to "shed light" on this growing "global authoritarian solidarity".

"This is dictators helping each other crush dissent," he told reporters.

title: Four days, four protests — Desperate Joburg residents hit the streets over water cuts
summary: Soiled nappies piled up, toilets went unflushed and dirty bed linen could not be washed as a five-day water outage plunged a Johannesburg home for people with disabilities into a hygiene crisis. At St Giles Association for the Physically Di
content:
Soiled nappies piled up, toilets went unflushed and dirty bed linen could not be washed as a five-day water outage plunged a Johannesburg home for people with disabilities into a hygiene crisis.

At St Giles Association for the Physically Disabled in Dewetshof, near Kensington, many of the 29 residents are frail or physically disabled and rely on caregivers to get out of bed, dress, bathe and use the toilet. Some need to be bathed two or three times a day because of incontinence.

“The past few days have been hell. We have never had such a long outage, and for us it was a complete nightmare,” said manager Palesa Nhlapo.

Emergency reserves of 25 litres in each bathroom ran out within a morning. Dirty linen and clothing accumulated, floors could not be washed properly and staff struggled to keep toilets clean, raising fears about the spread of disease.

“We keep 25 litres of water in every bathroom for emergencies, but that was finished in one morning,” Nhlapo said.

Even preparing meals and providing drinking water, tea, coffee and juice became difficult in the heat.

Alongside water donated from the Kensington community, St Giles manager Palesa Nhlapo (left) sits with a disabled resident. (Photo: Jamie Ho)

Staff hired a bakkie to collect water from the Jeppe Fire Station – an extra expense for a struggling nonprofit whose residents contribute only about 40% of its running costs.

“It has been very distressing and caused a lot of anxiety as we watched the pile of soiled bedding and clothing and nappies grow, wondering about the spread of infection and germs. Not only were our 58 members of staff alarmed, but it deeply affected our most vulnerable residents who were not being given their regular care,” Nhlapo said.

But when the home’s plight was shared through the Water Crisis Committee network, neighbours arrived with bottled drinking water and filled 25-litre containers.

“The outpouring of love has overwhelmed us. People have been coming in for days now, just bringing whatever water they can. We are truly grateful. We now at least have containers, although we never know when there is going to be another outage,” Nhlapo said.

### **Residents take to the streets**

The ordeal at St Giles comes as water shortages trigger protests across Johannesburg in the days before the 4 November municipal elections. Some households say they have gone more than a week without running water or an emergency tanker delivery.

On Saturday, 24 October, residents of Mayfair, Crosby and surrounding areas protested outside Brixton Police Station after days without running water. They depend on the troubled Commando supply system, which includes the Brixton, Crosby and Hursthill reservoirs.

Further water protests have been announced in the coming days.

Melville residents plan to gather at Main Road and Fourth Avenue from 6am to 8am on Wednesday, 28 October, urging neighbours to bring bottles and “make some noise”.

On Thursday, 29 October, residents of Kensington, Observatory, Bezuidenhout Valley, Bertrams, Judith’s Paarl, Yeoville, Berea and surrounding areas plan to meet at Queen Street and Albertina Sisulu Road from 5pm to 7pm.

The Water Crisis Committee says many have been without reliable supply since 22 October. It is demanding emergency water deliveries, clear restoration timelines and repairs, and has barred political branding from the protest.

Parktown West residents plan to gather on Jan Smuts Avenue, between Loch Avenue and Seymour Road, from 7am to 9am on Friday, 30 October.

Their notice reads: “Weeks Dry. ZERO Answers.”

Residents also protested in February, when some reported weeks without dependable water.

In Lenasia, service-delivery protesters blocked the N12 near Nana’s Farm on 26 October, after another demonstration the previous week. Their grievances have included water and electricity shortages.

> ### **Join the protests**
>
>
> If you’ve been affected by the water cuts or want to protest in solidarity, you can make your voice heard at one of the above protests. The events are aimed at being peaceful and are not affiliated to political parties. Pitch up with or without a sign and feel free to bring something to make some noise.

### **Desperation in the suburbs**

In Malvern, opposite Malvern West Primary School, a resident reported this week seeing people illegally opening a municipal fire hydrant and filling 20-litre containers, which were loaded on to a bakkie. It is not known who opened the hydrant, whether they were authorised or what the water was intended for.

In neighbouring Bezuidenhout Valley, Johannesburg Water issued a warning on 24 October after receiving reports of a private truck selling water on Ninth Avenue.

“The source and quality of the water being sold have not been verified,” the utility said, urging residents not to buy it because its safety could not be guaranteed. Water delivered by authorised Johannesburg Water tankers is free and must not be sold, it said.

Yet residents complain that official tankers are not reaching them. One person living in flats opposite 226 Sixth Avenue in Bezuidenhout Valley wrote in a community WhatsApp group: “9 days without water and not even a water truck in 9 days.”

The resident questioned how many germs were accumulating in homes where people could no longer maintain basic hygiene in the heat.

A Kensington resident complained that emergency supplies appeared to be concentrated in Bezuidenhout Valley.

“It feels as though we in Kensington are being punished, despite also having had no water since Thursday last week,” the resident wrote.

“To make matters worse, water tankers are not reaching us, and when assistance does arrive, it appears to go only to Bez Valley.”

The complaints about unequal tanker distribution have not been independently verified.

Melville residents collect water from a tanker during a previous outage. (Photo: Archive / Ihsaan Haffejee)

Despite their growing desperation, residents have expressed appreciation for the community volunteers trying to help them.

“We appreciate you guys, heartily! You are doing a noble job,” one resident wrote in the Water Crisis Committee’s WhatsApp group.

“We just can’t help but cry out loud right here when the pain of being waterless cuts deep.”

At least 11 care, medical and educational facilities have been identified in or near the eastern suburbs, including homes for elderly people and people with disabilities that were left without water for days.

### **Water that may not be safe**

Bezuidenhout Valley residents face a second difficulty: a precautionary water contamination warning after a drinking-water pipe was damaged during sewer-replacement work.

Initial tests showed no indication of contamination, but Johannesburg Water warned residents in a limited section of Eighth Avenue, near Fourth to Seventh streets, not to use tap water until further clearance.

On 26 October, the utility said a supply interruption had delayed further sampling. Councillor Neuren Pietersen said this was because there was no water to test as the pipes were empty.

### **Financial strain**

The failures are unfolding as Johannesburg grapples with serious financial pressures.

In April, Finance Minister [Enoch Godongwana warned Mayor Dada Morero](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-05-06-finance-minister-warns-joburg-is-in-severe-financial-distress-in-letter-to-mayor-morero/) about mounting debt, weak revenue collection and an unfunded budget.

The City has rejected suggestions that it is bankrupt and says it is working to restore services. Residents, however, are judging those plans by whether water flows, the lights stay on and rubbish is collected.

Pietersen said the shortages were part of a province-wide crisis, with Johannesburg losing an estimated 400 million litres of water daily and Ekurhuleni another 200 million litres, while Rand Water struggled to meet demand of about five billion litres a day.

On Friday, Rand Water said, “To protect the water supply system and ensure equitable distribution, Rand Water will begin restricting supply to municipalities that continue to exceed their allocated consumption volumes. These restrictions may result in low water pressure or intermittent water supply in affected municipalities.”

Following a public meeting with MP Stephen Moore, Pietersen said the national government was considering stronger measures to compel municipalities to reduce water losses and protect revenue for infrastructure maintenance.

An O6 pipeline (a high-capacity bulk water transmission main) and pump station project was already under way to improve supply to the Yeoville reservoir serving his ward. However, he warned that residents needed to conserve water to reduce pressure on the system and avoid further restrictions while infrastructure was repaired.

### **Power failures**

Electricity outages are adding to the pressure on households and businesses. Repeated fires and explosions at City Power’s Central Substation left sections of the CBD without power, forcing businesses to buy diesel for generators or interrupt trading. Another explosion on 14 October delayed repairs; by 23 October, City Power said it had restored supply to about 98% of affected customers.

Elsewhere, residents continue to report unplanned outages linked to ageing equipment, faults, theft and vandalism. City Power has also scheduled maintenance interruptions in several areas. Those planned shutdowns are distinct from breakdowns, but both leave households and businesses having to make alternative arrangements.

### **Refuse collection**

Rubbish has also gone uncollected in parts of Johannesburg as Pikitup struggles with vehicle shortages and recurring collection backlogs. The entity acknowledged delays earlier this month and said teams were clearing missed rounds. Previous disruptions included protests affecting six depots in August, while its reliance on hired trucks has raised further questions about the sustainability of the services. **DM**

27 October 2026

[Capital FM (Nairobi)](https://capitalfm.africa/ "Visit Capital FM (Nairobi)")

Nairobi — Police are investigating a violent robbery at a construction site along Kilungu Road in Nairobi's Kilimani area, where three Chinese nationals were held hostage and property and cash stolen.

According to a police report filed at Kilimani Police Station, the incident occurred on the night of Sunday, with the victims managing to raise the alarm at about 5am on Monday.

The report indicates that one of the victims returned to the Luna Oak construction site at around 11pm and found the site's security guard, Augustine Momanyi, who works for Marshall Security Company, dressed in civilian clothes instead of his security uniform.

The guard was reportedly accompanied by three men who turned against the returning resident and attacked him with a kitchen knife.

The attackers allegedly took the house keys from his pocket, entered the residence, tied his hands and legs with a rope and confined him in the washroom.

At around midnight, two other Chinese nationals, identified as Chen Guang Jun, 37, and Yang Bin, 40, returned to the house and were also held hostage.

The suspects allegedly used crude weapons to break into other rooms, ransacked the house and stole electronic equipment, construction materials and cash.

According to the police report, Chen lost three mobile phones -- an iPhone 13 Pro, an iPhone 10 and a Huawei phone -- as well as a Huawei laptop and two television sets measuring 50 inches and 45 inches.

The suspects also stole 50 bags of scaffolding materials, two generators and KSh30,000 in cash.

Chen further reported that KSh10,000 was transferred from his Stanbic Bank account and another KSh87,000 from his M-Pesa account.

Yang reportedly lost an Oppo mobile phone and KSh80,000 in cash, while a further KSh2,000 was transferred from his account.

A third victim, Qian Hongxing, 53, reported the loss of two Oppo 13 mobile phones.

The attackers also disconnected and stole the CCTV installations at the premises, potentially removing equipment that could have helped investigators establish how the robbery was carried out.

The victims managed to raise the alarm at around 5am on Monday, prompting police officers to visit the scene.

Scenes of Crime personnel processed the premises as part of the investigation, while the crude weapons allegedly used during the robbery were preserved as exhibits.

The victims were taken to Nairobi Hospital, where they were receiving treatment in stable condition, according to the police report.

Police are expected to investigate the circumstances surrounding the incident, including the alleged involvement of the security guard and the identity of the three men who reportedly accompanied him.

The report did not indicate whether any arrests had been made or whether the stolen property had been recovered.

The total value of the stolen property and the money lost through the reported transfers had not been established.

title: Uganda: Besigye, Bobi Wine Absence Raises Questions About Opposition's Future
summary: Uganda's opposition is grappling with the absence of two of its most influential figures, Dr Kizza Besigye, who remains in detention amid serious health concerns, and National Unity Platform (NUP) leader Robert Kyagulanyi, popularly known a
content:
Uganda's opposition is grappling with the absence of two of its most influential figures, Dr Kizza Besigye, who remains in detention amid serious health concerns, and National Unity Platform (NUP) leader Robert Kyagulanyi, popularly known as Bobi Wine, who is in exile.

Their absence has raised questions about the opposition's leadership, mobilisation and ability to sustain pressure on the ruling National Resistance Movement (NRM).

Opposition leaders say the absence of the two figures has created a significant leadership gap, limiting their ability to organise political activities and advance their agenda.

Political analysts, however, argue that the situation also exposes a longstanding weakness: the failure of opposition parties to build strong institutions capable of surviving beyond their most prominent leaders.

Besigye, a former president of the Forum for Democratic Change (FDC) and a key figure in the formation of the People's Front for Freedom (PFF), has been one of Uganda's most prominent opposition figures since the return to multiparty politics in 2005.

He remains in detention facing treason-related charges, which his supporters have described as politically motivated.

His political rise inspired many Ugandans to participate in opposition politics. Kyagulanyi later emerged as another major opposition figure, leading NUP in the 2021 and 2026 general elections.

Both leaders attracted substantial public support among Ugandans seeking political change but also faced repeated confrontations with the government.

Besigye's continued detention and Kyagulanyi's departure from Uganda have left their parties confronting the challenge of maintaining momentum without their direct involvement in domestic political activities.

Kyagulanyi left Uganda in March 2026 after spending weeks in hiding following the disputed January presidential election. He said he had left for engagements abroad and would return.

His departure followed claims that security agencies were pursuing him, which the government's actions and statements have made a subject of continuing political dispute.

Besigye's health has also become a major concern. He collapsed during a court appearance in July and was hospitalised before being returned to prison medical care.

In October, associates reported that he was undergoing rehabilitation to regain his ability to speak and walk, while prison authorities said his condition was improving.

The uncertainty surrounding both leaders has fuelled debate about the opposition's capacity to mobilise supporters, coordinate its activities and maintain a sustained presence in the political arena.

"Reaching out is a matter of mobilisation. For as long as they are still locked out there, then we assume it is unsafe for mobilisation," Alice Alaso, the secretary general of the Alliance for National Transformation (ANT), told Nile Post.

Alaso said the absence of the two leaders had deprived the opposition of valuable political experience, ideas and leadership at a time when coordination and mobilisation were critical.

"Their absence denies us the leadership, their absence denies us their ideas and their experience, and as a result, that gap is very significant," she said.

Kira Municipality MP George Musisi said the circumstances surrounding Besigye's detention and Kyagulanyi's exile remained unresolved, making it difficult to assess what role the two leaders could play under the prevailing political conditions.

"The circumstances that led to the incarceration of leaders like Dr Besigye and the exile of NUP president Kyagulanyi Ssentamu are prevailing, and I don't think that there can be any meaningful discussions as to what role they would play in these circumstances," Musisi said.

He argued that restoring the rule of law and allowing political leaders to operate within the framework of a multiparty system were necessary steps towards addressing the challenges facing the opposition.

"The issue is, let us go back to the basics of the rule of law. If we have agreed to go back to the multiparty dispensation, let all the political leaders play their role within the law," he added.

While opposition leaders attribute their difficulties to restrictions on political activity and the absence of key figures, political analyst Gerald Karyeija sees a deeper structural weakness in the way opposition parties are organised.

The limited visibility of opposition activities has coincided with continued mobilisation by the NRM-linked Patriotic League of Uganda (PLU), raising questions about the opposition's ability to maintain its political presence while some of its leading figures remain outside the country's political arena.

Karyeija argued that opposition parties had failed to establish strong institutions capable of sustaining their activities independently of their founders and most prominent leaders.

"If the parties were standing without individuals as their face, then they would be felt whether those individuals are in exile or in prison. So, having political leaders outlive their founders and charismatic leaders is still a problem," Karyeija said.

NRM Secretary General Richard Todwong similarly argued that the opposition's difficulties were partly rooted in the failure to develop clear ideological foundations and institutional structures capable of sustaining political parties over time.

"You don't see grounded ideological and philosophical thought in the formation of these opposition parties, just like NRM has. And because of that, they could not stand longevity in opposition against a government that is well-rooted like that of NRM," Todwong said.

However, Alaso and Musisi reject the argument that the opposition's difficulties can be attributed solely to weak party structures. They say the political environment has constrained their ability to organise, mobilise supporters and participate freely in public activities.

Their concerns include reports of restrictions on opposition supporters during public activities, with some alleging that even attending religious services while wearing party attire can attract security scrutiny or intervention.

For the opposition, the challenge is therefore twofold: addressing restrictions that leaders say impede political participation while building organisations capable of maintaining momentum when prominent figures are unavailable.

Todwong said a stronger opposition would benefit the NRM by forcing the ruling party to defend its policies and respond to alternative proposals on national issues.

"I would be much better as a political party to be checked by my opponent, who is also ideologically thorough. I want to hear opposition members challenging our manifesto. I want to hear them challenging our policy on education, our policies on health, our policies on fighting poverty by giving better alternatives," Todwong said.

He added that opposition parties should engage more substantively with national issues, including public debt and strategies for reducing it.

"I want to hear them speaking on the debt-to-GDP ratio and how we can reduce it. I want to hear tangible criticism from the opposition, speaking to things that matter to the country," he said.

Whether Uganda's opposition can overcome its current challenges may depend not only on the future of Besigye and Kyagulanyi but also on its ability to strengthen party structures, sustain grassroots mobilisation and develop policy alternatives that can endure beyond individual leaders.

Federica Baggio

11 小时前 11 小时前

广告

（德国之声中文网）[以色列](https://dw.com/zh/%E4%BB%A5%E8%89%B2%E5%88%97/t-40363274)国内外普遍将此次选举视为对总理内塔尼亚胡领导能力的一次信任公投。他的主要挑战者艾森科特（Gadi Eisenkot）能否阻止他第七度出任总理是主要看点。以下是这场选举的关键信息。

## 这场选举有何重要性？

这是自2023年10月7日[哈马斯恐怖攻击](https://dw.com/zh/%E5%93%88%E9%A9%AC%E6%96%AF%E6%81%90%E8%A2%AD%E4%BB%A5%E8%89%B2%E5%88%973%E5%91%A8%E5%B9%B4-%E9%BB%98%E8%8C%A8%E5%BC%BA%E8%B0%83%E5%BE%B7%E5%9B%BD%E5%9D%9A%E5%AE%9A%E7%AB%99%E5%9C%A8%E4%BB%A5%E8%89%B2%E5%88%97%E4%B8%80%E8%BE%B9/a-79578715)以来，以色列首次举行全国大选。

这场选举被广泛视为对总理内塔尼亚胡的一次信任公投。过去近20年来，内塔尼亚胡长期主导以色列政坛，如今正寻求第七度出任总理。

## 选战的关键议题

*   对10月7日[哈马斯恐袭事件](https://dw.com/zh/%E4%BB%A5%E8%89%B2%E5%88%97-%E5%93%88%E9%A9%AC%E6%96%AF%E6%88%98%E4%BA%89/t-68961301)的究责

*   国家安全与军事战略

*   持续上升的生活成本

*   司法改革与法治

*   极端正统派犹太教徒服兵役问题

至于如何制定对巴勒斯坦人的政策，并未成为这次选战的主要议题。

在希伯伦市巴勒斯坦人居住区，以色列士兵在巡逻 图像来源: Ammar Awad/REUTERS

## 谁有投票权？

以色列约有730万名合格选民，其中17%为阿拉伯裔以色列人，他们通常也认同自己是巴勒斯坦人。

居住在[约旦河西岸](https://dw.com/zh/%E4%BB%A5%E8%89%B2%E5%88%97%E5%B0%86%E5%9C%A8%E5%A4%A7%E9%80%89%E6%97%A5%E5%85%B3%E9%97%AD%E6%89%80%E6%9C%89%E7%BA%A6%E6%97%A6%E6%B2%B3%E8%A5%BF%E5%B2%B8%E5%8F%A3%E5%B2%B8/a-79756249)的以色列定居者拥有投票权，但生活在包括东耶路撒冷在内的被占领土的巴勒斯坦人则无法参与这场选举。

以色列不允许邮寄投票，也不开放海外投票，只有驻外官方使节例外。

## 以色列选举制度如何运作？

以色列选民投票支持的是政党，而非直接选出总理。

本次大选共有38个政党参选，政党必须获得至少3.25%的选票，才能进入以色列国会（Knesset）。

要组成政府，一个政党必须取得国会120席中的至少61席，或与其他政党组成联合政府。迄今从未有单一政党独自赢得过半席位。

选举站还未开门，已有投票人等在门口 图像来源: Ohad Zwigenberg/AP Photo/picture alliance

## 谁暂时领先?

纳坦雅胡的主要对手是前以色列国防军总参谋长艾森科特（Gadi Eisenkot）。这位政坛新秀目前领导中间派政党“正直党”（Yashar）。

民调显示，内塔尼亚胡领导的右翼及宗教政党阵营，与艾森科特领导的反对党阵营，目前势均力敌。

然而，预计双方都无法单独取得组阁所需的61席。

## 何时公布选举结果？

投票所将于当地时间晚上10点关闭，通常随后就会公布出口民调。

正式选举结果将于11月4日完成确认。

随后一周内，以色列总统将指定其认为最有可能组成联合政府的政党领袖，并委托其展开组阁谈判。

# US Army queries industry’s ability to build 21,000 Infantry Squad Vehicles

By

Michael Peck

Oct 27, 2026

*   [Share on Facebook (Opens in new window)Facebook](https://www.defensenews.com/industry/2026/10/27/us-army-queries-industrys-ability-to-build-21000-infantry-squad-vehicles/?share=facebook&nb=1)

An Infantry Squad Vehicle—Utility that underwent testing in August by U.S. Army DEVCOM Ground Vehicle Systems Center engineers. (Jennifer DeHaan/U.S. Army)

The U.S. Army is asking whether the defense industrial base can deliver and support nearly 21,000 [Infantry Squad Vehicles](https://www.militarytimes.com/news/your-military/2026/10/12/us-army-gm-defense-agree-to-add-12000-infantry-squad-vehicles-to-fleet/).

An Army [market survey](https://sam.gov/workspace/contract/opp/4b14f7606884428c8338e3c0c8ba1711/view) published Monday focuses on two ISV versions: the ISV-9, which carries nine passengers, and the ISV-Utility, which carries five passengers plus a utility bed to haul cargo.

“The estimated total requirement is for 20,787 vehicles (9,003 ISV-9 and 11,784 ISV-U), subject to fund availability and requirements from the U.S. Army, other sister services and potential Foreign Military Sales (FMS) customers,” the survey said.

“To ensure the most streamlined, competitive, and cost-effective approach, the government is utilizing the results of this market survey to determine the feasibility of several procurement pathways.”

The ISV, from GM Defense, is based on General Motors’s commercial Colorado and Silverado pickups. GM Defense was awarded a $697.7 million contract modification last month for engineering changes to the ISV-U and the ISV-U Utility Winch Kit, bringing the cumulative value to $915.6 million.

GM Defense announced Oct. 12 that the Army expanded orders for the ISV from an initial 649 to nearly 12,000.

In the market survey, contractors are asked to provide the Army with manufacturing cost estimates based on “varying annual production volumes (e.g., 100, 500, 1,000, and 1,500+ units per year) to evaluate economy-of-scale thresholds.”

The survey also includes a timeline that begins in fiscal 2028 with an acquisition of 106 vehicles. The acquisition continues to fiscal 2036, with the Army receiving around 2,000 to 2,100 vehicles per year.

The survey also listed numerous technical specifications. The ISV-9 and ISV-U will have a maximum vehicle curb weight of 5,200 pounds, plus an operational payload of 5,000 pounds for the ISV-9 and a payload capacity of 5,000 pounds for the ISV-U. Both versions will have a gross vehicle weight rating of up to 10,200 pounds, the survey said.

Both vehicles require baseline military modifications, including blackout lights, 24V electrical systems, main power disconnect, run-flat tires, the ability to ford both salt and fresh water, MIL-STD-814/MIL-STD-209K life and tie-down provisions, 24V NATO slave receptacles on the front and rear bumper, an integrated winch and Military Petroleum, Oils, and Lubricants (POL) compatibility.”

The ISV-9 and ISV-U will have full rollover protection for their passengers. The ISV-U will also have a winch, a 4,000-watt inverter with multiple electrical outlets, towing capacity of up to 6,500 pounds and the capability to carry “non-ambulatory patients as a kit.”

The vehicles should be capable of traveling up to 55 miles per hour on good paved roads and 17 miles per hour cross country.

“Both the ISV-9 and ISV-U shall be capable of traversing longitudinal grades up to 60% and must reliably meet stringent mobility profile requirements across improved, secondary, and un-improved surfaces (trails and cross-country) without fatiguing the occupants when the platform is operating at GVW [gross vehicle weight],” the Army said.

# Taiwan's 2027 budget with NT$10,000 handouts heads to committee

10/27/2026 07:04 PM

[](jsvscript:)[](jsvscript:)[](javascript:void(0))[Listen](javascript:)

Premier Cho Jung-tai. CNA photo Oct. 27, 2026

Taipei, Oct. 27 (CNA) The central government's proposed 2027 general budget, which includes funding for NT$10,000 (US$307.40) cash handouts, was referred to committee review in the Legislative Yuan on Tuesday.

The bill advanced after Premier Cho Jung-tai (卓榮泰) answered lawmakers' questions about the government's spending plan.

The NT$3.92 trillion general budget proposal includes NT$235.7 billion for the cash handouts, which the government says will be funded entirely by higher tax revenue from growth in technology-related industries amid forecast economic growth of 11.05 percent in 2026.

The government has said the handouts are intended to let the public share in the benefits of economic growth driven by Taiwan's booming high-tech sector.

Under the Executive Yuan's proposal, eligible recipients would include citizens with household registration in Taiwan and nationals without household registration who have obtained residence permits.

Foreign nationals with permanent residence permits would also be eligible, as would spouses of Taiwanese nationals from China, Hong Kong, Macau or other countries who hold residence permits. Government personnel posted overseas and their dependents would qualify if both hold Taiwan nationality.

A competing bill backed by the main opposition Kuomintang, which would require the government to issue NT$20,000 handouts instead, was referred to committee review earlier this month. However, the bill refers only to "eligible individuals" and does not specify eligibility criteria.

(By Sean Lin)

content:
华盛顿 —

美国国土安全部星期二(10月27日)宣布将暂停中国公民前往美国位于西太平洋的海外领地北马里亚纳群岛的免签旅行计划，在此之前，多位共和党议员警告该计划可能助长“生育旅游”并构成国家安全风险。新措施将于美国东部时间10月30日下午2时生效。

免签计划全名为“经济活力与安全旅行授权计划”（EVS-TAP)，由拜登政府于2024年制定，并于2025年2月20日正式实施。该计划允许符合条件并获得美国海关与边境保护局(CBP)电子旅行授权的中国公民，可免签前往北马里亚纳群岛，最长停留14天。

国土安全部在宣布该决定的[公告](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/27/2026-21880/suspension-of-the-commonwealth-of-the-northern-mariana-islands-cnmi-economic-vitality-and-security)中指出，该计划可能助长“生育旅游”、间谍活动，并导致中国公民非法前往邻近的关岛那里是重要的美国军事枢纽，带来“安全和执法风险”。

**免签证项目曾带来医疗压力和安全风险**

该项目将于美国东部时间10月30日下午2点起暂停实施，适用于新申请者和已获批准的旅客。措施生效前已经入境而且仍在何方停留期限内的人员，可以继续停留至期限届满。此后前往北马里亚纳群岛，则须申请美国签证，除非符合其他入境豁免的条件。

国土安全部表示，此次暂停时为了重新评估该计划的运作和相关风险，在与国务卿和内政部长共同评估该项目期间，暂停措施将持续有效。目前，公告没有设定恢复日期。

国土安全部警告称，免签证项目可能会使中国公民更容易前往北马里亚纳群岛生育。“虽然生育旅游在北马里亚纳群岛一直是一个问题，但根据经济活力与安全旅行授权计划提供的免签旅行和简化的审查程序，可能会降低这种做法的门槛。”公告指出。

生育旅游是指外国人前往美国的主要目的是生育，以便其子女获得美国公民身份。美国国土安全部说，2025财年有超过3000名中国公民利用该项目进入北马里亚纳群岛。

国土安全部还表示，生育旅游会给这些岛屿的医疗系统带来压力。不过，公告没有提供通过免签证计划入境的旅客相关的生育数量。

该部门警告说，免签旅行可能被人用于在美国军事设施附近收集情报。北马里亚纳群岛是天宁岛(Tinian)美军空军基地的所在地，而关岛则是美军在西太平洋的重要战略据点。

尽管该计划不允许游客前往关岛或美国本土，但国土安全部列举了此前一些案例，涉及中国公民从北马里亚纳群岛乘船偷渡到关岛的案件。国土安全部表示，这些案例表明，相关风险尚未完全消除。

暂停免签是特朗普政府加大力度打击生育旅游的一部分。美国国务院于8月12日成立“生育旅游预防特别工作组”(Birth Tourism Prevention Task Force)，负责调查相关活动及打击牟利中介。

《纽约邮报》10月20日的一篇[报道](https://nypost.com/2026/10/20/us-news/over-300k-visas-revoked-so-far-in-trumps-second-term-state-department-announces/)说，自从唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)总统在去年上任以来，美国政府已经撤销了超过30万份签证，其中至少4，000份被取消是因为签证持有人“参与或协助生育旅游”。白宫官方账号“快速反应47”(Rapid Response 47)当天转发了这篇报道。

**共和党议员们庆祝这一决定**

来自犹他州共和党籍联邦参议员迈克·李(Mike Lee)星期一晚间在X平台上上发帖庆祝这一决定。“美国不是中共窃取公民身份的温床。”李写道，“感谢特朗普总统！”

迈克·李、佛罗里达州州共和党籍参议员里克·斯科特(Rick Scott)、德克萨斯州共和党籍联邦参议员约翰·科宁(John Cornyn)以及路易斯安那州共和党籍联邦参议员比尔·卡西迪(Bill Cassidy)在月曾致函穆林，敦促他终止该项目，并警告称该项目助长了生育旅游，构成国家安全风险。

德克萨斯州共和党众议员奇普·罗伊(Chip Roy)的新闻办公室也对这一举措表示欢迎，并说自己和威斯康星州共和党众议员汤姆·蒂芙尼(Tom Tiffany)在3月就对该项目表示担忧。

“罗伊众议员很高兴听到特朗普政府堵上了这一危险的漏洞。”他的办公室在X网站上写道。

来自弗吉尼亚州的民主党众议员詹姆斯·沃金肖(James Walkinshaw)今年9月在接受美国之音采访时曾表示，美国公民身份不应被滥用，任何从事“生育旅游”的人都应受到法律追究。

但来自宾夕法尼亚州的民主党籍众议员，众议员司法委员会宪法与有限政府小组委员会的首席成员玛丽·盖伊·斯坎伦(Mary Gay Scanlon)曾在9月表示，围绕“生育旅游”和“定锚婴儿”(anchor babies)的许多说法，是过于夸大和“凭空臆想”。

title: 在多家中企宣布终止合作后，法国球星姆巴佩公开道歉 美国会委员会：他不应该道歉
