content:
美国之音 —

法国足球明星基利安·姆巴佩(Kylian Mbappe)在多家中国企业宣布终止与其合作后，发表公开道歉，表示自己此前涉及中国的言论“欠妥”，伤害了“中国及世界各地华人社区的许多人”。姆巴佩在一次访谈中表示，把自己的头像安在一位“中国独裁者”脸上的表情包最让自己发笑。美国国会的一个与中国有关的委员会发表声明说，姆巴佩不应该为“称毛泽东为独裁者而道歉”。

姆巴佩在最新的声明中用中法两种语言表示，他在近期一次访问中的言论欠妥，如今明白，有关言论伤害了“中国及世界各地许多华人社区的许多人”。他强调，这绝非他的本意，自己对中国人民和历史怀有深深的敬意，并向所有受到有关言论伤害的人道歉。

在姆巴佩道歉后几个小时，美国国会众议院美国与中共战略竞争特设委员会在X平台发表声明说，姆巴佩不应该为称毛泽东为独裁者而道歉。

贴文说：“毛泽东的确是独裁者，而且他对中国人民造成的伤害远比一个足球运动员的言论要严重得多。”

贴文继续说：毛泽东曾担任中共领导人数十年，他的独裁统治和灾难性政策导致数千万中国人死于文化大革命、大饥荒和其他暴行。毛泽东自1921年中共第一次全国代表大会起就参与其中，他是这个至今仍在推行压迫和意识形态清洗的政党的主要历史人物。几十年来，中共剥夺了中国人民的基本人权，包括言论自由和宗教自由。这些权利是姆巴佩和世界各地数百万人享有的，姆巴佩应该利用这个机会，揭露毛泽东独裁统治的可怕真相。”

声明说，这则新闻真正令人愤慨的是，一些公司急于道歉，以便继续在中国开展业务。中共是压迫中国人民及其人权的最大压迫者，而那些与中共合作的企业则助长了其残酷暴行的正常化。

前NBA球星，人权活动人士埃内斯托·坎特.自由 (Enes Kanter Freedom)对姆巴佩选择道歉表示遗憾，但他同时认为，这应该是姆巴佩在压力下作出的选择。

“我亲身经历过，公开发声批评中国后会发生什么。我失去了篮球生涯，也失去了数百万美元的机会，因为我拒绝保持沉默。但我并非要指责姆巴佩的道歉行为。我不知道他承受了怎样的压力。当运动员必须在个人原则和职业生涯之间做出选择时，这就说明我们面临着一个严重的问题。所以，我认为他选择道歉是一件令人遗憾的事，因为毛泽东是个独裁者。”

**姆巴佩遭到中国企业抵制**

星期一起，一段姆巴佩接受法国忘了访谈节目“The Bridge“访谈片段在Reddit、X以及Threads等社交平台上广泛流传。视频显示，被问及使用姆巴佩头像的表情包，哪一个最让他发笑时，他说，最好笑的是有人将他的脸合成到一名“中国独裁者”的照片上。他还说，自己与朋友打电玩时经常使用这张迷因图。

尽管姆巴佩在回答中并未点名，但是，节目后期制作加上了一张将他的面孔与毛泽东形象合成的图片，让人觉得他所指的就是毛泽东。这段访谈在中国引发强烈反弹。

中国东鹏饮料、蒙牛乳业和妙可蓝多等多家企业星期二发布声明，宣布终止与姆巴佩德全部合作，并强调对“伤害中国人民感情的言行”零容忍。相关品牌也在社媒网络平台删除了与姆巴佩相关德内容。中国中央电视台更是从星期一晚间起，全面停播涉及西班牙甲组足球联赛和姆巴佩德赛事，姆巴佩德广告也全部下架。

在姆巴佩公开道歉，中国中央广播电视总台相关人士表示，已经注意到相关信息，“我们听其言更观其行，希望西甲、皇马和姆巴佩本人切实从中吸取教训，真诚道歉、痛改前非。”

姆巴佩现在效力西班牙皇家马德里，并担任法国国家队队长。他曾帮助法国队夺得2018年的世界杯冠军，并在2022年的世界杯决赛上，一个人踢进了三个球。 姆巴佩被认为是当今足坛最具有影响力和商业价值的球员之一。 在中国市场，他也曾长期受到品牌的青睐，先后与蒙牛、东鹏饮料以及小红书等企业合作。

中国外交部发言人郭嘉昆星期二在例行记者会上在被问到如何看待姆巴佩因一段网上流传的视频遭到数家中国公司解约品牌代言一事， 郭嘉昆说回应说：“伤害中国人民感情的言行自然会遭到中国社会各界的共同抵制。”

**中文网友表示姆巴佩“不用道歉”**

姆巴佩的声明在X平台发布仅2个小时后，就引起了1004万的点击，至少一万条评论，其中有不少中文评论者表示，姆巴佩不用道歉，因为他说的是事实。

一位叫“强国蛙哈哈”的用户写道：“你不用道歉，你没有错， 错的是那个变态的不承认自己有那么多独裁领导的中共独裁政府。”

一个署名“勃勃OC” 的网民写道：“其实你并没有伤害中国人，特别是世界各地的华人 你伤害了咱们党，以及他在国内的统治。仅此而已了。”

一个署名“天才王”的网友则写道：“只是无意间讲了实话，何错之有？什么蠢货才会把对于那一人的客观评价当成对整个民族的侮辱？”

**更多被中国抵制过体坛人士和明星**

姆巴佩不是第一个因为言论在中国遭到不同程度的封杀或抵制的体育明星和体坛人士，下面只是几个例子。

*   NBA火箭队的前总管达雷尔·莫雷(Daryl Morey)，2019年10月发推特支持香港民主示威者，遭中国指为辱华，官媒中央电视台即刻宣布暂停转播NBA比赛，直到隔年10月才首度直播湖人对热火总决赛，又迟至2022年3月才全面恢复正常转播。NBA总裁萧华(Adam Silver)曾表示，NBA因此损失了数亿美元。
*   2019年12月13日，前德国国脚、英超阿森纳队球员梅苏特·厄齐尔(Mesut Özil)在社交媒体上发文，批评中国政府对新疆维吾尔族人的政策与拘禁行为，引发了巨大的政治与舆论风暴。
*   德怀特·霍华德(Dwight Howard)：2023年与台湾政治人物合拍宣传片，在片中称“台湾是一个国家”，激起中国网民强烈抗议与联合抵制。
*   埃内斯托·坎特.自由 (Enes Kanter Freedom)：因为多次在社交媒体及比赛上公开发表有关西藏、新疆以及台湾的政治言论，其当时所在的波士顿凯尔特人队比赛在中国遭到停播，腾讯体育等平台全面下架其相关视频与商品。

美国之音记者许湘筠对本文也有贡献。

# Special Wednesday Event - Fete

[![Image 8: Photo of the user Kevin P](https://secure.meetupstatic.com/photos/member/9/f/5/a/thumb_322780794.jpeg?w=96) ![Image 9: Badge for Kevin P](https://secure.meetupstatic.com/next/images/avatar/super-organizer.webp?w=48) Hosted by Kevin P. and Kera Kevin P. is a Super Organizer](https://www.meetup.com/grapes-gusto-charleston-wine-meetup-group/events/317076637/attendees/)

## Details

Let's go visit the newest wine garden downtown! You may recognize some of the faces working at Fete since it was created in partnership with Wine & Company. Fete is an outdoor wine garden and we are in October, I recommend dressing for some cool evening weather. There is a small interior area, but the wine garden is where the Halloween action will be occurring.

Kevin: We are throwing a Halloween party at Fete! It's gonna be the greatest thing ever.
 Kera: Someone will die.
 Kevin: Of fun!
 Kera: And of murder.
 Kevin: And there's gonna be wine, pumpkins...
 Kera: Bloody goblins.
 Kevin: Fake ones! It's gonna be awesome. We have decorations...
 Kera: Dead people that we just murdered.
 Kevin: Not... murdered. But pictures of dead people from TV or movies!
 Kera: Mutilated bodies.
 Kevin: B-But fake ones. Candy, dancing, more wine, all kinds of food and snacks!
 Kera: Blood orphans.
 Kevin: No blood orphans. I... I don't know what that is.

## Details

Come join us for Wednesday evening Riichi Mahjong! We will have teaching equipment available for new players!

We will be at Earth Fare grocery’s cafeteria in Summerville SC!
 (Cafeteria is right of the store entrance).

1101 N Main St. Ste 306
 Summerville, SC 29483

🀄 About Riichi Mahjong
 Mahjong is a four-player game that blends strategy and luck. There are dozens of variants from all over the world. Our club plays Riichi, a variant from Japan known for its strategic depth.
 🀄New to Riichi?
 If you’ve never played mahjong or only know another variant, we’ll have a teaching table set up for newcomers. One of our hosts will guide you through the basics of Riichi, including how to build a hand and win the game.

## Details

RESERVATIONS ARE CALLED IN TO THE RESTAURANT ON THE **MONDAY** PRIOR, SO **PLEASE BE SURE TO RSVP BY THEN**!

Join your Humanist friends on the **second Tuesday** of each month for Happy Humanist Hour, where we will share a meal, drinks, and good company.

For November we will be going to **Metro Diner** located at 1808 Sam Rittenberg Blvd #1 in West Ashley, which is at the corner of Sam Rittenberg and Ashley River Roads. You can **[review their extensive menu here](https://metrodiner.com/menu/)**.

Dinner group is always a fun and relaxing evening of stimulating conversation over drinks (alcohol is optional) and yummy food among old and new friends! Hope to see you all there!

**NOTE:** We'll send out a reminder email a few days before the event so you can update your RSVP if your plans have changed. **We frequently have some no-shows and want to avoid that as much as possible**. Having an accurate count for the restaurant is important.

_Thanks to the generosity of our donors, SHL has funds available to ensure everyone feels welcome and able to participate. If the cost of participation presents a challenge, please email us at [shl@lowcountryhumanists.org,](http://shl@lowcountryhumanists.org,/) and we can discreetly arrange to cover your costs._

content:
## Details

**LFDT Labs Introduces CLPR - An Architectural Deep Dive into CLPR (Cross-Ledger Protocol)**

Join us for an in-depth technical session introducing CLPR (Cross-Ledger Protocol), a newly approved open-source project hosted under the LF Decentralized Trust Labs.
 Traditional cross-chain bridges often introduce security vulnerabilities, liquidity locking, and third-party trust assumptions. CLPR takes a fundamental shift: enabling direct, asynchronous ledger-to-ledger communication using cryptographic state proofs.

In this Meetup, we will explore:
**Architectural Overview (20–30 min)**
 The problem with traditional bridges.
 Core trust model.
 Breakdown of the protocol layers.
 How to adapt CLPR for arbitrary EVM, non-EVM, public, and enterprise ledger types.

**Implementation Deep Dive (45–60 min)**
 Hiero Native Implementation
 Besu Reference Implementation

**Live Software Demo and Q&A (30 min)**
 Live Demonstration: Watching CLPR execute cross-ledger state proof verification in real time.

**Q&A and Community Discussion and get involved in the LFDT Lab.**

**Zoom Meeting Link**: [https://zoom.us/my/hyperledger.community.3?pwd=UE90WHhEaHRqOGEyMkV3cldKa2d2dz09](https://zoom.us/my/hyperledger.community.3?pwd=UE90WHhEaHRqOGEyMkV3cldKa2d2dz09)

**Please note: This event is being shared with our entire global community. If you're interested in this content but can't attend the event live, feel free to sign up and we will send you a link to the recording after the meetup is over.**

### Speaker

#### Edward Wertz

[Edward Wertz](https://www.linkedin.com/in/edward-wertz-6aa26012/) ([https://github.com/edward-swirldslabs](https://github.com/edward-swirldslabs))

Edward Wertz is a software architect at Hashgraph, the developers of the Hedera blockchain. He is one of the maintainers of the LFDT CLPR LAB that enables cross ledger communication. Prior to Hashgraph, he worked for L3Harris as a data engineer and software architect. He completed his PhD in knowledge representation and reasoning in 2019.

## Details

**Protest with SHL! ✊ in front of Charleston City Hall at 2 pm on Sunday, October 11.**

Join us as we stand up for **First Amendment freedoms**—including the separation of church and state, press freedom, and freedom of speech and assembly.

📢 Bring a sign if you’d like (we’ll have extras on hand if you don’t).

To comply with Charleston’s restrictive protest ordinance, we’re capping this action at **24 participants**. Please RSVP here on meetup.

👉 Why the cap? The City of Charleston requires a permit for protests with more than 24 people and has been forcing permitted groups into out-of-the-way locations like Hampton Park. To make our voices heard in **well-trafficked downtown spaces**, we’re joining Silence Is Not an Option's (SINO) effort to hold **pop-up protests every 2nd Sunday of the month**, each in small groups of 24 or fewer.

Come make your voice heard!

title: ONSITE Self-Exploration through Poetry w/ Tish Voit, Thu, Nov 5, 2026, 6:00 PM   | Meetup
summary: #### **6:00 - 7:00 pm (EST), every 1st and 3rd Thursday at bliss, 1007 Johnnie Dodds Blvd, The Mezzanine Suite 228 in Mt. Pleasant.** When bliss connections & experiences nourish your soul, please consider making a donation at[ [givetobliss
content:
#### **6:00 - 7:00 pm (EST), every 1st and 3rd Thursday at bliss, 1007 Johnnie Dodds Blvd, The Mezzanine Suite 228 in Mt. Pleasant.**

When bliss connections & experiences nourish your soul, please consider making a donation at[ [givetobliss.com](http://givetobliss.com/)](http://givetobliss.com).
 Thank-you for your continued friendship & support.

After a brief round of introductions, we will begin each class with a fun warm-up exercise to get our creative juices flowing.

Next, we will explore utilizing a fresh writing prompt for each class to delve a bit deeper during a 20-minute timed stream of consciousness writing exercise designed to quiet the inner critic.

Then we will have the opportunity to share what we have put on paper in its pure unedited form.

All levels are welcomed and encouraged to enter our circle. Sharing your work is optional and helps us discover more about you.
 We may offer further growth opportunities to share your poems through open poetry reading events at bliss and other local venues.

Facilitator: Tish Voit,[ [tish@blissspiritualco-op.org](mailto:tish@blissspiritualco-op.org)]([mailto:tish@blissspiritualco-op.org](http://mailto:tish@blissspiritualco-op.org/))

From early childhood I have experienced an intimate connection with spirit. This ever loving, encouraging and persistent guide from within has directed me to become a dedicated leader for causes that help others by building community. I am a playful and intuitive visionary, artist, singer, author, cook, and friend. My favorite place to be is home which I co-create wherever I am.

I write to explore my soul self, which is eternal, expansive, and uniquely creative. I enjoy sharing my poems and hearing what others create. To be known is a blessing. Please join us for this inward journey whenever you feel called.

title: DIA Releases Clearest Image of China’s Reusable Spaceplane with Service Module Attached
zh_title: DIA发布中国可重复使用航天飞机附有服务舱的最清晰图像
source: 航空报 The Aviationist（战机/无人机/防空）
summary: DIA 报告回顾了 2020 年至 2023 年期间执行的三项任务，重点介绍了中国在 2026 年 2 月再次发射该航天器之前第二次和第三次飞行中报告的交会和接近操作。美国国防情报局 (DIA) 发布了一张中国秘密可重复使用航天飞机的新图像，该图像由 Maxar Technologies 航天器于 2024 年拍摄。发表于 DIA 的《太空安全挑战》 2026 年 10 月 26 日报道，这张照片提供了在轨航天器及其附有服务舱的罕见视图。中国可重复使用实验航天
content:
DIA 报告回顾了 2020 年至 2023 年期间执行的三项任务，重点介绍了中国在 2026 年 2 月再次发射该航天器之前第二次和第三次飞行中报告的交会和接近操作。美国国防情报局 (DIA) 发布了一张中国秘密可重复使用航天飞机的新图像，该图像由 Maxar Technologies 航天器于 2024 年拍摄。发表于 DIA 的《太空安全挑战》 2026 年 10 月 26 日报道，这张照片提供了在轨航天器及其附有服务舱的罕见视图。自 2020 年 9 月以来，中国可重复使用的实验航天器由长征二号F火箭发射，已执行四次轨道飞行任务。第一次任务持续了两天；第二颗于 2022 年 8 月发射，在轨运行了 276 天；第三个项目于 2023 年 12 月启动，历时 268 天。第四次任务于 2026 年 2 月开始。在 Maxar 图像发布之前，公共图像仅限于颗粒状的地面望远镜观测结果和带有中文标记的计算机生成的插图。 2023年初的太空跟踪论坛观察到中国航天器多次与另一个物体连接，但当时没有图像。 DIA 报告中使用的 Maxar 图像可追溯到 2024 年，当时 2023 年 12 月发射的航天器在其第三次任务中仍在轨道上。
因此，尽管捕获的确切日期尚未公开，但时间与该飞行器拍摄的照片一致。看哪：美国国防情报局发布了一份关于太空安全挑战的报告，其中包括 2024 年从 Maxar 拍摄的中国航天飞机的 NEI 图像。https://t.co/F3msSwoFph — Andrew Jones (@AJ_FI) 2026 年 10 月 27 日该报告指出了两种中国太空模型：神龙和腾云，但不知道图像中的是哪一个。中国的航天器经常与美国太空部队的 X-37B 进行比较，因为两者都是无人驾驶的可重复使用轨道飞行器，旨在返回地球。然而，中国车辆的设计、有效载荷和任务目标在很大程度上仍未公开。跟踪数据表明它已经部署了物体并执行了交会和接近操作，但这些观察结果并没有确定航天器的预期军事作用。这架太空飞机出现在国防情报局对太空相关能力和威胁进行更广泛的评估中，其目标是覆盖战略竞争对手的能力。新闻稿称：“更新后的报告详细介绍了中国、俄罗斯以及新兴太空强国伊朗和朝鲜的太空防御和军事目标，包括战略、计划和意图。”长征二号F/T运载火箭，类似于运载中国可重复使用航天飞机的运载火箭，从酒泉卫星发射中心升空。
|资料来源：新华社 中国航天器 该图片显示了中国可重复使用航天飞机的底部视图，其服务舱已安装并部署了太阳能电池板。据了解，该模块在轨道任务期间提供电力和推进力，然后在重返大气层之前与航天飞机分离，类似于 X-37B 的服务舱。该图像似乎还显示了航天器的有效载荷舱门，尽管可见特征的精确配置和功能尚未公开详细说明。其中的可能性包括机械臂、小型卫星或在轨测试样本等系统。

【原文 English Original】
The DIA report reviews the three missions flown between 2020 and 2023, highlighting reported rendezvous and proximity operations during the second and third flights, before China launched the spacecraft again in February 2026.  The U.S. Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) has released a new image of China’s secretive reusable spaceplane, captured by a Maxar Technologies spacecraft in 2024. Published in the DIA’s “Challenges to Security in Space” report on Oct. 26, 2026, the photo provides a rare view of the spacecraft in orbit with its service module attached. China’s reusable experimental spacecraft has flown four orbital missions since September 2020, launched aboard Long March 2F rockets. The first mission lasted two days; the second, launched in August 2022, remained in orbit for 276 days; and the third, launched in December 2023, lasted 268 days. A fourth mission began in February 2026. Before the release of the Maxar image, public imagery was limited to grainy ground-based telescope observations and computer-generated illustrations with Chinese markings. Space tracking forums in early 2023 observed the Chinese spacecraft connecting with another object multiple times, but no image existed at the time. The Maxar image used in the DIA report is dated to 2024, when the spacecraft launched in December 2023 was still in orbit during its third mission. The timing is therefore consistent with the photograph depicting the vehicle during that flight, although the exact date of capture has not been publicly disclosed. Behold: The US Defense Intelligence Agency has released a report on challenges to security in space, including an NEI image of China’s spaceplane from Maxar, taken in 2024. https://t.co/F3msSwoFph — Andrew Jones (@AJ_FI) October 27, 2026 The report identifies two Chinese space models, Shenlong and Tengyun, but it is not known which of those is in the image. The Chinese spacecraft is often compared with the U.S. Space Force’s X-37B because both are uncrewed reusable orbital vehicles designed to return to Earth. However, the Chinese vehicle’s design, payload, and mission objectives remain largely undisclosed. Tracking data indicate that it has deployed objects and performed rendezvous and proximity operations, but these observations do not establish the spacecraft’s intended military role. The spaceplane appears in the DIA’s broader assessment of space-related capabilities and threats, whose goal is to cover the capabilities of strategic rivals. “The updated report details the space defense and military goals, including strategies, plans and intentions, of China, Russia and the emerging space powers of Iran and North Korea,” says the press release . The Long March 2F/T launch vehicle, similar to the one used to carry the Chinese reusable spaceplane, lifting off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center. | Source: Xinhua Chinese spacecraft The image provides a view of the underside of China’s reusable spaceplane, with its service module attached and solar arrays deployed. The module is understood to provide electrical power and propulsion during the orbital mission before separating from the spaceplane ahead of reentry, similarly to the X-37B’s service module. The image also appears to show the spacecraft’s payload-bay doors, although the precise configuration and function of the visible features have not been publicly detailed. Among the possibilities are systems like robotic arms, small satellites or specimens for in-orbit testing. Now then — this could be something exceptional. The rumours are that inside this exceptional payload fairing atop a CZ-2F is a CASC spaceplane, launching from Jiuquan Friday. Source: 俊了个锅 via 林晓弈。 https://t.co/qs6VRfzQoP https://t.co/ZPnpwAIfyO — Andrew Jones (@AJ_FI) September 3, 2020 Beijing launched its first ever reusable spaceplane prototype on Sep. 4, 2020 aboard a Long March 2F carrier rocket from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwestern China’s Gobi desert. The spacecraft remained in orbit for two days before returning to Earth. Although Chinese authorities did not initially disclose the landing site in detail, open-source analysis of satellite imagery associated the landing with a runway near the Lop Nur nuclear test site in northwestern China. Since its launch on 4 August 2022, we observed multiple large maneuvers raising the object’s altitude — as well as repeated deployments, formation flying, and docking of a sub-satellite Object J (NORAD ID 54218). https://t.co/ORVgSXYKmJ — LeoLabs (@LeoLabs_Space) May 8, 2023 The second launch of the space plane took place on Aug. 4, 2022, this time spending 276 days in orbit until May 8, 2023. According to the DIA, the vehicle appeared to “maneuver with a companion satellite and conduct station-keeping at around 1 km separation.” “At one point, the two objects appeared within 100 meters of one another. The spaceplane and satellite possibly rendezvoused before the satellite was re-released,” the DIA report said. This event tested our object tracking and maneuver detection and characterization capabilities, proving that we can provide critical intelligence on the behaviors and activities of objects in #LEO thanks to our continuous, real-time operations. https://t.co/WDP06ffBSv — LeoLabs (@LeoLabs_Space) May 8, 2023 On May 8, 2023, commercial space-tracking company LeoLabs reported that its observations indicated repeated deployments, formation flying, and apparent docking or capture operations involving ‘Object J’: “Since its launch on 4 August 2022, we observed multiple large maneuvers raising the object’s altitude – as well as repeated deployments, formation flying, and docking of a sub-satellite Object J (NORAD ID 54218). We’ve determined that the Test Spacecraft2 has propulsive capability and engaged in proximity operations with Object J, including what appeared to be at least two and possibly three capture/docking operations.” China launched the spacecraft on its third orbital mission on Dec. 14, 2023. It remained in orbit for 268 days, returning on Sept. 6, 2024, according to the DIA report. The U.S. Space Force’s X-37B Orbital Test Vehicle Mission Seven successfully landed at Vandenberg Space Force Base, Calif., March 7, 2025. | Source: U.S. Space Force courtesy photo During that flight, the spacecraft again “released and interacted with an object,”according to the DIA. Considering that the Maxar image was captured in 2024, we can presume the vehicle was photographed during this third mission. Although this was not covered by the report, the spacecraft’s fourth mission began in February 2026. Orbital-tracking data analyzed by astronomer Jonathan McDowell indicated that the vehicle released and subsequently recaptured the same object, whose precise identity and purpose remain unknown, with similar operations reportedly repeated later in the flight. then executed a rerendezvous with the subsat on Sep 10 and a recapture on Sep  13. This analysis is based on USSF GP data. USSF also cataloged an additional object 24J on about Sep 10, but with no orbit data; I think this was a mistake and is a duplicate of object 24H. — Jonathan McDowell (@planet4589) September 23, 2026 Future and purpose The spacecraft’s proximity operations have raised questions about potential counterspace applications, with some theories assigning more exotic kinetic ‘anti-satellite’ capabilities to the Chinese spacecraft. While there is no evidence yet the vehicle is designed as a kinetic anti-satellite weapon, and the spaceplane’s intended mission remains undisclosed, space is becoming a contested domain. The observed rendezvous and capture capabilities can support satellite inspection and servicing, but could also enable interference with other spacecraft. The spacecraft’s potential military applications remain uncertain. While there is no public evidence confirming that the vehicle carries military payloads, such a platform could be used for space-based reconnaissance, intelligence-gathering, and monitoring of other space objects, as well as kinetic missions possibly involving the use of directed energy weapons, offensive weapons or electronic warfare. America’s X37B compared to China’s orbital Spaceplane. https://t.co/DPC4W3euTW — David Willis (@ThePrimalDino) October 27, 2026 China has however maintained a non-military purpose for this spacecraft. A machine translation of a Xinhua report of the Aug. 5, 2022 launch said: “The test spacecraft will be in orbit for a period of time before returning to the scheduled landing site in China, during which reusable and in-orbit service technology verification will be carried out as planned to provide technical support for the peaceful use of space.”

The Donald Trump–Vladimir Putin–Xi Jinping Summit: A New Yalta? bbert@hudson.org Tue, 10/27/2026 - 11:55 SVG Commentary Oct 26, 2026 National Interest The Donald Trump–Vladimir Putin–Xi Jinping Summit: A New Yalta? An unprecedented summit with Putin and Xi could demonstrate Washington’s unmatched diplomatic reach. But it may also reveal the growing gap between America’s power and its credibility.   Tsiporah Fried Visiting Senior Fellow Tsiporah Fried Commentary Caption US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin arrive for a press conference at Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson on August 15, 2025, in Anchorage, Alaska. (Getty Images) Toggle Table of Contents Contents Contents Share to Twitter Twitter Share to Facebook Facebook Share to LinkedIn LinkedIn Share to E-mail E-mail Print Print President Donald Trump ’s openness to an unprecedented trilateral summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping , potentially on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation ( APEC ) summit in Shenzhen this November, raises questions far beyond the war in Ukraine . The proposal reportedly originated in Moscow, with Putin seeking to capitalize on his improving relationship with Trump. The American president, however, has suggested that such a gathering should focus primarily on nuclear disarmament rather than Ukraine . Yet the significance of such a summit would extend well beyond its immediate agenda. It would reflect a broader transformation in international relations: the growing temptation to replace established institutions, alliances, and multilateral frameworks with direct transactions among great powers. 美国选举的辉煌 bbert@hudson.org 星期二, 10/27/2026 - 12:17 SVG 评论 2026 年 10 月 26 日 华盛顿时报 美国选举的辉煌 当政府无法被投票淘汰时，渎职行为可能会变成灾难性的   于文贵 (Miles Yu) 高级研究员兼中国中心主任 于文贵 (Miles Yu) 评论说明文字 选民在投票站填写选票2025 年 11 月 4 日，弗吉尼亚州希尔斯伯勒的希尔斯伯勒老石学校。 (Getty Images) 切换目录 目录 目录 分享到 Twitter Twitter 分享到 Facebook Facebook 分享到 LinkedIn LinkedIn 分享到电子邮件 电子邮件 打印 打印 选举又来了。它们吵闹、有党派之争、价格昂贵，而且常常让人筋疲力尽。政客们做出奢侈的承诺，攻击他们的对手，并用广告轰炸选民。然而，在所有这些骚动的背后，隐藏着现代文明最伟大的成就之一：能够和平、定期地纠正政治错误，而不会导致国家分裂。当美国人为 11 月 3 日的中期选举做准备，台湾选民期待 11 月 28 日的地方选举（包括戏剧性的台北市长竞选）时，我们正在见证民主的发挥。民主的真正力量并不在于它总能产生优秀的领导人或明智的政策，而是在于它赋予人们在出现问题时改变方向的权力。每个政客都容易傲慢。每个执政党最终都会面临将自身利益与国家利益混淆的风险。
选举中断了这种危险的趋势，提醒当权者，他们的权力是暂时的、有条件的，最终属于人民。没有什么比输掉选举的前景更能让政客感到谦卑的了。竞选活动迫使官员离开舒适的办公室，倾听愤怒选民的声音，解释失败并捍卫他们宁愿忘记的决定。这就是vox populi，人民之声的实际意义。美国的中期选举制度尤其巧妙。将其视为大学期中考试。作为一名教授，我知道只在学期结束时收到反馈的学生往往发现自己的错误为时已晚。期中考试会告诉他们在期末考试之前他们的处境、他们的误解以及他们必须改进的地方。美国民主的运作方式也类似。总统任期四年，但选民每两年选举一次整个众议院和大约三分之一的参议院。他们可以改变国会的控制权、限制总统的举措并要求政策调整——而不会罢免总统或引发宪法危机。中期选举也对政治极端主义提供了纠正。偏离普通选民担忧太远的政党可能会失去权力。陷入意识形态斗争的政客可能会发现选民更关心就业、通货膨胀、公共安全和有能力的政府。选举并不能消除党派之争。
它们为政治挫折提供了一个定期、和平的发泄途径。台湾提供了一个有启发性的对比。其总统和国家立法机关的任期均为四年，没有美国式的全国立法中期选举。 2024 年选举后，总统赖清德上台，反对党——主要是国民党和台湾人民党——获得了立法多数。结果是预算、立法权和总统议程上的长期对抗。那次对抗助长了台湾的伟大

The Brilliance of US Elections bbert@hudson.org Tue, 10/27/2026 - 12:17 SVG Commentary Oct 26, 2026 Washington Times The Brilliance of US Elections When government cannot be voted out, malfeasance can become catastrophic   Miles Yu Senior Fellow and Director, China Center Miles Yu Commentary Caption Voters fill out their ballots at a polling station in the Hillsboro Old Stone School on November 4, 2025, in Hillsboro, Virginia. (Getty Images) Toggle Table of Contents Contents Contents Share to Twitter Twitter Share to Facebook Facebook Share to LinkedIn LinkedIn Share to E-mail E-mail Print Print Elections are here again. They are noisy, partisan, expensive and often exhausting. Politicians make extravagant promises, attack their opponents and bombard voters with advertisements. Yet beneath all this commotion lies one of the greatest achievements of modern civilization: the ability to correct political mistakes peacefully, regularly and without tearing the country apart. As Americans prepare for the Nov. 3 midterms and Taiwanese voters look toward their Nov. 28 local elections, including the dramatic Taipei mayoral race, we are witnessing democracy at work. Democracy’s real strength is not that it always produces good leaders or wise policies, but that it gives people the power to change course when things go wrong. Every politician is susceptible to arrogance. Every governing party eventually risks confusing its own interests with those of the nation. Elections interrupt this dangerous tendency, reminding those in power that their authority is temporary, conditional and ultimately belongs to the people. Nothing humbles a politician like the prospect of losing an election. Campaigns force officials to leave their comfortable offices, listen to angry constituents, explain failures and defend decisions they would rather forget. This is the practical meaning of vox populi, the voice of the people. The American midterm system is particularly ingenious. Think of it as a college midterm examination. As a professor, I know that students who receive feedback only at the end of a semester often discover their mistakes too late. A midterm tells them where they stand, what they have misunderstood and what they must improve before the final exam. American democracy works similarly. Presidents serve four-year terms, but every two years, voters elect the entire House of Representatives and roughly one-third of the Senate. They can change congressional control, restrain presidential initiatives and demand policy adjustments — without removing the president or provoking a constitutional crisis. Midterms also offer a corrective to political extremism. Parties that stray too far from ordinary voters’ concerns risk losing power. Politicians consumed by ideological battles may discover that voters care more about jobs, inflation, public safety and competent government. Elections do not eliminate partisanship. They provide a regular, peaceful outlet for political frustration. Taiwan offers an instructive contrast. Its president and national legislature both serve four-year terms without an American-style nationwide legislative midterm. After the 2024 elections, President Lai Ching-te took office while opposition parties — principally the Kuomintang and the Taiwan People’s Party — secured a legislative majority. The result was prolonged confrontation over budgets, legislative authority and the president’s agenda. That confrontation helped fuel Taiwan’s Great Recall movement in 2025, when activists attempted to remove some of the most intransigent, partisan opposition legislators before their terms expired, though all recall efforts ultimately failed. Supporters saw the recalls as necessary accountability; opponents viewed them as partisan attempts to reverse legitimate election results. Four years is a long time for a divided government to remain locked in political warfare without a scheduled national legislative election. Taiwan’s recall mechanism provides a remedy, but it is no substitute for the routine accountability of American midterms. The U.S. can change the balance of congressional power every two years without resorting to a nationwide recall campaign. Taiwan’s 2025 Great Recall Movement functioned as a grassroots political corrective to the island democracy’s lack of a midterm electoral mechanism. In communist China, the fundamental problem is not simply that elections are absent but that the ruling party has made itself virtually immune to accountability. The Chinese Communist Party claims that one-party rule delivers efficiency and stability by eliminating electoral competition. What it actually eliminates is the people’s power to dismiss those who govern them. The CCP investigates, judges, disciplines and ultimately absolves itself. It decides what constitutes success, what counts as failure and who must take the blame. The public has no independent electoral means of challenging that verdict. This creates a dangerous political culture. Leaders who never have to face voters become accustomed to issuing commands rather than answering questions. Criticism becomes disloyalty, dissent a security threat. Over time, unchecked power breeds an arrogant, aggressive, imperious ruling party convinced that its authority is beyond challenge at home and that its will should be imposed abroad. Communist China constitutes the bloodiest regime in human history, with an estimated 80 million unnatural deaths in its decades of totalitarian rule. Mao Zedong’s Great Leap Forward produced one of history’s deadliest famines. The Cultural Revolution devastated Chinese society for a decade. The early opacity and mismanagement of COVID-19 under Xi Jinping’s administration exacerbated a pandemic that ultimately resulted in an estimated 15 million excess deaths worldwide, including more than 1 million Americans. In these cases, the concentration of political authority and suppression of dissent allowed disastrous policies to continue long after their consequences became evident. Who was held politically accountable for these failures? No national election allowed Chinese citizens to judge the leadership’s record. No opposition party could campaign on an alternative policy. Democracies also make serious policy mistakes, but their leaders face independent scrutiny and the possibility of electoral defeat. In China, political survival depends principally on loyalty within the ruling party, not the consent of the governed. The lesson is unmistakable: When a government cannot be voted out, its mistakes can become national catastrophes. When rulers face no effective public accountability, their greatest incentive is often not to correct failure but to conceal it. The American Founders understood this danger. James Madison wrote in Federalist No. 51 that “Ambition must be made to counteract ambition.” Democracy’s noisy arguments, frustrating compromises and constant campaigns are not necessarily signs of weakness. They are part of a system that allows political conflict to be settled without repression or revolution. The real test of a political system is not whether its leaders make mistakes, but whether those mistakes can be exposed, corrected and punished without bloodshed. So when Americans complain about another exhausting election season, they should remember what is at stake. The same goes for Taiwanese voters navigating their own contentious democracy. Elections are democracy’s periodic examinations. They do not guarantee that governments will always pass. They guarantee that governments must answer to the people. Read in The Washington Times. 执行摘要：7 月份，Rosatom 将 2026 年投资计划削减了近一半。这使得耗资巨大的承诺变得紧张，例如哈萨克斯坦耗资 165 亿美元的巴尔喀什工厂，其中 85% 的资金将由俄罗斯国家贷款提供。为了对冲俄罗斯的风险，乌兹别克斯坦于六月向金砖国家新开发银行寻求资助其吉扎克工厂。哈萨克斯坦指定中国核工业集团公司在 2025 年领导其第二座核电站，据报道，乌兹别克斯坦计划与北京合作建设第二座核电站。除中亚之外，俄罗斯国家原子能公司还与中东、非洲和东南亚国家签署了协议，通过燃料供应、维护和技术合作确保莫斯科拥有数十年的影响力。 9月3日，俄罗斯Rosatom国家核公司子公司Atomstroyexport与哈萨克斯坦签署了工程、采购和施工合同（《阿斯塔纳时报》9月3日）。该协议凸显了该公司在该地区的持久影响力。然而，近几个月来，有迹象表明，Rosatom 可能面临财务限制，这可能使其在中亚的核能项目变得复杂，特别是在哈萨克斯坦和乌兹别克斯坦（Anhor.uz，7 月 23 日）。俄罗斯国家原子能公司自己的领导层也承认了这种压力。 7 月，Rosatom 总干事阿列克谢·利哈乔夫 (Alexei Likhachev) 承认，在经济形势不利的情况下，该公司正在减少投资计划（国际文传电讯社，7 月 16 日）。
利哈乔夫还证实，某些项目已被放弃或推迟，公司打算减少运营支出（Anhor.uz，7 月 23 日）。Rosatom 经济和金融副总干事伊利亚·雷布罗夫（Ilya Rebrov）此前承认，Rosatom 企业 2025 年的投资请求超出了可用融资资源的四倍（KazanFirst，2025 年 8 月 12 日）。他补充说，该公司预计 2025 年至 2030 年的投资需求增长速度远远快于预期的营业收入。主要问题是，俄罗斯国家原子能公司的传统竞争优势——提供核技术以及俄罗斯国家支持的大量融资的能力——对于莫斯科来说，在对乌克兰的战争中维持这一优势的成本变得越来越高。哈萨克斯坦的旗舰项目说明了这种财政负担的规模。 5 月，俄罗斯和哈萨克斯坦签订了政府间协议，涵盖巴尔喀什核电站（核电站 (NPP)）的建设和融资，估计成本为 165 亿美元（Anadolu Ajansı，5 月 29 日）。融资结构设想俄罗斯通过国家出口贷款提供约 85% 的建设资金，哈萨克斯坦提供剩余的 15%（Fergana.News，5 月 28 日）。潜在的挑战是莫斯科必须在延长的建设期内分配大量资金，在收到全额偿还之前提供融资。
该项目还面临成本超支和延误的风险。乌兹别克斯坦提出了不同的挑战，因为塔什干一直不愿使其核计划完全依赖俄罗斯的融资。吉扎克正在建设的综合核电站结合了两个 VVER-1000 反应堆（俄罗斯设计的压水反应堆，每个容量约为 1,000 兆瓦）和两个较小的 RITM-200N 装置，这是为俄罗斯核破冰船提供动力的紧凑型反应堆的陆基版本（Atom Media，2025 年 9 月 26 日）。塔什干探索了fina

Executive Summary: In July, Rosatom moved to cut its 2026 investment program by nearly half. This strains costly commitments such as Kazakhstan’s $16.5 billion Balkhash plant, 85 percent of which a Russian state loan will finance. Hedging against Russia, Uzbekistan courted the BRICS New Development Bank to finance its Jizzakh plant in June. Kazakhstan named China National Nuclear Corporation to lead its second plant in 2025, and Uzbekistan reportedly plans its second with Beijing. Beyond Central Asia, Rosatom signed deals with countries across the Middle East, Africa, and Southeast Asia, securing Moscow decades of leverage through fuel supply, maintenance, and technological cooperation. On September 3, Atomstroyexport, a subsidiary of Russia’s Rosatom state nuclear corporation, signed an engineering, procurement, and construction contract with Kazakhstan ( The Astana Times , September 3). The agreement highlights the company’s enduring influence in the region. In recent months, however, there have been indications that Rosatom might be facing financial constraints that could complicate its nuclear energy projects in Central Asia, particularly in Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan ( Anhor.uz , July 23). Rosatom’s own leadership has acknowledged the strain. In July, Rosatom Director General Alexei Likhachev acknowledged that the corporation was reducing its investment program amid unfavorable economic conditions ( Interfax , July 16). Likhachev also confirmed that certain projects had been abandoned or postponed and that the corporation intended to reduce operating expenditures ( Anhor.uz , July 23). Rosatom Deputy Director General for Economics and Finance Ilya Rebrov had previously acknowledged that investment requests from Rosatom enterprises in 2025 exceeded available financing resources by a factor of four ( KazanFirst , August 12, 2025). He added that the company’s projected investment requirements for 2025–2030 were growing considerably faster than expected operating earnings. The main problem is that Rosatom’s traditional competitive advantage—its ability to offer nuclear technology together with substantial Russian state-backed financing—is becoming expensive for Moscow to sustain amid the war against Ukraine. Kazakhstan’s flagship project illustrates the scale of this financial burden. In May, Russia and Kazakhstan concluded intergovernmental agreements covering the construction and financing of the Balkhash Nuclear Power Plant (Nuclear Power Plant (NPP), at an estimated cost of $16.5 billion ( Anadolu Ajansı , May 29). The financing structure envisages Russia providing approximately 85 percent of construction funding through a state export loan, with Kazakhstan covering the remaining 15 percent ( Fergana.News , May 28). The potential challenge is that Moscow must allocate substantial capital over an extended construction period, providing financing well before it receives full repayment. The project also faces risks of cost overruns and delays. Uzbekistan presents a different challenge because Tashkent has been reluctant to make its nuclear program entirely dependent on Russian financing. The integrated NPP under construction in Jizzakh combines two VVER-1000 reactors, Russian-designed pressurized water reactors with a capacity of about 1,000 megawatts each, with two smaller RITM-200N units, a land-based version of the compact reactors that power Russia’s nuclear icebreakers ( Atom Media , September 26, 2025). Tashkent has explored financing from multiple international institutions, including the BRICS New Development Bank, rather than relying exclusively on Russian state credits. Tashkent has not ruled out a Russian export loan. It is also discussing financing with other lenders, however ( UzDaily , June 5). Given Rosatom’s traditional business model, which combines reactor construction with attractive state-backed financing, its ability to offer a fully integrated Russian package could become less appealing if the corporation increasingly depends on third-party lenders. Cooperation with Rosatom remains comfortable for Central Asian countries. Moscow’s competitive advantage lies partly in its willingness to pursue nuclear energy agreements without imposing the political conditions often associated with Western partnerships. Russia also offers a comprehensive package of services covering reactor construction, nuclear fuel supply, personnel training, regulatory assistance, and spent-fuel management. Rosatom’s ability to tailor its proposals to different reactor capacities, deployment models, and financing arrangements further enhances its appeal to Central Asian governments. At the same time, this package creates fertile ground for Moscow to build its long-term influence with regional governments. This flexibility is particularly attractive to regional capitals pursuing diversified foreign policies, often described as multi-alignment, which prioritize maintaining productive relationships with competing global powers rather than committing exclusively to any single geopolitical bloc. For Russia, this approach provides an opportunity to expand its long-term technological and economic presence in the region without requiring host governments to make explicit geopolitical commitments to Moscow. Nuclear diplomacy is a key tool for Russia to maintain, and in some respects expand, its influence in Central Asia. Russia faces growing rivalry as more foreign nuclear companies seek to enter the Central Asian market. Central Asian states also fear exclusive dependence on Russia, which explains why they are open to cooperation with other players in the nuclear sphere. This shift is already visible. A Chinese company will build Uzbekistan’s second nuclear plant ( Gazeta , September 8). Similarly, the state-run China National Nuclear Corporation will build Kazakhstan’s third NPP ( RBC , July 31, 2025).  Rosatom has been expanding its presence in the Middle East, Africa, and Southeast Asia. Russia and Vietnam have signed an intergovernmental agreement to build Vietnam’s first NPP ( Rossiyskaya Gazeta , March 23). Russia and Mongolia are currently in talks over Rosatom’s proposal to build a small NPP ( TASS , October 15). In Africa, Russia and the Republic of the Congo signed an energy deal on developing nuclear energy in 2024 ( Business Insider Africa , July 18, 2024). Russia and Rwanda signed a roadmap agreement to develop a small modular reactor (SMR) nuclear power project ( The New Times , June 30). The agreement follows Likhachev’s statement in May that Moscow and Kigali had reached an understanding on the construction of an NPP ( Russia’s Pivot to Asia , July 1). Iran remains Rosatom’s most important partner in the Middle East. In 2025, Moscow and Tehran signed a memorandum of understanding on the construction of small NPPs in Iran ( RIA Novosti , September 25, 2025). In Türkiye, Rosatom is constructing the Akkuyu NPP, valued at approximately $20 billion. The project is being delivered under a Build-Own-Operate model, with Rosatom retaining ownership and operational control. Once all four 1,200-megawatt units are online, Akkuyu is expected to supply about 10 percent of Türkiye’s electricity. The first unit is due to be commissioned this year, with the remaining units phased in through 2028. Rosatom is also building Egypt’s El Dabaa NPP. In January, Rosatom submitted proposals to the United Arab Emirates for large and small, land-based and floating NPPs ( Interfax , January 29). In February, Rosatom pitched large and small reactors, including floating units, at an industrial exhibition in Riyadh, building on its 2015 cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia ( Atom Media , February 12). In 2024, Rosatom also signed a memorandum of understanding on the peaceful use of atomic energy with Iraq ( Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research in Iraq , September 17, 2024). For Moscow, the nuclear projects in Central Asia would consolidate its position in the region’s nuclear energy sector and create opportunities for long-term technological cooperation, fuel supply, and maintenance contracts, potentially strengthening Russia’s influence over the regional countries’ civilian nuclear infrastructure for decades. 美国国防情报局（DIA）证实，网上流传多年的一张图像确实显示了中国实验性可重复使用航天飞机在轨道上运行。新发布的高分辨率图像副本强调，该设计几乎与美国太空军目前运营的 X-37B 微型航天飞机一模一样。国防情报局在昨天发布的一份关于地球大气层以外的全球安全挑战的新非机密报告中纳入了中国航天飞机的高分辨率图像。 Maxar Technologies（现为 Vantor）的一颗卫星捕捉到了这张图像，但具体时间仍不清楚。它的版权日期确实是 2024 年。该图像显示了一个类似微型航天飞机的设计，带有小机翼和双垂直尾翼。它还在中央有效载荷舱上方设有向上打开的门。尾部还有一个延伸部分，两侧都部署了太阳能电池板。有一些看起来并排的腹侧舱，很可能用于三轮起落架配置中的主起落架。总体而言，其核心设计与美国X-37B极其相似，同样采用三轮起落架，并且还可以在尾部安装扩展有效载荷模块。一个主要区别是，与 X-37B 相比，中国设计的机翼弦长得多。中国实验性可重复使用航天飞机（左）和美国的在轨拍摄的并排比较
X-37B 配备了扩展有效载荷模块，正准备发射（右图）。 Maxar（现为 Vantor），来自 DIA/美国太空军 另一张 X-37B 的照片，图中可以看到从太空任务返回后坐在三轮车起落架上。美国空军 X-37B 于 2022 年 11 月 12 日返回地球后在肯尼迪航天中心航线上执行 OTV-6 任务。美国空军“可重复使用太空活动的关键能力是像 Maxar 捕获的这架中华人民共和国航天飞机这样的航天飞机。航天飞机可以发射到轨道以将物体放置在太空中，甚至测试它们并返回地球[原文如此]，”DIA 报告中的图片说明如此写道。如前所述，该图像存在的基本事实并不新鲜。时任美国太空军驻韩国 (SPACEFOR-KOR) 负责人的美国太空军上校约翰·帕特里克 (John Patrick) 在 2024 年韩国开放空间论坛的演讲中加入了分辨率低得多的版本。当时还不清楚该图片是否只是显示了一架 X-37B。 TWZ 当时联系了美国太空军和 Maxar 以获取更多信息，但两者均拒绝置评。自2010年以来，建造了两架X-37B，总共执行了八次轨道飞行任务。轨道测试飞行器8号（OTV-8）任务于2025年8月22日发射。X-37B在轨道上被地面望远镜拍摄到？
pic.twitter.com/YPj8I4cQmZ — 笑脸男人 (@lfx160219) 2024 年 11 月 8 日 据了解，自 2020 年以来，中国使用同一实验飞行器进行了四次独立的轨道航天飞机任务。其中 3 次任务在帕特里克上校发表演讲之前就已结束。最近一次发射发生在今年 2 月 7 日，至少据我们所知，该车辆尚未返回。在2023年12月14日至2024年9月6日的第三次任务中，观察到中国航天飞机将多个较小的物体释放到轨道上。这些有效载荷可能是什么仍然未知，但

【原文 English Original】
The U.S. Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) has confirmed that an image that has been circulating online for years does indeed show an experimental Chinese reusable spaceplane in orbit. A newly released higher-resolution copy of the image underscores that the design is nearly a dead ringer for the X-37B miniature space shuttles now operated by the U.S. Space Force . DIA included the higher-resolution image of the Chinese spaceplane in a new unclassified report on global security challenges outside of the Earth’s atmosphere, which was released yesterday . A satellite belonging to Maxar Technologies (now Vantor) captured the image, but when exactly remains unclear. It does have a 2024 copyright date. The image shows a miniature space shuttle-like design with small wings and twin vertical tails. It also has upward-opening doors above a central payload bay. There is also an extension at the tail end with solar panels seen deployed on either side. There are what look to be side-by-side ventral bays, which are likely for the main gear in a tricycle landing gear configuration. Overall, the core design is extremely similar to that of the U.S. X-37B , which also features tricycle landing gear and can also be fitted with an extended payload module at the tail. One major difference is that the wings on the Chinese design have a much longer chord compared to the X-37B. A side-by-side comparison of the on-orbit shot of the experimental Chinese reusable spaceplane (at left) and a U.S. X-37B fitted with an extended payload module being prepared for launch (at right). Maxar (now Vantor) via DIA/US Space Force Another look at an X-37B, seen here sitting on its tricycle landing gear after returning from a mission in space. USAF The X-37B used on the OTV-6 mission on the flight line at the Kennedy Space Center after its return to Earth on November 12, 2022. USAF “A key capability for reusable space activities are spaceplanes like this PRC [People’s Republic of China] Spaceplane captured by Maxar. Spaceplanes can launch into orbit to place objects in space or even test them and return to earth [sic],” reads the caption to the picture in DIA’s report. As noted, the basic fact of the existence of this image is not new. U.S. Space Force Col. John Patrick, then head of U.S. Space Forces-Korea (SPACEFOR-KOR), included a much lower-resolution version in a presentation at the Open Space Forum in South Korea in 2024. It was also not immediately clear at that time whether or not the picture simply showed an X-37B. TWZ had reached out at the time to the U.S. Space Force and Maxar for more information, and both had declined to comment. Two X-37Bs were built, and they have sent on eight orbital missions, in total, since 2010. The Orbital Test Vehicle 8 (OTV-8) mission was launched on August 22, 2025. X-37B in orbit photographed by ground-based telescopes？ pic.twitter.com/YPj8I4cQmZ — 笑脸男人 (@lfx160219) November 8, 2024 China is understood to have conducted four separate orbital spaceplane missions using the same experimental vehicle since 2020. Three of those missions had concluded before Col. Patrick gave his presentation. The most recent launch occurred on February 7 of this year, and the vehicle has not yet returned, at least as far as we are aware. On the third mission, which lasted from December 14, 2023, to September 6, 2024, the Chinese spaceplane was observed releasing multiple smaller objects into orbit. What those payloads may have been remains unknown, but they could have been released from the main payload bay, which is seen open in the on-orbit image. The bay could have opened without any subsequent release of objects on either of the two prior missions, as well. As an aside, the spaceplane appears to have released at least one more object earlier this year in the course of its latest mission. A secretive airbase in the northwest end of China, sporting one of the longest runways in the world at 16,400 feet, looks to be where the spaceplane has landed after missions. The facility, which has been expanded massively in recent years , is now loosely akin to America’s top-secret proving ground at Area 51 , and has been the site of other advanced aviation test efforts . DIA’s report also says that “China has two primary spaceplane models: the Shenlong and Tengyun,” but does not specify which one is seen in the image. The name Shenlong has been commonly used to refer to the spaceplane China has been experimenting with to date. Images said to show a prototype or test article of this design slung underneath an H-6 bomber for testing purposes had emerged in 2007. Images that emerged in 2007 of a reusable spaceplane prototype, or a related test article, referred to as Shenlong, underneath an H-6 bomber. Chinese internet The state-run China Aerospace Science and Industry Corporation (CASIC) unveiled the Tengyun design in 2016 as part of a so-called two-stage-to-orbit system that uses a mothership aircraft flying within the atmosphere as part of the launch method rather than a traditional space launch rocket. As of 2020, CASIC was aiming for a live test of Tengyun in 2025 , but it is not immediately clear whether or not that occurred. Images showing wind tunnel testing of a Chinese two-stage-to-orbit concept. Chinese internet There have been other spaceplane developments in China in recent years. This includes designs from the China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC) and Aviation Industry Corporation of China (AVIC) subsidiary Chengdu. The design from Chengdu is called Haolong and has been in development officially as an option for resupplying the country’s Tiangong space station . They seem not only got a model but also a full-scale prototype. HaoLong-1 cargo spaceplane https://t.co/VI1Yoh3sRj pic.twitter.com/Dthfd1gi1v — CNSPACE (@CNSpaceflight) November 11, 2024 In general, “spaceplanes are … reusable and feature enhanced maneuverability, making them more suitable for certain missions than traditional satellites,” DIA’s report notes. TWZ has highlighted in the past how reusable space shuttle-like vehicles offer ideal platforms for rapidly deploying small satellites and any other payloads into orbit. In this way, they can be critical assets for space-based experimentation, as well as operational activities. This could include intelligence gathering , and even on-orbit attacks , areas of clear interest to the Chinese government . As we often mention in the context of the X-37B , spaceplanes also have distinct advantages when it comes to rendezvousing with and maneuvering very close to other objects in space. They can execute course changes and other maneuvers in ways that traditional satellites cannot. All of this only underscores their potential as weapon systems , as well as for gathering intelligence. The fact that a Maxar (now Vantor) satellite took an on-orbit picture – a service the company is known to offer – of a Chinese spaceplane further highlights the kind of cat-and-mouse games that are increasingly emerging in space. The general risks posed by these kinds of activities were recently thrust into the public eye by the unprecedentedly close shadowing of a commercial radar imaging satellite tied to Ukraine by another satellite belonging to Russia. China has been making massive investments, in general, in new space-based intelligence and other capabilities in recent years. Chinese space developments have now also extended into reusable space launch rocket boosters . Space launch company LandSpace became the first in China to achieve a successful recovery of a reusable space launch rocket booster on land in August. That followed CASC’s successful recovery of a reusable space launch rocket booster at sea using a specially configured ship the month before. In general, “access to space traditionally requires expendable spacecraft: single-use launch vehicles, satellites, and one-time use capsules designed to maximize performance. Reliance on expendable vehicles has made access to space expensive and exclusive,” DIA’s report explains. “Reusable technologies, while even more difficult and expensive to develop and build, stand to greatly reduce the cost of spaceflight by recovering, refurbishing, and reusing rocket stages, fairings, and capsules.” Chinese spaceplanes, one of which we have not definitively gotten a view of in orbit, look set to become an increasingly important part of this growing ecosystem. Contact the author: joe@twz.com The post U.S. Intel Confirms This Is China’s Secret Spaceplane appeared first on TWZ .

content:
1.4K views · 17 reactions | Real Madrid superstar Kylian Mbappé is at the centre of a controversy in China after a viral video featuring his remarks about a meme depicting him as a Chinese dictator triggered a backlash. Two major Chinese brands, beverage company Dongpeng and dairy giant Mengniu, have announced that they are ending their partnerships with the French footballer. The controversy centres on a clip in which Mbappé reportedly describes a favourite meme as one featuring a 'Chinese dictator'. The footage appears to reference imagery associated with former Chinese leader Mao Zedong, prompting criticism on Chinese social media. The backlash highlights the cultural and political sensitivities surrounding Mao's legacy in China — and the risks international celebrities face when viral jokes collide with national sentiment. Mbappe had previously spoken about memes depicting him as a dictator, saying that while some were intended as humour, comparisons with historical figures responsible for mass suffering were less amusing. From the reaction online to the commercial consequences for two major brands, this is how a meme became a global sports and business controversy. Josh Barnes brings you the story on Firstpost Live. #FirstpostLIVE | Firstpost

# Iron Ore Languishes at Four-Year Lows

in [Commodity News](https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/category/commodities/commodity-news/)27/10/2026

Iron ore futures declined toward CNY 660 per ton on Tuesday, hitting fresh four-year lows amid signs of abundant global supply and a deteriorating demand outlook.

China is entering a seasonally weaker period for steel consumption, while elevated oil prices have heightened concerns about the broader global economic outlook.

World economy reports

Deteriorating profitability among Chinese steelmakers has further weighed on demand expectations, with industry data showing that the blast furnace operating rate across 247 Chinese steel mills stood at 80% last week, down 4.3 percentage points from the same period a year earlier.

On the supply side, shipments from four major iron ore producers, including Rio Tinto Group and BHP Group, are expected to increase by nearly 20 million tons in the fourth quarter, while Guinea’s Simandou mine continues to expand production.
 Source: Trading Economics

# 中国将派驻菲律宾使馆国防武官出席东盟防长扩大会

茉莉花综合报道 2026年10月27日 22:17

中国国防部10月27日在官网宣布，10月29日，中国驻菲律宾使馆国防武官将作为中方代表，出席在菲律宾宿务举行的第13届东盟防长扩大会。国防部说，武官将同各方就坚持对话协商、增进理解互信交换意见，重申坚定支持东盟在区域架构中的中心地位。东盟防长会议和东盟防长扩大会28日至29日在宿务都会区的拉普拉普市举行，由菲律宾国防部长铁欧多洛主持；东盟防长扩大会把东盟的防务对话扩大到澳大利亚、中国、印度、日本、新西兰、韩国、俄罗斯和美国8个对话伙伴。

受影响的有日本：日本防卫大臣小泉进次郎周三起赴菲律宾，计划同美国、菲律宾和韩国的防长举行双边会谈；他27日说，会出席会议到周五。小泉说日本始终对对话持开放态度，但防卫省当时还没有确认中国国防部长董军会不会出席；他对记者说，如果董军出席，他打算就各种问题和关切坦率讨论。去年11月1日在吉隆坡举行东盟防长扩大会期间，小泉同董军谈了约50分钟，这是两人第一次、也是至今唯一一次会谈；小泉当时对中国在东海和太平洋日益加剧的军事活动表示严重关切。日本首相高市早苗近一年前谈到日本可能军事介入台湾危机，此后日中关系转冷。

菲律宾国防部发言人安多隆27日在会前记者会上被问到董军会不会出席时说，菲方已发出邀请，但截至当天上午还没有收到中方确认出席人员。中国外交部发言人郭嘉昆26日被问到中方是否派高级别官员或代表团出席时，没有回答派谁，只说东盟防长扩大会理应为地区国家加强对话、增进互信、推动合作发挥积极作用，“我们反对任何势力公器私用，绑架东盟，搅局生事”。美国战争部长赫格塞斯预定28日访问菲律宾；安多隆说，美菲将举行“2+2”会谈。

菲中关系正因南海争议紧张，铁欧多洛多次在国际安全论坛上公开批评中方；安多隆说，南海问题预料仍会列入这次会议的讨论。9月，菲律宾海军曾邀请一艘中国海军军舰参加东盟防长

content:
香港
香港法律周将于11月2日至6日举行，汇聚全球法律专家讨论跨境问题。该活动标志着国际统一私法协会成立一百周年和贸易法委员会成立六十周年。

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

香港法律周定于11月2日至6日举行，汇聚全球法律从业者和其他行业专家，探讨跨境法律问题并加强国际联系。

律政司司长林定国宣布，为期五天的旗舰活动将以法律协同、共建未来为主题。

此次年度聚会恰逢国际统一私法协会 (UNIDROIT) 成立一百周年和联合国国际贸易法委员会 (UNCITRAL) 成立 60 周年，在香港举行的活动期间纪念了这两个全球里程碑。

林指出，香港法律周是一个重要的国际平台，旨在汇集来自不同司法管辖区和专业背景的专业人士。他指出，此次活动旨在让与会者分享经验、建立持久联系并进行建设性对话。
谈及活动发布的宣传片时，林郑月娥强调，各路人物以充满活力的方式抵达香港的形象，象征着世界范围内呼吁全球法律专业人士齐聚一堂，参加一年一度的盛会。

为期五天的课程以每日主题为主题，解决现代跨境互动中出现的实际法律问题。第一天将举行国际统一私法协会亚太区域会议开幕式和亚太联络处开幕式。

随后举行的会议包括第三届亚太国际私法峰会、联合国国际贸易法委员会成立60周年纪念活动等。与会者还将出席第四届互联互通与发展法律论坛、法律科技论坛、第二届粤港澳大湾区律师论坛，内容涵盖国际私法、跨境商贸、科技融合、区域法律合作等领域。

林郑月娥表示，希望与会人士，无论其司法管辖区、专业领域、经验水平如何，都能抓住香港交流的机会，共同构建前瞻性的法治蓝图。

Hong Kong Legal Week will be held 2-6 November, gathering global legal experts to discuss cross-border issues. The event marks UNIDROIT's centenary and UNCITRAL's 60th anniversary.

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

27 Oct 2026 at 19:09 HKT · 2 min read

Hong Kong Legal Week is scheduled to take place from 2 to 6 November, gathering global legal practitioners and other industry specialists to explore cross-border legal issues and strengthen international ties.

Secretary for Justice Paul Lam Ting-kwok announced that the flagship five-day event will be held under the theme of legal synergy and building the future together.

The annual gathering coincides with the centenary of the International Institute for the Unification of Private Law (UNIDROIT) and the 60th anniversary of the United Nations Commission on International Trade Law (UNCITRAL), with both global milestones being commemorated during the programme in Hong Kong.

Lam noted that Hong Kong Legal Week serves as a key international platform designed to bring together professionals from diverse jurisdictions and professional backgrounds. He pointed out that the event aims to enable attendees to share experiences, build lasting connections, and engage in constructive dialogue.

Referring to the promotional video released for the event, Lam highlighted that the imagery of various figures arriving in Hong Kong in a dynamic manner symbolises a worldwide call for global legal professionals to convene and take part in the annual showcase.

The five-day programme features daily themes addressing practical legal issues arising in modern cross-border interactions. Proceedings will commence on the first day with the opening ceremony of the UNIDROIT Regional Conference for the Asia-Pacific and the Opening Ceremony of the Asia-Pacific Liaison Office.

Subsequent sessions include the third Asia-Pacific International Private Law Summit and commemorative activities honouring the 60th anniversary of UNCITRAL. Participants will also attend the fourth Legal Forum on Interconnectivity and Development, the LawTech Forum, and the second Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area Lawyers Forum, covering extensive ground across private international law, cross-border commerce, technology integration, and regional legal cooperation.

Lam expressed hope that participants, regardless of their jurisdictions, areas of expertise, or levels of experience, will seize the opportunity to connect in Hong Kong and jointly construct a forward-looking blueprint for the rule of law.

title: Hong Kong police arrest two drivers in undercover crackdown on cross-border illegal taxi services
zh_title: 香港警方秘密打击跨境非法出租车服务逮捕两名司机
summary: 香港警方在针对社交媒体上宣传的非法跨境出租车服务的卧底行动中逮捕了两名司机。警员冒充乘客预订前往深圳的行程，分别支付港币 950 元和港币 1,050 元的费用，然后拘捕司机，因为司机没有报酬载客 [![图 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), 主编 2026 年 10 月 27 日 19:57 香港时间 · 2 分钟读 香港警方在卧底行动中逮捕了两名司机
content:
香港
香港警方在针对社交媒体上宣传的非法跨境出租车服务的卧底行动中逮捕了两名司机。警员冒充乘客预订前往深圳的行程，并支付港币950元及港币1,050元的费用后，拘捕载客无酬载乘客的司机。

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

香港时间 2026 年 10 月 27 日 19:57 · 阅读时间 2 分钟

香港警方在打击跨境非法出租车服务（即“白牌”汽车）的卧底行动中逮捕了两名司机。港岛总区交通部及管制组特遣队高级督察施思豪表示，10 月 27 日，一名 33 岁的本地司机和一名 27 岁的持有双向许可证的中国内地司机被拘留。

警方表示，非法服务中介利用各种社交媒体平台招募乘客，提供豪华七座车，从香港经陆路边境检查站前往中国内地城市。警察冒充乘客联系了两个社交媒体账户，请求前往深圳。账户报价分别为港币950元及港币1,050元，需于出发前将全额车费存入指定电子钱包。
缴付车费后，执法人员于行动当日登上两辆香港注册、挂有跨境车牌的豪华七座车。旅程开始后，警方透露了他们的身份并逮捕了两名司机。当地司机涉嫌无证载客取酬、无第三方保险驾驶。该内地司机还涉嫌违反逗留条件。两人仍被拘留接受调查，警方不排除进一步逮捕的可能性。两辆车被扣押接受检查。

警方提醒公众，仅使用有执照的公共交通工具，切勿乘坐非法营运的车辆以获取报酬。他们警告说，如果车辆被用于非法出租，第三方保险可能会失效，从而使乘客和其他道路使用者在发生事故时得不到保护。司机们被敦促不要从事非法出租或带报酬活动。首次定罪可处以最高 10,000 港元罚款及六个月监禁，而第二次定罪可处以最高 25,000 港元罚款及最高一年监禁。被定罪的司机将面临至少 12 个月至最多 3 年的驾驶资格取消，并且他们的车辆执照可能会被吊销。
警方补充，如果涉案车辆属于跨境车辆，运输署将吊销其通行许可证（跨境许可证）。如果涉及中国大陆司机，警方将调查他们是否从事非法就业或违反其他法律，包括停留条件。证据充分就会导致起诉。警方指出，内地执法部门严格规范车辆运营和有偿出租活动。在内地非法营运的司机也将面临调查和检控，警方呼吁所有司机切勿心存侥幸或违法。

[![图片3：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

主编

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong
Hong Kong police arrested two drivers in an undercover operation targeting illegal cross-border taxi services advertised on social media. Officers posing as passengers booked trips to Shenzhen, paying fees of HK$950 and HK$1,050 before arresting the drivers for carrying passengers for reward without

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

27 Oct 2026 at 19:57 HKT · 2 min read

Hong Kong police have arrested two drivers in an undercover operation against cross-border illegal taxi services, known as “white plate” cars. A 33-year-old local driver and a 27-year-old mainland Chinese driver holding a two-way permit were detained on 27 October, according to Senior Inspector Sze Sze-ho of the港島總區交通部執行及管制組特遣隊 (Hong Kong Island Regional Traffic Division Enforcement and Control Group Taskforce).

Police said intermediaries for the illegal services used various social media platforms to recruit passengers, offering luxury seven-seater vehicles to travel from Hong Kong to cities in mainland China via land border checkpoints. Officers posed as passengers and contacted two social media accounts requesting trips to Shenzhen. The accounts quoted prices of HK$950 and HK$1,050 respectively, requiring the full fare to be deposited into designated e-wallets before departure.

After the fares were deposited, officers boarded two Hong Kong-registered luxury seven-seater vehicles bearing cross-border number plates on the day of the operation. Once the journeys began, police revealed their identities and arrested both drivers. The local driver was suspected of carrying passengers for reward without a licence and driving without third-party insurance. The mainland driver was additionally suspected of breaching his stay conditions. Both remain in custody for investigation, and police did not rule out further arrests. The two vehicles were seized for examination.

Police reminded the public to use only licensed public transport and not to take vehicles operating illegally for reward. They warned that third-party insurance could be invalidated if a vehicle is used for illegal hire, leaving passengers and other road users unprotected in the event of an accident. Drivers were urged not to engage in illegal hire or reward-carrying activities. A first conviction carries a fine of up to HK$10,000 and six months in jail, while a second conviction can result in a fine of HK$25,000 and up to one year’s imprisonment. Convicted drivers face disqualification from driving for a minimum of 12 months and up to three years, and their vehicle licences may be revoked.

Police added that if the vehicles involved are cross-border vehicles, the Transport Department will revoke their通行許可證 (cross-border permits). Where mainland Chinese drivers are involved, police will investigate whether they are engaged in illegal employment or have breached other laws, including stay conditions. Sufficient evidence would lead to prosecution. Police noted that mainland law enforcement authorities strictly regulate vehicle operations and hire-for-reward activities. Drivers operating illegally on the mainland would also face investigation and prosecution, and police urged all drivers not to take chances or break the law.

title: International Gas Union to hold first Hong Kong summit on 29 October
zh_title: 国际天然气联盟将于10月29日在香港举行首次峰会
summary: 香港 国际天然气联盟（IGU）将于10月29日首次在香港举行2026年理事会会议及峰会，云集超过400名能源专家。该活动将重点关注亚太天然气市场增长、能源转型和绿色金融。 [![图片 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编 2026 年 10 月 27 日 21:03 HKT · 2 分钟阅读《国际天然气》联盟 (IGU) 即将召开 2026 年理事会会议并“赋能可持续未来”
content:
香港
国际天然气联盟（IGU）将于10月29日首次在香港举行2026年理事会会议及峰会，云集超过400名能源专家。该活动将重点关注亚太天然气市场增长、能源转型和绿色金融。

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

2026 年 10 月 27 日 21:03 香港时间 · 阅读时间 2 分钟

随着亚洲天然气市场的增长，国际天然气联盟 (IGU) 首次在香港举行 2026 年理事会会议和“赋能可持续未来”峰会。此次峰会将于 10 月 29 日举行，来自世界各地的 400 多名能源专家、行业领袖和政策制定者将齐聚一堂，就亚太地区及其他地区的技术创新和投资机会交换意见。

IGU 主席 Andrea Stegher 表示，IGU 的成员遍布 70 多个国家，代表着一个服务于全球约四分之一能源需求的行业。他强调，天然气不仅是一种能源，也是化肥和药品的关键投入。 “亚洲是不断增长的能源计划的一部分，不仅仅是天然气，但天然气肯定可以发挥作用，特别是当我们看到煤炭在全球这一地区的能源结构中仍然发挥着重要作用时，”他说。
当被问及为什么该组织选择香港举办此次活动时，斯蒂格表示，香港提供了罕见的高密度生活与成熟的人造燃气系统相结合的案例，使其有机会了解如何将当前的交付与持续的创新相结合。主办机构中华煤气董事总经理黄伟仪表示，随着亚洲天然气市场不断增长，IGU成员希望探索亚洲天然气行业，寻找更多机会。

峰会将探讨四个核心主题：亚太和中国天然气市场发展、亚洲能源转型战略路线图以及利用绿色金融支持可持续能源基础设施。黄说，香港能源转型的核心是以天然气替代煤炭，并补充说，中华电力和港灯两家电力公司也在使用天然气替代煤炭发电。他表示，港华煤气正在研究低碳天然气，并探索使用其3,700公里管网中的低碳氢气。
黄还列举了2006年与一家澳大利亚供应商签订的为期25年的长期天然气合同，当时的价格是固定的，他估计过去20年为香港客户节省了约250亿港元。关于地缘政治紧张局势，斯蒂格表示，中东海湾的中断不是供应问题，而是供应链问题，影响了全球约3%的天然气需求，主要是一些亚洲市场。他表示，全球新能源生产设施在很大程度上抵消了损失，使天然气系统保持弹性。

[![图片3：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong
The International Gas Union (IGU) will hold its 2026 Council Meeting and summit in Hong Kong for the first time on 29 October, bringing together over 400 energy experts. The event will focus on Asia-Pacific gas market growth, energy transition, and green finance.

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

27 Oct 2026 at 21:03 HKT · 2 min read

The International Gas Union (IGU) is holding its 2026 Council Meeting and “Empowering a Sustainable Future” Summit in Hong Kong for the first time, as the Asian gas market grows. The summit, to be held on 29 October, will bring together more than 400 energy experts, industry leaders, and policymakers from around the world to exchange views on technological innovations and investment opportunities across Asia-Pacific and beyond.

IGU president Andrea Stegher said the IGU, with members in more than 70 countries, represents an industry serving about one-quarter of global energy needs. He highlighted that gas is not only an energy source but also a key input for fertilisers and medicines. “Asia is part of the growing energy schemes, not just for gas, but gas for sure can play a role, especially when we look at the important role coal still has in the energy mix in this part of the globe,” he said.

When asked why the organisation chose Hong Kong to host the event, Stegher said the city offers a rare case of high-density living combined with a mature manufactured gas system, giving it a chance to see how current delivery can be combined with ongoing innovation. Peter Wong Wai-yee, managing director of Towngas, the host organisation, said IGU members want to explore Asia’s natural gas sector to find more opportunities, as the Asian natural gas market is growing.

The summit will examine four core themes: Asia-Pacific and China’s natural gas market developments, strategic roadmaps for Asia’s energy transition, and leveraging green finance to support sustainable energy infrastructure. Wong said Hong Kong’s energy transition is centred on replacing coal with natural gas, adding that two electricity companies, CLP Power and HK Electric, are also using natural gas to replace coal in power generation. He said Towngas is researching lower-carbon gas and is exploring the use of low-carbon hydrogen from its 3,700-kilometre pipeline network.

Wong also cited a 25-year long-term gas contract signed with an Australian supplier in 2006, with prices fixed at the time, which he estimated had saved Hong Kong customers about HK$25 billion over the past 20 years. On geopolitical tensions, Stegher said disruption in the Middle East Gulf is not a supply issue but a supply-chain issue, affecting about three per cent of global gas demand, mainly in some Asian markets. He said new energy production facilities worldwide had largely offset the losses, leaving the gas system resilient.

title: Hong Kong to host Consensus flagship conference for three years from 2027
zh_title: 香港将从 2027 年起连续三年举办共识旗舰会议
summary: 香港 由香港旅游发展局和 CoinDesk 合作，香港将于 2027 年至 2029 年主办 Consensus 数字资产和人工智能会议。该交易旨在提升香港的创新中心地位并吸引高价值商务访客。 [![图片 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编 2026 年 10 月 27 日 21:21 HKT · 3 分钟阅读香港将连续三年主办Consensus全球数字资产与人工智能大会
content:
香港
香港旅游发展局与 CoinDesk 合作，将于 2027 年至 2029 年在香港主办 Consensus 数字资产和人工智能会议。该交易旨在提升香港的创新中心地位并吸引高价值商务访客。

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

香港时间 2026 年 10 月 27 日 21:21 · 阅读时间 3 分钟

香港旅游发展局（HKTB）与 CoinDesk 于 10 月 27 日签署战略合作伙伴关系后，香港将于 2027 年至 2029 年连续三年主办 Consensus 全球数字资产和人工智能大会。

根据谅解备忘录，这一亚洲旗舰盛会将继续在香港举行，首先是 2 月 1 日至 3 日在香港会议展览中心举行的“Consensus Hong Kong 2027”。此次合作旨在巩固香港作为国际金融和创新中心的地位，同时吸引高价值的会议、展览和商务访客。

Consensus 会议最初于 2025 年在香港首次亮相，并于 2026 年回归。这项为期三年的新协议巩固了香港作为该会议亚洲旗舰版的永久举办地的地位，汇聚了金融科技、Web3 和新兴领域的国际政策制定者、机构投资者、企业家、科技公司和初创企业。
Consensus Hong Kong 主席 Michael Lau 表示，自在香港举办以来，该会议得到了业界的大力参与。他表示，香港拥有得天独厚的商业环境、发达的基础设施、与中国内地和国际市场的直接联系，是举办峰会的天然基地。刘补充道，随着数字资产和人工智能日益融合，未来版本将把人工智能与区块链和数字金融一起作为核心主题。他表示相信，在未来三届中与旅游部门的密切合作将鼓励跨界别合作，并提升香港作为亚洲首要创新中心的声誉。

该协议在香港会议展览中心正式签署，香港旅游发展局执行董事刘镇镇及刘敏华在该文件上签署。仪式由旅发局主席林建岳博士、CoinDesk 母公司 Bullish Group 机构销售总监 Sean Whipkey 以及来自旅游、金融科技和科技领域的业界代表共同见证。
旅游官员强调，这一多年合作伙伴关系代表了国际数字经济对香港制度优势投下的强有力的信任票。林博士表示，Consensus Hong Kong不仅仅是一个行业会议，更是跨境合作和商业交流的重要平台。他强调，汇聚来自金融科技、Web3和数字资产领域的全球领导人，可以加强香港作为中国内地与全球市场之间超级联系人的作用。他补充说，高消费商务旅客的涌入将为当地酒店、餐饮店、零售企业和专业服务提供商带来巨大的溢出效益。

除了主要会议议程外，前几届香港共识还促成了超过 350 场会外活动

Hong Kong will host the Consensus digital asset and AI conference from 2027 to 2029 under a partnership between the Hong Kong Tourism Board and CoinDesk. The deal aims to boost Hong Kong's innovation hub status and attract high-value business visitors.

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

27 Oct 2026 at 21:21 HKT · 3 min read

Hong Kong will host the Consensus global digital asset and artificial intelligence conference for three consecutive years from 2027 to 2029, following a strategic partnership signed between the Hong Kong Tourism Board (HKTB) and CoinDesk on 27 October.

Under the Memorandum of Understanding, the flagship Asian gathering will continue to be staged in the city, beginning with Consensus Hong Kong 2027 at the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre from 1 to 3 February. The collaboration is designed to reinforce Hong Kong's standing as an international financial and innovation hub while attracting high-value convention, exhibition, and business visitors.

Consensus initially debuted in Hong Kong in 2025 before returning in 2026. The new three-year agreement solidifies Hong Kong as the permanent home of the conference's Asian flagship edition, bringing together international policymakers, institutional investors, entrepreneurs, technology firms, and startups across fintech, Web3, and emerging sectors.

Consensus Hong Kong Chairman Michael Lau said the conference had received strong industry engagement since its local launch. He said Hong Kong offered an advantageous commercial environment, well-developed infrastructure, and direct links to mainland China and international markets, making the city a natural base for the annual summit. Lau added that as digital assets and artificial intelligence increasingly converge, future editions will incorporate artificial intelligence as a core theme alongside blockchain and digital finance. He expressed confidence that working closely with tourism authorities over the next three editions would encourage cross-sector collaboration and enhance Hong Kong's reputation as a premier innovation hub in Asia.

The agreement was formalised at the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre, where HKTB Executive Director Anthony Lau and Michael Lau signed the document. The ceremony was witnessed by HKTB Chairman Dr Peter Lam and Sean Whipkey, institutional sales director of CoinDesk's parent company Bullish Group, alongside industry delegates from the tourism, fintech, and technology sectors.

Tourism officials highlighted that the multi-year partnership represents a strong vote of confidence from the international digital economy in Hong Kong's institutional strengths. Dr Lam said that Consensus Hong Kong serves as a vital platform for cross-border cooperation and commercial exchange rather than merely an industry conference. He emphasised that convening global leaders from the fintech, Web3, and digital asset sectors strengthens Hong Kong's role as a super-connector between mainland China and global markets. He added that the influx of high-spending business travellers would generate significant spillover benefits for local hotels, food and beverage outlets, retail businesses, and professional service providers.

Beyond the main conference programme, previous editions of Consensus Hong Kong have catalysed over 350 side events across the city, including investment forums, networking gatherings, and startup showcases. The tourism board expects the extended partnership to sustain this momentum, further elevating Hong Kong's profile as a premier destination for major international conventions and technological exchange.

summary: 香港 香港国际美酒展将于 11 月 5 日至 7 日回归，吸引来自 25 个国家的 620 多家参展商。该活动由香港贸发局主办，重点展示新兴葡萄酒产区、中国白酒品牌，以及香港在进出口额不断上升的情况下作为全球贸易中心的角色。 [![图片 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编 2026 年 10 月 27 日 22:44 HKT · 2 分钟阅读《香港报》国际葡萄酒及烈酒博览会将于 5 日至 7 日回归

香港
香港国际美酒展将于 11 月 5 日至 7 日回归，吸引来自 25 个国家的 620 多家参展商。该活动由香港贸发局主办，重点展示新兴葡萄酒产区、中国白酒品牌，以及香港在进出口额不断上升的情况下作为全球贸易中心的角色。

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

香港时间 2026 年 10 月 27 日 22:44 · 阅读时间 2 分钟

香港国际美酒展将于11月5日至7日回归，为全球买家提供一站式采购平台，重点关注新兴葡萄酒产区和中国顶级白酒品牌。今届展会由香港贸易发展局（香港贸发局）主办，云集超过25个国家及地区超过620家参展商，展示来自全球超过40个原产地的葡萄酒、烈酒、清酒、啤酒、低酒精及无酒精饮料及相关产品。

其中一大亮点是烈酒世界专区的回归，共有来自16个国家和地区的参展商，其中包括来自墨西哥、葡萄牙、斯洛伐克和英国的首次参展。在葡萄酒方面，来自格鲁吉亚和意大利卡拉布里亚地区的展馆将首次亮相，为买家提供发现反映其独特传统的独特葡萄酒的机会。
香港贸发局联席总裁林玉峰强调香港的独特优势，包括自由港地位、世界一流的物流基础设施、资本自由流动以及连接中国内地与全球市场的战略地位。林郑月娥表示，今年首8个月，香港葡萄酒进口额同比增长16%，出口额同比增长8%。受惠于酒类关税下调及市场需求增加，2025年烈酒进口量按年增加逾5%，预计进口额将增加近1亿港元。

林郑月娥补充说，葡萄酒及烈酒贸易的发展也将为相关行业带来机遇，包括物流、零售、仓储、餐饮、旅游和投资。本届展会还凸显了香港作为内地与世界各地的“超级联系人”和“超级增值者”的作用，支持葡萄酒及烈酒行业高质量发展。
白酒成为本届展会最强的品类之一，“中国十大白酒品牌”将齐聚今年的展会，其中包括贵州茅台和洋河等知名品牌。凭借香港作为国际葡萄酒及烈酒贸易中心的独特地位，参展的白酒生产商正利用展会作为开拓海外市场的平台，加速白酒的全球扩张、复兴和多元化。来自新疆、宁夏、西藏等中国主要葡萄酒产区的参展商将向国际买家展示他们的产品，展示内地国内葡萄酒行业不断增长的潜力。

展会的公共区域“周六嘉年华”将于活动最后一天向18岁或以上的葡萄酒爱好者开放。它将为公众提供品尝和购买全球葡萄酒和烈酒以及参与一系列互动主题活动的机会。

Hong Kong
The Hong Kong International Wine & Spirits Fair returns from 5-7 November, featuring over 620 exhibitors from 25 countries. Organised by HKTDC, the event highlights emerging wine regions, Chinese baijiu brands, and Hong Kong’s role as a global trading hub, amid rising import and export values.

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

27 Oct 2026 at 22:44 HKT · 2 min read

The Hong Kong International Wine & Spirits Fair is set to return from 5 to 7 November, serving as a one-stop sourcing platform for global buyers and spotlighting emerging wine regions and top Chinese baijiu brands. Organised by the Hong Kong Trade Development Council (HKTDC), this year's fair will bring together more than 620 exhibitors from over 25 countries and regions, showcasing wines, spirits, sake, beer, low- and no-alcohol beverages and related products from more than 40 places of origin worldwide.

A major highlight is the return of the World of Spirits zone, featuring exhibitors from 16 countries and regions, including first-time participants from Mexico, Portugal, Slovakia and the United Kingdom. On the wine front, pavilions from Georgia and Italy’s Calabria region will make their debut, offering buyers an opportunity to discover distinctive wines that reflect their unique heritage.

Smilely Lam Yuk-fung, associate executive director of the HKTDC, highlighted Hong Kong’s unique advantages, including its free-port status, world-class logistics infrastructure, free flow of capital, and its strategic position connecting Mainland China with global markets. Lam noted that the city recorded a year-on-year increase in wine import value of 16 per cent and export value of 8 per cent in the first eight months of the year. Spirits import volumes increased by more than 5 per cent year on year in 2025, benefiting from a reduction in liquor duty and growing market demand, with the import value expected to rise by nearly HK$100 million.

The development of the wine and spirits trade would also generate opportunities for related industries including logistics, retail, warehousing, catering, tourism and investment, Lam added. The fair also highlights Hong Kong’s role as a “super-connector” and “super-value-adder” between the mainland and the rest of the world, supporting the high-quality development of the wine and spirits industry.

Baijiu stands out as one of the fair's strongest categories, as the “Top 10 Chinese Baijiu Brands” will converge at this year's fair, including renowned names such as Kweichow Moutai and Yanghe. Leveraging Hong Kong's unique position as an international wine and spirits trading hub, participating baijiu producers are using the fair as a platform to develop markets overseas and accelerate baijiu's global expansion, rejuvenation and diversification. Exhibitors from major Chinese wine-producing regions, including Xinjiang, Ningxia and Xizang, will showcase their products to international buyers, demonstrating the growing potential of the mainland's domestic wine industry.

The fair's public zone, Saturday Fiesta, will open to wine enthusiasts aged 18 or above on the final day of the event. It will offer the public an opportunity to sample and purchase global wines and spirits, as well as participate in a series of interactive thematic activities.
