title: Royal Navy Lacks Ships, Capabilities to Defend High North from Russia, Says U.K. Committee Report - USNI News
zh_title: 英国委员会报告称，英国皇家海军缺乏舰艇和防御俄罗斯高北地区的能力 - USNI 新闻
summary: 北约于 2026 年 10 月 26 日发布的北约常备海事大队 (SNMG1) 观察到的一艘位于高北地区的俄罗斯基洛级潜艇。 北约照片 两党下议院国防委员会周四警告称，英国皇家海军目前缺乏保卫高北地区免受俄罗斯侵害所需的舰艇和能力。在周四发布的[“高北防御”报告](https://news.usni.org/2026/10/22/u-k-committee-report-on-defense-in-the-high-north)中，该委员会称皇家海军正受到造船延误、维护积压和潜艇日益萎缩的困扰。
content:
北约第一常备海事大队 (SNMG1) 观察到的北约高北地区的一艘俄罗斯基洛级潜艇，北约于 2026 年 10 月 26 日发布。北约照片

英国下议院防务委员会周四警告称，英国皇家海军目前缺乏保卫高北地区免受俄罗斯侵害所需的舰艇和能力。

在周四发布的[“高北防御”报告](https://news.usni.org/2026/10/22/u-k-committee-report-on-defense-in-the-high-north)中，该委员会描述英国皇家海军受到造船延误、维护积压和潜艇部队萎缩的困扰。

“英国需要愿意面对一个残酷的事实：它目前并不具备在高北地区成功行动的所有能力。俄罗斯潜艇和在高北地区的破坏力量对北大西洋和英国构成了直接风险，包括核威慑力量。尽管如此，英国国防部已经接受了反潜战方面存在的严重差距。公开的证据表明驱逐舰、护卫舰和攻击潜艇的可用性较低，这让人质疑英国是否能够履行其在高北地区的承诺。高北地区”，国防委员会主席兼议会工党议员 Tan Dhesi 说道。
该报告将 2030 年作为英国做好军事准备以阻止或击败俄罗斯威胁的最后期限，并援引时任首相基尔·斯塔默 (Keir Starmer) 6 月份的声明称，根据英国及其盟国情报部门的评估，俄罗斯最早可能在 2030 年对北约发起攻击。

“如果英国政府言出必行——俄罗斯最早可以在 2030 年攻击北约——那么纠正这些漏洞的工作就不可能很快开始，”德西说。

6 月份发布的英国国防投资计划承诺在未来四年内投资 2980 亿英镑（3979 亿美元），到 2030 年国防支出将达到国内生产总值 (GDP) 的 2.7%。该委员会注意到北约起草的一份内部文件，该文件旨在衡量成员国履行重整军备承诺的有效性。根据委员会的报告，英国在 32 个联盟国家中排名第 31 位。

2026 年 10 月 9 日，英国皇家海军龙号驶入朴茨茅斯陛下海军基地。英国国防部照片

委员会报告中写道：“只有冰岛这个没有军事能力的国家排名较低。”
英国皇家海军的反潜战护卫舰和核动力潜艇对俄罗斯在高北地区的活动具有最大的威慑力，但由于维护问题，它们都已经老化或无法使用。此外，英国皇家海军于 2010 年提出了建立一支由 6 艘驱逐舰和 13 艘护卫舰组成的舰队的要求，但一直难以满足这一要求。目前的舰队由六艘 45 型驱逐舰和五艘 23 型护卫舰组成——仅是 19 艘舰艇舰队需求的一半。

报告中写道：“尽管新护卫舰最终将加入足够数量的舰队，但目前的舰队战备状况令人怀疑英国能否在 2030 年之前维持高北地区所需的海上任务。”

对于高北地区所需的能力特别重要的是，13 艘护卫舰中的 8 艘需要配备声纳 2087 拖曳阵列以进行反潜战行动。拖曳阵列是当前

【原文 English Original】
A Russian Kilo-class submarine in the High North, observed by Standing NATO Maritime Group 1 (SNMG1), released by NATO on Oct. 26, 2026. NATO photo

The Royal Navy currently lacks the ships and capabilities needed to defend the High North from Russia, the bipartisan House of Commons Defense Committee warned on Thursday.

In its[“Defense in the High North” report](https://news.usni.org/2026/10/22/u-k-committee-report-on-defense-in-the-high-north) issued on Thursday, the committee described the Royal Navy as being plagued by shipbuilding delays, maintenance backlogs and an atrophying submarine force.

“The U.K. needs to be willing to address a hard truth: it does not currently have all the capabilities to operate successfully in the High North. Russian submarine and sabotage forces in the High North pose direct risks to the North Atlantic and the U.K., including the nuclear deterrent. Despite this, the Ministry of Defense has accepted a serious anti-submarine warfare gap. Publicly available evidence of low availability among destroyers, frigates and attack submarines calls into question whether the U.K. can meet its commitments in the High North,” [said Tan Dhesi](https://committees.parliament.uk/committee/24/defence-committee/news/218377/report-glaring-capability-gaps-in-high-north-leave-uk-vulnerable/), chair of the defense committee and a Labor Party member of Parliament.

The report put 2030 as the deadline for the U.K. to be militarily ready to deter or defeat a Russian threat, citing then-Prime Minister Keir Starmer’s statement in June that there could be an attack by Russia on NATO as soon as 2030, according to an assessment by the U.K. and allied intelligence services.

“If the U.K. government means what it says – that Russia could attack NATO as soon as 2030 – then work to rectify these vulnerabilities cannot start soon enough,” Dhesi said.

The U.K. Defense Investment Plan released in June committed to investing £298 billion – $397.9 billion – across the next four years to reach 2.7 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) spent on defense by 2030. The committee noted an internal document drawn up by NATO to measure how effectively members are meeting their rearmament promises. The U.K. was at number 31 out of 32 Alliance countries, according to the committee report.

HMS Dragon sails into His Majesty’s Naval Base Portsmouth on Oct. 9, 2026. UK Ministry of Defense photo

“Only Iceland, a country with no military capability, is lower on the table,” reads the committee report.

The Royal Navy’s anti-submarine warfare frigates and nuclear-powered submarines offer the greatest deterrent to Russian activities in the High North, however both are aging or unavailable due to maintenance issues. Additionally, the Royal Navy established in 2010 a requirement for a fleet of six destroyers and 13 frigates but has struggled to meet this requirement. The current fleet consists of six Type 45 destroyers and five Type 23 frigates – barely half of the requirement for a 19 ship fleet.

“Although new frigates will eventually join the fleet in sufficient numbers, the current fleet readiness picture raises doubts about whether the U.K. could sustain the maritime tasks required in the High North by 2030,” reads the report.

Particularly critical to the capabilities needed in the High North is the requirement for eight of the 13 frigates to be fitted with the Sonar 2087 towed array to undertake anti-submarine warfare operations. The towed array is currently on all the remaining five Type 23s.

The slow construction and delivery of the Type 26s has led to a capability gap in the Royal Navy’s ASW frigate numbers. The first-in-class Type 26 was laid down in 2017 and is scheduled to be accepted in 2027. Eight Type 26 frigates will take over the ASW role in the future with five Type 31 general purpose ships making up the remaining frigate requirement.

The ASW frigates could be as low as five for the next three years, according to the committee. Two of the under construction Royal Navy Type 26s will be sold to meet Norway’s 2025 order – to be in service by 2039 – which means the Royal Navy won’t meet its eight ASW frigate requirement until 2037.

The Defense Committee recommended that no more Type 23s should leave service until they are replaced on a one-for-one basis by the Type 26.

Tugs spray water as aircraft carrier HMS Prince of Wales (R09) approaches Rounds Tower in England, Nov. 30, 2025. Royal Navy photo

The Royal Navy has also faced challenges in maintaining its destroyers, aircraft carriers, amphibious ships and submarines, all of which can provide military capabilities useful for High North operations, the Defense Committee said.

Both the Royal Navy’s Queen Elizabeth-class carriers broke down in 2022 and 2024 due to propeller shaft issues. The Royal Navy’s two specialist amphibious assault ships were decommissioned in November of 2024 ahead of their planned inactivation dates of 2033 and 2034. The U.K. and the Netherlands have since signed a contract to procure a fleet of four amphibious vessels each, but these are unlikely to be in service until the 2030s.

Destroyer HMS _Dragon_ (D35) was pulled out of maintenance in March to deploy to Cyprus to defend against drone attacks.

“The fact that no other destroyer was ready to deploy from the fleet of Type 45 vessels may reflect the lack of deployable ships. As these platforms provide air defense, they would be equally important in any High North operation,” said the Defense Committee.

In addition, all five Astute-class nuclear attack submarines were all recently tied up in dockyards at the same time, with none deployed. The Defense Committee also pointed to the atrophying of the Royal Navy’s submarine capability and questioned its ability to operate under the ice.

Astute-class nuclear submarine HMS Ambush. UK Royal Navy photo

“Without a credible under-ice capability, the U.K. is less able to contest Russian freedom of action in the High North and risks being forced into a more defensive posture. Russia can then use the ice to conceal and protect its own submarines, while threatening NATO sea lanes, U.K. critical infrastructure and the nuclear deterrent,” said the Defense Committee.

The report recommended that the government provide the Defense Committee with a plan outlining how the Ministry of Defense will improve the availability of the Royal Navy’s frigates, destroyers and attack submarines before 2030. This update may be presented at a classified level, but the committee will expect a version to be publicly available.

The Defense Committee report calls for the government to brief its progress to re-establish an under-ice capability for at least some of the Astute-class submarines.

Regarding the U.K.’s Hybrid Navy program, the committee said it is not convinced that the £1.3 billion – or $1.7 billion USD – allocated for the program will be sufficient. While the committee encourages the pursuit of naval exports, it said the government needs to ensure that the exports did not compete with the U.K.’s own requirements for scarce ships, systems and skilled labor.

The allocated funds cover the procurement of five vessel types – the Type 91 uncrewed missile platform, Type 92 uncrewed sloop with underwater sensors, Type 93 extra-large uncrewed underwater vessels (XLUUVs), Type 94 uncrewed radar platforms and a future class of crewed Common Combat Vessels (CCV). The report calls on the government to set out the basis on which it judges the current funding allocation to be adequate.

The Defense Committee said that defense exports can strengthen the U.K.’s position in the High North when they help closely aligned allies field capabilities that are interoperable with the Royal Navy and are suited to northern operations. The Type 26 agreement with Norway could expand NATO’s ASW capacity on the northern flank and deepen U.K.-Norwegian operational and industrial integration. However, the report said export success must not come at the expense of the Royal Navy’s own Type 26 frigate delivery timelines.

“The government must ensure that naval exports expand industrial capacity and allied capability, rather than competing with U.K. requirements for scarce ships, systems and skilled labor,” reads the Defense Committee report.

In contrast, the committee said the Royal Marines capabilities for High North operations were excellent, due to its expertise from regular deployments to Northern Norway, logistic capabilities and the Commando Helicopter Force. However, the Royal Marines can’t compensate for the naval platforms’ shortfalls.

title: Grass is far more than the lawn you lounge on
summary: Watching grass grow is supposed to be what you do when every other possibility for entertainment has been exhausted. Craig Morris made a career of it. The surprising thing, once you listen to him, is that the rest of us have managed to find
content:
Watching grass grow is supposed to be what you do when every other possibility for entertainment has been exhausted. Craig Morris made a career of it. The surprising thing, once you listen to him, is that the rest of us have managed to find grass boring.

We walk over it, mow it, feed it to livestock and occasionally set it alight. We admire it when it resembles a billiard table and complain when it gets ideas above its station. A flower-filled patch becomes neglected. A chemically assisted green rectangle becomes a garden achievement.

Morris, a grassland ecologist, would like us to get down on our knees and reconsider.

His fascination began as a schoolboy in the Cathedral Peak area of the Drakensberg, surrounded by a sea of grass beneath the mountains. Learning to identify a few species led to discovering that grassland science was something one could actually study.

Research in high mountain grasslands deepened the attachment. He remembers a landscape so unfamiliar it brought to mind the worlds at the top of Enid Blyton’s The Magic Faraway Tree.

“It was a magical place to spend a couple of years collecting data, so that really entrenched my love of grasslands and open ecosystems, as they call them now.”

An early scientific lesson was more unsettling. When grazing animals were removed from a long-running experiment, he found “there was rapid and irreversible change”. Taking away disturbance was itself a disturbance. Leaving a grassland alone, he discovered, does not necessarily preserve it.

To understand why, first meet the grass.

What looks like a flimsy tuft is, in Morris’ account, a well-equipped survivor. Its growing points sit “right down near the soil surface”, protected from grazing mouths and flames. Buds supply replacement shoots, called tillers, which carry the potential for further shoots.

“So you’ve got a whole set of modular units that can regrow and create more,” he explains.

Craig Morris. (Photo: Supplied / Source)

Bite it, burn it or mow it and the plant can rebuild from below the damage. That, Morris explains, is central to its persistence. Anyone pulling grass from between paving stones may already suspect they are up against a formidable opponent.

Its success extends to our dinner plates. Wheat, rice, maize, sugar cane and bamboo are all grasses, as Morris confirms.

“Most people eat grass every day.” We are “grass eaters and then eaters of eaters of grass”.

Your cereal is grass. So is the source of the sugar you perhaps should not have added. Eat beef and you have simply lengthened the supply chain.

Morris mentions writer Michael Pollan’s suggestion that plants have recruited _us_ to further their interests. “We even grow these fantastic lawns, we spend millions on it, we create stadiums around it,” he says.

For an organism without a brain, grass has acquired an impressive maintenance department.

But now Morris wants us to look between the tufts.

“What you’ll really notice is in between the grasses are all the wild flowers.”

These and other herbaceous plants, known as forbs, account for much of a grassland’s plant diversity, he explains. They feed pollinators, provide food for grazing animals and include medicinal plants. They’re not decorative extras scattered through the real business of producing cattle feed.

The diversity of grassland flowers is extraordinary. (Photo: Craig Morris)

And the view changes as you move.

“When you look at the next-door square metre, you get different sets,” he says. Understanding that patchiness is important to how a grassland is managed.

Then there is the part we cannot see.

Morris describes an underground world of roots, bulbs, tubers and rhizomes, where plants maintain reserves against difficult times.

“Grassland soils are a really good store of carbon,” he says. Some organic matter becomes strongly attached to minerals. “That’s not easy for the microbes to get at. So, that’s a more permanent store.”

Fungi’s mycorrhizal filaments add another layer of activity.

“They connect to grasses and extend their root system far and so wide.” In exchange for carbon from plants, Morris explains, the fungi supply nutrients. The apparently simple surface conceals an underground economy.

It also conceals age. Morris describes ancient communities whose plants keep renewing themselves, sometimes through clonal growth or persistent underground organs.

“How old is a grass plant? That’s a question that needs to be answered.” For some underground structures, dating is difficult: “We don’t know, because they don’t have tree rings.” New leaves don’t mean a new plant. They clone, so they could be eternal.

That’s why he objects to treating grasslands as unfinished forests, awaiting an enthusiastic person with a spade and some saplings.

“It’s worth being grassland. Should be grassland,” he says.

Fire helps explain why. Morris describes how burning removes accumulated old growth and lets light reach new shoots. “They’re almost like farmers of fire,” he says of grasses. “They use disturbance, also like grazing, to entrench their position and gain advantage.

“I’m not going to call it a disturbance any more because it’s part of the grassland rhythm.”

That doesn’t mean burning everywhere. Morris distinguishes fire-dependent grasslands from drier systems requiring different management. But suppressing fire can have dramatic consequences, as long-running experiments show.

In unburnt plots, “the grass is almost gone, you’ve just got trees”. His conclusion is blunt: “The removal of fire, removal of disturbance is effectively destroying the grassland.”

Grazing demands care too. His research points to damage when repeated trampling destroys wildflower leaves before plants replenish their underground reserves.

Much of southern and Central Africa is rolling savanna, supporting millions of herbivores. (Photo: Craig Morris)

“You don’t need to trample a good intact grassland. You shouldn’t do that relentlessly year after year.”

Which brings us to the suburban lawn, that small kingdom in which almost everything must be the same height.

Morris has little affection for the manicured ideal. Asked whether it’s the opposite of the variety he values, his reply is emphatic: “Exactly the opposite.”

“We should manage grassland to create patchiness,” he explains. Birds, for example, have different requirements: “Some need long grass to nest in, some like the short grass to feed.

“You need that patchiness to cater for a whole variety of biodiversity.”

His own garden reinforced the lesson. As he watched, a bare patch beneath a tree, seemingly a failure to grow grass, proved valuable to wildlife. The gardener’s disappointment was another creature’s opportunity.

“You need those bare parts of your lawn,” he says. “You need a habitat if you want wildlife in the gardens.”

For Morris, the guiding principle is simple: “You don’t want uniformity. You want variation.”

The public’s great misunderstanding is contained in two words: just grass. After talking to Morris, they seem a remarkably small description for an ancient, busy, partly buried world on which we all depend. **DM**

title: SA Rights Commission urges stronger laws to protect children online
summary: The law and institutions of South Africa were built for an earlier era of technology, and children are carrying the cost of the delay in reform. Commissioner Nomahlubi Khwinana of the South African Human Rights Commission (SAHRC) noted that
content:
The law and institutions of South Africa were built for an earlier era of technology, and children are carrying the cost of the delay in reform. Commissioner Nomahlubi Khwinana of the South African Human Rights Commission (SAHRC) noted that with many children already online, the question was not whether they should be there, but if duty bearers were doing enough to keep them safe.

Khwinana was presenting an SAHRC report, [Children’s Rights to Privacy and Safety on Online Platforms](https://sahrc.org.za/index.php/publications/633-children-s-conference-report/viewdocument/633), that looked at legislative gaps for child protection, and the case for reform. The commission found that existing legal frameworks, including the Protection of Personal Information Act (Popia) and the Cybercrimes Act, did not address platform design choices such as addictive algorithmic feeds, default data-sharing settings or age verification at sign-up, allowing technology companies to profit from children’s engagement while bearing insufficient accountability for resulting harms.

SAHRC commissioner Nomahlubi Khwinana at the SAHRC national inquiry into hunger in South Africa. (Photo: Lillian Roberts)

The SAHRC report follows a stakeholders’ conference held on 28 March 2026 in Johannesburg, under the leadership of Khwinana, which brought together government departments, UN agencies, industry regulators, technology companies, civil society organisations and children themselves. The event highlighted the urgent need to safeguard children in an increasingly digital world.

“Children told us in March exactly what they need:safe-by-default platforms; reporting they can use; privacy they understand; and a seat at the table… The task is no longer to find the gaps. It is to close them together in the right way,” said Khwinana.

### Gaps in legislation

There is no one policy framework in South Africa that deals with all aspects of children’s digital safety, but rather a web of different pieces of legislation that collectively seek to protect children from online harms. They include:

*   The [Cybercrimes Act](https://www.solacebenefits.co.za/legal-hub/a-south-african-parents-guide-to-digital-safety-social-media-law-and-sanity#:~:text=South%20Africa's%20Cybercrimes%20Act%20makes%20it%20an,(CSAM)%20crimes%20and%20carries%20serious%20criminal%20penalties.), which makes it an offence to disclose intimate images without consent, and strictly penalises the manufacturing, distribution or possession of child sexual abuse material, among other crimes;

*   The Protection of Personal Information Act, which treats children as a special category of the population requiring stricter safeguards, prohibiting the processing of a child’s personal information by apps, websites or social media platforms unless a “competent person” (a parent or legal guardian) gives consent; and

*   The Film and Publications Act, which enables the Film and Publication Board to issue take-down notices for harmful content, hate speech or explicit material involving children, and mandates that commercial online distributors adhere to age-rating and classification laws to protect children from seeing mature, violent or sexually explicit digital media.

The Department of Communications and Digital Technologies published the [Draft White Paper on Audio and Audiovisual Media Services and Online Safety](https://www.gov.za/sites/default/files/gcis_document/202507/52972gen3369.pdf) for public comment in mid-2025. Daily Maverick asked the department about the timeline for implementation of the white paper, but had not received a response by the time of publishing.

Another piece of legislation in the works is the Draft National Artificial Intelligence (AI) Policy, which was withdrawn by Minister of Communications and Digital Technologies Solly Malatsi in April 2026 after it was discovered to contain AI-generated, fictitious academic citations. The target deadline for re-releasing the revised policy for a new public comment period is January 2027.

Minister of Communications and Digital Technologies Solly Malatsi. (Photo: Gallo Images / OJ Koloti)

Among the recommendations in the SAHRC report are:

*   The amendment of sections 34 and 35 of Popia by Parliament and relevant government departments to ensure children’s data is processed only with plain-language, meaningfully informed consent;

*   Extending Popia’s mandate to address passive data collection, harmful platform design and cross-border enforcement;

*   Amending the Children’s Act to address the abusive posting of children’s images and information by parents and caregivers;

*   Amending the Films and Publications Amendment Act to cover algorithmically served content, livestreams and AI-generated child sexual abuse material, while also introducing mandatory age verification and child-friendly reporting tools;

*   Empowering the Information Regulator and the Film and Publications Board to proactively assess platform safety by design, rather than relying solely on complaints-based enforcement; and

*   Amending the Cybercrimes Act to address addictive algorithmic design and the commercial exploitation of children’s data for targeted advertising.

The commission also recommended an amendment to the Electronic Communications and Transactions Act to require age verification for SIM registration, with parental involvement for minors.

“Jurisdiction and cross-border reach is a huge policy question. Most platforms are incorporated abroad, so investigation and accountability is hard. We have recommended extra-territorial investigative powers [for regulators],” said Khwinana.

Responding to a question from Daily Maverick, Khwinana said that big technology companies such as Meta were represented at the conference in March, where they indicated a willingness to “come on board” in order to bridge the gap for children’s online safety.

“The beauty of it is really that they are there, they are willing to participate, but of course, with this report, we’re hoping that with the recommendations we have come up with, we’ll take it forward,” she said.

### Children’s participation

The SAHRC emphasised the importance of including children’s voices in shaping the rules around online safety. Khwinana noted that a Children’s Declaration was adopted by child participants at the conference in March, affirming children’s rights and setting out a direct call to action for the government, technology companies, schools, parents and civil society.

“This declaration builds on many calls to action by children around the continent, including the Nelson Mandela Children’s Fund’s 2025 [Digital Justice] Summit, which involved 82 children,” she said.

The Nelson Mandela Children’s Foundation (NMCF) told Daily Maverick that the SAHRC’s most important findings concerned design, noting that laws regulated content, conduct and the processing of information, but did not reach how platforms were built.

“The timing is important. The African Union Model Law on Child Online Safety has been validated by member states and endorsed by ministers, yet it remains guidance rather than a treaty; South Africa should adopt it with amendments shaped by children as rights holders,” said the NMCF.

“The Nelson Mandela Children’s Fund is working with many stakeholders to align efforts across areas affected by AI and digital progress, under our programme titled Digital Justice. The [SAHRC] report notes that recommendations will reach portfolio committees, but their impact will depend on subsequent steps. We aim to continue engaging the commissioner... to strengthen key areas; no single entity can manage this issue alone, as the risk to children is too high.”

It highlighted the recommendation around regulation of design and the commercial use of children’s data, with regulators able to act before products launch and to investigate companies based abroad, as critical.

However, the NMCF also spotlighted certain issues that had not been included in the report, including the need clarify social workers’ roles in online safety incidents, and providing support to teachers by building digital safety education into school-based psychosocial and child-protection programmes.

It noted that “online harm is not separate from offline harm”.

“Children experiencing violence, abuse or neglect offline face heightened risk online, because digital spaces amplify the reach, frequency and duration of harm. South Africa should use existing child protection and psychosocial programme data, alongside evidence on children’s digital experiences, to identify vulnerable communities and target prevention,” the NMCF said. **DM**

title: El Niño threatens to deepen southern Africa’s poverty
summary: October is a special month in global agricultural and food organisations. On the 16th many celebrated World Food Day, which marks the founding of the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization in 1945. It also gives countries a chance
content:
October is a special month in global agricultural and food organisations. On the 16th many celebrated World Food Day, which marks the founding of the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization in 1945.

It also gives countries a chance to reflect on their food security conditions and outline plans to strengthen resilience and contribute to efforts to reduce poverty in countries that remain highly impoverished.

But this year’s World Food Day celebrations were different. Unlike in previous years, when some countries reported declining poverty levels, the outlook for 2027 is worrying, particularly in southern Africa.

### Ongoing geopolitical conflicts

Many countries in the region face rising costs because of ongoing geopolitical conflicts, which have not only increased energy costs but also complicated supply chains. Compounding the challenge in 2027 is the likely El Niño drought, which could push poverty up across most of southern Africa.

Already, the Food and Agriculture Organization suggests the region may face challenging conditions that could be worse than the 2015-16 drought.

In late June 2026, commenting on southern Africa’s recent droughts of 2015-16 and the expected 2026-27 drought, the Food and Agriculture Organization stated that “the most recent El Niño cycle brought the region’s worst drought in more than a century, leaving 61 million people in need of assistance, straining livestock, water systems and pasturelands, and pushing more than 8 million people into food insecurity.

“The forecast points to a greater than 50% probability of agricultural drought across large parts of Namibia and Botswana, extending into Angola, Zambia, Zimbabwe, South Africa and parts of Mozambique and Madagascar.”

Under such prospects, fears are rising that the southern Africa region would face this challenge at a time when global humanitarian aid is also less available.

Recent wars in the Black Sea and Middle East mean resources that would ordinarily be channelled to natural causes of poverty, such as the expected drought, are now constrained by competing needs in war zones.

Moreover, the US Administration’s decision to abandon US Aid also meant that the World Food Programme budget, which relied heavily on US Aid funding, will have fewer resources to assist. Therefore, if the expected drought devastates agricultural production, the southern Africa region may face a much tougher period than in the recent past in terms of food supplies.

### Challenges ahead

Right now, the region is already at a point where farmers have started planting crops for the 2026-27 season, although some know the coming months may bring challenges. This also means governments have a limited window to assist with the current season.

Countries that can import need to ensure they have access to food supplies and that the private sector has a clearer pathway to import. This means that where there are limitations on grain imports, such as bans on non-genetically-modified grains, such bans may need to be suspended for a period during the time of food needs.

Moreover, ensuring feed supplies for livestock is another important consideration. Where fiscal space allows, household assistance may be necessary in the coming months, depending on whether the season turns out in the worrying way we fear.

In countries with agricultural supplies in the region, it may be tempting to impose an export ban to protect domestic supplies. But such policy actions typically further exacerbate the challenge.

They reduce incentives for agribusinesses and farmers to expand production in favourable seasons and cause price shocks that worsen conditions for importing countries.

What matters is transparent, timely information sharing so market participants can make timely decisions, and prices that adjust quickly to reflect each country’s realities in the region.

### South Africa’s position

Closer to home, South Africa remains in a more fortunate position than much of southern Africa. The 2025-26 season was a period of abundance in grains and oilseed, ensuring ample supplies to cushion the country going into the next year.

For example, the maize harvest is at a record 17.5 million tonnes, against the annual consumption of 12.0 million tonnes. Stocks were also ample at the start of the year, which further improved supplies.

Moreover, South African agribusinesses are better placed to import when supply glitches occur. The country’s dam water supplies are over 80% full, which also suggests that fruit and vegetables typically produced under irrigation may be spared, to an extent, from the challenge we may witness in other countries in the region.

In essence, southern Africa is likely to see a rise in poverty in 2027 because of the El Niño drought. While South Africa is as exposed to the drought challenge as the rest of the region, the impact may be much milder here.

Still, the country may have to shoulder the region’s challenges, and export produce to its neighbours to stabilise regional food needs.**DM**

title: Parliament demands answers on deepening turmoil at SAA
summary: Transport Minister Barbara Creecy has called on SAA board chair Sedzani Mudau to account for the airline’s governance and financial issues. The chairperson of Parliament’s standing committee on appropriations, Bosa leader Mmusi Maimane, tol
content:
Transport Minister Barbara Creecy has called on SAA board chair Sedzani Mudau to account for the airline’s governance and financial issues.

The chairperson of Parliament’s standing committee on appropriations, Bosa leader Mmusi Maimane, told Daily Maverick on Monday, 26 October, that an “urgent committee meeting” was planned within days of the 4 November elections and SAA was expected to bring “properly crafted financial statements”.

This comes after internal SAA information reached the committee, raising serious concerns about “executive appointments and the accuracy of SAA’s financial position”, according to a 19 October letter sent by Maimane to Creecy.

The committee has asked whether employees’ concerns were addressed, and for details of SAA’s current financial situation, how the R1.1-billion proceeds from [selling a Heathrow slot](https://africa.businessinsider.com/local/markets/south-african-airways-delays-salaries-despite-dollar61-million-state-guarantee/tkvdnnw) were used, and “any anticipated request for state support”.

The standing committee on appropriations oversees how public funds are allocated and spent, with a focus on appropriation Bills, but crucially also ensures fiscal accountability and transparency by monitoring spending patterns and investigating financial irregularities.

As Maimane put it, “We need to understand fully where the guarantees will end up.”

The chairperson of Parliament’s Standing Committee on Appropriations, Mmusi Maimane. (Photo: Jeffrey Abrahams / Gallo Images)

Delivering the [Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-10-21-medium-term-budget-policy-statement-full-speech/) last Wednesday, Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana said SAA had received a R1-billion guarantee in August for working capital requirements following “pressure on its operations and finances from the fuel price shock”.

Another R223-million in government guarantees relates to liabilities for unflown tickets – effectively refunds – and credits. The risks depended on SAA’s “ability to absorb these pressures and meet its operating and financing requirements without additional government support”.

SAA failed to submit its 2025/26 annual report as statutorily required by 30 September because the audit process was still under way.

“It is anticipated that the annual financial statements will be finalised and ready for tabling by the end of October 2026,” Creecy told Parliament in a letter dated 4 September and published in the [Announcements, Tablings and Committee Reports](https://www.parliament.gov.za/storage/app/media/Docs/atc/01ls62wgejvuaqnojs2nglxqzhchmewvvk.pdf).

### Reduced flights

On Monday, Maimane said, “I fly [with] SAA a lot. If you look at the regularity of its flights, these have severely reduced.”

This month, SAA staff are being paid in relays from 27 October to 30 October, according to the [Sunday Times](https://www.sundaytimes.timeslive.co.za/news/2026-10-24-saas-finances-under-fire-as-cash-squeeze-tightens/), which quoted a source saying this was the second such salary delay. “SAA is running out of money, and may soon be grounded,” said the source.

Evidence of SAA’s fragile financial standing also surfaced last year when the national carrier received a disclaimed audit opinion. In the airline’s annual report for the financial year ending 31 March 2025, the Auditor-General said the financial statements were submitted late and were not in the required format. On procurement, said the Auditor-General:

> “I was unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence that all contracts and quotations were awarded in accordance with the legislative requirements due to poor record-keeping and inadequate procedures for maintaining comprehensive procurement and contract registers.”

SAA board chairperson Sedzani Mudau. (Photo: Facebook)

SAA [exited business rescue](https://www.sanews.gov.za/south-africa/saa-takatso-deal-collapses) in May 2021, on the back of a 51% private equity partner deal with Takatso, after years of financial turmoil. Since 2017, the airline has received government bailouts of at least R15-billion, alongside an agreement by the government to pay another R9.2-billion in maturing debt.

However, the planned deal terminated in March 2024, when Takatso and the Department of Public Enterprises parted ways over a controversial revaluation of the flag carrier.

But for Maimane, the situation at SAA went beyond finances to the airline’s recent ructions in leadership.

In April, Group CEO Professor [John Lamola](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-04-12-lamolas-exit-exposes-saas-shaky-foundations-and-questionable-profits/) resigned at short notice. [Matshela Seshibe](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-04-27-new-broom-promises-to-clean-up-saa-and-improve-accountability/), the CEO of SAA’s subsidiary Air Chefs, was appointed acting chief executive amid a public commitment that “the process to recruit the permanent GCEO will commence shortly”. But he was put on [special leave](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-08-14-saa-acting-ceo-put-on-immediate-special-leave-as-board-conducts-internal-investigation/) in August with immediate effect pending internal proceedings. **DM**

title: Nigeria: Tinubu Launches Reelection Bid Amid Economic Woes
summary: _President Bola Tinubu promised "a better tomorrow" for Nigerians while kicking off his next electoral campaign, while also blaming his rivals for poverty plaguing Africa's most populous nation._ [Nigeria](https://www.dw.com/en/nigeria/t-18
content:
_President Bola Tinubu promised "a better tomorrow" for Nigerians while kicking off his next electoral campaign, while also blaming his rivals for poverty plaguing Africa's most populous nation._

[Nigeria](https://www.dw.com/en/nigeria/t-18943620)'s President [Bola Tinubu](https://www.dw.com/en/bola-ahmed-tinubu/t-76831921) on Saturday formally launched his campaign for a second term.

"We have prosperity, consistency, growth, recovery and opportunity," Tinubu said at a rally in the northwestern state of Kaduna.

"You grant me the privilege to promise you once again, there is that promise of a better tomorrow," he added.

Keep up with the latest headlines on [WhatsApp](https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K) | [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/)

Africa's most populous country will hold [its next presidential election in January 2027](https://www.dw.com/en/nigeria-election-campaign-2027-tinubu/a-78421873). The campaign is expected to focus on Nigeria's economy and security challenges.

**Nigeria's worsening cost of living**

After taking power in 2023, [Tinubu](https://www.dw.com/en/nigerias-tinubu-touts-economy-amid-cost-of-living-anger/a-72716580) sparked anger by scrapping decades-long fuel subsidies — a move that has fueled Nigeria's inflation.

On Saturday, [the incumbent president](https://www.dw.com/en/tinubu-must-go-nigerias-northern-protests-test-limits-of-political-dissent/a-79713785) dismissed criticisms about his economic policies.

"I hear my opponents talking about hunger and poverty. Who created it? They did," Tinubu said at the crowded rally. "They created the hunger, they created the poverty. We are trying to eradicate it."

Earlier this month, the 74-year-old acknowledged [Nigeria's economic issues](https://www.dw.com/en/africa-nigeria-lagos-president-bola-tinubu-subsidy-inflation-cost-of-living-food-prices-economy/a-75503303). In his Independence Day address, he argued that his administration's reform "did not create the weaknesses in our economy," but actually "confronted them."

Tinubu's government announced potential price caps on fuel soon after.

**Security threats to play big role in Nigeria's election**

Apart from grappling with a cost-of-living crisis, Nigeria continues to [struggle with armed bandits and kidnappers](https://www.dw.com/en/nigerias-leader-battles-security-political-crises/a-76903098).

On Friday, gunmen killed at least 20 people in an attack on a village in the country's northeast.

The nation has also been fighting a long-running jihadist insurgency, sparked by [Boko Haram](https://www.dw.com/en/boko-haram/t-18172785)'s 2009 uprising.

**Another three-man race**

[Tinubu](https://www.dw.com/en/who-is-nigerias-new-president-bola-tinubu/a-64851330)'s main challengers are expected to be former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and former state governor Peter Obi.

In the [2023 presidential election,](https://www.dw.com/en/nigeria-elections-2023/t-64740501)Tinubu only managed to secure less than 36.6% of the valid votes cast, with Abubakar at 29% and Obi at 25.4%.

_Edited by: Darko Janjevic_

content:
【精選書摘】

如果「中南海」是一座劇場，誰在編劇？誰在演戲？又是誰在暗處窺視？

中南海，原為遼至清五代的皇家園林，1949年後成為中共最高決策與行政中樞，國務院、中央書記處、軍委會皆座落於此，歷任最高領導人與中常委亦在此辦公居住。

如今，眾所皆知的「中南海」已是中共最高權力核心的代名詞。但鮮為人知的是，它只是中共五大禁苑的其中之一。

「禁苑」一詞在中共政治語境中，象徵著極致的權力與絕對的神祕。從紅牆環繞的中南海、宏偉肅穆的人民大會堂、軍委主席坐鎮的玉泉山，以及釣魚台與京西賓館，這五大禁苑構成的中共「大內」，不僅是國家決策核心，更是外界難以窺透的黑盒子。

著名經濟學家、普林斯頓大學《當代中國研究》主編程曉農博士，曾在1980年代擔任趙紫陽的核心智庫。他將自己進入權力巔峰處的觀察、親歷與省思寫進[《紅色高牆：直擊中共五大禁苑的權力運作邏輯》](https://www.books.com.tw/products/0011065947?loc=P_0005_002)，以「牆內者」的獨特視角，帶領讀者穿透紅色高牆，還原禁苑內的權力暗流與決策邏輯。

本文節選自《紅色高牆》，文章標題與文內小標經《報導者》編輯改寫，經今周刊出版授權刊登。

共產黨領導模式：從集體領導到個人集權的「鐘擺規律」

接班人困局只是紅色政權政治統治的一個特點，而另一個很少引起注意的特點是其領導模式的「鐘擺規律」。

共產黨國家的高層權力格局，有個人專權、寡頭統治和集體領導這三種模式。寡頭統治是指兩、三個黨內派系的高層領袖，共同決定國家的主要路線。

在不同的歷史階段，共產黨的領導模式會在個人專權和集體領導兩者之間，像鐘擺那樣擺動，寡頭統治則處於個人專權和集體領導的中間，是一個過渡階段。這種擺動並不是隨意的，它有明顯的規律。只要從政治、經濟的全方位角度去分析，而不是只關注個人之間的權力鬥爭，就會發現這個「鐘擺規律」。

我提出這個「鐘擺規律」，當然不是出於隨意想像，而是對蘇聯和中國兩個紅色大國領導模式觀察對比中得出的結論，算是比較政治研究的一個結論。當我把共產黨國家的高層權力格局區分成個人專權、寡頭統治和集體領導這三種，再觀察蘇共和中共領導模式變化的軌跡，就發現，在蘇聯和中國，從共產黨建立政權起，「鐘擺規律」都呈現四個階段。

這個「鐘擺」的兩端分別是集體領導和個人集權，共產黨的高層權力結構就在這兩端之間有規律地擺動，先集體領導，然後個人集權，再集體領導，最後個人集權。

鐘擺的第一階段是共產黨建政初期，那時往往都是集體領導，蘇共在[列寧](https://zh.wikipedia.org/zh-tw/%E5%BC%97%E6%8B%89%E5%9F%BA%E7%B1%B3%E5%B0%94%C2%B7%E5%88%97%E5%AE%81)時代、中共在50年代初都是如此。

在鐘擺的第二階段，黨內高層的政治氣氛決定了最高領導人容不得對自己的批評，清洗有不同意見的高層成員，必然成為常態。在[史達林](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E7%BA%A6%E7%91%9F%E5%A4%AB%C2%B7%E6%96%AF%E5%A4%A7%E6%9E%97)時代的前期，史達林打擊、驅逐黨內與其競爭的另一個寡頭[托洛茨基（Leon Trotsky）](https://zh.wikipedia.org/zh-tw/%E5%88%97%E5%A4%AB%C2%B7%E6%89%98%E6%B4%9B%E8%8C%A8%E5%9F%BA)，就是清除寡頭的行動。

走向個人專權的過程中，最高領導人個人有無威權，取決於他對軍隊和情報部門的絕對控制，還需要推動個人崇拜，在輿論上為個人威權造勢。史達林和[毛澤東](https://zh.wikipedia.org/zh-tw/%E6%AF%9B%E6%B3%BD%E4%B8%9C)就這樣鞏固了個人威權，以此取代了集體領導。

在鐘擺的第三階段，個人威權的領導人去世後，又重回集體領導。從蘇聯的[赫魯雪夫（Nikita Khrushchev）](https://zh.wikipedia.org/zh-tw/%E5%B0%BC%E5%9F%BA%E5%A1%94%C2%B7%E8%B5%AB%E9%AD%AF%E6%9B%89%E5%A4%AB)到[契爾年科（Konstantin Chernenko）](https://zh.wikipedia.org/zh-tw/%E5%BA%B7%E6%96%AF%E5%9D%A6%E4%B8%81%C2%B7%E5%A5%91%E5%B0%94%E5%B9%B4%E7%A7%91)，長達30年的過程中，蘇共一直處於集體領導模式。

在中國，[華國鋒](https://zh.wikipedia.org/zh-tw/%E5%8D%8E%E5%9B%BD%E9%94%8B)時代、[江澤民](https://zh.wikipedia.org/zh-tw/%E6%B1%9F%E6%B3%BD%E6%B0%91)時代和[胡錦濤](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E8%83%A1%E9%94%A6%E6%B6%9B)時代，基本上都是如此，只有[鄧小平](https://zh.wikipedia.org/zh-tw/%E9%82%93%E5%B0%8F%E5%B9%B3)時代是華國鋒時代和江澤民時代之間的寡頭過渡模式。如果扣除了鄧小平時代從1982年到1992年那十年與[陳雲](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E9%99%88%E4%BA%91)一起的寡頭統治階段，那麼，中共從1977年到2013年間，處於集體領導的年分是26年，與蘇聯的集體領導年分長度差不多。

到了鐘擺的第四階段，重建最高領導人的個人威權，其過程與第二階段相似。中共進入[習近平](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E4%B9%A0%E8%BF%91%E5%B9%B3)時代以後，在高層權力鬥爭和反腐運動中，習近平建立了個人的專權領導模式。蘇聯則是進入[戈巴契夫（Mikhail Gorbachev）](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E7%B1%B3%E5%93%88%E4%BC%8A%E5%B0%94%C2%B7%E6%88%88%E5%B0%94%E5%B7%B4%E4%B9%94%E5%A4%AB)時代以後，戈巴契夫因推動政治開放時，遇到黨內保守派的強烈阻力，最後他決定實行總統制。

蘇聯的總統制自然是一種個人集權體制，但戈巴契夫還未有效形成個人威權，很快就遇到了蘇聯保守派發動的[政變](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%85%AB%E4%B8%80%E4%B9%9D%E4%BA%8B%E4%BB%B6)。政變失敗後，由蘇共官員組成的蘇聯國會──最高蘇維埃，通過了決議，宣布蘇聯共產黨為非法組織。蘇聯解體了，蘇聯總統、蘇共總書記戈巴契夫因此失去了權力，走入了歷史。

談到「鐘擺規律」的過程時，還有一個必須提到的寡頭統治階段。我把這個階段歸類為過渡階段，是因為寡頭領導人的壽命終有極限。

權力真空期的「高成本統治模式」，造就人民「生活最好的年代」

需要指出的是，在鐘擺從集體領導向個人專權擺動的過程中（即第一與第二階段之間），很少會停留在寡頭統治階段，因為試圖實現個人專權的領導人，會迅速排除其他與之爭鋒的政治寡頭。

而當鐘擺從個人專權向集體領導擺動時，卻可能會暫時停留在寡頭統治階段（比如鄧小平時代），然後再過渡到集體領導階段。

分析紅色大國共產黨政權的執政史，用鐘擺規律來觀察共產黨領導模式的演變，當然不是單純的學術興趣；我這樣研究的真正意圖在於，透過對比蘇共和中共的鐘擺規律，看能不能發現共產黨政權的生命週期。

對比蘇共和中共執政後的「鐘擺」擺動過程，從中當然會發現一系列權力鬥爭，但更大程度上，「鐘擺」的「擺動」與共產黨的統治需要有密切關係。

從集體領導到個人獨裁轉變的原因是，史達林和毛澤東都急於完成工業化，建立強大的軍事工業，這需要最大限度地集中資源，同時把民眾的生活降到最低限度，還要打擊黨內為民請願的官員，消滅任何不同聲音。

於是，一種依靠對領袖的個人崇拜和大範圍政治清洗的統治模式就建立起來，即政治壓力最大、經濟成本最低的統治模式。

從個人獨裁到集體領導轉變，則是因為個人威權的最高領導者死後出現權力真空，為穩定政局，接班人通常會恢復集體領導模式，讓最高層的領導集體分享權力；同時，透過平反過去的冤假錯案來贏得民心，再花錢買政治安定，提高民眾的生活水準，也包括用允許腐敗換取官員們效忠，這種局面一段時期內似乎可以長期穩定下去。

這是紅色政權的一種「高成本統治模式」。蘇聯的[布里茲涅夫（Leonid Brezhnev）](https://zh.wikipedia.org/zh-tw/%E5%88%97%E6%98%82%E5%B0%BC%E5%BE%B7%C2%B7%E5%8B%83%E5%88%97%E6%97%A5%E6%B6%85%E5%A4%AB)時代和中國的鄧小平時代、江澤民時代和胡錦濤時代就是如此。蘇聯和中國民眾覺得生活最好的年代，就是在這樣的統治模式之下出現的。俄羅斯人懷念布里茲涅夫時代，中國人懷念江澤民時代和胡錦濤時代，都出於相同的原因。

當「花錢買穩定」耗盡經濟資源

集體領導是否再向個人集權轉變，其觸因是，「花錢買穩定」會消耗當局掌控的經濟資源，這是集體領導模式的致命弱點。「高成本統治模式」快要耗盡當局的經濟資源時，可能會倒逼改革，或者倒逼集權。

集體領導模式之下，通常會有部分高層人員抵制改革，鄧小平時代、戈巴契夫時代都是如此；集體領導模式也必然阻止反腐敗。這兩種抵制的根源，都是掌權的利益集團反對不利於自己的變化。

戈巴契夫因為推動政治改革受阻，就改變領導模式，實行總統制；習近平因為高層權力鬥爭爆發，為應付權力鬥爭而開始集權，又因為反腐敗受阻，最後走上了恢復個人集權的道路。

這些簡單的對比分析說明，共產黨的領導模式從集體領導走向個人專權，不單純是最高領導人的個人性格使然，還有其統治需要的規律型特徵。而個人專權模式必定引起共產黨內和社會上的種種不滿，這樣的不滿是否能終止個人專權呢？

最近十年來，中共黨內和中國社會中，對經濟現狀的不滿和對政治高壓的不滿日益累積。因此，官場中人和民間就可能出現「耳語」，希望不滿個人專權領導人的高官，能像華國鋒那樣，採取祕密逮捕之類的行動

1976年10月6日，毛澤東逝世一個月後，時任中共中央第一副主席、國務院總理兼公安部部長華國鋒，聯合中共中央副主席、中央軍委副主席、國防部部長[葉劍英](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%8F%B6%E5%89%91%E8%8B%B1)和中共中央政治局委員、中央辦公廳主任[汪東興](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%B1%AA%E4%B8%9C%E5%85%B4)等黨政軍要人於北京中南海以「隔離審查」名義抓捕並拘禁「[四人幫](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%9B%9B%E4%BA%BA%E5%B8%AE)」成員（包含：時任中共中央副主席[王洪文](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E7%8E%8B%E6%B4%AA%E6%96%87)；中共中央政治局常委、國務院副總理、上海市委書記、市革委會主任[張春橋](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%BC%A0%E6%98%A5%E6%A1%A5)；中共中央政治局委員、毛澤東遺孀[江青](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%B1%9F%E9%9D%92)；中共中央政治局委員、上海市革委會第一副主任[姚文元](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%A7%9A%E6%96%87%E5%85%83)）和中共中央政治局聯絡員、毛澤東侄子[毛遠新](https://zh.wikipedia.org/zh-tw/%E6%AF%9B%E8%BF%9C%E6%96%B0)等五人。

事後華國鋒被推舉擔任中共中央代理主席、中央軍委代理主席，實質上結束了由毛澤東所發動的「文化大革命」。後來，四人幫及其主要追隨者均遭政治清洗，有的則遭刑事追究。這場自我政變事件又稱「[粉碎四人幫](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E7%B2%89%E7%A2%8E%E5%9B%9B%E4%BA%BA%E5%B8%AE)」。

，或集體勸退現任最高領導人。

在[張又俠](https://zh.wikipedia.org/zh-tw/%E5%BC%A0%E5%8F%88%E4%BE%A0)被抓之後，海外與國內傳出的各種「政變」謠言，其實就隱含著這樣的情緒，他們寧可希望張又俠率兵對抗習近平。然而，共產黨的個人專權模式本來就建立在最高領導人對高官的警衛管控之上，本書已經談過很多了。假如習近平這樣的個人獨裁者未能掌控警衛大權，他事實上就無法個人專權。

另一方面，中國社會當中，出於對個人專權模式的厭惡，很多人會盲目懷念共產黨的集體領導模式。其實，真正懷念集體領導模式的是官場中人，因為集體領導模式之下，貪官遍地，高官家族普遍經商發財，「中南海

位於中國北京西城區西長安街街道，是中共中央委員會與國務院的主要辦公場所，長期也作為部分黨和國家領導人的居住區域，因而被視為中國政治最高權力的核心區域。「中南海」亦常被用來代指中共中央領導層。

」不會推動大規模、長時期的反貪腐運動。所以，相對於個人專權模式，集體領導模式是官員們的「天堂」。

官員為何懷念集體領導

但是，官員們很少會按照「鐘擺規律」來理解高層領導模式的改變，因為，一旦高層領導模式發生鐘擺式改變，其變動方向就必定是個人專權，而個人專權更可能導致大規模反貪腐。官員們討厭反腐敗，自然就希望高層的集體領導「長命百歲」。

可是，從旁觀者的角度去看，高層的集體領導模式之下，往往就是官場貪腐最嚴重的時候。蘇聯的布里茲涅夫時代如此，中國的江澤民時代和胡錦濤時代也同樣如此。在經濟對外開放的情況下，大規模、長時期的官場貪腐，必然導致大規模資金外流，因為官員貪腐後不敢把錢財留在國內。

這種無數官員同時把貪腐所得向國外轉移的行為，往往發生在個人專權模式開始出現的時刻。個人專權領導人在權力鬥爭中打壓異己，最方便使用的罪名就是貪腐，而搜查少數高官的貪腐所得，就會「一石激起千層浪」，讓眾多官場中人如驚弓之鳥，紛紛向境外轉移錢財。

所以，從民眾的角度看，共產黨高層的領導模式是集體領導，還是個人專權，主要影響的是官場中人的利益，能讓民眾感受到的，頂多是小小的「涓滴效應」。

奪取軍隊指揮權，習近平的個人專權之路

習近平走上個人專權之路，實際上是從隔代奪取軍權開始的。我在 第八章

第八章〈南巡與「政變」〉中提及，習近平在2012年正式取得總書記與軍委主席職務，不過習時代初期的中央警衛局長仍為胡錦濤時代提拔的[曹清](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%9B%B9%E6%B8%85_(1952%E5%B9%B4))。上任兩年多後，習近平才借外媒曝光中央警衛局利用其專機自非洲走私象牙一事，並在2015年3月初，無預警將曹清調任北京軍區副政委。

裡重點講述了他抓警衛大權的過程，這裡介紹他奪取軍隊指揮權的步驟。

中共建立政權之後的軍隊管控，是總參謀長和總政治部主任分別掌握軍隊核心權力的雙頭體制。總參謀部負責軍令業務，總政治部負責政工和人事，而中共的國防部實際上是虛設的。這種軍令和軍政合一的軍隊體制是蘇聯模式，與美、英、日等國軍令、軍政分離的軍隊管理體制完全不同。

習近平上台後發現，副總參謀長[郭伯雄](https://zh.wikipedia.org/zh-tw/%E9%83%AD%E4%BC%AF%E9%9B%84)和總政治部主任[徐才厚](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%BE%90%E6%89%8D%E5%8E%9A)在胡錦濤時代已自成體系，自己掌握不住，所以決心拿軍隊系統開刀，建立他個人對軍隊的控制權。他先以年齡超過70歲為理由，安排這兩人退休，再以腐敗罪抓了這兩個軍隊高官，換掉了一批軍隊高級將領；同時，取消了已被[周永康](https://zh.wikipedia.org/zh-tw/%E5%91%A8%E6%B0%B8%E5%BA%B7)變成「第二軍隊」的「[武裝警察部隊](https://zh.wikipedia.org/zh-tw/%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E4%BA%BA%E6%B0%91%E6%AD%A6%E8%A3%85%E8%AD%A6%E5%AF%9F%E9%83%A8%E9%98%9F)」，把這支部隊拆散。

在這個基礎上，習近平為了真正掌握軍權，又進一步徹底改變了軍隊管理體制，把總參謀部、總政治部、總後勤部和總裝備部分拆成16個部，取消了原來的總參、總政、總後和總裝備部裡面的二級部，總參謀長和總政主任這兩個職務也取消了。

在這16個部之上，習近平設立了「軍委聯合作戰指揮中心」，自己以「軍委聯合作戰指揮中心總指揮」的身分，擔任了實際上的軍令、軍政一把抓的最高軍隊司令官，現在軍隊系統這16個部都直接對習近平報告。

中共過去的軍委主席對軍隊的管控是虛的，軍委主席不負責軍隊日常運轉的維持，只透過任命總參謀長和總政主任，依靠這兩個人對最高領導人的個人效忠來掌握軍隊；習近平則把軍委主席變成實際掌控軍隊日常運轉的職位，透過「軍委聯合作戰指揮中心辦公室」，直接把軍隊完全掌握在自己手裡。

抓貪官、查財產，對內收緊政治高壓

這種局面幾乎恢復到了毛澤東對軍隊直接掌控的狀態，是歷任集體領導時代從未出現過的模式。當習近平把高官的警衛系統和軍隊指揮權都抓在手裡的時候，他不僅建立了中共最高領導人傳統的真實權力基礎，同時也震動了官場。

與此同時，習近平在清洗政敵的同時，從2014年下半年開始，抓貪官、查財產的動作也達到了峰值。這些舉動嚇壞了官場，大批官員匆忙把財產向海外轉移，一是怕留在中國成為證據，二是怕一旦被抓就被抄沒。這就產生了習近平時代的個人專權與毛澤東時代的個人專權最大的不同結果。

習近平個人集權後，中國的外匯儲備在短短的兩年多時間裡，少了1兆美金，2014年6月的外匯儲備是3兆9,932億美金，而2017年1月只剩下2兆9,982億美金。這個事件發生在10年前，現在很多人已經忘記了。

這次財產大逃亡讓中共非常擔憂，於是進一步收緊對官員行為的監管。中共收繳官員護照、嚴審查官員出境申請的做法，實際上阻斷了官員國內發財、國外享受的傳統路徑。

習近平對外窮兵黷武，對內政治高壓愈來愈緊，官場許多人貪汙的手腳被捆住了，轉移到國外的錢財摸不著了，拿到了外國綠卡也不能溜出去。這就是共產黨政權自生的制度難題。

經濟改革必然會放鬆對經濟的管制，可以讓經濟活躍起來，但官員們的貪汙也蔚然成風了，這還只是問題的一個側面；另一個側面是，官場及官員親屬的貪腐愈嚴重，這些人就愈發把中國當作一個「撈金窟」，然後把上兆美金的財產轉移到西方國家。

中國一旦進入個人專權的領導模式之後，不管習近平是否戀棧權力，都無法不掀起政治風浪而平穩轉移權力了，尤其是2020年習近平點燃美中冷戰的情勢之下。高度緊張的外部環境，使中共的個人專權領導模式不可能順利轉換成集體領導模式；也就是說，鐘擺擺到個人獨裁以後，很可能不會再平穩地擺回去了。

冷戰終局的推算

冷戰的結果將決定中國執政黨的結局。很多人問過我，美中冷戰的結局是什麼？冷戰從來是紅色大國點燃的，世界上僅有的兩場冷戰，一場是蘇共點燃的，一場是中共點燃的。美蘇冷戰的結局是蘇聯消失，美中冷戰的結局應該也是紅色政權的失敗。

為什麼？因為，冷戰是紅色大國挑戰國際秩序，試圖威脅美國，進而取得國際競爭中的優勢。然而，共產黨政權的制度本質，無法與美國的自由民主制度匹敵。雖然在冷戰初期，國際社會看到一個貌似強大的紅色大國在耀武揚威，但是，隨著雙方在軍事、經濟等多層面的競爭深化，紅色大國就逐漸變得衰弱而無以為繼。

美蘇冷戰與美中冷戰還有一個最大的不同，那就是，美蘇冷戰是發生在蘇聯二戰後的經濟科技上升期，而美中冷戰發生在中國經濟的墜落期。蘇聯點燃冷戰之後，一直到上個世紀70年代才陷入經濟困境；而中共事實上是在經濟困境到來時點燃冷戰的。

冷戰比拚的是軍事和科技實力，而軍備競賽靠的是源源不斷的資金投入。中共的中央財政收入2025年下降6.5％，這就是它的冷戰能力開始弱化的信號。所以，從冷戰能力來評估，美蘇冷戰當中，蘇聯撐了40年，而中共可能只能支撐20年上下；也就是說，從中共2020年點燃美中冷戰算起，到2040年左右，我們就能看到美中冷戰的結局了。

事實上，習近平點燃美中冷戰後，他的個人集權還遇到了來自軍方的挑戰，那就是，軍方可能不願意為了中共最高領導人的個人意願，打一場可能用到核子武器的世界大戰。

張又俠被抓的內幕

最近，中國發生了震動中國政局和軍界的大事，2026年1月24日，共軍的軍委副主席、掌管共軍日常運轉的張又俠上將被抓。這個事件還有一個更加詭異的畫面，1月25日《華爾街日報》（The Wall Street Journal）英文版[發表](https://www.wsj.com/world/china/chinas-top-general-accused-of-giving-nuclear-secrets-to-u-s-b8f59dae)了一篇報導〈中國最高將領被控向美國洩露核機密〉（China’s Top General Accused of Giving Nuclear Secrets to U.S.）。

這則消息直接把張又俠被抓與美中冷戰掛鉤了。1月24日上午，中共在北京突然舉辦了一個高級別的不公開內部簡報會，出席簡報會的主要是中共的官媒記者，但這些記者不許寫報導。會上宣布，共軍的最高將領張又俠已被抓，因為他向美國洩露了中共核武器計畫的訊息。

有趣的是，出席內部簡報會的人會後馬上把張又俠洩露核武器訊息這件事，透露給《華爾街日報》駐北京的記者了。透露重大資訊給外國媒體，應該是中共事先安排好的，目的是放風，這就有了《華爾街日報》1月25日的那篇報導。

中共有誣陷高級官員「裡通外國」這種迫害政敵的傳統。毛澤東時代，國防部長[彭德懷](https://zh.wikipedia.org/zh-tw/%E5%BD%AD%E5%BE%B7%E6%80%80)和總參謀長[粟裕](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E7%B2%9F%E8%A3%95)曾被毛澤東指責是勾結蘇聯；鄧小平時代，[趙紫陽](https://zh.wikipedia.org/zh-tw/%E8%B5%B5%E7%B4%AB%E9%98%B3)曾被誣陷為美國中央情報局間諜。這次是不是故伎重演？我認為不會，因為，中共軍方向美國軍方洩露高級軍事機密，5年前就發生過。

冷戰當中，彼此對另一方最主要的戰略威脅就是核武器，而投送核武器要靠洲際飛彈。所以，洲際飛彈發射部隊的編制和位置，甚至比核彈頭的機密更重要。洲際飛彈分陸地發射和水下的戰略核潛艇發射。共軍負責陸地發射洲際飛彈的部隊叫火箭軍。所以，火箭軍所轄部隊的分布位置和編制，是共軍的最高機密。

然而，這個共軍的最高機密早就送到美軍手裡，而且被美軍公開了。2022年10月24日美國空軍大學的「[中國航空航天研究所](https://zh.wikipedia.org/zh-tw/%E7%BE%8E%E5%9B%BD%E7%A9%BA%E5%86%9B%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E8%88%AA%E7%A9%BA%E8%88%AA%E5%A4%A9%E7%A0%94%E7%A9%B6%E6%89%80)」突然公開[發布](https://www.airuniversity.af.edu/CASI/Display/Article/3193056/pla-rocket-force-organization/)了一份絕密報告，標題是〈解放軍火箭軍的組織〉（PLA Rocket Force Organization）。這份報告總共242頁，把中共火箭軍司令部指揮系統的具體組織結構，以及火箭軍下轄的全部單位都開列出來了。

火箭軍情報外洩

共軍火箭軍一共15萬兵力，編制是9個師（共軍內部稱每個師級單位為「基地」）。這份報告還詳細列出了每個旅的司令部、政治部等編制和每個下屬單位的地址電話、郵政編碼、各基層單位主官姓名（均為中文）。我下載了這份報告後，確認這份報告的真實程度是可信的。

共軍高層對戰略敵人故意洩露自己的絕密軍事情報，到底是為什麼？目前不可能得知真相，但我可以分析這個既成事實背後的邏輯。習近平在2020年決定，把中共的軍事戰略從「積極防禦」變成了「戰略威懾」；也就是說，共軍從此要主動威脅美國和周邊國家，而且要用到戰略核武器。這樣的話，火箭軍就不再是備而不用的手段了。

當來自中南海的壓力高到足夠大的時候，火箭軍跟中共軍方高層就可能不得不考慮自救了。因為，讓火箭軍走向實戰，就等於讓火箭軍乃至共軍軍方高層都灰飛煙滅。曾接待張又俠訪問美國的美國前國防部官員唐安竹（Drew Thompson）對張又俠有這樣一種判斷，他是那種「經歷過戰爭，並對戰爭心存敬畏的人」。

所以，共軍上層就可能會想到，能不能主動跟美國軍方示好？一方面火箭軍自己放慢備戰進度，用各種技術性藉口拖延實戰準備；另一方面讓美方相信，共軍其實不願意主動發起核攻擊，因此希望美國能透過外交手段，來軟化習近平的強硬立場。

共軍高階將領可能會有這些想法，因為他們比較懂冷戰一點，知道不可以真跟美軍對抗。然而，他們的意圖慢慢會被習近平察覺，於是習近平跟張又俠的對立與衝突就不可避免了。

雖然習近平對軍隊高層的大清洗動到了共軍的整個指揮系統，讓短期內共軍可能忙於應付內部清查，高階軍官要人人過關，好像對外的軍事壓力會減輕，但這就像股市的短多長空。不管台灣願意還是不願意，必須要看到，習近平跟軍方高層的對立，最後可能反而會逼出新任將領的冒進跟冒險。

中共火箭軍一共9個師，5個擺在西北，如果共軍從中國西北部發射洲際飛彈打美國，這些飛彈只能經過俄羅斯和北極的上空，再經過格陵蘭，然後威脅加拿大和美國。

只要美軍在格陵蘭設立足夠強的預警系統和攔截裝備，美國就能用「金色穹頂」（Golden Dom）計畫，南防中共海軍戰略核潛艇的威脅，北防中共陸基火箭部隊的恫嚇。

美國把本土的防中共洲際飛彈威脅措施完成以後，中共火箭軍也好、海軍的戰略核潛艇也好，就很難用洲際飛彈傷害到美國了。中共對美國的戰略威脅能力受到約束之後，美國的戰略威脅能力將繼續對中共造成壓力。這樣的話，美中冷戰中雙方的態勢就變成我強敵弱，對中共形成壓倒性優勢，那美國強化東亞地區對中共威脅的處置，就游刃自如了，中共會比較不敢輕舉妄動。

《紅色高牆：直擊中共五大禁苑的權力運作邏輯》，程曉農著，今周刊出版

title: Guinea: 'Go Green and Go Thirsty' - Guinea's Plastic Ban Clashes With Need for Safe Water
summary: _Plastic water sachets are an essential way to provide people in Guinea with safe and affordable drinking water. But their use clashes with the government's objective of outlawing single-use plastics. Until a solution can be found, authorit
content:
_Plastic water sachets are an essential way to provide people in Guinea with safe and affordable drinking water. But their use clashes with the government's objective of outlawing single-use plastics. Until a solution can be found, authorities have been forced to lift a ban, less than three weeks after implementing it._

The [Republic of Guinea](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/guinea/ "https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/guinea/") passed its law to ban single-use plastics two years ago, but only enforced it on 20 September.

However, in the face of mounting public anger, it was forced to do a U-turn and lifted the ban on 7 October, for the next six months.

"To govern is to foresee. The ban was a most reckless decision," said Emmanuel, who buys water sachets every day in the capital Conakry.

Keep up with the latest headlines on [WhatsApp](https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K "https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K") | [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/ "https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/")

"How can you ban the population's only access to safe drinking water without having provided an alternative solution?" asked Oumou, also from Conakry. "You can't suddenly go green and make people go thirsty."

RFI also spoke to Faya Blaise, who said he would like government ministers to "come see how life goes in the poorer neighbourhoods".

"They should see how we live and the difficulties we face before making decisions that impact us directly."

Health issues

The World Bank describes Guinea as [a country with poor infrastructure and widespread poverty](https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/bae48ff2fefc5a869546775b3f010735-0500062021/related/mpo-gin.pdf "https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/bae48ff2fefc5a869546775b3f010735-0500062021/related/mpo-gin.pdf"), with ⁠3.7 million of its 15.1 million people living on less than $4.20 per day.

Emmanuel in Conakry described the lengths he has to go to for safe drinking water, given the expense of buying it bottled.

"I pay CFA 3,000 [around €4.50] for a small bottle of water and CFA 500 [€0.75] for a water sachet of 400ml. I decided to collect rainwater and bought a product at the pharmacy to kill the bacteria it might contain and purify it."

Jonas from Dabola, in central Guinea, told RFI that nobody in his small town drinks the tap water provided by the national water company.

"It is as filthy as water in a pig's wallow. It contains bits of clay, and I have to filter it to bathe."

[Disappointment and anger after world fails to agree plastic pollution treaty](https://www.rfi.fr/en/environment/20250815-disappointment-and-anger-after-world-fails-to-agree-plastic-pollution-treaty "https://www.rfi.fr/en/environment/20250815-disappointment-and-anger-after-world-fails-to-agree-plastic-pollution-treaty")

Ben Youssouf Keita, a doctor who runs a medical centre in Conakry, told RFI there had been a rise in the number of patients with water-borne diseases after the ban was enforced in September.

"A lot of patients were admitted for abdominal pain and diarrhoea. After talking to them, we found out that they have been drinking water from boreholes, or tap water."

He welcomed the temporary pause in the ban, saying it could avert cases of typhoid or dysentery, adding: "Meanwhile, the government should launch an awareness campaign on the need to boil water wherever it comes from - rain, river, wells - before drinking it."

Alternative solutions

Following the lifting of the ban, factories producing single-use plastic water sachets have resumed their activities - for the next six months, at least.

Abdoulaye Fofana heads a water sachet production plant and is the chairman of the Union of Mineral Water Producers. He told RFI that the sector needs to quickly find environmentally friendly solutions.

"We are challenging our suppliers to find biodegradable plastics. In order, hopefully, to set up small companies for collecting and recycling the plastic. That should ensure a healthy, unpolluted [environment](https://www.rfi.fr/en/environment/ "https://www.rfi.fr/en/environment/")."

Abdoulaye heads up a small industrial sanitation company. He said that bags made of cassava fibre could replace plastic sachets.

"It is environmentally friendly because it is biodegradable and takes six months to disintegrate. Cassava is widely consumed in Guinea. This is an alternative that will give work to the farmers," he said.

However, the price of biodegradable sachets is far higher than that of [plastic](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/plastic/ "https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/plastic/") sachets.

In light of this, Mamady Aminata Touré, an environmental campaigner, is calling on the government to focus its efforts on developing the recycling sector.

"There aren't many companies involved in plastic processing and recycling in Guinea. We need to develop this sector and build confidence in these companies. And that's where the government has a role to play with incentives and subsidies."

For M'Bany Sidibé, head of the Union for the Defence of Consumers in Guinea, the best long-term solution is to develop the national water authority.

"It will take at least five to 10 years to get safe, drinking water across the whole of Guinea," he told RFI.

Sidibé warns that in the absence of an alternative that is as cheap as plastic water sachets, they will remain essential.

BRP Sarangani (6177) 于 2026 年 10 月 2 日受命加入菲律宾海岸警卫队。WPS 基金会照片

菲律宾马尼拉——周五，菲律宾海岸警卫队从台湾派来的新巡逻舰在棉兰老岛附近对中国海军辽宁舰航母战斗群进行了跟踪。

BRP_Sarangani_ (6177) 在巴西兰海峡跟踪 60,000 吨级的中国航母_辽宁_(16) 及其导弹驱逐舰护航舰_鞍山_(101)、_无锡_(104) 和_淮南_(123)，当地媒体 [_Bilyonaryo News Channel_](https://bnc.bilyonaryo.com/chinese-warships-transit-basilan-strait-shadowed-by-ph-vessels/news/)周六报道。据报道，菲律宾海军护卫舰 BRP _Diego Silang_ (FFG-7) 和巡逻舰 BRP _Emilio_ _Jacinto_(PS-35) 也观察到了辽宁舰。

此次护航是前台湾海岸警卫队管理局船只_金门_(123)（现为_萨兰加尼_）在菲律宾服役的首次公开任务。上个月，马尼拉海事安全机构通过“我们保护我们的海洋基金会”移交了这艘船，条件是该船不会在台湾附近或针对台湾使用。在 10 月 2 日该船试运行期间，PCG 表示“Sarangani”将驻扎在棉兰老岛。
本月早些时候，中国人民解放军海军打击群在东海[正式开始横跨西太平洋的训练活动](https://news.usni.org/2026/10/14/chinese-motive-strike-group-drills-in-the-philippine-sea)。 10月14日以来，辽宁舰先后绕日本琉球群岛、菲律宾海、吕宋海峡进入南海。在[过去两周](https://x.com/PhilippMonitor/status/2114564286047805726/photo/1)内，辽宁舰的航程已完成3次过境第一岛链。

2026年10月菲律宾海军对辽宁舰航母战斗群的监视和护航。菲律宾的新战略思路信息图

近年来，中国海军越来越多地利用苏禄海和南棉兰老岛的菲律宾群岛水域来过境第一岛链。中国的航母和间谍船曾利用这条航线进入菲律宾海，在澳大利亚周围进行训练活动和行动。

虽然菲律宾武装部队大部分现役部队驻扎在该地区，但马尼拉在棉兰老岛的态势重点是应对海盗和反叛乱等内部安全威胁。中国军舰和巡逻艇最近的出现推动了新部队的部署，以应对南部海域的常规威胁。
致力于监测中国军事活动和发展的组织“PLA Tracker”的创始人本·刘易斯表示，与菲律宾北部、台湾和日本南部之间的传统海上咽喉要道相比，棉兰老岛周围的水域可以提供另一条通往太平洋公海的鲜为人知的路线。

刘易斯告诉美国海军学院新闻：“吕宋海峡受到台湾、菲律宾、日本和美国的密切关注。苏禄海的关注度要低得多，这为解放军海军提供了进入太平洋的另一条途径，并让其船员熟悉这一地区。”

### [亚伦-马修·拉里奥萨](https://news.usni.org/author/amlariosa)

【原文 English Original】
BRP Sarangani (6177) was commissioned into the Philippine Coast Guard on Oct. 2, 2026. WPS Foundation photo

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine Coast Guard’s new patrol vessel from Taiwan shadowed the Chinese Navy’s Liaoning Carrier Strike Group on Friday off Mindanao.

BRP _Sarangani_ (6177) shadowed the 60,000-ton Chinese aircraft carrier _Liaoning_(16) and its guided-missile destroyer escorts _Anshan_(101), _Wuxi_(104) and _Huainan_(123) in the Basilan Strait, local media outlet [_Bilyonaryo News Channel_](https://bnc.bilyonaryo.com/chinese-warships-transit-basilan-strait-shadowed-by-ph-vessels/news/) reported Saturday. Philippine Navy frigate BRP _Diego Silang_ (FFG-7) and patrol vessel BRP _Emilio_ _Jacinto_(PS-35) also observed the Liaoning CSG, according to the report.

The escort is the first publicized tasking for the ex-Taiwan Coast Guard Administration vessel _Kinmen_(123) – now _Sarangani_ – in Philippine service. Transferred through the We Protect our Seas Foundation last month, Manila’s maritime security agency took possession of the vessel under the condition that it would not be used near or against Taiwan. During the vessel’s commissioning on Oct. 2, the PCG said that _Sarangani_ would be stationed in Mindanao.

The People’s Liberation Army Navy strike group [officially began training activities across the Western Pacific](https://news.usni.org/2026/10/14/chinese-carrier-strike-group-drills-in-the-philippine-sea) earlier this month in the East China Sea. Since Oct. 14, the Liaoning CSG has sailed around the Japanese Ryukyu Islands, into the Philippine Sea, through the Luzon Strait and into the South China Sea. Within the [last two weeks](https://x.com/PhilippMonitor/status/2114564286047805726/photo/1), the Liaoning CSG’s voyage has seen three First Island Chain transits.

Philippine naval monitoring and escort of the Liaoning Carrier Strike Group in October of 2026. New Strategic Thoughts for the Philippines infographic

In recent years, the PLAN has increasingly used Philippine archipelagic waters in the Sulu Sea and Southern Mindanao to transit the First Island Chain. Chinese aircraft carriers and spy ships have used the route to access the Philippine Sea for training activities and operations around Australia.

While the region hosts the bulk of the Armed Forces of the Philippines active forces, Manila’s posture in Mindanao is focused against internal security threats such as piracy and counter-insurgency. The recent appearance of Chinese warships and cutters has fueled the deployment of new units to face conventional threats in the southern waters.

Compared to the traditional maritime chokepoints between the Northern Philippines, Taiwan and Southern Japan, the waters around Mindanao can offer another less observed route into the open waters of the Pacific, according to Ben Lewis, founder of PLA Tracker, an organization dedicated to monitoring Chinese military activity and development.

“The Luzon Strait is heavily watched by Taiwan, the Philippines, Japan and the U.S. The Sulu Sea is much less so, which gives the PLAN another way into the Pacific and gets its crews familiar with it,” Lewis told USNI News.

content:
瑞士船舶电力公司 WinGD 已获得三项长期服务协议，涵盖 14 艘双燃料液化天然气运输船。与领先的液化天然气船舶管理公司签署的协议表明，行业对 OEM 主导的终身支持的信心不断增强，并标志着 WinGD 全球服务业务扩张取得了重大进展。

与中远海运液化天然气（香港）船舶管理公司、NYK 液化天然气船舶管理公司和 TMS 卡迪夫天然气公司签订的协议涵盖了采用不同代 WinGD X-DF 双燃料技术的船舶。这些合同反映了船东和运营商对长期服务合作伙伴关系日益增长的需求，这些合作伙伴关系在整个发动机生命周期中支持船舶性能、可靠性和运营效率。

WinGD 市场开发副总裁 Benny Hilström 表示：“这些协议表明运营商越来越重视原始发动机设计者提供的长期生命周期支持。

“液化天然气市场依赖于及时、可靠和安全的交付，因此支持全球贸易的船舶的性能至关重要。这些长期服务协议使我们的客户（一些航运界的知名企业）能够持续获得所需的专业知识、维护和技术支持，以保持其发动机在整个使用寿命期间可靠运行。
[![图片 2](https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Global-Service-by-WinGD_1.jpg)](https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Global-Service-by-WinGD_1.jpg)

WinGD 的全球服务汇集了知识、见解和全球服务网络来支持

“这些合作伙伴关系不仅仅是服务协议，还可以帮助客户最大限度地提高可靠性、效率和运营绩效，同时满足日益复杂的技术和监管要求。”

该服务包包括定期维护备件、技术人工、车间服务和咨询支持，以及通过 WinGD 的 WiDE 平台进行远程监控、故障排除和发动机优化。

[![图片3](https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/52324.jpg)](https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/52324.jpg)

将物理服务与持续的数字洞察相结合，可以根据每艘船舶的运营情况制定维护计划和发动机优化。

石油运输服务

最新协议扩大了 WinGD 在主要液化天然气运输市场的全球服务范围，并进一步加强了该公司不断增长的长期生命周期支持合同组合。
最近赢得的合同包括与中远海运液化天然气（香港）船舶管理公司签订的为期十年的协议，涵盖六艘由 WinGD 6X72DF 发动机提供动力的液化天然气运输船。
 WinGD 还与日本 NYK LNG Shipmanagement 签署了一份为期五年的服务协议，涵盖五艘液化天然气运输船的 10 台 X-DF 双燃料主发动机。该机队采用了几代 X-DF 技术。 HHI 和 SHI 分别于 2022 年和 2024 年建造的两艘船舶均由 WinGD 5X72DF 发动机提供动力，而 HHI 于 2025 年和 2026 年建造的三艘新船则配备了 5X72DF-2.1 发动机。

在世界主要船东和船舶管理市场之一的希腊，WinGD 签署了一份长期发动机服务协议，涵盖由雅典 TMS 卡迪夫天然气有限公司运营的三艘新建液化天然气运输船。

【原文 English Original】
Swiss marine power company WinGD has secured three long-term service agreements covering 14 dual-fuel LNG carriers. The agreements with leading LNG ship managers demonstrate growing industry confidence in OEM-led lifetime support and mark significant progress in the expansion of WinGD’s global service business.

The agreements with COSCO Shipping LNG (Hong Kong) Ship Management, NYK LNG Shipmanagement and TMS Cardiff Gas cover vessels powered by different generations of WinGD’s X-DF dual-fuel technology. The contracts reflect growing demand from owners and operators for long-term service partnerships that support vessel performance, reliability and operational efficiency throughout the engine lifecycle.

Benny Hilström VP Market Development at WinGD, said: “These agreements demonstrate the growing importance operators place on long-term lifecycle support from the original engine designer.

“LNG markets depend on timely, reliable and safe deliveries, making the performance of the vessels supporting this global trade critical. These long-term service agreements give our customers, some of the biggest names in shipping, consistent access to the expertise, maintenance and technical support needed to keep their engines performing reliably throughout their operational lives.

[![Image 2](https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Global-Service-by-WinGD_1.jpg)](https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Global-Service-by-WinGD_1.jpg)

Global Service by WinGD, brings together knowledge, insights and a worldwide service network to support

“More than service agreements, these partnerships help customers maximise reliability, efficiency and operational performance while navigating increasingly complex technical and regulatory requirements.”

The service package includes spare parts for scheduled maintenance, technical labour, workshop services and advisory support, alongside remote monitoring, troubleshooting and engine optimisation through WinGD’s WiDE platform.

[![Image 3](https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/52324.jpg)](https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/52324.jpg)

Combining physical service with continuous digital insight enables maintenance planning and engine optimisation tailored to each vessel’s operating profile.

Discover more

Market data reports

Economic news analysis

Oil transport services

The latest agreements expand Global Service by WinGD’s presence across major LNG shipping markets and further strengthen the company’s growing portfolio of long-term lifecycle support contracts.

The recent contract wins include a ten-year agreement with COSCO Shipping LNG (Hong Kong) Ship Management covering six LNG carriers powered by WinGD 6X72DF engines.
 WinGD has also signed a five-year service agreement with Japan’s NYK LNG Shipmanagement covering ten X-DF dual-fuel main engines across five LNG carriers. The fleet spans several generations of X-DF technology. Two vessels, built in 2022 and 2024 at HHI and SHI respectively, are powered by WinGD 5X72DF engines, while three newer vessels, built in 2025 and 2026 by HHI, are equipped with 5X72DF-2.1 engines.

In Greece, one of the world’s major shipowning and ship management markets, WinGD has signed a long-term engine service agreement covering three newbuild LNG carriers operated by Athens-based TMS Cardiff Gas Ltd. Built by HD Hyundai Samho in South Korea, the vessels are each equipped with two WinGD 5X72DF dual-fuel engines.

Carmelo Cartalemi, Head of Strategic Marketing of WinGD, said: “No one understands X-DF engines quite like the people who designed them. We’ve spent years developing these engines and working with customers to understand how they perform in service, across different vessels and operating conditions. That experience gives us a real advantage in supporting them throughout their lifetime.

“Through Global Service by WinGD, we bring together that knowledge, insights from digital monitoring and a worldwide service network to support LNG carrier operators wherever their vessels are operating. This is not an off-the-shelf service offering. Every vessel and operator has different requirements, and our understanding of the engines, their operating history and individual vessel needs allows us to anticipate challenges, inform maintenance decisions and provide targeted technical support wherever it is needed.”

Launched in 2025, Global Service by WinGD brings together more than 125 years of two-stroke engine design expertise with a worldwide network providing field service, technical support, spare parts and digital expertise. The service extends WinGD’s involvement beyond engine delivery, giving operators direct access to OEM knowledge and support throughout the operational lifecycle. The latest contract awards demonstrate the market’s growing recognition of the value of that approach.
 Source: WinGD

title: 海格塞斯将出席东盟防长扩大会议，预计再谈加强威慑和“责任分担”
summary: 华盛顿 — 美国战争部长皮特·海格塞斯(Pete Hegseth)将前往菲律宾，出席本星期晚些时候在菲律宾宿务举行的东盟防长扩大会议(ADMM-Plus)。美国战争部说，海格塞斯将重申，在太平洋地区，美国致力于以实力求和平战略。 根据战争部星期天(10月25日)发布的[新闻稿](https://www.war.gov/News/Advisories/Advisory/Article/4633052/secretary-of-war-pete-hegseth-to-visit-
content:
华盛顿 —

美国战争部长皮特·海格塞斯(Pete Hegseth)将前往菲律宾，出席本星期晚些时候在菲律宾宿务举行的东盟防长扩大会议(ADMM-Plus)。美国战争部说，海格塞斯将重申，在太平洋地区，美国致力于以实力求和平战略。

根据战争部星期天(10月25日)发布的[新闻稿](https://www.war.gov/News/Advisories/Advisory/Article/4633052/secretary-of-war-pete-hegseth-to-visit-the-philippines-and-participate-in-the-a/)，海格塞斯在会议期间将举行双边和多边会谈，以“加强威慑、推进关键联盟和伙伴关系，并扩大在该地区的责任分担”。

美国在2026年防务战略在谈到美国在亚太的政策时，明确地将盟友间强调“责任分担”列为核心支柱之一。

战争部的新闻稿没有具体说明海格塞斯将与何人会晤，但菲律宾和日本媒体报道说，菲律宾国防部长吉尔伯托·特奥多罗(Gilberto Teodoro Jr.)和日本防卫大臣小泉进次郎(Shinjirō Koizumi)预计都将与海格塞斯举行双边会晤。

菲律宾通讯社星期一援引特奥多罗的话说，他与海格塞斯一定会在东盟防长扩大会议期间举行双边会晤。“我肯定会与海格塞斯举行双边会晤和小组会议，而且我几乎会与所有相关方举行双边会晤。”

特奥多罗表示，他将与海格塞斯讨论“加强防务关系”等议题，目标是“(探讨)我们是否需要增加现有工作，是否需要加快、放缓或其他方面的进展”。

第13届东盟防长扩大会议(ADMM-Plus)和第20届东盟防长会议(ADMM)将于10月28日至29日在菲律宾宿务省拉普拉普市举行。东盟防长会议(ADMM)成立于2006年，是东盟最高级别的防务磋商与合作机制，而东盟防长扩大会议(ADMM-Plus)则于2010年启动，旨在扩大东盟成员国与美国、澳大利亚、印度、日本、新西兰、韩国、俄罗斯和中国等八国之间的区域防务对话与合作。

值得一提的是，星期一，在中国外交部的例行记者会上，在被问到中方是否会派高级别官员或代表团出席本周三在马尼拉举行的东盟防长扩大会时，中国外交部发言人郭嘉昆没有直接回答，却表示，“东盟防长扩大会理应为地区国家加强对话、增进互信、推动合作发挥积极作用。我们反对任何势力公器私用，绑架东盟，搅局生事。”

郭嘉昆没有说明谁可能会“公器私用、搅局生事”。菲律宾是2026年东盟的轮值主席国，特奥多罗上星期五公开表示，如果中国采取武力拖走非法“坐滩”在第二托马斯礁(中国称仁爱礁，菲律宾称阿云津礁)的“马德雷山”号军舰，或对该军舰采取武力行动，将构成针对菲律宾的“战争行为”。

特奥多罗还表示，在东盟防长会议期间，各国国防部长还将讨论区域安全、人道主义援助和灾害应对等问题。

特奥多罗在星期一还提到，菲律宾有可能与志同道合的国家扩大其访问部队地位协定(SOVFA)，以加强国际维和合作，提升军事互操作性，并在联合国的主持下推进集体安全努力。

“这也让我看到了加强关系的可能性，或许可以与那些与我们基本价值观一致的国家签署访问部队地位协定。”他说道。迄今为止，菲律宾已与五个国家签署了访问部队地位协定，分别是法国、加拿大、澳大利亚、日本和新西兰。

另一方面，日本防卫大臣小泉进次郎星期五表示，他正在安排下星期与美国战争部长海格塞斯会面，因为他正在考虑是否出席在菲律宾举行的东盟防长扩大会议。

《今日日本》报道援引消息人士的话说，如果小泉进次郎与海格塞斯会面，两人预计将讨论如何应对近期一名驻冲绳县美军士兵因涉嫌抢劫和谋杀被捕一事。日本媒体报道，日本冲绳县那霸地方检察厅星期天已经以抢劫杀人罪起诉驻日美国海军陆战队士兵德文·雅各布·巴拉德(Devin Jacob Ballard)。

title: 百家争鸣的悖论：思想繁盛何以催生王权专制（金陵钟）
summary: 2026-10-22 胡述安 万维网博客 在中外思想发展的普遍认知中，思想自由、学术争鸣往往是民主意识萌发、政治体制开放的重要推手，思想的多元碰撞终将推动社会治理的民主化、多元化发展。这是人类文明演进的通用逻辑，也是后世解读思想革新与政治变革关联的核心范式。但历史学家刘泽华在《中国的王权主义》中，抛出了一个颠覆常规认知的历史悖论：战国时代空前繁盛的百家争鸣，并未孕育出民主思想与民主政治，反而成为君主专制主义理论成熟、集权制度固化的核心推手，最终为秦朝大一统专制帝国的建立铺就
content: 2026-10-22  胡述安 万维网博客 在中外思想发展的普遍认知中，思想自由、学术争鸣往往是民主意识萌发、政治体制开放的重要推手，思想的多元碰撞终将推动社会治理的民主化、多元化发展。这是人类文明演进的通用逻辑，也是后世解读思想革新与政治变革关联的核心范式。但历史学家刘泽华在《中国的王权主义》中，抛出了一个颠覆常规认知的历史悖论：战国时代空前繁盛的百家争鸣，并未孕育出民主思想与民主政治，反而成为君主专制主义理论成熟、集权制度固化的核心推手，最终为秦朝大一统专制帝国的建立铺就了思想与制度基石。这一看似矛盾的历史现象，撕开了先秦诸子思想的底层底色，也揭示了中国早期政治文明独特的发展轨迹。   春秋战国是中国历史上思想最自由、学术最繁荣的时代。周王室衰微，礼乐崩坏，宗法分封制逐步瓦解，旧的思想桎梏被打破，士人阶层崛起，各家学派纷纷著书立说、周游列国、辩难争鸣，构建起 “ 百家争鸣 ” 的文化盛世。世人向来将这场思想盛宴视为中国古代思想解放的巅峰，认为其彰显了思想自由的价值，蕴含着朴素的民本与平等理念。然而拨开表层的思想繁盛，深入诸子学说的核心逻辑便会发现，这场跨越数百年的学术争鸣，从根源上从未跳出君主制度的框架，所有思想辩论的终极目的，从来不是颠覆王权、革新体制，而是优化、完善、强化君主统治。   刘泽华精准点明了这一历史悖论的核心症结：战国诸子的思想交锋，从未涉及 “ 是否需要君主制 ”“ 以何种制度取代君主制 ” 的根本性体制探讨。除农家等极少数学派曾隐晦质疑君主集权、倡导均平民生、挑战既定王权秩序外，道、儒、墨、法等所有主流学派，都将君主专制制度作为不可动摇的理论前提与社会基石。各家学派争鸣的核心议题，不是要不要王权，而是如何更好地构建王权、巩固王权、治理天下。这场声势浩大的思想竞赛，本质上是一场 “ 君主治理方案的优化比拼 ” ，而非政治体制的革新博弈。   主流学派的思想内核，无一例外都是王权主义的理论延伸，只是治理路径与统治手段各不相同。儒家以 “ 仁政 ”“ 礼治 ” 为核心，构建了以德辅政的君主统治体系。孔子倡导 “ 君君、臣臣、父父、子子 ” ，严格界定君臣尊卑秩序，强调君主的道德表率作用，主张君主以礼制约束天下、教化万民。孟子的 “ 民贵君轻 ” 历来被视作古代民本思想的典范，但深究其意，其核心并非限制君权、赋予民众政治权利，而是告诫君主 “ 得民心者得天下 ” ，是为君主长治久安提供的治国策略，本质上服务于君主统治的稳固。荀子更是直接为集权秩序背书，提出人性本恶，需要君主 “ 起礼义，制法度 ” ，以王权权威矫饰人性、规整社会，直接将礼制改造为君主专制的统治工具。   墨家的思想看似平民化、平等化，实则同样依附于王权体系。墨子倡导 “ 兼爱 ”“ 非攻 ”“ 尚同 ” ，否定贵族世袭的等级特权，却极力推崇自上而下的绝对秩序。 “ 尚同 ” 思想要求百姓、士人、官员层层向上认同，最终统归于君主意志，实现天下思想、政令、行动的绝对统一。这种思想消解了民间的多元诉求，弱化了社会的自主空间，极大强化了君主的思想统治权与政治主导权，为中央集权的形成提供了思想支撑。   道家以 “ 无为而治 ” 著称，看似疏离政治、主张放任自治，实则是另一种君主治理的智慧范式。老子提出的 “ 治大国若烹小鲜 ” ，并非否定君主权威，而是倡导君主减少过度扰民的苛政，以简约治理实现天下安定。其核心目的是规避苛政引发的社会动荡，维护王权统治的长久稳定，本质上仍是服务于君主专制的治国方略，从未动摇君主制度的根本。   而法家更是君主专制主义的集大成者，直接将王权集权理论推向极致。商鞅、韩非等法家代表摒弃道德教化，以人性好利为底层逻辑，主张君主以法、术、势驾驭群臣、管控天下。法家明确否定贵族分权、民间自治，主张君主独掌立法、行政、司法、军事所有权力，构建绝对的中央集权体系。相较于其他学派，法家的理论最贴合战国诸侯富国强兵、集权争霸的现实需求，成为各国强化君主专制的核心指导思想，也为秦朝大一统专制制度的建立提供了完整的理论体系。 正是这种 “ 全员默认君主制、各派优化君主制 ” 的争鸣逻辑，造就了独特的历史走向。百家争鸣的思想自由，没有转化为约束君权、开放民权的政治力量，反而通过多元的思想碰撞，从道德、制度、治理、思想、秩序等各个维度，填补了君主专制体系的理论空白。各家学派取长补短、相互辩驳、相互融合，不断完善王权统治的理论体系，让君主专制从早期简陋的王权制度，逐步发展为体系完备、逻辑严密、适配性极强的成熟政治模式。每一次学术辩难，都是对君主治理体系的一次打磨；每一种思想流派的传播，都是对王权合法性、合理性的一次论证。   思想的演变与现实政治的发展高度同频。战国数百年间，各诸侯国依托诸子治国理论，不断削弱贵族势力、强化君主集权、完善官僚体系、集中国家权力，君主专制制度在各国持续落地、不断强化。从列国各自的集权改革，到思想理论的高度统一，最终在秦朝实现汇总，形成了中国历史上第一个高度集中的君主专制大一统王朝。可以说，秦朝的专制制度并非偶然诞生，而是战国百家争鸣长期塑造、层层铺垫的必然结果。   厘清这一历史悖论，是读懂中国传统政治思想的关键。后世常将百家争鸣视为中国古代民主思想的源头，但刘泽华的王权主义研究打破了这一认知误区。先秦诸子的民本思想、仁爱理念、自治智慧，始终依附于王权框架之下，民本不等于民主，治民不等于民权。所有思想的核心落脚点，都是 “ 如何让君主更好地治理百姓、稳固天下 ” ，而非 “ 如何保障民众权利、限制君主权力 ” 。   这场跨越百年的思想盛宴，最终没有开出民主自由的果实，反而孕育出成熟的君主专制文明，深刻塑造了此后两千余年中国传统政治的核心底色。 王权至上、集权统一、君权主导的政治逻辑，贯穿了中国古代社会的发展历程，而其思想根源，正藏于战国百家争鸣这场特殊的思想革新之中。 读懂这一悖论，方能跳出传统认知的局限，真正洞悉中国传统政治思想的本质，理解中国古代政治文明独特的发展脉络与历史基因。

title: 王丹：是時候可以討論後習時代了
