title: Former Japanese PM Fukuda, Dove Who Engaged Korea and China, Dies at 90
summary: Former Japanese Prime Minister Yasuo Fukuda. Yonhap News Yasuo Fukuda, the former Japanese prime minister credited with working to improve relations with South Korea, China and other Asian nations, has died at the age of 90. The Liberal Dem
content:
Former Japanese Prime Minister Yasuo Fukuda. Yonhap News

Yasuo Fukuda, the former Japanese prime minister credited with working to improve relations with South Korea, China and other Asian nations, has died at the age of 90.

The Liberal Democratic Party said Fukuda died of heart failure at a Tokyo hospital on the 22nd, according to Kyodo News and the Nihon Keizai Shimbun on the 26th.

Fukuda took office as prime minister in September 2007 and served for one year until September 2008. The son of former Prime Minister Takeo Fukuda, he became the first son of a prime minister to hold the office in Japan's constitutional history.

He entered politics in 1990, winning a seat in the House of Representatives at age 53 as a candidate in the former Gunma No. 3 district, and was reelected seven consecutive times. He joined the Cabinet for the first time in 2000, serving as chief cabinet secretary under Prime Minister Yoshiro Mori.

Fukuda was regarded as a leading dove, or moderate, within the LDP who consistently stressed the importance of diplomacy toward Asia. Shortly after taking office as prime minister, asked by reporters about visits to the Yasukuni Shrine, he replied, "Is there any need to do something the other side dislikes?" During his tenure as chief cabinet secretary in the Junichiro Koizumi Cabinet, he served as the channel of communication with South Korea and China as they protested the prime minister's shrine visits, and grappled with how to respond.

His connection to South Korea dates back to his father's time as prime minister. Takeo Fukuda helped persuade Japanese political and business circles to allow the late POSCO Honorary Chairman Park Tae-joon to use funds from Japan's postwar claims settlement to build a steel mill. Fukuda himself also built extensive networks in South Korean political and government circles and took the lead in improving ties.

At a 2008 summit with then-President Lee Myung-bak, Fukuda emphasized building a future-oriented relationship between the two countries. That same year, when Chinese President Hu Jintao visited Japan rather than South Korea, the two sides agreed to develop a "mutually beneficial strategic relationship." In 2009, after leaving office, he attended the state funeral of former President Roh Moo-hyun as head of the Japanese delegation of mourners and was present at the memorial service.

In September 2024, he attended a memorial ceremony for victims of the Kanto Massacre held at the Korean Cultural Center in Tokyo, where he said "the killing of Koreans is a historical fact" and raised the need for a joint South Korea-Japan investigation. The remarks drew praise as confronting history without compromising with right-wing views in Japan.

Even after retiring from politics by declining to run in the 2012 House of Representatives election, Fukuda worked to find openings in the frozen relationship between Japan and China. In 2014, as tensions escalated over the Senkaku Islands, known in China as the Diaoyu Islands, he made a secret trip to China and met President Xi Jinping, laying the groundwork for a meeting between Xi and then-Prime Minister Shinzo Abe.

After stepping down as prime minister, he repeatedly voiced his conviction that politics stirring nationalism by invoking the China threat is dangerous. At an August 2017 news conference, he said, "As long as Japan does not act in a hostile manner, China will place importance on relations with Japan." During a visit to China in June 2018, he visited the Nanjing Massacre Memorial Hall, laid flowers for the victims and observed a moment of silence.

According to Kyodo News, Fukuda recently told those around him of his concern that "if Japan and China display hostility toward each other, public opinion on both sides could overheat and spiral out of control. It could even lead to war."

title: Kim Jong-un's Dandong visit is wake-up call for S. Korea-US-Japan partnership
summary: Chun In-bum By **Chun In-bum** North Korean leader Kim Jong-un’s Oct. 24 visit to Dandong, China, and his meeting with Wang Huning should not be dismissed as another diplomatic ceremony. It was a carefully staged demonstration of strengthen
content:
Chun In-bum

By **Chun In-bum**

North Korean leader Kim Jong-un’s Oct. 24 visit to Dandong, China, and his meeting with Wang Huning should not be dismissed as another diplomatic ceremony. It was a carefully staged demonstration of strengthening relations between Beijing and Pyongyang. More importantly, it should serve as a warning to the United States, South Korea and Japan that the strategic environment in Northeast Asia is changing.

Wang Huning is not an ordinary Chinese official. He ranks fourth in the Chinese Communist Party hierarchy and serves as chairman of the Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference. A former professor at Fudan University, Wang has been one of China’s most influential political thinkers and strategists, advising three successive leaders: Jiang Zemin, Hu Jintao and Xi Jinping.

Few Chinese officials have enjoyed such sustained influence across three administrations. Wang has helped shape the ideological foundations of modern Chinese governance. His involvement in Kim’s visit, including conveying Chinese President Xi’s personal greetings, underscores the political significance Beijing attaches to its relationship with North Korea.

Equally important was Kim’s crossing of the recently opened New Amnok River Bridge connecting the Chinese border city of Dandong with North Korea's Sinuiju. Completed in 2014, the bridge remained unused for approximately 12 years before opening this October. Its four lanes and modern infrastructure provide new opportunities for transportation, trade and economic cooperation. The bridge is more than concrete and steel. It is a political statement. China and North Korea are signaling their intention to expand economic engagement. The opening of the bridge could facilitate the movement of industrial equipment, raw materials, energy products and other goods essential to North Korea’s economy.

This raises an uncomfortable question: What remains of the international sanctions regime against North Korea?

United Nations sanctions have not formally ended. Nevertheless, sanctions are effective only when major countries enforce them. If China expands economic cooperation while Russia continues its military relationship with Pyongyang, the practical effectiveness of international pressure could be seriously weakened. The international community must distinguish between sanctions that exist on paper and sanctions that actually influence North Korean behavior.

There is another dimension to this development. North Korea is strengthening its relations with both China and Russia. These relationships are not identical. China provides North Korea with its principal economic lifeline, while Russia has become an increasingly important military partner. Together, these relationships could give Pyongyang greater strategic flexibility and reduce its incentive to negotiate seriously over its nuclear weapons. This is a serious development for the United States and its allies.

However, the challenge is not exclusively military. Economic dependence has become a strategic vulnerability, and South Korea provides a clear example. China remains an enormous market for South Korean businesses and an important supplier of industrial materials, components, and critical minerals. South Korea cannot simply abandon this economic relationship without significant consequences for its industries and national economy. At the same time, South Korea relies on foreign suppliers for essential energy resources, including nuclear fuel. Russia has been a significant supplier of enriched uranium used in South Korea’s civilian nuclear power industry. These dependencies create potential vulnerabilities during periods of international confrontation.

The United States frequently encourages its allies to reduce their strategic dependence on China and Russia. That objective is understandable. But Washington must recognize that economic independence cannot be achieved through political declarations alone. If America expects its allies to diversify away from potentially unreliable suppliers, it must help provide practical alternatives.

This means expanding cooperation in critical minerals, advanced manufacturing, energy security and nuclear fuel supplies. It also means strengthening investment, encouraging reliable supply chains and accepting that economic security requires long-term commitments. America cannot expect its allies to assume substantial economic risks without helping them manage the consequences.

Equally important is the relationship between South Korea and Japan. The two countries are democratic, economically advanced and closely allied with the United States. They face many of the same security challenges, particularly North Korea’s nuclear weapons and missile capabilities.

Yet historical disagreements continue to undermine political trust. Japan must recognize that historical sensitivities among Koreans are real and cannot simply be dismissed as outdated nationalism. Japan’s colonial rule over Korea remains an important part of Korean historical memory. Symbolic gestures by Japanese political leaders matter. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s offerings to Yasukuni Shrine, where convicted Class-A war criminals are enshrined alongside Japan’s war dead, create unnecessary tensions.

Japan has every right to remember those who died in its service. But its leaders should find ways to honor their dead without reopening historical wounds among neighboring countries. Such gestures are particularly unhelpful when regional security cooperation is becoming more important. South Korea also has responsibilities. Koreans must recognize that legitimate historical grievances cannot become a permanent obstacle to necessary security cooperation. Geography, economic interdependence and shared security interests make cooperation with Japan indispensable.

Neither country needs to forget its history. Both must understand that protecting their future requires practical cooperation today. This cooperation should include intelligence sharing, missile defense coordination, maritime security, supply-chain resilience and closer communication between political and military leaders.

The United States has a particularly important responsibility in making this possible. American leadership in Northeast Asia is urgently needed, but leadership means more than maintaining military forces or demanding increased defense spending from allies. It requires consistent diplomatic engagement, credible security commitments and a willingness to help allies overcome political and economic obstacles.

Washington must understand that strengthening the U.S.–South Korea alliance and the U.S.–Japan alliance separately is not enough. It must also encourage a durable relationship between Seoul and Tokyo. The three countries do not have to agree on every political issue. But they must recognize that their security interests are closely connected.

China and North Korea are strengthening their relationship. Russia continues to deepen its cooperation with Pyongyang. These developments do not necessarily mean that Beijing, Moscow and Pyongyang constitute a unified military alliance. Their interests differ, and those differences should not be ignored. Nevertheless, their growing cooperation presents challenges that deserve serious attention.

Kim’s visit to Dandong should therefore be understood as more than a bilateral diplomatic event. It is a reminder that economic relationships, military cooperation and political symbolism are increasingly intertwined. The United States, South Korea and Japan must respond with greater strategic coordination, not complacency or unnecessary confrontation

Military deterrence remains essential. But deterrence without economic resilience, political trust and sustained American leadership will not be sufficient to preserve stability in Northeast Asia.

_Chun In-bum is the former commander of the Republic of Korea Army Special Warfare Command._

title: What Chinese State Council Order No. 841 Means for EB-5 Migration Agents, Regional Centers, and Issuers
summary: #### The China Channel Gets a Regulator ##### _What State Council Order No. 841 Means for EB-5 Migration Agents, Regional Centers, and Issuers_ _**By: Osvaldo F. Torres, Esq. | Torres Law PA**_ On July 22, 2026, Premier Li Qiang signed Stat
content:
#### The China Channel Gets a Regulator

##### _What State Council Order No. 841 Means for EB-5 Migration Agents, Regional Centers, and Issuers_

_**By: Osvaldo F. Torres, Esq. | Torres Law PA**_

On July 22, 2026, Premier Li Qiang signed State Council Order No. 841, promulgating the Regulations of the State Council on Exit and Entry Administration (the “Regulation”), which took effect on September 15, 2026.[[1]](https://iiusa.org/what-chinese-state-council-order-no-841-means-for-eb-5/#_ftn1) Most early commentary from the international trade bar has focused on Article 4, which authorizes the Ministry of Commerce and other authorities to bar Chinese citizens from leaving China for export-control and technology-transfer violations.[[2]](https://iiusa.org/what-chinese-state-council-order-no-841-means-for-eb-5/#_ftn2) That provision deserves attention, but for the EB-5 industry the more consequential text sits a few articles later.

Articles 7 through 13 create a national filing and conduct regime for “outbound and inbound intermediary services,” defined to include policy consultation, document processing, and procedure handling on behalf of persons leaving or entering China. That description fits the day-to-day work of the Chinese migration agencies that introduce investors to EB-5 offerings, assemble source-of-funds files, and coordinate with U.S. counsel. Mainland China has long been the largest single source of EB-5 capital, and the migration agent remains the principal channel through which that capital reaches U.S. projects. A new regulatory layer on that channel therefore reaches, directly or indirectly, most regional centers and new commercial enterprises (NCEs) that raise capital in China.

This article summarizes the intermediary provisions, identifies where they intersect with U.S. securities and EB-5 compliance obligations, and suggests practical steps for sponsors before the first filing deadline in December.

#### The Intermediary Framework in Brief

The Regulation implements the Exit and Entry Administration Law, which took effect in 2013. According to official explanatory remarks, one of its three stated objectives is to improve regulation of the immigration intermediary service market.[[3]](https://iiusa.org/what-chinese-state-council-order-no-841-means-for-eb-5/#_ftn3) The Regulation pursues that objective through four mechanisms.

**Mandatory filing.** Agencies providing intermediary services must file with the local immigration administration within 15 days of establishment. Individual practitioners are filed through their agencies.[[4]](https://iiusa.org/what-chinese-state-council-order-no-841-means-for-eb-5/#_ftn4) Agencies already operating before September 15, 2026 must complete the filing within 90 days, which is on or about December 14, 2026.[[5]](https://iiusa.org/what-chinese-state-council-order-no-841-means-for-eb-5/#_ftn5) The National Immigration Administration, working with the State Council’s market-supervision authorities, is charged with issuing detailed filing measures, and none had been published as of this writing.[[6]](https://iiusa.org/what-chinese-state-council-order-no-841-means-for-eb-5/#_ftn6)

**Qualification standards.** Article 8 requires that an agency be lawfully established; that its legal representative not have been criminally punished for an intentional crime; that it have staff with professional knowledge of exit-entry law and policy, together with funds and premises proportionate to its services; that client-facing staff not have been convicted of intentional crimes endangering national security, public safety, or border administration; and that it maintain management systems covering personnel, training, data preservation, data security, and compliance.[[7]](https://iiusa.org/what-chinese-state-council-order-no-841-means-for-eb-5/#_ftn7) Two further provisions in Article 8 matter most for EB-5, and are discussed below. First, agencies engaged in outbound services “should also have established cooperative relationships with relevant overseas service agencies or signed valid letters of intent for cooperation.” Second, “[f]oreign companies and institutions are prohibited from providing outbound and inbound intermediary services within China.”

**Prohibited conduct.** Article 10 bars intermediaries from (i) publishing false information or soliciting clients through “exaggerated or misleading publicity”; (ii) providing false materials or helping others obtain visas, residence permits, or other documents illegally; (iii) disclosing, selling, or illegally providing trade secrets, personal privacy, or personal information learned in the course of their services; (iv) operating beyond the scope of their registration; (v) organizing or assisting cross-border illegal activity; and (vi) other acts that endanger national security or disrupt exit-entry order. Article 9 directs immigration authorities, together with the commerce, education, human resources, market supervision, and other departments, to supervise intermediaries and to publish information on violations and adverse records.[[8]](https://iiusa.org/what-chinese-state-council-order-no-841-means-for-eb-5/#_ftn8)

**Penalties.** An agency that fails to file or does not meet the Article 8 conditions will be ordered to rectify. If it refuses, it faces fines of RMB 5,000 to 10,000 and suspension; in serious cases, fines of RMB 10,000 to 50,000 and revocation of its business license. Article 10 violations carry confiscation of illegal gains and a fine of one to five times those gains where they exceed RMB 20,000, or RMB 20,000 to 50,000 otherwise, along with possible suspension or license revocation and fines of RMB 10,000 to 50,000 on directly responsible managers. Issuing false invitation letters or supporting materials is separately fined under Article 11. Article 16 requires immigration authorities to maintain open reporting channels, and Article 17 preserves criminal liability.[[9]](https://iiusa.org/what-chinese-state-council-order-no-841-means-for-eb-5/#_ftn9)

The monetary penalties are modest by U.S. standards. The reputational and operational consequences, however, can be significant. Public adverse records, suspension, and license revocation could each remove an agent from the market in the middle of an offering.

#### Why It Matters for EB-5 Sponsors

##### 1. Cooperation agreements put U.S. sponsors in the Chinese record

Because Article 8 expects outbound agencies to show a cooperative relationship or letter of intent with an overseas service provider, Chinese agents will likely ask their U.S. counterparties to sign one. In EB-5, that counterparty is usually the regional center or NCE, and sometimes U.S. immigration counsel. Some agents may present short-form documents drafted for submission to Chinese authorities rather than the negotiated agent agreement.

Sponsors should treat these documents as offering-related materials. A cooperation letter that describes the sponsor’s program, the agent’s role, or the investment’s features in terms that differ from the private placement memorandum creates a second, inconsistent record, and one that now sits in a government file. Any such document should be reviewed by securities counsel, conform to the agent agreement and the offering documents, and avoid statements about returns, visa outcomes, government endorsement, or the sponsor’s regulatory status.

##### 2. The foreign-firm prohibition limits direct-to-investor models

Article 8 prohibits foreign companies and institutions from providing intermediary services within China. The Regulation does not define the boundary between “outbound policy consultation” and adjacent activities. A U.S. sponsor’s staff, or even a U.S.-licensed immigration attorney, explaining EB-5 eligibility, the I-526E process, or conditional residence to prospective investors at an in-China seminar could plausibly be characterized as the former.

Structures that warrant review include representative offices or wholly foreign-owned enterprises of U.S. regional centers, roadshows and seminars led by U.S. personnel, China offices of U.S. law firms that advise on immigration process, and hybrid models in which a U.S. sponsor effectively runs a domestic agent’s client service. The prohibition could also limit the participation of regional centers and U.S. immigration law firms in conferences and events in China, including those organized by Chinese organizations such as provincial exit-entry associations. The sale of an interest in a U.S. limited partnership is conceptually distinct from an immigration intermediary service. In EB-5, however, the two are marketed together, and Chinese authorities may not separate them. The offering of foreign securities in China also raises its own PRC securities and foreign-exchange questions that fall outside this Regulation.

Until the implementing measures clarify scope, the conservative approach is to have in-China immigration consulting performed by filed domestic agencies, to confine U.S. personnel to activities that PRC counsel has confirmed fall outside Article 8, and to document that analysis.

##### 3. The misleading-publicity ban converges with U.S. antifraud standards

Article 10(i)’s prohibition on “exaggerated or misleading publicity” reaches the marketing claims that have repeatedly caused trouble in EB-5: “guaranteed” green cards, “guaranteed” return of capital, implied U.S. government backing, and understated risks or timelines. Those claims already expose issuers and anyone who makes them to liability under Section 17(a) of the Securities Act and Rule 10b-5.[[10]](https://iiusa.org/what-chinese-state-council-order-no-841-means-for-eb-5/#_ftn10) They also implicate the [Reform and Integrity Act’s](https://www.congress.gov/117/plaws/publ103/PLAW-117publ103.pdf) promoter provisions and the regional center’s obligation to oversee persons involved in its offerings.[[11]](https://iiusa.org/what-chinese-state-council-order-no-841-means-for-eb-5/#_ftn11)

The practical change is that agent misstatements now carry regulatory risk in China as well as the United States, and Chinese enforcement may produce a public adverse record. Migration agents may respond by curtailing their EB-5 marketing, particularly on social media platforms such as WeChat, to reduce the risk of an Article 10(i) violation. Sponsors should plan for that possibility in their fundraising timelines. They should also require agents to use only sponsor-approved materials, including reviewed Chinese-language translations; prohibit agent-generated summaries of offering terms; keep copies of all materials in circulation; and add the Article 9 adverse-record publications to their periodic diligence on agents.

##### 4. Screening for public officials and military personnel

The final paragraph of Article 10 directs that where public officials, military personnel, or other individuals entrust agencies to “illegally process foreign nationality, permanent residency status abroad, foreign residency documents, or other outbound and inbound documents or procedures,” the agency “shall not process such applications and shall promptly report such cases to supervisory authorities.”[[12]](https://iiusa.org/what-chinese-state-council-order-no-841-means-for-eb-5/#_ftn12) An EB-5 petition is, by definition, a step toward permanent residence abroad. The qualifier “illegally” matters: the provision appears aimed at persons whose positions restrict foreign residency, not at emigration generally.

The provision has two consequences for sponsors. First, investor pipelines may narrow because agents are likely to decline clients who hold, or recently held, government, military, or state-enterprise positions subject to restrictions on foreign residency. Second, an investor’s file may be reported to Chinese authorities before it reaches USCIS. Sponsors should add a representation on public-official and military status to s

title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on October 26, 2026
summary: At the invitation of Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Minister of Foreign Affairs Wang Yi, Minister for Foreign Affairs of Iceland Þorgerður Katrín Gunnarsdóttir will visit China from October 26 to 31. **CCTV:
content:
At the invitation of Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Minister of Foreign Affairs Wang Yi, Minister for Foreign Affairs of Iceland Þorgerður Katrín Gunnarsdóttir will visit China from October 26 to 31.

**CCTV: China released the Progress Report on the AI Capacity-Building Action Plan for Good and for All at the 2026 Global Governance Forum (Xiong’an). How does China see the role of AI capacity-building in global governance?**

Guo Jiakun: Artificial intelligence is an emerging field in global governance, and a litmus test for the effectiveness of the global governance system. The global governance system would not become more just and equitable without the collective capacity enhancement of the Global South, and requires concrete efforts to strengthen the representation and voice of developing countries. China advocates for respecting the digital sovereignty of all countries. We believe that every country has the right to possess the foundational capabilities for independent AI development, and to seek a development path suited to its national conditions and practical needs, one that enables AI to be applied in real-world scenarios, address real problems, and generate sustained value.

As a responsible major country, China remains committed to providing global public goods in the field of AI. In 2024, China promoted the adoption of a UN General Assembly resolution on enhancing international cooperation on capacity-building of artificial intelligence, established the Group of Friends for International Cooperation on AI Capacity-Building, and released the AI Capacity-Building Action Plan for Good and for All. Over the past two years, China has taken major steps and practical measures to honor its commitment in advancing the above-mentioned initiative. Recently, at the 2026 Global Governance Forum (Xiong’an), China released the Progress Report on the AI Capacity-Building Action Plan for Good and for All, which systematically reviews the cooperation outcomes, practical experience and specific cases since the Action Plan was launched two years ago. The report identifies access to technology as the starting point and independent development as the goal, stresses the importance of demand-driven approaches, joint consultation and co-development for project delivery, and calls for promoting openness and open source and advancing AI models, data, and talent in a coordinated manner.

Looking ahead, we welcome more countries to join the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization, to explore more pathways for international cooperation on AI capacity-building, and to promote global AI development for good and for all with concrete actions.

**Brasil de Fato: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has just won the reelection. Does the Chinese foreign ministry have a comment or message regarding the outcome of this election and the prospect of China-Brazil relations on Lula’s next term? (Similar question from UOL of Brazil)**

Guo Jiakun: China takes note of the announcement by Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court of President Lula’s runoff victory and extends congratulations on that. China stands ready to work with Brazil to advance the building of the China-Brazil community with a shared future.

**Asahi Shimbun: Former Japanese Prime Minister Yasuo Fukuda just passed away. What’s your comment?**

Guo Jiakun: We express deep condolences and grief over former Prime Minister Yasuo Fukuda’s passing and heartfelt sympathies to his family.

Mr. Yasuo Fukuda is an old friend of the Chinese people, who actively contributed to the improvement and development of China-Japan relations. He has long been committed to the friendship between our two countries, and held a correct view of history. During his tenure as prime minister, China and Japan signed the fourth political document. After leaving office, he visited the Memorial Hall of the Victims in Nanjing Massacre. What’s more, he served for many years as Chairman of the Boao Forum for Asia, playing an important role in facilitating exchanges and cooperation in Asia.

Mr. Yasuo Fukuda once noted that the four political documents between China and Japan stipulated the principles governing bilateral relations, which we must bear in mind and never deviate from. Those firm and important remarks reflected the honor and responsibility of Japan’s statesman of the older generation and should evoke self-reflection and soul-searching among those currently running the Japanese government.

**AFP: Just following up on Brazil, Bolsonaro has called for those election results to be annulled. Does China have a comment on that?**

Guo Jiakun: China respects the choice of the Brazilian people.

**People’s Daily: On October 23, Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Foreign Minister Wang Yi announced at the opening ceremony of the Global Governance Forum (Xiong’an) that China would issue a Position on Strengthening Outer Space Governance. Could you offer more information?**

Guo Jiakun: Outer space is the common frontier of all humanity and space exploration is humanity’s common endeavor. As announced by Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Foreign Minister Wang Yi at the opening ceremony of the Global Governance Forum (Xiong’an), China has issued its Position on Strengthening Outer Space Governance. This is a major step by China to deliver on the four major global initiatives and advance efforts in building a community with a shared future for humanity in outer space.

The position paper takes the common values of humanity as the fundamental guidance and advocates that the development and security, as well as the stability and sustainability of outer space, should be pursued in a balanced way. It proposes that we should commit to openness and shared benefit, abide by the international rule of law, respect the rights of all States, advance innovation and development, safeguard common security, prevent armed conflicts, reduce misunderstanding and misperception, regulate commercial space activity, deepen international cooperation, and promote global governance.

The position paper outlines constructive approaches to address issues of common concern including development, security and governance in outer space, and provides a blueprint for relevant discussions and formulation of rules by the international community. China will continue working together with all parties in an open and constructive spirit to ensure that the outcomes of space development better benefit all humanity.

**China Daily: To follow up on Icelandic Foreign Minister Gunnarsdóttir’s upcoming visit you just announced, how does China see the current state of China-Iceland relations? What are your expectations for the visit?**

Guo Jiakun: We welcome Foreign Minister Gunnarsdóttir to visit China. China-Iceland relations have enjoyed sound momentum of growth in recent years. In 2025, when President Tómasdóttir was in China for the Global Leaders’ Meeting on Women, President Xi met with her and they reached important common understandings on deepening cooperation in such areas as economy and trade, geothermal energy, and people-to-people and cultural exchanges. As we mark the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic ties between China and Iceland this year, the Chinese side looks forward to in-depth exchanges with the Icelandic side on bilateral relations and international and regional issues of mutual interest to further enhance trust, advance cooperation and renew our friendship.

**Yonhap News Agency: General Secretary of the Workers’ Party of Korea (WPK) and President of the State Affairs of the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) Kim Jong Un visited Dandong, China last week. Was the visit proposed by China or the DPRK? Can you share more information on this visit?**

Guo Jiakun: On October 24, Member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and Chairman of the National Committee of the Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC) Wang Huning accompanied General Secretary of the WPK and President of the State Affairs of the DPRK Kim Jong Un on a visit to Dandong. Wang Huning conveyed General Secretary of the Central Committee of the CPC and President Xi Jinping’s cordial greetings and best wishes to Kim Jong Un. China released a readout, which you may refer to.

China and the DPRK are friendly neighbors. It is an unswerving strategic policy of the CPC and the Chinese government to maintain, consolidate and develop China-DPRK relations. The sound and steady development of the China-DPRK traditional friendly cooperative ties is in the interest of both peoples and conducive to regional peace, stability, development and prosperity. China stands ready to work with the DPRK to deliver on the important common understandings of the two heads of state and further advance bilateral ties.

**Reuters: Regarding the ASEAN Defense Ministers’ Meeting Plus that will be held from this Wednesday in Manila, will China be participating in that meeting? Whether it’s sending high-level officials or delegation?**

Guo Jiakun: The ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting Plus is meant to play a positive role in enabling regional countries to step up dialogue, increase trust and promote cooperation. We oppose attempts by anyone to use this platform to seek selfish gains, hijack ASEAN and create trouble.

**AFP: The United States last week designated the Confucius Institute Cultural Centers on American universities and campuses as a threat to U.S. national security, would China like to comment?**

Guo Jiakun: We reject vilification and smears against Confucius Institute. Educational exchange and cooperation between China and the U.S. help enhance mutual understanding between the peoples of the two countries. They are desired by both sides and benefit both sides and should not be held back or disrupted.

**Beijing Youth Daily: Yesterday, the 25th of October, is the eighth Anti-Sanctions Day designated by the Southern African Development Community. Zimbabwe recently held commemorative events and called for the immediate removal of the illegal sanctions imposed by Western countries. What’s your comment?**

Guo Jiakun: China supports Zimbabwe in commemorating the Anti-Sanctions Day.

The illegal sanctions imposed by certain Western countries on Zimbabwe have lasted for over 20 years. The practice is a typical example of hegemonism. It seriously violates Zimbabwe’s national sovereignty, undermines Zimbabwean people’s right to development, and hurts international fairness and justice. China has supported the just aspiration of Zimbabwe and other African friends in various ways for eight consecutive years. China solemnly calls on certain Western countries to immediately remove the illegal sanctions imposed on Zimbabwe, and take responsible and concrete actions to develop the economy and improve people’s livelihoods there. China will work with African countries and the rest of the world to safeguard international fairness and justice, and support Zimbabwe in defending independence and sovereignty as well as achieving development and revitalization.

**AFP: Serbia’s student-led movement won parliamentary elections on Sunday, ending 14 years in power for Aleksandar Vucic’s party. I was wondering if China would comment on the fact that Vucic said that the student movement was carried out with direct support from various European countries and the U.S. deep state.**

Guo Jiakun: China upholds the principle of non-interference in internal affairs and respects the independent choice of the people of other countries.

We attach great importance to China-Serbia relations and stand ready to work with Serbia’s new government to carry forward our traditional friendship, consolidate political mutual trust and expand practical cooperation on the basis o

title: Strength vs. Confrontation: Do American Forces in the First Island Chain Deter or Invite War?
summary: “We are not going to get involved militarily in any way on the Island of Formosa,” [announced Secretary of State Dean Acheson](https://www.jstor.org/stable/pdf/44639236.pdf) in January 1950. Taiwan fell outside of America’s security commitm
content:
“We are not going to get involved militarily in any way on the Island of Formosa,” [announced Secretary of State Dean Acheson](https://www.jstor.org/stable/pdf/44639236.pdf) in January 1950. Taiwan fell outside of America’s security commitment. He further described an [American defensive perimeter](https://www.cia.gov/readingroom/docs/1950-01-12.pdf) spanning from the Aleutian Islands through Japan and the Philippines. For the rest of the Pacific, he said that “a [security] guarantee is hardly sensible or necessary within the realm of practical relationship.”

Along with Taiwan, Korea fell outside American guarantees. Concerned about provoking a conflict in Korea, the [United States pressed South Korea](https://history.army.mil/portals/143/Images/Publications/catalog/30-3.pdf) to build a small, constabulary army that lacked heavy weapons. Without an American security commitment, forward-deployed United States forces, or a capable South Korean army, North Korea saw an opportunity to quickly reunify the peninsula. Five months after Acheson’s speech, North Korean forces invaded. T-34 tanks, invulnerable to South Korea’s light weaponry, spearheaded the attack and almost conquered the South [before the United States could deploy forces](https://www.armyupress.army.mil/Journals/Military-Review/English-Edition-Archives/May-June-2025/Preparing-Advisors/) to halt the communist offensive at the Pusan Perimeter. By October, China entered the war. This deterrence failure cost the lives of [](https://web.archive.org/web/20190724211722/https:/history.army.mil/brochures/kw-stale/stale.htm#analysis)[36,516 Americans](https://web.archive.org/web/20190724211722/https:/history.army.mil/brochures/kw-stale/stale.htm#analysis), hundreds of thousands of Chinese, and over two million Koreans.

After the deterrence failure that led to the Korean War, the United States recognized the necessity of forward presence to prevent war. Within two days of the start of that war, President Harry S. Truman [deployed the 7th Fleet](https://www.trumanlibrary.gov/library/public-papers/173/statement-president-situation-korea) to defend Taiwan. In September 1954, the Chinese shelled Taiwan’s Kinmen Island. Two months later, the United States had signed a mutual defense treaty with Taiwan, which deterred further Chinese escalation.

**The US Commitment to the First Island Chain**

As the risk of a catastrophic war in East Asia has reemerged, the United States must maintain this lesson: When it has defended forward and demonstrated the capability and resolve to make [aggression infeasible](https://editorials.voa.gov/a/time-for-pacific-allies-to-share-defense-burden/8157641.html), it has deterred opponents. When it has not, it has invited war.

With that understanding, the 2026 [](https://media.defense.gov/2026/Jan/23/2003864773/-1/-1/0/2026-national-defense-strategy.pdf)[National Defense Strategy](https://media.defense.gov/2026/Jan/23/2003864773/-1/-1/0/2026-national-defense-strategy.pdf) commits the military to “build, posture, and sustain a strong denial defense along the [first island chain],” which includes Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, and the Philippines. By focusing on forward-deployed forces, which could immediately respond to Chinese aggression, [the strategy](https://yalebooks.yale.edu/book/9780300268027/the-strategy-of-denial/) reduces the potential for China to achieve its policy objectives in a quick, cheap war. The strategy prioritizes cost-effective, asymmetric capabilities to buttress America’s allies. It prevents war for cheap, so what is the argument against it?

In a [recent analysis](https://www.defensepriorities.org/explainers/a-second-island-chain-strategy-for-asia/), Jennifer Kavanagh asks whether America’s commitments to the first island chain “really make Americans safer and more prosperous?” She argues that since the United States has limited interests in the region, it should withdraw to the more defensible second island chain and end its security commitments to the countries of the first island chain. While she leads a worthwhile thought exercise, her recommendations risk Chinese regional hegemony, war, and economic upheaval while precluding an overdue shift by the American military to cheap, asymmetric military capabilities.

At the moment, her argument seems far from becoming policy. Elbridge Colby, head of policy in the Pentagon, recently [briefed the Senate](https://media.defense.gov/2026/Sep/28/2004007869/-1/-1/1/UPDATE-ON-IMPLEMENTATION-OF-THE-2026-NATIONAL-DEFENSE-STRATEGY-AS-SUBMITTED-TO-THE-SENATE-ARMED-SERVICES-COMMITTEE.PDF) on the implementation of the National Defense Strategy, discussing the increasing complexity of [Exercise Balikatan](https://www.pacom.mil/Media/News/News-Articles/Article/4483964/philippines-us-conclude-balikatan-2026/) in the Philippines, which included a live fire of the new [Typhon missile system](https://www.navalnews.com/naval-news/2026/05/us-fires-tomahawk-missile-from-typhon-launcher-in-philippines-for-the-first-time/). He also argued that America’s posture has led to increased commitment by South Korea, Japan, and Australia to regional security.

However, some recent events have raised questions about the endurance of America’s commitment to the first island chain. For example, the United States [did not counter a Chinese diplomatic and economic campaign against Japan](https://reader.foreignaffairs.com/2026/09/28/japan-is-giving-the-united-states-a-chance-in-asia/content.html) following Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s statement that a Chinese use of force against Taiwan would constitute an “[existential threat](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/world/japan-and-china-trade-barbs-after-pm-takaichi-says-an-attack-on-taiwan-would-be-an-existential-threat)” for her country. The United States has also [postponed missile shipments](https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/japans-order-tomahawk-missiles-delayed-by-us-use-iran-bloomberg-news-says-2026-04-03/) to Tokyo, paused a planned arms sale to Taiwan, temporarily operated [without an aircraft carrier](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/world/u-s-pulls-last-aircraft-carrier-in-asia-as-trump-focuses-on-iran-and-the-western-hemisphere) in the region, and [scaled back military exercises](https://mwi.westpoint.edu/ulchi-freedom-shield-one-shortened-exercise-does-not-mean-us-south-korean-conventional-nuclear-integration-is-breaking-down/) with South Korea. Whether a critic’s charge that all of this amounts to “[great-power collusion](https://www.foreignaffairs.com/united-states/trump-rise-and-fall-great-power-competition)” or it is just the messy detritus of multifaceted great-power competition is not the point. The point is that perceptions of a weakened commitment could undermine allied confidence and create opportunities for China to expand its sphere of influence within the first island chain.

The US administration would argue that these moves are apart of deterrence as it attempts to navigate the trade-offs of deterring China “[through strength, not confrontation](https://media.defense.gov/2026/Sep/28/2004007869/-1/-1/1/UPDATE-ON-IMPLEMENTATION-OF-THE-2026-NATIONAL-DEFENSE-STRATEGY-AS-SUBMITTED-TO-THE-SENATE-ARMED-SERVICES-COMMITTEE.PDF)”—seeking to preserve the capability to deny Chinese aggression while not provoking Beijing—it raises an important question: Where does the balance lie between strength and confrontation?

**The Problem with Narrow National Interests**

To provide the foundation of her argument for restraint, Kavanagh begins by defining US interests in Asia, which she does more narrowly than either the current and previous administrations. She writes that “The United States has two core interests in Asia worth protecting with military power: defending the US homeland and safeguarding access to key economic markets and trade routes.”

While such an approach can seem intellectually fruitful, the use of national interests to drive policy can be [problematic](https://www.econlib.org/Columns/y2018/Lemieuxnationalinterest.html#_ftnref4). A narrow list of national interests cannot capture the complexity of American foreign relations.

Kavanagh mentions safeguarding markets, but she sees no core interest in ensuring peace in the region, although the United States [traded $2 trillion in goods](https://www.census.gov/foreign-trade/balance/c0016.html) with Asia in 2025. A war over Taiwan would indefinitely disrupt the world’s supply of advanced computer chips. As the American economy has become reliant on those chips to fuel its [economic growth](https://am.jpmorgan.com/us/en/asset-management/adv/insights/market-insights/market-updates/on-the-minds-of-investors/how-much-of-the-ai-boom-is-adding-to-us-growth/) and technological competitiveness, a prolonged interruption in their production would risk an economic crisis.

**The Risk of War**

When Kavanagh does discuss the risk of war, she seems to see the main threat as being unintended escalation. She argues that “The United States should also remove the long-range fire system (the Typhon) currently located in the Philippines, as it’s both unnecessary to support the commitments outlined here and highly escalatory.” Her argument raises a crucial debate on whether forward-deployed forces deter conflict or escalate its risks.

China would certainly argue that the American deployments of [Typhon to the Philippines](https://mb.com.ph/2025/1/28/china-mum-marcos-typhon-deal) or [THAAD to Korea](https://digital-commons.usnwc.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1736&context=nwc-review) are escalatory. But that is Chinese messaging, not reality. In a similar vein, Xi Jinping [regularly cites](https://hegemon.substack.com/p/chinas-favorite-american-idea)[_The Thucydides Trap_](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/26/xi-trump-thucydides-trap-us-china.html). Even though that book has [several](https://substack.com/home/post/p-153768458)[methodological](https://www.airuniversity.af.edu/Portals/10/SSQ/documents/Volume-15_Issue-4/SC-Hanania.pdf)[problems](https://issforum.org/roundtables/12-2-thucydides), it provides Xi with a means to argue that provocative moves could lead to war.

In contrast to Xi’s self-serving argument, historical experience provides little support for the proposition that provocation through position is itself the primary cause of war. Of course, leaders often cite enemy provocations to legitimize military action, but that does not mean those incitements actually caused a war. Adolf Hitler blamed Polish “[saboteurs](https://tvpworld.com/82061340/tracing-the-origins-of-world-war-two-the-gleiwitz-incident-85-years-on)” for war in 1939. Vladimir Putin blamed Ukrainian “[fascists](https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2022/02/24/putin-denazify-ukraine/)” for war in 2022. In fact, both Poland and Ukraine, in worrying about provoking war through escalation, delayed military mobilization and so [presented tempting targets](https://www.brookings.edu/books/surprise-attack/).

Whatever their public justifications, leaders tend to initiate wars when they gamble that a short war could be [a cost-effective means of achieving a policy objective](https://cornellpress.cornell.edu/book/9780801493461/conventional-deterrence/#bookTabs=1). In addition to the Korean War, modern history is replete with examples of leaders gambling on a short war: the Suez Crisis, the Six-Day War, the Indo-Pakistan War of 1971, the Yom Kippur War, the Cambodian-Vietnamese War, the Sino-Vietnamese War, the Soviet-Afghan War, the Iran-Iraq War, the Falklands War, the Persian Gulf War, the Afghanistan War, the Iraq War, the Russo-Georgian War, and the Russo-Ukrainian War. As with those examples, the risk of war in the first island chain comes not from US provocation but from Xi Jinping betting he could quickly seize Taiwan in a [fait accompli](https://people.tamu.edu/~ahmertarar/fait_accompli.pdf) before American intervention.

 10-26-2026

MANILA – A sharp exchange between Philippine and Chinese officials over the South China Sea is highlighting rising tensions in the region, even as the movement of the USS George Washington carrier group from Japan to the Middle East raises questions about the U.S. military commitment to the Indo-Pacific.

At a security forum in Seoul, Philippine Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. was emphasizing the importance of international law when a South Korean staff member handed him a note from a Chinese official challenging Manila's position on the South China Sea.

Teodoro read the message aloud before delivering a pointed response.

"China neither recognizes nor accepts the award. Of course, because you lost. And opposes it and will never accept any claim or action arising from it," Teodoro said.

He then criticized the delivery of the message, calling it disrespectful to international law, South Korean hosts and the audience.

"This is actual coercion, bullying and aggression," he said.

The confrontation underscores a long-running dispute over the 2016 international arbitral ruling that rejected the legal basis for China's expansive claims in the South China Sea. The ruling remains a major point of contention between Beijing and Manila, with China refusing to accept the decision.

Now, questions about the movement of major U.S. naval assets are adding another dimension to regional security concerns. The departure of the USS George Washington carrier group from Japan has prompted questions about whether a shift in American military deployments could affect deterrence in the Indo-Pacific.

Philippine military officials, however, say there is no reason for alarm.

Philippine Navy spokesman Rear Admiral Roy Trinidad said Manila remains confident in its security arrangements with Washington, despite the movement of U.S. naval vessels.

"We are not concerned about any reduction in US forces or other like-minded nations' forces in the Indo-Pacific Region. Despite the transfer of US naval vessels, the Mutual Defense Treaty remains in place," Trinidad said.

He added that military activities had been planned and approved in advance, with many exercises already conducted this year and additional joint exercises scheduled for next year.

International security expert Dr. Renato de Castro said U.S. carrier strike groups serve as a visible demonstration of American naval power and help deter potential aggression by China.

However, he noted that American military capabilities in the region extend well beyond aircraft carriers.

"Aside, of course, from the American battle groups, you have also the operation of nuclear attack submarines and American ballistic missile submarines. They are there; they operate. They are also very deadly, but of course they're not visible," De Castro said.

Meanwhile, Chinese military activity continues to raise concerns among U.S. allies and partners. Chinese warships have increased operations near Japan and the Philippines, while Taiwan has reported 118 sightings of Chinese vessels, highlighting the continuing pressure around the island.

De Castro said countries across the region are responding by strengthening their own defense capabilities rather than simply relying on the United States.

The goal, he said, is to ensure that security alliances with Washington remain a two-way commitment as regional tensions continue to mount.

广告

（德国之声中文网）该文称来自美俄中三国的消息人均证实，特朗普政府已就此事与[欧尔班](https://dw.com/zh/%E5%8C%88%E7%89%99%E5%88%A9%E5%A4%A7%E9%80%89%E5%8F%98%E5%A4%A9-%E6%AC%A7%E7%9B%9F%E7%9C%BC%E4%B8%AD%E9%92%89%E6%AC%A7%E5%B0%94%E7%8F%AD16%E5%B9%B4%E6%94%BF%E6%9D%83%E5%91%8A%E7%BB%88/a-76759942)（Viktor Orbán）进行接触，计划让他以三国共同支持的候选人身份参与竞选。

根据该报道，这一想法最初由美国提出。目前，最终决定尚未做出，欧尔班本人对这一提议持开放态度。不过，除非有把握胜选，否则他不太可能正式参选。

现任联合国秘书长[古特雷斯](https://dw.com/zh/%E8%B0%81%E5%B0%86%E6%98%AF%E5%8F%A4%E7%89%B9%E9%9B%B7%E6%96%AF%E7%9A%84%E6%8E%A5%E7%8F%AD%E4%BA%BA/a-76641389)（António Guterres）的任期将于12月31日结束，继任者的角逐正日趋激烈地展开。目前，尚未出现一位能够获得联合国安理会大力支持的明确领跑者。

《华尔街日报》援引一名美国国务院官员表示，欧尔班可以轻松地得到15个[安理会](https://dw.com/zh/%E8%81%94%E5%90%88%E5%9B%BD%E5%AE%89%E7%90%86%E4%BC%9A/t-41549339)成员国中的8票，拿下10票也是可能。

不过，英国和法国在安理会也拥有否决权，虽然这两个国家以往均非常谨慎的使用这一权力，但如果使用，欧尔班将没有胜算。

# Brief showers forecast Monday for Greater Taipei, eastern half of Taiwan

10/26/2026 10:52 AM

Taipei, Oct. 26 (CNA) The Greater Taipei area and the eastern half of Taiwan are expected to see brief isolated showers Monday, while areas south of Taoyuan will be cloudy to sunny, according to the Central Weather Administration (CWA).

Due to the influence of northeasterly winds, brief isolated afternoon showers may also occur in the mountainous areas of Nantou County, the CWA said.

Meanwhile, daytime temperatures will range between 26 and 28 degrees Celsius in northern, northeastern and eastern Taiwan on Monday, the CWA said.

Elsewhere, highs of 30-32 degrees can be expected, but inland areas of southern Taiwan may see even higher temperatures during the day, the CWA added.

On Monday night, the mercury will drop to lows of 21-24 degrees Celsius across the country, the CWA said.

Strengthening northeasterly winds on Tuesday and Wednesday will bring slightly cooler weather to northern and northeastern Taiwan, with daytime highs of around 25-26 degrees, the CWA said.

During those two days, brief isolated showers can be expected in areas north of Taoyuan, in eastern Taiwan, and on the Hengchun Peninsula in the south, the CWA forecast.

Other areas will be cloudy to sunny, but mountainous areas of Nantou County may also see some brief isolated afternoon showers on those two days, the CWA said.

The seasonal wind system is forecast to weaken Thursday and Friday, giving way to sunny to cloudy skies nationwide, before northeasterly winds strengthen again Saturday, bringing brief isolated showers to some areas, according to the CWA.

It also gave an update on Tropical Storm In-Fa, which it said was located about 4,640 kilometers east of Eluanbi in southern Taiwan as of 8 a.m. Monday.

The storm is forecast to move northwest before turning west-northwest, with no direct impact on Taiwan, the CWA said.

(By Chang Hsiung-feng and Ko Lin)

title: 被控涉数千万美元加密货币诈骗案，一名中国公民被引渡至美国受审

content:
美国司法部加利福尼州中区联邦检察官办公室10月23日宣布，44岁的中国公民赵正(音译，Zheng Zhao)从荷兰被引渡至美国后于当天首次出庭。联邦检察官表示，赵正被控参与一起涉及金额为3690万美元的国际加密货币投资骗局串谋，该骗局由位于柬埔寨的诈骗中心实施，受害者中有174人被确认为美国公民。

根据法庭文件，赵正是检方所说的“一个国际犯罪网络”的一分子，该网络诱使美国受害者将资金转入由共谋者控制的账户，这些共谋者随后通过美国空壳公司、国际银行账户及数字资产钱包，窃取受害者的资金并进行洗钱操作。骗局流程始于犯罪网络成员通过不请自来的社交媒体讯息、电话和短信与受害者建立联系，骗取他们的信任，然后诱惑他们进行虚假的加密货币投资。诈骗分子建立貌似真实加密伙伴交易平台的假网站，说服受害者通过假网站投资，一面告诉他们投资不断升值，一面窃走这些资金。

联邦检察官表示，在赵正被控参与的这起骗局中，超过3690万美元的受害者资金从由共谋者控制的美国银行账户转至巴哈马的德尔泰克银行(Deltec Bank)的一个账户中。检方说，赵正及其同伙安排德尔泰克银行将这些受害者的资金兑换为稳定币泰达币(USDT)，并将兑换后的资金转移至一个位于柬埔寨、由他们控制的数字资产钱包中。随后，身处柬埔寨的共谋者将这些泰达币转移给了该地区各地诈骗中心的头目。

“随着犯罪活动的全球化，执法部门将罪犯定位并抓获的能力也全球化了，”加利福尼亚州中区联邦检察官办公室首席助理检察官比尔·埃萨利(Bill Essayli)在10月23日的声明中说。“当无辜美国民众受到网络犯罪分子及其帮凶伤害时，我们及全球各地的合作伙伴将不遗余力地确保这些人在美国法庭上受到法律制裁。”

“此次引渡对所有企图从海外侵害美国弱势群体的人来说，都应是一次教训，”美国司法部负责刑事司的助理部长A·泰森·杜瓦(A. Tysen Duva)在声明中说。“无论身处世界何地，我们都将追捕那些受到指控的被告，尤其是那些被控窃取钱财、将其转换为加密货币，并在此过程中利用外国金融机构来隐藏和混淆其罪行的人。无论你们藏身何处，我们都有能力找到你们。”

法官下令将赵正拘押，对他的提审被安排在11月30日，地点是洛杉矶市中心的联邦地区法院。按照美国的刑事诉讼程序，在提审(又译“传讯”)环节，被告出庭听取对其的指控，并被要求回答有罪或无罪。

如被定罪，赵正面临的法定最高处罚是在联邦监狱服刑20年。

联邦检察官在声明中提到，刑事诉状只是指称，所有被告在被法庭排除合理怀疑而证明有罪之前，均被推定无罪。

美国司法部一直在调查和追究那些向全球各地诈骗中心提供便利的人员。

赵正被引渡是本案最新进展。到目前为止，已有八名同案共谋者承认有罪，包括2025年认罪的加州居民何生生(音译，ShengSheng He)与中国公民[苏景亮](https://www.voachinese.com/a/chinese-national-sentenced-to-nearly-4-years-for-role-in-multimillion-dollar-cryptocurrency-scam-targeting-us-victims-20260128/8107548.html)(音译，Jingliang Su)。何生生和苏景亮分别被判处在联邦监狱服刑51个月和46个月。

title: 中国印尼将举行反恐联合训练，分析：北京有意制衡菲律宾

content:
中国国防部宣布，中国与印尼近期将在广东举行陆军反恐联合训练。观察人士指出，中国拉拢印尼在南中国海问题上抗衡菲律宾应是中国的重点考量之一，而印尼则是希望能在美中两大国之间求取平衡关系。

根据中国国防部10月26日发布的声明，中印尼将在10月下旬至11月上旬举行“利刃-2026”陆军反恐联合训练；此次联训以山地联合反恐营救行动为课题，主要进行山地攀登、特种驾驶、直升机索降、近距离突击、有人无人协同等内容训练。

中方声明表示，该系列联训有助于持续深化两军务实交流合作，提升双方部队联合行动能力。

2011年，印尼与中国举行了首次“利刃”双边反恐演习。该演习由两国军队的特种部队参与，模拟了人质营救场景。该系列演习到2015年暂停。

2015年后，由于中国和印尼在一些主权和自然资源问题上的冲突，两国大规模双边联合演习出现了一段较长的空白期，

2024年12月，印尼和中国举行了代号为“和平神鹰”的双边联合军事演习。2026年8月，中国军方称与印度尼西亚海军在台湾东部海域完成“实兵演习”。

**印尼希望平衡与美中关系**

外界普遍认为，印尼作为东盟大国，在外交关系中多采取平衡策略，目的在于能在大国之间找到安全与合作的空间。

台湾淡江大学“国际事务与战略研究所”学者林颖佑就是这种观点的支持者。他在接受美国之音(VOA)采访时表示，中印尼联合训练传递出的信号就是：印尼一直在华盛顿和北京之间寻求关系平衡。

林颖佑说：“印尼之前有跟中国空军购买歼十战斗机，但同样的印尼也会希望能够跟中国有更多的军事上的合作。这一次他们聚焦在陆军反恐的一个相关的演习，我觉得印尼希望借由这一个反恐或者是非传统安全这样的议题，去加强跟中国的相互合作。”

**北京意在制衡菲律宾**

对北京而言，印尼在中国外交与安全政策中发挥着重要作用。印尼是马六甲海峡的核心沿岸国家，而马六甲海峡是中国大部分能源进口的必经之处，因此，与印尼保持稳定的防务关系，对于维护中国能源进口至关重要。

另外，林颖佑指出，印尼在区域事务中具有一定影响力，在中国和菲律宾于南中国海地区不断发生冲突和纷争之际，中国拉拢印尼制衡菲律宾也是北京的一个重要考量。

2026年9月17日，在“北京香山论坛”期间，中国中央军委副主席张升民会见了印尼国防部长沙夫里·沙姆苏丁(Sjafrie Sjamsoeddin)，就双方在防务交流与合作等议题进行了讨论。

**美国和印尼承诺以实力实现和平**

自20世纪80年代以来，美国一直是印尼重要的安全伙伴，为印尼军队提供军事装备和训练。

今年4月13日，美国战争部长皮特·海格塞斯(Pete Hegseth)和到访的印尼国防部长沙夫里举行双边会晤，进一步推动了美国总统唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)在印太地区通过实力实现和平的愿景，建立了主要防务合作伙伴关系，提升了两国长期的安全关系。

双方在一份联合声明说，两国已同意探索“前沿倡议”，其中包括在海上、水下和自主系统战争领域共同开发复杂的非对称能力；两国还将展开合作，以提升该地区的战备状态，并开展联合特种部队训练。

声明说：“通过这一宣布，两国重申了维护印太地区和平与稳定的共同承诺。”

截至发稿，美国战争部(DOW)尚未回复美国之音关于中印尼反恐联合训练的置评请求。

**学者：应关注中印尼合作对台湾带来的间接影响**

8月，中国军方称与印尼海军在台湾东部海域举行“通航演练”后，引起台湾强烈不满，台湾外交部称此举为中国“恶意寻衅”、严重侵害台湾主权并威胁区域安全。

对于印尼在短期内第二次和中国展开联合军事行动，淡江大学的国防与战略研究学者林颖佑表示，台湾要关注的不是这个演习对台湾造成直接的影响，而是其它间接但重要的影响。

林颖佑说：“我觉得相对来说比较重要的是，台湾要去关注中国跟印尼的合作关系加强后，印尼会不会限制对台湾的能源出口？或者是中国会施加压力，要求印尼不要卖那么多的能源给台湾？”

长期以来，印尼是台湾的重要能源与物资进口来源之一。根据台湾驻印尼代表处公布的[数据](https://www.roc-taiwan.org/id/post/44.html)，煤炭和液化天然气一直占据着台湾从印尼进口的主要产品的榜首。

title: 程翔：龍應台的「最後的停頓」
summary: 作者： 程翔 追光者【京城外望】 2026 年 10 月 26 日 最近，台灣和平論者龍應台在聯經出版的《思想》第54期中發表文章〈十日之行：人類最後的停頓〉[1]，透過歷史寓言與現代科技的對比，指出和平的關鍵在於給予人類理性的停頓空間，並主張透過道德理性與戰略嚇阻並重的雙軌手段來化解戰爭危機。她說，在台海及全球地緣政治籠罩在戰爭陰影的當下，人類必須死守住屬於理性、倫理與對話的最後停頓。她所指的「停頓」，是指在「決定開戰」與「正式執行」之間，留出讓人類理性、外交斡旋與倫理思考
content: 作者： 程翔 追光者【京城外望】  2026 年 10 月 26 日 最近，台灣和平論者龍應台在聯經出版的《思想》第54期中發表文章〈十日之行：人類最後的停頓〉[1]，透過歷史寓言與現代科技的對比，指出和平的關鍵在於給予人類理性的停頓空間，並主張透過道德理性與戰略嚇阻並重的雙軌手段來化解戰爭危機。她說，在台海及全球地緣政治籠罩在戰爭陰影的當下，人類必須死守住屬於理性、倫理與對話的最後停頓。她所指的「停頓」，是指在「決定開戰」與「正式執行」之間，留出讓人類理性、外交斡旋與倫理思考介入的緩衝時間。龍應台之所以強調需要「最後的停頓」，是因為現代科技（如AI自主武器、網路戰、高超音速飛彈）正在消滅這個讓人獲得緩衝化解矛盾的機會。 筆者擔心，她這種「和平觀」會產生麻痺作用，就如她過去的和平論一樣，把和平建築在中共的理性上。將和平寄託於對方的「理性」、「倫理」或「對話」，在現實中是極其危險的麻痺劑，因為：   第一，她誤判了楚王（中共）的「理性」定義 龍應台文中的邏輯是：墨子透過兵推，讓楚王意識到「代價太高，無法必勝」，於是楚王選擇了不著兵戈的理性放棄。但現實是：中共是一個極權體制的政權，其「理性計算」與自由民主社會完全不同。中共也是一個由意識形態驅使的政權，台灣問題常被提升到「歷史定位」、「政權合法性」與「民族復興」的至高層次。在這種情況下，即便代價極高、即便兵推顯示會傷亡慘重，決策者仍可能認為開戰是「理性的、必須付出的代價」。將和平建立在「對方會因為不化算而收手」的假設上，容易導致防線的心理麻痺。 第二，她看不到台灣現行的「防禦體系」會被「反戰言論」削弱 龍應台自己說：墨子勸阻楚王之所以成功，是因為宋國城牆上真的站滿了「三百名墨子的弟子」，他們能用墨子傳授的技術反制公輸般（按：即魯班）的發明，這正好說明積極防禦的重要性。所以她應該看到，在台灣的輿論環境中，過度強調「反戰」、「和平對話」或「不要挑釁」，往往在無形中解構了這「三百名弟子」的抵抗意志。當社會普遍瀰漫著「開戰就是兩敗俱傷、所以大家都不要打」的和平主義時，往往會導致兵役改革、國防預算、民防準備受到掣肘。沒有強大意志與實力支撐的「墨子」，只會變成跪求和平的宋國。 第三，模糊了「侵略者」與「被侵略者」的本質區別 龍應台文中的邏輯：墨子與楚王、公輸般是平等的智者對話，戰爭是一個可以被討論、被推演的技術和倫理問題。但現實是：兩岸問題的本質，是一方不承認另一方的主權地位與生活方式。龍應台過去常將戰爭的責任簡化為「執政者的挑釁」或「大國角力的棋子」，這種「各打五十大板」的論述，容易模糊了「侵略者」與「被侵略者」的本質區別，進而讓防守方產生「只要我們不挑釁，對方就會停下來」的麻痺幻想。 她所提倡的「停頓」，更是對「AI自動化殺人」的恐懼。在過去，楚王要攻宋，尚有「十日之行」的時間和空間可以去勸阻。但未來的AI戰爭，演算法可能在0.001秒內就判定敵方有威脅並自動發射飛彈，人類決策者甚至連「停頓」的機會都沒有，就已經進入核末日了。她所以強調，過去國際間很多危機，都是靠有片刻「停頓」的空間而得以化解。 今天龍應台提出「停頓」，可說是正中中共的下懷。歷史經驗說明，每當中共力有不及時，它會和對手談「停戰」、談「和平」、談「統戰」，用親情、友誼、同根生來麻痺對手；但當它力有所及時，它會徹底消滅對手。關於這個特點，筆者曾經引用中共的內部檔，把這套伎倆呈現出來[2]，這裡不贅。今天中共沒有武統台灣，恰恰反映它力有不及的實際處境，這個時候它需要的是一個積聚實力（直接軍事打擊及建立內應勢力）的時候，龍應台的「停頓」，正契合它這個時候的需要。當然，我不是說龍應台是主動配合中共的策略，但很遺憾她在這個時候推出「停頓」論，客觀上產生同一個配合中共需要的效果。 龍應台應該從西藏《十七條協議》（1951年）與香港《中英聯合聲明》的「十二條方針」（1984年）這兩個歷史「前車之鑑」，得出一個結論：當中共能力有所不及時，它會講協商、一旦到它能力足夠時，它會用武力。請看下表： 歷史的鏡子：西藏與香港的「和平麻醉」 案例 中共「實力不夠／有所顧忌」時的和平姿態 中共「實力足夠／時機成熟」時的武力與收權 西藏《十七條》 1951年 中共剛建政，西南局勢未穩，且藏區地形險要。為了順利進軍，中共承諾「西藏現行政治制度不予變更」、達賴喇嘛的固有地位及職權不予變更。 1959年，解放軍公路修通、對藏控制力穩固。中共開始強推「民主改革」與集體化，最終撕毀協議，引發拉薩騷亂，達賴喇嘛被迫流亡至今。 香港《一國兩制》十二條 （1984） 鄧小平時代，中國剛實施改革開放，急需香港作為引進外資、技術和西方體制的窗口，且忌憚英國與國際社會的反應。承諾「港人治港、高度自治、五十年不變」。 隨著中國成為全球第二大經濟體，香港的經濟佔比驟降，國際依賴度減弱。2014年發表《一國兩制白皮書》，強調「全面管治權」，2020年，直接跨過香港立法會強推《香港國安法》，一國兩制實質上變為「一國一制」。 所以，對中共而言，任何「和平協議」或「政治承諾」都不是神聖不可侵犯的法律，而是一種「在其實力不足、或有戰略需要時，用來麻痺對手、爭取時間的戰術工具」。一旦兩岸或國際的實力天平徹底傾斜，這些承諾就會變成「權宜之計」或中共外交部口中的「歷史檔」。 從這「十七條」和「十二條」兩個歷史案例出發，我們可以看清當實力不對等時，盲目追求政治對話和協議會帶來怎樣的災難性後果。 既然歷史給了如此沉痛的教訓，台灣社會在面對中共的「和平、可親、願意交朋友」（如推動兩岸大融合、文化交流、青年創業優惠）的基調時，就必須：一、採取「現實主義的防禦眼光」：拒絕任何形式的「和平協議」政治談判、看穿「以經促統、以民逼官」的麻醉劑。二、當中共對台展現「和平惠台」的姿態時，其核心目的是為了弱化台灣內部的防衛意志，以及將和平建立在「中共付不起代價」的硬實力上。 所以，龍應台在文中所說的「停頓」，如果變成對中共善意的天真期待，將會成為致命的麻醉劑。台灣社會必須牢記西藏與香港的血淚教訓：和平從來不是談出來的，而是當你手裡握有讓侵略者折斷牙齒的武器時，對方不得不表現出來的「暫時客氣」。 [1] 《夾縫中的馬華社會（思想54）》，2026年10月22日。 https://store.linkingbooks.com.tw/product/15708954 [2] 程翔〈中共對美開展微笑外交〉，自由亞洲電台2025年1月6日。 https://www.rfa.org/cantonese/commentaries/ching/china-us-relations-smile-diplomacy-01062025132207.html

title: Hong Kong police officer stabbed during 2020 protest seeks at least HK$220K in damages
zh_title: 2020年抗议期间被刺伤的香港警察寻求至少22万港元的赔偿
summary: 一名香港警察向一名在 2020 年抗议活动中刺伤他的男子寻求至少 22 万港元的赔偿。2020 年 7 月 1 日，铜锣湾警察。资料照片：May James/HKFP。吕俊杰周一在区域法院法庭发言，证实他多处肌肉撕裂，需要手术。 2020年7月1日下午，该警官在进行人群控制时，肩膀和左肘被刀刺伤。当天，抗议者聚集在铜锣湾，反对北京在反逃犯送中后通过香港国家安全法。
content:
一名香港警察向一名在 2020 年抗议活动中刺伤他的男子寻求至少 22 万港元的赔偿。2020 年 7 月 1 日，铜锣湾警察。资料照片：May James/HKFP。吕俊杰周一在区域法院法庭发言，证实他多处肌肉撕裂，需要手术。 2020年7月1日下午，该警官在进行人群控制时，肩膀和左肘被刀刺伤。当天，抗议者聚集在铜锣湾，反对北京在去年开始的反送中抗议和骚乱后通过香港国家安全法。他向黄官华寻求赔偿，但他没有出庭。黄承认犯有2022年骚乱和意图造成严重身体伤害的伤人罪，并被判入狱五年。据《证人》报道，吕告诉法庭，他必须参加 15 次物理治疗，并于 2020 年 9 月完成。但他的左肩活动仍然有限，直到2022年才完全康复。吕现在警方公关团队工作。当时他是警察机动部队的一名警官，并于同年 12 月被调往紧急部队。湾仔区域法院。资料图片：HKFP。 “我更喜欢业务工作。现在，我在警察局做后台文书工作。感觉很失望，”吕用粤语说。
他补充说，当他回到袭击发生地附近的高士威道时，他的记忆闪回。法庭获悉，他寻求的 22 万港元是为了补偿他的痛苦、收入损失以及“永久丧失赚钱能力和晋升机会”。 “剧痛” 根据一份法庭文件，吕和他的同事于2020年7月1日下午晚些时候被部署到铜锣湾举行非法集会。抗议者占领了主要道路，无视警方驱散的警告。当吕先生进行逮捕时，抗议者包围了他并试图干预。 7 月 1 日，民间人权阵线组织的游行，资料图片：Joshua Kwan/联合社会通讯社。他向法庭作证说，有人掐住了他的脖子，一名女子用雨伞打了他。 “当时很多人围着我，突然，我感觉左肩一阵剧痛，好像有什么东西刺穿了……然后，我的手臂就软了，”雷用广东话说道。在吕先生作证之前，卢菲丽斯法官质疑为何吕先生的法律团队在案件开始三年后才添加额外的赔偿条款。 Loh还质疑为何要求赔偿额从近100万港元减少至约22万港元，表明吕一开始夸大了金额。预计她将在三个月内做出判决。

【原文 English Original】
A Hong Kong police officer has sought at least HK$220,000 in damages from a man who stabbed him during a protest in 2020. Police in Causeway Bay on July 1, 2020. File Photo: May James/HKFP. Lui Chun-kit addressed the courtroom at the District Court on Monday, testifying that he sustained multiple muscle tears and required surgery. The officer was knifed in the shoulder and left elbow on the afternoon of July 1, 2020 while carrying out crowd control. That day, protesters had gathered in Causeway Bay to oppose Beijing’s passing of a national security law for Hong Kong following the anti-extradition protests and unrest that began the year before. Wong Kwan-wa, from whom he is seeking the compensation, did not appear in court. Wong pleaded guilty to rioting and wounding with intent to do grievous bodily harm in 2022, and was jailed for five years . Lui told the court that he had to attend 15 physiotherapy sessions, which he completed in September 2020, The Witness reported . But he continued to have limited mobility in his left shoulder, and only fully recovered in 2022. Lui now works in the police’s public relations team. He had been an officer in the Police Tactical Unit at the time, and was due to be transferred to the Emergency Unit that December. District Court in Wan Chai. File photo: HKFP. “I prefer operational work. Now, I am doing back-office clerical work for the police. It feels like a letdown,” Lui said in Cantonese. He added that he suffers flashbacks when he returns to Causeway Road, near where the attack happened. The HK$220,000 he is seeking is for his suffering, loss of income, and “permanent loss of earning capacity and promotion opportunities,” the court heard. ‘Sharp pain’ According to a court document, Lui and his colleagues were deployed to an unlawful assembly in Causeway Bay on the late afternoon of July 1, 2020. Protesters had occupied main roads and ignored police warnings to disperse. When Lui was carrying out arrests, protesters surrounded him and attempted to intervene. A march organised by the Civil Human Rights Front on July 1, File photo: Joshua Kwan/United Social Press. He testified to the court that somebody grabbed him in a chokehold, and a woman used an umbrella to hit him. “As many people were surrounding me, suddenly, I felt a sharp pain in my left shoulder, like something had pierced it… then, my arm went limp,” Lui said in Cantonese. Ahead of Lui’s testimony, Judge Phyllis Loh questioned why Lui’s legal team was only adding additional clauses for compensation now, three years after the case began. Loh also raised questions about why the damages sought were reduced from almost HK$1 million to around HK$220,000, suggesting Lui had exaggerated the amount at the beginning. She is expected to hand down her judgement within three months.

summary: 香港数码港将于 11 月 4 日至 5 日举行的年度风险与资本论坛将重点关注人工智能、数字资产和个人公司。该活动旨在帮助初创企业和投资者克服融资和市场扩张障碍，凸显香港作为连接中国内地、东盟和中东地区的门户[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编 2026 年 10 月 26 日 20:52 香港时间 · 更新于 10 月 27 日，04:26 · 阅读 2 分钟 人工智能、数字资产等
content:
香港
数码港将于 11 月 4 日至 5 日举行的年度风险与资本论坛将重点关注人工智能、数字资产和个人公司。该活动旨在帮助初创企业和投资者克服融资和市场拓展障碍，凸显香港作为连接中国内地、东盟和中东的门户

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

2026 年 10 月 26 日，香港时间 20:52 · 更新于 10 月 27 日，04:26 · 阅读时间 2 分钟

组织者周一表示，人工智能、数字资产和个人公司（OPC）将成为[数码港](https://clb.org.hk/en/hong-kong/Six-charged-over-HK-20m-digital-grant-fraud-involving-Cyberp-21d5e8)风险与资本论坛的重点关注点，该论坛将于11月4日至5日在数码港举行，与会者将探讨新兴市场机遇和全球扩张战略。

据 Cyber​​port 称，该论坛的主题是“在不断变化的世界中扩展：赢得下一个竞争周期”，将汇集全球投资者和企业家，讨论企业和代理人工智能、OPC 和前沿技术。该活动旨在帮助初创企业和投资者突破融资和市场拓展障碍，抓住新的市场机遇。
数码港表示，香港还将凸显其作为连接中国内地、东盟、中东、全球创新和融资网络的战略门户的独特地位。

数码港强调，其初创企业去年筹集了 745 亿港元的资金，有 481 家公司加入，展现了强劲的筹款表现。年内，数码港共有 19 家公司成功上市，并新增两家独角兽公司。

数码港行政总裁郑崇智表示：“随着全球创新和资本市场加速重塑，人工智能、数据技术和新兴产业已成为推动经济增长的重要引擎。”

Cyber​​port 表示，最近的高价值融资轮包括 Finloop、Qupital、Premialab 和 Buy&Ship，其中许多都利用了人工智能、区块链和数字资产。

CIN指导集团主席、中手游科技联合创办人兼弘昌资本董事长冼亨德里表示：“数码港投资者网络（CIN）今年已迈入九周年，我们的网络由超过240名全球投资者组成，已成功促成超过133个项目配对，金额超过60亿港元，较去年增加超过19个项目。”
今年的论坛将继续举办广受欢迎的“投资者配对”环节，根据投资者和初创企业的技术重点和投资偏好，与他们进行面对面和在线配对。其他亮点包括 80 多个实体展示摊位、资助者力量推介、初创诊所和研讨会，为与会者提供实用见解和战略建议。

数码港与戈壁创投和泰国国家创新局等国际合作伙伴也将于当天签署一份谅解备忘录。另一个亮点将是代理经济峰会，汇聚人工智能先驱、监管机构和金融巨头，探讨数字身份、机构代币化、港元稳定币发行、可编程支付和机器对机器商务如何构建未来的金融轨道。

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong
Cyberport's annual Venture & Capital Forum on November 4-5 will focus on AI, digital assets and one-person companies. The event aims to help start-ups and investors overcome financing and market expansion barriers, highlighting Hong Kong as a gateway connecting mainland China, ASEAN and the Middle E

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

26 Oct 2026 at 20:52 HKT · updated 27 Oct, 04:26 · 2 min read

Artificial intelligence, digital assets and one-person companies (OPCs) will be key focuses at the [Cyberport](https://clb.org.hk/en/hong-kong/Six-charged-over-HK-20m-digital-grant-fraud-involving-Cyberp-21d5e8) Venture & Capital Forum, to be held on November 4-5 at Cyberport, where participants will explore emerging market opportunities and global expansion strategies, the organiser said on Monday.

Themed “Scaling in a Changing World: Winning the Next Competitive Cycle,” the forum will bring together global investors and entrepreneurs to discuss enterprise and agentic AI, OPCs and frontier technology, according to Cyberport. The event aims to empower start-ups and investors to break through financing and market expansion barriers, seizing new market opportunities.

Hong Kong will also spotlight its unique position as a strategic gateway connecting the Chinese mainland, ASEAN, the Middle East, global innovation and funding networks, Cyberport said.

Cyberport highlighted that its start-ups raised HK$74.5 billion in funding last year, demonstrating robust fundraising performance with 481 companies joining the community. During the year, 19 Cyberport companies successfully listed, alongside the addition of two new unicorns.

“As global innovation and capital markets undergo accelerated reshaping, AI, data technology, and emerging industries have become crucial engines driving economic growth,” said Cyberport’s chief executive Rocky Cheng.

Recent high-value fundraising rounds include Finloop, Qupital, Premialab and Buy&Ship, many of which leverage AI, blockchain and digital assets, Cyberport said.

“Cyberport Investors Network (CIN) has come to its 9th anniversary this year, and our network of over 240 global investors has successfully facilitated more than HK$6 billion across over 133 project matchings, representing an increase of over 19 projects compared to last year,” said Hendrick Sin, CIN Steering Group’s chairman, CMGE Technology’s co-founder and China Prosperity Capital’s chairman.

This year’s forum will continue to feature the popular “Investor Matching” session for face-to-face and online pairing with investors and start-ups, based on their technological focus and investment preferences. Additional highlights include over 80 physical showcase booths, funder power pitches, a start-up clinic and workshop, providing attendees with practical insights and strategic advice.

Cyberport and international partners, including Gobi Partners and Thailand’s National Innovation Agency, will also sign a memorandum of understanding on the day. Another highlight will be the Agentic Economy Summit, bringing together AI pioneers, regulators and financial giants to examine how digital identity, institutional tokenisation, HKD stablecoin issuance, programmable payments and machine-to-machine commerce are building the financial rails of the future.

[![Image 3: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

title: Messages reveal childhood struggles: ‘Scold me less, hug me more’
zh_title: 信息揭示了童年的挣扎：“少骂我，多拥抱我”
summary: 香港 为香港的一次展览收集的 2,000 多份匿名自白揭示了儿童面临的情感压力，自卑和家庭冲突被认为是导致不快乐的主要原因，其程度超过了学业压力。 [![图片 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编 2026 年 10 月 26 日 22:09 HKT · 2 分钟阅读 超过2000条反映童年挣扎的匿名信息揭示了香港年轻人面临的情感压力
content:
香港
香港的一次展览收集了超过 2000 份匿名供述，揭示了儿童面临的情感压力，自卑和家庭冲突被认为是导致不快乐的主要原因，其程度超过了学业压力。

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

2026 年 10 月 26 日 22:09 香港时间 · 阅读 2 分钟

超过2000条反映童年挣扎的匿名信息揭示了香港年轻人面临的情感压力，许多人表达了希望得到父母更多关爱和理解的愿望。这些信息是为了本月早些时候在铜锣湾诚品书店举办的一场题为“不快乐的告白”的情感治疗展览而收集的，该展览由艺术和心理治疗团体Not a Gallery举办。

手写信息包括“少骂我，多拥抱我”和“给我一个拥抱”等恳求，引发了网上关于孩子们情感需求和心理健康的讨论。根据主办方引用的统计数据，自卑和被批评的感觉是学生感到不快乐的主要原因，占受访者的50%以上。
家庭冲突和父母期望位居第二，约占45%，而学业压力，包括公开考试和成绩，约占40%。研究结果表明，情感斗争和家庭关系对学生的影响可能比单纯的学业压力更大。

一名10岁的学生描述了自己被作业、复习、补习班和父母之间争吵所困扰，表达了一个简单的愿望，希望别人“少骂我，多拥抱我”。一名 15 岁的孩子还写到自己很难理解爱的含义，她说，虽然他们知道母亲爱他们，但他们感觉不到，只是希望她“给我一个拥抱”。

一名 19 岁的青少年描述自己的感觉就像一个拼图，永远无法正确拼凑在一起，但在与其他人竞争时，他的碎片不断被拼凑到位。 “我感觉自己就像一个永远无法正确拼凑在一起的拼图，但人们不断地把各个碎片拼凑到位。我必须继续与其他人竞争。这很疯狂，也很累人。请别打扰我！”少年写道。
成年人也分享痛苦的童年记忆。一个人将成长描述为“将哭泣的音量降低到无声的过程”，而另一个人则将其比作收集邮票等创伤。焦点教育集团创办人侯嘉仪表示，参观“不开心的告白”展览引起了她的共鸣，让她想起了自己在孩子们身上看到的压力和不开心。 “有时候，成年人认为孩子太小，无法理解，或者他们会克服一些事情。但孩子也有感情，即使他们无法用语言表达这些感情，也不意味着他们没有受到伤害。有时，他们最需要的只是有人倾听并认真对待他们的感受，”她说。

[![图片3：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

主编

负责 CLB.org.hk 报道和编辑标准的主编。

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong
Over 2,000 anonymous confessions collected for a Hong Kong exhibition reveal emotional pressures on children, with low self-esteem and family conflicts cited as leading causes of unhappiness, surpassing academic stress.

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

26 Oct 2026 at 22:09 HKT · 2 min read

More than 2,000 anonymous messages reflecting on childhood struggles have shed light on the emotional pressures faced by young people in Hong Kong, with many expressing a desire for greater affection and understanding from their parents. The messages were collected for an emotional healing exhibition titled “Unhappy Confessions,” organised by art and psychological therapy group Not a Gallery at Eslite Bookstore in Causeway Bay earlier this month.

Among the handwritten messages were pleas such as “Scold me less, hug me more” and “Give me a hug,” prompting online discussions about children’s emotional needs and mental health. According to statistics cited by the organiser, low self-esteem and feelings of being criticised were the leading reasons students felt unhappy, accounting for more than 50 per cent of responses.

Family conflicts and parental expectations ranked second, at around 45 per cent, while academic pressure, including public examinations and grades, accounted for approximately 40 per cent. The findings suggest that emotional struggles and family relationships may weigh more heavily on students than academic pressure alone.

One 10-year-old student described being troubled by homework, revision, tutorial classes and arguments between their parents, expressing a simple wish for others to “scold me less and hug me more.” A 15-year-old also wrote about struggling to understand the meaning of love, saying that although they knew their mother loved them, they could not feel it and simply wished she would “give me a hug.”

A 19-year-old described feeling like a puzzle that could never fit together properly, yet whose pieces were constantly forced into place while they competed with others. “I feel like a puzzle that can never fit together properly, but people keep forcing the pieces into place. I have to keep racing against others. It’s crazy and exhausting. Please leave me alone!” the teenager wrote.

Adults also shared painful childhood memories. One described growing up as “the process of turning the volume of crying down to silent,” while another compared it to collecting trauma like stamps. Jovy Hau, founder of Focus Education Group, said visiting the “Unhappy Confessions” exhibition had struck a chord with her, reminding her of the pressure and unhappiness she had observed among children. “Sometimes, adults assume children are too young to understand or that they will simply get over things. But children have feelings too, and even if they cannot put those feelings into words, it does not mean they are not hurting. Sometimes, what they need most is simply for someone to listen and take their feelings seriously,” she said.

[![Image 3: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)
