title: Russia’s Drone Surge Depends on Chinese Supplies
zh_title: 俄罗斯无人机激增依赖中国供应
summary: 内容提要 中华人民共和国（PRC）已成为俄罗斯无人机的主要外国供应商，提供发动机、导航部件和技术支持，一家中国国有公司现在也运输用于制造无人机碳纤维的前体。俄罗斯国营公司 Rosatom 于 2021 年开设了一家工厂，以结束俄罗斯对中国前体的依赖。然而，进口量持续激增，2026 年批准的新生产线再次寻求进口替代。俄罗斯向中国支付其无法大规模生产的商品的溢价不断上涨。与此同时，乌克兰不断扩大的长期需求
content:
内容提要 中华人民共和国（PRC）已成为俄罗斯无人机的主要外国供应商，提供发动机、导航部件和技术支持，一家中国国有公司现在也运输用于制造无人机碳纤维的前体。俄罗斯国营公司 Rosatom 于 2021 年开设了一家工厂，以结束俄罗斯对中国前体的依赖。然而，进口量持续激增，2026 年批准的新生产线再次寻求进口替代。俄罗斯向中国支付其无法大规模生产的商品的溢价不断上涨。与此同时，乌克兰不断扩大的远程打击威胁着关键的工业基地，这些工业基地的损失将加深俄罗斯对中国零部件的依赖。乌克PAN 前体是用于制造碳纤维的丙烯酸纤维，Alabuga-Volokno 在鞑靼斯坦的 Alabuga 经济特区开展业务，该经济区还拥有俄罗斯最大的 Geran 无人机工厂。这批货物被申报为民用纺织品，文件显示自 2022 年以来至少有八次类似招标。
这批货物是最新的证据，表明中华人民共和国 (PRC) 已成为俄罗斯无人机战争的主要外国供应商，其援助现已涵盖制造无人机的基本材料。它还暴露了俄罗斯国家原子能公司 (Rosatom) 在 2021 年做出的承诺的失败，当时该公司开设了一家旨在使俄罗斯摆脱中国前体的工厂（Rosatom，2021 年 11 月 22 日）。这种动态揭示了俄罗斯在制裁下实现自给自足的局限性，以及中国如何维持俄罗斯无人机行业。远程攻击无人机已成为俄罗斯打击乌克兰城市和基础设施的主要工具。据乌克兰情报总局 (HUR) 称，俄罗斯国家对 Shahed 型无人机的订单从 2024 年的约 12,000 架增加到 2026 年的超过 100,000 架，新型喷气动力 Geran-4 和 Geran-5 的产量已达到每月约 3,000 架（Ukrinform，6 月 1 日）。俄罗斯政府将无人机行业的发展视为技术独立的问题，目标是到 2030 年将该行业的自给率从 2024 年的 37.8% 提高到 81.1%（塔斯社，2025 年 1 月 9 日）。然而，实际上，扩张几乎在每个阶段都依赖中国供应商，从单个部件到完整的发动机和技术支持。
俄罗斯 Gerans 使用源自伊朗原始设计的德国发动机的中国仿制品，以及中国导航模块和调制解调器（基辅邮报，2023 年 12 月 10 日；The Insider，3 月 24 日）。第二架俄罗斯攻击无人机 Garpiya 使用来自厦门林巴赫的发动机，美国于 2024 年 10 月制裁了这家中国公司，作为美国首次指定与俄罗斯联合开发完整武器系统的中国公司的一部分（美国财政部，10 月） 2024 年 17 日）。尽管如此，随后发动机仍不断抵达，并被宣称为工业制冷机组，中国专家多次访问库波尔测试无人机并培训工作人员（路透社，2025年7月23日；RBC-乌克兰，2025年9月25日）。跨越更广泛的战场货品

【原文 English Original】
Executive summary The People’s Republic of China (PRC) has become Russia’s main foreign supplier of drones, providing engines, navigation components, and technical support, and a Chinese state-owned company now also ships the precursor used to make the drones’ carbon fiber. Russia’s state corporation, Rosatom, opened a plant in 2021 to end Russia’s reliance on Chinese precursors. Imports kept surging, however, and a new line approved in 2026 again pursues import substitution. Russia pays the PRC a rising premium for goods it cannot produce at scale. At the same time, Ukraine’s expanding long-range strikes threaten critical industrial sites, whose loss would deepen Russia’s dependence on Chinese components. Documents obtained by Ukraine’s Security and Cooperation Center (USCC) and shared with Politico in September revealed that Jilin Chemical Fiber Group, a Chinese state-owned company, had shipped 46 metric tons of polyacrylonitrile (PAN) precursor to Alabuga-Volokno, a subsidiary of Russia’s state corporation Rosatom ( Politico , September 4). PAN precursor is the acrylic fiber used to make carbon fiber, and Alabuga-Volokno operates in Tatarstan’s Alabuga Special Economic Zone, which also hosts Russia’s largest factory for Geran drones. The cargo was declared as civilian textile, and the documents point to at least eight similar tenders since 2022. The shipment is the latest evidence that the People’s Republic of China (PRC) has become the main foreign supplier of Russia’s drone warfare, and that its assistance now reaches the basic materials from which the drones are built. It also exposes the failure of a pledge that Rosatom made in 2021, when it opened a plant meant to free Russia from Chinese precursors ( Rosatom , November 22, 2021). This dynamic reveals both the limits of Russia’s drive for self-sufficiency under sanctions and how the PRC sustains the Russian drone industry. Long-range attack drones have become Russia’s main instrument for striking Ukrainian cities and infrastructure. According to Ukraine’s Main Directorate of Intelligence (HUR), the Russian state order for Shahed-type drones grew from about 12,000 units in 2024 to more than 100,000 in 2026, and output of the newer jet-powered Geran-4 and Geran-5 has reached about 3,000 units a month ( Ukrinform , June 1). The Russian government has framed the growth of its drone industry as a matter of technological independence, aiming to raise the industry’s self-sufficiency from 37.8 percent in 2024 to 81.1 percent by 2030 ( TASS , January 9, 2025). In practice, however, the expansion has relied on Chinese suppliers at almost every stage, ranging from single components to complete engines and technical support. Russian Gerans use Chinese copies of the German engine from the original Iranian design, along with Chinese navigation modules and modems ( Kyiv Post , December 10, 2023; The Insider , March 24). A second Russian attack drone, the Garpiya, uses engines from Xiamen Limbach, a Chinese firm the United States sanctioned in October 2024 as part of its first designation of Chinese companies for jointly developing a complete weapons system with Russia ( U.S. Treasury Department , October 17, 2024). Nevertheless, the engines kept arriving afterward, declared as industrial refrigeration units, and Chinese specialists visited Kupol repeatedly to test drones and train staff ( Reuters , July 23, 2025; RBC-Ukraine , September 25, 2025). Across the wider range of battlefield goods that Western governments have placed under export controls, the PRC accounts for about 75 percent of Russia’s imports ( Kyiv School of Economics , July 3). The precursor trade extends this pattern to the material from which the drones themselves are built. Carbon fiber keeps Russia’s drones light enough to carry fuel and explosives over more than 1,000 kilometers (621 miles) and increases stealthiness. The Geran-2 fuselage and wings are built on a carbon fiber structural frame, and the newer jet-powered Geran-5 has a carbon fiber skin, wings, and tail mounted on the internal airframe ( Ukrainska Pravda , November 25, 2023; New Voice of Ukraine , January 19). Without this material, drones would be heavier, sacrificing either range or payload.  Carbon fiber is only as good as its precursor. Research on carbon fiber production shows that the fiber’s mechanical properties depend heavily on precursor quality ( Progress in Materials Science , 2020). The precursor accounts for about half the cost of standard carbon fiber and more than three-quarters of the cost of fine grades used in aerospace ( Heliyon , October 2019). Producing it requires specialized expertise in polymer chemistry and fiber spinning, which Russia has long lacked. Until 2021, the PRC supplied about 80 percent of Russia’s precursor supply ( Economic Security Council of Ukraine , 2025). The war has further narrowed Russia’s options. Sanctions and export controls imposed since 2022 have cut Russia off from Western and Japanese high-grade fiber producers. In the first nine months of 2024, Chinese companies supplied 72 percent of Russia’s carbon fiber imports by weight ( Economic Security Council of Ukraine , 2025). The PRC has since become the world’s leading producer, holding more than half of global carbon fiber capacity in 2025, with Jilin Chemical Fiber as the world’s largest producer ( ATA Carbon Fiber Technology , 2025).  Rosatom’s precursor plant was meant to end this dependence. Opened at Alabuga in November 2021, it was designed to produce 5,000 tons of precursor a year and to replace the material previously imported from the PRC ( Rosatom , November 22, 2021). Trade data, however, show that Chinese precursors continued to arrive after the plant opened. Between March 2022 and January 2025, Alabuga-Volokno imported about 3,000 tons of Chinese synthetic yarn worth $21.4 million from two companies of the Jilin group ( Frontelligence Insight , August 21, 2025). Because each ton of carbon fiber requires 2 to 2.5 tons of precursor, these imports, at roughly 1,000 tons a year, would have produced about 400–500 tons of fiber, close to the 407 tons Alabuga-Volokno produced in 2022 ( Economic Security Council of Ukraine , 2025). Chinese precursors alone could have supplied almost the entire output of Rosatom’s fiber line, suggesting the domestic plant has not replaced Chinese supply. Since 2022, demand has risen sharply. By early 2024, Umatex, the Rosatom division that owns Alabuga-Volokno, reported that its carbon fiber plant was fully loaded and that customers were waiting in line for its output, a change it attributed to the growth of Russia’s civilian composites market ( Atomvestnik , April 1, 2024). The timing coincides with the expansion of drone production at Alabuga, however, where the plant has become an important source of carbon fiber for Shahed-type drones. In May, Russian officials approved a new Alabuga-Volokno line with its own precursor unit, due in 2027, and justified it as import substitution ( Politico , September 20; Ukrainska Pravda , September 21). Five years after the first plant opened, Rosatom is building a second to solve the same problem, implicitly admitting the 2021 plant did not end Russia’s reliance on Chinese precursors. Chinese assistance comes at a growing price for Russia. Moscow paid roughly 300 percent more for Chinese battlefield goods in 2025 than Beijing’s other customers did, and this premium has risen in step with Russia’s reliance on Chinese supply ( Kyiv School of Economics , July 3). The relationship is asymmetric. Russia depends on the PRC for materials it cannot produce at the required scale, while the PRC can set the price and terms. The optical fiber case shows what this dependence looks like when domestic production disappears altogether. Russia’s only optical fiber plant, located in Saransk, stopped working after Ukrainian drone strikes in the spring of 2025, which left Moscow completely dependent on Chinese optical fiber ( Militarnyi , February 26). For Ukraine, the case points to targets that are harder for Russia to replace than other defense-industrial infrastructures. A carbon fiber plant takes years to build and relies on highly specialized equipment; losing it would affect every drone that depends on its output, inflicting significant damage on the entire industry. It would raise the cost of war for Russia, as it would be forced to deepen its dependence on Chinese components to keep delivering drones to the frontline. Russia treats Alabuga-Volokno as a site worth protecting, as satellite imagery shows lattice towers built around the plant to carry nets against Kyiv’s long-range drones ( Institute for Science and International Security , August 27; New Voice of Ukraine , August 29). For Russia, the drone program is absorbing capacity once meant for civilian industry. Carbon fiber from the Alabuga plant was intended for civilian aviation and Rosatom’s nuclear fuel centrifuges, yet by 2030 up to 89 percent of the plant’s output is expected to go to defense enterprises ( Militarnyi , September 7). For Europe, sanctioning the Chinese side of this chain could be politically coherent and costly at the same time. When the European Union listed Chinese entities in its sanctions package in July, Beijing responded the following day by placing 14 European companies and institutions under its own export controls ( European Commission , July 22; South China Morning Post , July 24). Consequently, sanctioning Chinese suppliers such as Jilin would come at a cost, including for European defense companies that depend on Chinese components. The Jilin shipment is small in isolation. It confirms, however, that the PRC’s assistance to Russia’s drone industry now extends from engines and electronics to the materials used to build the drones. Rosatom promised in 2021 to end Russia’s reliance on Chinese precursors, and five years later it is building a second plant to reach the same goal, most plausibly because the first cannot produce the fine grades required by the drone program at scale. The rapid scaling of Ukraine’s long-range drone attacks poses a new threat to Russia’s carbon fiber supply chain, since plants such as Alabuga-Volokno now lie within reach of Ukrainian strikes. The post Russia’s Drone Surge Depends on Chinese Supplies appeared first on Jamestown .

title: Lula’s Brazil win puts rare earths in Trump’s crosshairs
zh_title: 卢拉在巴西的胜利使稀土成为特朗普的瞄准目标
summary: 巴西总统路易斯·伊纳西奥·卢拉·达席尔瓦的选举胜利将加强政府对该国丰富的稀土资源的控制，增加外国矿商的赌注以及华盛顿减少对中国依赖的努力。卢拉在周日竞争激烈的决选中击败了极右翼参议员弗拉维奥·博尔索纳罗，如果选举当局确认结果，他将获得第四个非连续任期。他的下一个任期将于 2027 年 1 月 5 日开始，延长一项旨在将更多矿产加工和制造业留在巴西的产业政策。 “这个国家不会接受成为任何人的bac
content:
巴西总统路易斯·伊纳西奥·卢拉·达席尔瓦的选举胜利将加强政府对该国丰富的稀土资源的控制，增加外国矿商的赌注以及华盛顿减少对中国依赖的努力。卢拉在周日竞争激烈的决选中击败了极右翼参议员弗拉维奥·博尔索纳罗，如果选举当局确认结果，他将获得第四个非连续任期。他的下一个任期将于 2027 年 1 月 5 日开始，延长一项旨在将更多矿产加工和制造业留在巴西的产业政策。卢拉在胜选演讲中表示，“这个国家不会接受成为任何人的后院”，这表明他将继续抵制美国总统唐纳德·特朗普的压力，特朗普政府对巴西商品征收了更高的关税。 GEM 矿业咨询公司首席执行官胡安·伊格纳西奥·古兹曼 (Juan Ignacio Guzmán) 表示，这一结果强化了巴西最近制定的关键矿产战略，而不是标志着重大政策转变。古兹曼告诉 MINING.COM：“卢拉的胜利最终巩固了巴西近年来的发展轨迹，特别是确认了该国今年 9 月推出的关键矿产政策，因此仍然相对较新。”巴西拥有世界第二大稀土储量，美国地质调查局估计为 2100 万吨 (Mt)，仅次于中国。
这一资源基础使该国成为西方政府寻求电动汽车、风力涡轮机和国防技术所用材料替代供应的日益重要的目标。 稀土野心 尽管卢拉政府采取行动加强对战略矿产资产的监管，但外国投资者已经准备开发巴西尚未开发的稀土潜力。巴西国家矿业局截至 6 月份的记录显示，该国 2,727 份稀土勘探申请中，外资公司占 42%，其中以澳大利亚、美国和加拿大投资者为主。超过 86% 的申请是在过去三年提交的，突显出人们对存款的兴趣迅速增加，这有助于实现中国主导的供应链多元化。该国唯一的商业稀土生产商 Serra Verde 被美国稀土公司（纳斯达克股票代码：USAR）收购，美国政府持有该公司 10% 的股份，凸显了华盛顿对巴西矿产生产日益增长的经济利益。古兹曼表示，卢拉的做法可能会强调采矿业与下游工业活动（特别是炼油业）之间的更大程度的整合。莱纳斯计划在国家支持下建设巴西稀土厂“如果开发新的稀土开采项目，理想的目标不仅是生产原矿或精矿，而且还要在巴西境内开展精炼活动，”他说。
巴西的关键矿产政策建立了一个框架，以便政府对战略矿产资产进行更严格的审查，包括可能影响国家经济或地缘政治安全的公司控制权和国际供应协议的变化。这些措施可能会使收购和投资决策复杂化，特别是在交易涉及重大外国影响力的情况下。巴西矿业律师兼 Mattos Filho Advogados 合伙人阿德里亚诺·德拉蒙德·特林达德 (Adriano Drummond Trindade) 表示，业界主要关注的是政府将如何实施新政策，而不是卢拉连任本身。 “矿业投资者习惯于政府

【原文 English Original】
Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s election victory is set to reinforce government control over the country’s vast rare earth resources, raising the stakes for foreign miners and Washington’s efforts to reduce dependence on China. Lula defeated far-right Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in Sunday’s closely contested runoff, securing a fourth nonconsecutive term if electoral authorities confirm the result. His next term begins Jan. 5, 2027, extending an industrial policy that seeks to keep more mineral processing and manufacturing in Brazil. “This country will not accept being anyone’s backyard,” Lula said in his victory speech , signalling continued resistance to pressure from US President Donald Trump, whose administration has imposed higher tariffs on Brazilian goods. The outcome reinforces Brazil’s recently established critical minerals strategy rather than signalling a major policy shift, according to Juan Ignacio Guzmán, CEO of GEM Mining Consulting. “Lula’s win ultimately reinforces Brazil’s trajectory in recent years and, in particular, confirms the country’s critical minerals policy, which was launched in September of this year and is therefore still relatively new,” Guzmán told MINING.COM. Brazil holds the world’s second-largest rare earth reserves , estimated at 21 million tonnes (Mt) by the US Geological Survey , trailing only China. That resource base makes the country an increasingly important target for Western governments seeking alternative supplies of materials used in electric vehicles, wind turbines and defence technologies. Rare earth ambitions Foreign investors are already positioning themselves to develop Brazil’s largely untapped rare earth potential, even as Lula’s government moves to strengthen oversight of strategic mineral assets. Records from Brazil’s National Mining Agency through June show that foreign-owned companies filed 42% of the country’s 2,727 rare earth exploration applications, led by investors from Australia, the US and Canada. More than 86% of the applications were submitted over the past three years, highlighting the rapid acceleration of interest in deposits that could help diversify supply chains dominated by China. The country’s only commercial rare earth producer, Serra Verde, was acquired by USA Rare Earth (Nasdaq: USAR) in which the US government holds a 10% stake , underscoring Washington’s growing financial interest in Brazilian mineral production. Guzmán said Lula’s approach would likely emphasize greater integration between mining and downstream industrial activities, particularly refining. Lynas plans Brazil rare earths plant with state support “If new rare earth mining projects are developed, the goal would ideally be not only to produce raw minerals or concentrates but also to carry out refining activities within Brazil,” he said. Brazil’s critical minerals policy establishes a framework for greater government scrutiny of strategic mineral assets, including changes in corporate control and international supply agreements that could affect national economic or geopolitical security. The measures could complicate acquisitions and investment decisions, particularly where transactions involve substantial foreign influence. Adriano Drummond Trindade, a Brazilian mining lawyer and partner at Mattos Filho Advogados, said the industry’s principal concern is how the government will implement the new policy, rather than Lula’s re-election itself. “Mining investors are used to governmental screening, as long it is predictable, applied with consistency and in timely fashion,” Trindade told MINING.COM. He said the election gives the administration that negotiated the legislation in Congress responsibility for putting it into practice, providing continuity, but also placing greater importance on the forthcoming regulations. “As long as the three factors mentioned above – predictability, consistency and timely response – are adequately factored in the forthcoming regulations and in practice, the re-election shall not adversely affect investment in mining,” Trindade said. Antonia Godoy, policy and regulatory affairs analyst at Chilean consultancy Plusmining, said the impact on investor confidence would be mixed, as Brazil’s push to retain more value from its mineral resources creates both regulatory challenges and new opportunities. “On the one hand, Lula’s push for a greater role for the state and for retaining more value within the country may raise red flags among investors, as it implies stricter requirements and a different investment model,” Godoy told MINING.COM. She pointed to Lula’s difficult relationship with Congress as a potential constraint on more interventionist policies, arguing that the president will have limited room to manoeuvre and will need broad political agreements to advance his agenda. At the same time, the government is offering incentives to encourage companies to establish processing and refining operations within Brazil. Provisions include tax credits of up to 20% for eligible processing, transformation and urban-mining expenditures, capped at 1 billion reais ($192 million) annually from 2030 through 2034. Projects would require government approval to qualify. Brazil funds rare-earth project in effort to tap vast reserves “The government is working to create a favourable environment for the establishment and expansion of beneficiation, separation, processing, refining and advanced materials manufacturing in Brazil,” the Ministry of Mines and Energy told MINING.COM in a written statement . The challenge will be attracting sufficient foreign financing and technical expertise without imposing regulatory conditions that undermine project economics. Washington tensions Lula’s victory leaves Latin America’s two most populous countries, Brazil and Mexico, under left-of-centre leadership, complicating Trump’s efforts to expand US influence across the region. Brazil, Latin America’s largest economy with annual GDP of about $2.6 trillion, has resisted Washington’s demands despite increased US tariffs. Lula’s renewed mandate suggests that tensions over trade and national sovereignty could persist. The outcome contrasts with the approach advocated by Flávio Bolsonaro, who favoured closer ties with the Trump administration, including strategic cooperation on critical minerals. Godoy sees a broader geopolitical consequence, arguing that Lula’s victory introduces a counterweight to the growing alignment between Washington and several Latin American governments over critical minerals. She said recent electoral victories by leaders close to the US had been pushing the region towards a more uniform approach to Washington’s mineral security agenda, potentially limiting countries’ negotiating flexibility. Guzmán, however, does not expect the political differences between Lula and Trump to significantly disrupt cooperation in the sector. “Brazil is currently viewed as a strategic partner of the United States in the global race for critical minerals,” he said. “Therefore, I do not anticipate any major repercussions in this regard.” Op-Ed: Brazil’s critical minerals push comes with a catch Trindade also expects commercial interests to outweigh diplomatic friction, arguing that Brazil’s dependence on foreign capital limits how far the government can go in imposing additional conditions on mining investors. “Even if the Lula administration may want to increase screening and add requirements for local industrialization to a certain degree, such measures cannot simply scare away such investment that is so needed for Brazil’s mining sector,” he said. Washington has already signalled a willingness to support Brazilian processing and refining as part of its efforts to diversify critical minerals supply chains. US embassy sources told MINING.COM in September that American representatives had signalled a willingness to support domestic processing and refining, recognizing that agreements focused solely on raw-material exports may not satisfy Brazilian authorities. Trindade said US government agencies and private investors have continued pursuing opportunities in Brazil despite the introduction of the critical minerals policy and uncertainty surrounding the presidential election. “Given that mining investment is long term and high risk, the need for investment in the sector usually supplants political tensions,” Trindade said. Guzmán sees considerable scope for agreements combining US financing, technology transfers and long-term mineral supply contracts with Brazilian industrial development. Such arrangements could help finance projects with tighter economics, provided domestic processing is technically and commercially viable. The analyst cautioned that Brazil must also address regulatory uncertainty to attract the investment required. “The Brazilian government should provide clearer and more stable regulatory frameworks regarding permitting, ownership rights, and supply commitments to the United States and other countries,” Guzmán said. Lula’s political history suggests that industrial development and national sovereignty will remain prominent themes during what could be his final presidential term. The veteran leader began his career as a union leader in the 1970s before helping establish the Workers’ Party. After three unsuccessful presidential campaigns, he won the presidency in 2002 and secured re-election in 2006. He was succeeded in 2010 by former cabinet minister Dilma Rousseff, who won another term in 2014. Lula returned to power after defeating Jair Bolsonaro in 2022. Sunday’s victory, coming shortly before his 81st birthday, may mark the final electoral triumph of a political career spanning five decades. Mining companies will be looking at whether Lula can translate Brazil’s geological advantage into a competitive processing industry while maintaining the international partnerships needed to finance its development. The potential for cooperation with Washington remains substantial, but its success will depend on how both governments balance strategic mineral security, commercial viability and Brazil’s ambitions to capture more value from its resources.

content: 中美对标   @new_voa  ·  Oct 22 (上) 文章说：今天的中国，正在出现类似明朝的政治和社会特征。明朝初期曾经探索外部世界，但随后逐渐转向闭关锁国。统治者对外国的影响越来越警惕，强调恢复所谓正统的中华文明。习总近年来推动的意识形态政策，与明朝存在明显的相似之处。 例如，明朝压制某些外来宗教信仰；今天，北京推动基督教和伊斯兰教中国化。明朝强调儒r家伦2理和传统家庭秩序；习总则不断强调要求妇女发挥贤x妻良母、建设家庭文明的作用。这些政策不仅不能解决人口危机，反而可能让问题更加严重。 2013年至2024年，中国新登记结婚人数下降了约55%。越来越多女性希望接受教育、发展事业，拥有自主决定婚姻和生育的权利。但中共最高领导层全部由男性组成；他们仍然试图通过生育补贴、宣传多孩家庭，以及收紧离婚等措施，鼓励年轻人结婚生育。 这种政策忽视了年轻人的真实处境，也进一步加剧了男女之间的矛盾。中国人口在2021年达到约14亿的顶峰，此后每年减少300万到400万人，相当于每年少掉一座洛杉矶。按照作者引用的人口趋势，到2040年代，中国每年可能减少约1000万人。 另一个可能的解决生育率持续下降的办法，就是引进外国移民。韩国也曾经是一个相对封闭的社会，但为了应对劳动力短缺，已经开始接纳更多的外国劳工。如今外国居民约占韩国人口的5%。相比之下，外国居民只占中国人口的约0.1%。中共不断宣传外国文化渗透、间谍威胁和民族主义，可能让中国未来更难吸引外国劳工。 随着经济增长放缓、人口持续老化，中国面临的问题可能逐渐演变成更严重的社会不满。 但北京的应对方式，很可能不是进行制度改革，而是加强监控和维稳。文章预测，未来几十年，中共可能越来越倾向于把人口、经济，和社会问题，当成国家安全问题来处理；通过网格化管理、全面监控和政治压制，维持表面上的社会稳定。但是，压制不等于解决问题。(未完) (中) 明朝已经给我们提供了一个历史教训。到了16世纪末期，明朝已经出现严重的财政问题。长期战争和政府开支耗尽了国库。当时的改革家 张居正 试图扩大税基，让地主和权贵承担更多的财政负担。但这遭到了这些阶层的强烈反对。 1582年 张居正 去世之后，他推动的改革遭到推翻，甚至他本人也被追究。结果，国家财政负担最终落到了普通农民的身上。今天的中国也出现了类似的局面。 首先，中国的财政压力也已经开始显现。 一些地方政府出现赤字，甚至难以及时支付教师和公务员的工资和福利。与此同时，农村居民和农民工参加医保的个人缴费，在过去20年里平均每年上涨约20%。由于无力承担费用，近年来约8300万人退出了相关医保。最近，中共还开始大数据找人交社保。这些情况与明朝晚期的财政危机中，国家将负担不断转嫁给社会弱势群体的做法，非常相似。 明朝晚期的政治体系也逐渐陷入瘫痪。万历皇帝因为接班人问题，与朝廷官员长期对立。他在位后期，朝廷的大量奏z章无人批阅，重要官职长期空缺，官僚集团陷入严重的派系斗争。整个国家虽然仍然维持着庞大的行政体系，但最高层的政治僵局，已经严重削弱了政府的治理能力。 习总上台以后，政治权力重新向个人集中，官员们也越来越不敢纠正最高领导人的错误。疫情期间，上海官员发现，原本尝试采取相对精准的防疫措施与习总坚持的清零政策不一致之后，最终选择服从中央。 结果是，上海经历了长达两个月的严厉封锁，许多居民甚至无法稳定获得食物和药品。但上海市委书记李强没有因此失去政治前途，反而在2022年进入政治局常委，2023年成为国务院总理。这种政治环境向官员传递的信号是：执行最高领导人的意志，比解决实际问题更加重要。 这种政治瘫痪，也反映在中国的人口和社会保障政策上。中国长期实行较低的退休年龄。研究人员早已预测，覆盖约5亿城镇职工和退休人员的主要养老金基金，可能在2030年代中期耗尽。提高退休年龄的改革讨论了十多年，直到2024年才正式启动，而且要到2040年才能全部落实。(未完) (下) 习总长期掌权，官僚体系越来越缺乏自主决策能力，而接班人问题迟迟没有解决。到了2030年代或者2040年代，中国可能同时面临政治停滞、官僚体系衰弱，以及最高领导层的继承危机。 更值得注意的是，明朝最终并不是被某一个单独的问题击垮的。而是财政困难、政治瘫痪、社会不平等和自然灾害不断叠加，最终引爆的危机。 1620年代，明朝政府削减开支，导致原本担任驿站职员的 李自成 失去工作。后来他加入反叛势力，发动了起义；到了1630年代，严重的旱灾和饥荒，让大批走投无路的农民投靠李自成。1644年，明朝灭亡。 问题是，未来，中国如果为了应对财政危机，削减体制内人员的养老金和福利，会不会激起类似的不满？当政治制度长期无法解决社会矛盾时，看似不相关的问题，可能在某个时刻相互叠加，形成危机。 一些美国学者也担心，当中国领导层意识到国家实力可能已经接近顶峰、未来将面临更严重的人口和经济压力时，可能选择在形势进一步恶化之前，对台湾采取军事冒险。 很难想象，今天的中国可能面临类似明朝晚期的历史危机。但大国衰落往往不是因为某一天突然出现一个无法解决的问题。而是原本可以解决的问题，被统治者一再拖延；原本可以改革的制度，因为既得利益而无法改变；原本可以缓和的社会矛盾，在政治压制下不断累积。等到这些矛盾最终爆发时，往往已经太晚。 400多年前的明朝，曾经拥有庞大的疆域、人口和财富，却最终被财政崩溃、政治瘫痪与社会动荡拖入深渊。今天的中国当然不是明朝，历史也不会简单重复。但如果一个国家只能不断强化统治，却越来越无法解决自己的问题，那么再强大的国家机器，也不能够阻止它走向自己的黄昏。(完) https:// youtu.be/xrzgEVZXLNA?si =tuMtbmkcmC2mh41w 来自 @YouTube

title: 《克里姆林宮的中國急先鋒》簡介、目録、序
summary: 博客來 克里姆林宮的中國急先鋒 The Kremlin’s Chinese Advance Guard: Chinese Students in Soviet Russia, 1917–1940 作者： 達利亞．阿林切瓦 , 亞歷山大．潘佐夫 新功能介紹 原文作者： Daria A. Arincheva , Alexander V. Pantsov 譯者： 梁思文 , 何修瑜 出版社： 聯經出版公司 新功能介紹 出版日期：2026/10/15 ISBN：9789570881
content: 博客來 克里姆林宮的中國急先鋒 The Kremlin’s Chinese Advance Guard: Chinese Students in Soviet Russia, 1917–1940 作者： 達利亞．阿林切瓦 , 亞歷山大．潘佐夫   新功能介紹 原文作者： Daria A. Arincheva , Alexander V. Pantsov 譯者： 梁思文 , 何修瑜 出版社： 聯經出版公司   新功能介紹 出版日期：2026/10/15 ISBN：9789570881783 內容簡介 是浪漫的革命理想，還是殘酷的清洗與鬥爭地獄？ 在這個酷寒國度中，共產與理想的殿堂，將對兩位後來的國家領導人 ──蔣經國、鄧小平──帶來什麼樣的影響？   ★偉大理想與熱情青春，留下的卻是血色教訓。★   紅色麥加：救國理想與革命輸出的交會點 1920年代，莫斯科是全球共產革命者朝聖的「紅色麥加」。數以千計的中國青年懷抱救國理想，跨越西伯利亞進入蘇聯的共產主義大學，期望為中國打造新的未來，夢想規劃烏托邦中國的藍圖。但這一場浪漫的追求，卻一步步捲入極權政治的漩渦，最終成為一場煉獄。   領袖同窗：重塑國共兩黨的祕密基因 國共兩黨的未來領袖蔣經國與鄧小平，皆曾在此學習。學校刻入他們的記憶裡，不只是共產主義的理想，更有紀律、批鬥以及集權統治的思維。蔣經國對蘇聯經歷諱莫如深，但日後他的政治職務與手腕都隱含這段經歷的影響。鄧小平後來所推行的中國特色社會主義，也被認為帶有蘇聯基因。這段莫斯科歲月，深刻影響了中國與台灣的政治發展。   解密檔案：革命真的可以被「輸出」嗎？ 歷史學家阿林切瓦與潘佐夫運用了首度公開的布爾什維克黨的紀錄片素材與第三國際檔案，以及中國留學生與史達林的勞改營囚犯回憶錄，重建了1917至1940年間鮮為人知的歷史現場。當革命成為可以「輸出」的理想工程，等待這群年輕人的，究竟是烏托邦，還是權力吞噬信仰的血色教訓？   作者 簡介 達利亞．阿林切瓦（ Daria A. Arincheva ） 俄國莫斯科高等經濟學院（National Research University Higher School of Economics）中國研究的副教授。她已出版十五種以上著作，包括 Chinese Revolutionaries in Soviet Russia in the 1920s and the 1930s (2015)與 Lives and Fates of the First Chinese Communists (2021)。   亞歷山大‧潘佐夫（ Alexander V. Pantsov ） 美國俄亥俄州哥倫布市首都大學（Capital University）歷史學教授、愛德華與瑪麗‧凱薩琳‧吉賀德人文學講座（Edward and Mary Catherine Gerhold Chair in the Humanities）教授。潘佐夫生於莫斯科，畢業於莫斯科國立大學亞非學院（Moscow State University Institute of Asian and African Studies），獲俄羅斯科學院（Russian Academy of Sciences）頒授博士學位。出版多項著作，包括《蔣介石：失敗的勝利者》、《毛澤東：真實的故事》、《鄧小平：革命人生》等書。 譯者簡介 梁思文（ Steven I. Levine ） 美國蒙大拿大學（University of Montana）莫林‧曼斯菲爾德及邁克‧曼斯菲爾德中心高級研究員，哈佛大學博士。梁思文專攻現代中國政治及外交政策︑美國─東亞關係，曾出版多本譯作，包括《蔣介石：失敗的勝利者》、《毛澤東：真實的故事》、《鄧小平：革命人生》、與韓德（Micheal H.Hunt）合著的《弧形帝國：美國在亞洲的戰爭，從菲律賓到越南》（Arc of Empire: America''s Wars in Asia from the Philippines to Vietnam）等︒   何修瑜 台灣大學歷史系學士，紐約理工學院傳播藝術碩士。史學譯著包括《帝國的勝利：從哈德良到君士坦丁的羅馬世界》、《法蘭西全史》、《1953：伊朗關鍵之年，一場被掩蓋的政變》、《伊斯蘭新史》、《鄂圖曼帝國的殞落》、《在風暴來臨之前：羅馬共和國殞落的開始》等。 目錄 縮寫詞表 圖片目錄 人物介紹 前言 第一部 在俄國革命的旋風中 1 第一次世界大戰期間與大戰之後在蘇俄的中國人 2 在「紅色麥加」──東方勞動者共產主義大學的中國學生 第二部 莫斯科中山大學與中國勞動者共產主義大學 3 教育與史達林化 4 學生的派系鬥爭 第三部 俄國的中國共產黨與史達林的肅清運動 5 國際列寧學校的中國學生 6 「人民公敵」：從「赤色麥加」到勞改營 結語 致謝 附錄一：參加蘇聯國際共產黨會議的中國革命者 附錄二：國際共產主義運動最高機構的中國代表 附錄三：派駐蘇俄國際共產黨組織的中國成員與代表 註釋 索引 序 前言(節錄) 一九二一年六月二十二日傍晚七點，莫斯科大劇院裡坐滿了人。由俄國布爾什維克黨提供資金與指導方針的國際性革命組織共產國際（Communist International），召開第三次代表大會。來自五十二個國家、一百零三個共產主義組織的六百零五位代表以及為數眾多的來賓與記者，熱烈歡迎以主席團成員身分在舞台上就座的列寧（Vladimir Ilyich Lenin）、季諾維也夫（Grigorii Evseevich Zinoviev）、托洛斯基（Leon Davidovich Trotsky）與其他蘇俄領導者。名叫張太雷的二十三歲中國共產黨員是大會的正式代表，也是中國共產主義運動史上第一位與會的代表，與在場其他人一起熱烈鼓掌。他「身材高大，留著梳理整齊的長髮」，從他的圓眼鏡後方「以聰慧的堅定目光，無畏地注視著他人」，展露出開朗、燦爛的笑容。 三週後的七月十二日，在克里姆林宮豪華的安德烈耶夫廳（Andreev Hall）裡討論東方問題的第二十三次會議中，張太雷發表了一場關於中國共產黨運動的五分鐘演說。他的英語十分流利。按照大會規定，他的演說時間不能更長。他準備了一份二十二頁的書面報告，詳細說明中國政治與社會經濟現狀，以及日益壯大的共產主義勞工運動（他早在六月十日就已準備好）。這是一名實際參與發展中的中國共產黨運動成員所提交給共產國際的第一份書面報告。 除了張太雷，其他幾個中國人也參加了共產國際第三次代表大會，包括二十二歲的俞秀松，他是中國共產主義青年團臨時中央委員會書記，同時也是上海中國社會主義青年團書記的核心人物。他是中國社會主義青年團的非正式代表。此外還有二十二歲的瞿秋白，他是張太雷的同鄉與同窗，張太雷於一九二一年六月在莫斯科推薦他加入共產黨，他是以北京《晨報》記者的身分觀察大會。另一名觀察員是俞秀松與瞿秋白的同僚陳為人，是一九二○年七月十九日創建的上海布爾什維克黨圈子裡的成員，他和俞秀松也代表中國社會主義青年團。中國社會主義黨創始人之一，三十八歲的江亢虎也是正式代表，他有諮詢投票權，然而他並非共產黨員，並且在代表大會召開的第四天後，因為非正式代表俞秀松與正式代表張太雷寫了幾封信給共產國際執行委員會主席季諾維也夫，譴責他為「間諜」，他的出席資格遭取消。 張太雷、俞秀松、瞿秋白與陳為人從一開始就參與代表大會。但現在，在克里姆林宮的安德烈耶夫廳裡有同情中國共產主義的另一群人，他們三天前才來到莫斯科，剛拿到訪客通行證。他們來到這「紅色首都」，在剛開辦的共產國際學校──東方勞動者共產主義大學（俄文首字母縮寫為KUTV）上課。這些人包括劉少奇、羅亦農、吳芳、任培國（即任弼時）、蕭勁光、卜士畸、任岳、周兆秋、胡士廉、陳啟沃、謝文錦、 蔣光慈與廖劃平。他們都在上海共產黨員的推薦下抵達莫斯科。 東方勞動者共產主義大學是對中國革命分子敞開大門的第一所共產國際高等教育機構。不久之後，蘇俄將會設立全面的國際學校網絡。其目標是培訓國外的布爾什維克黨員，以便推動全世界社會主義革命，因為自從布爾什維克黨經由一九一七年的革命在俄國掌權之後，該黨從一開始就熱切地宣傳此一概念。 …… 一九一九年三月，列寧倡議的特殊組織──共產國際──在莫斯科創立，將許多國家的共產黨員集合在一起，其目的是掀起全球共產主義運動熱潮。共產國際並非政黨之間的聯盟，而是一個僅有單一計畫與章程的統一組織。它由選舉所產生的共產國際執行委員會所領導，不只是布爾什維克黨員，也有其他共產主義團體的代表參與其工作。然而俄國的共產黨員卻全盤掌握領導權。共產國際對其外國支部提供實質的組織、政治、意識形態、軍事、精神鼓舞與財務上的支援。 歐洲無產階級在一九一八至一九二三年的潰敗，尤其是一九二○年蘇俄入侵波蘭失敗，引發俄國共產黨自一九二○年代初開始，不只關注西方，也逐漸更關注東方的革命運動組織。在俄國革命與內戰期間，布爾什維克索求的大筆款項，開始透過共產國際流入各國，對象不只是歐洲與美國，也包括東方各國。中國、日本、印度、印度支那、埃及與土耳其的共產黨員都開始利用這些資金。一九二一年，共產國際給了中國共產黨一萬六千六百五十元中國幣，而在一九二二年又給了一萬五千元中國幣。如果考慮到當時的匯率是一枚中國銀元相當於金本位美元的五十分，那麼一九二一至一九二二年，共產國際給羽翼未豐的中國共產黨的金援，共計一萬五千八百二十五美元。這還只是一開始的數字。中國歷史學者楊奎松根據中共的檔案數據，斷言從中國共產黨第三次全國代表大會（一九二三年六月）開始，莫斯科幾乎全額資助該黨的運作。到了一九二七年，對中共的經濟援助已達一百萬中國幣，即五十萬美元。這筆資金分配的對象包括中國共產黨、中國共產主義青年團、工人與農民運動、對抗帝國主義、軍中的工作以及各式各樣的特別計畫。許多份俄國檔案中也顯示，不只在一九二○年代，共產國際與全聯盟共產黨（布爾什維克）在一九三○年代也對中國共產黨提供全方位的金援，這一點證實了楊奎松提出的資訊。援助的總金額高達數千萬美元。值得注意的是，即便在一九四一年六月二十二日遭到納粹德國攻擊之後，蘇聯依舊持續幫助中國共產黨。布爾什維克黨的政治局通過決議，授權共產國際執行委員會匯「一百萬美元協助中國共產黨中央委員會」。 協助的主要形式之一，就是扶持中國共產黨培訓革命幹部。以此為目標，蘇俄在許多共產國際的教育機構招收中國革命分子。一九二○與一九三○年代，蘇俄針對該領域投入許多心力。而此舉與當時中國革命運動的快速發展息息相關。 在這段時間，中國革命分子在完整的國際學校網絡求學。 …… 規模最大的教育中心，就是位於莫斯科的三所高等學府：於一九二一至一九二八年以及一九三三至一九三六年間開設給中國人就讀的東方勞動者共產主義大學，一九三六至一九三九年五月改為民族與殖民地問題科學研究院；一九二五至一九三○年間開設的莫斯科中山大學（該校於一九二八年九月重組為中國勞動者共產主義大學）；以及國際列寧學校（一九二六至一九三八年）。 一九二○與一九三○年代，有不少於三千名來自中國的共產黨與國民黨的革命分子與運動人士，在蘇維埃布爾什維克黨的直接控制之下，於這三所學校接受培訓。在保存於莫斯科的蘇聯共產黨中央委員會馬克思列寧主義研究院的原中央黨史檔案館（一九九一至一九九九年改名為俄國保存與研究當代歷史文件中心，現為俄國國家社會政治史檔案館）中，保存著中國國民黨與中國共產黨黨員的三千三百二十八份個人檔案。在這些檔案中，絕大多數都是當時在莫斯科共產國際學校就讀的中國學生。其中大約有四分之三都是中國共產黨員，而裡頭的一百六十七位黨員在中國共產黨的歷史上扮演了重要的角色。重要性特別顯著的，包括如中華人民共和國的領導人劉少奇、鄧小平、任弼時、楊尚昆、陳雲、葉劍英、鄧穎超、林彪、陳伯達、李富春、林伯渠（林祖涵）、劉長勝、吳玉章、董必武、徐特立、張聞天、王稼祥、劉伯承、蔡暢、聶榮臻、蕭勁光、烏蘭夫、閻紅彥、孔原、張琴秋、伍修權、王觀瀾。一九七○年代末與一九八○年代，這當中有許多人－－首先是鄧小平、陳雲、楊尚昆、葉劍英、烏蘭夫、鄧穎超與聶榮臻等人，在中國實施大規模經濟改革，促成中國蓬勃發展的開端。鄧小平與其他許多中共領導人在蘇俄期間以及他們的求學過程中與布爾什維克黨的接觸，無疑並沒有白費力氣。他們全都汲取了布爾什維克意識形態的影響。鄧小平領導集團引進中華人民共和國的「帶有中國特色的社會主義」概念，與蘇維埃新經濟政策極為類似，此一事實或許可解釋這些人接受蘇維埃教育的深度不可小覷。有著這樣的關聯性，研究在莫斯科接受培訓的中華人民共和國未來領導幹部的歷史，不只有助於我們了解一九二○與一九三○年代中國革命運動的發展，對於理解中華人民共和國目前的社會政治與經濟轉變，也有其顯著的重要性。 …… 一九五○到一九七○年代，對於此主題不感興趣的中國史學界，其原因顯然是遵循中國共產黨的指示。即便是在與蘇俄友好的年代，中國也無人提及一九二○至一九三○年代中國學生至蘇俄求學的事。唯一例外是中國勞工參與俄國內戰，且因此接受某些布爾什維克培訓的主題。例如一九五七至一九六一年間，雙語期刊《友誼》（Druzhba）經常提到那些經歷俄國內戰洗禮的中國人；而在一九五九年，歷史學者彭明甚至出版了一本書，書中以幾頁篇幅介紹了蘇俄工農紅軍的中國戰士。然而這位彭明卻完全沒有提到中國幹部在共產國際教育中心培訓的歷史。 這現象可以解釋，因為早在創立中華人民共和國之前，毛澤東與其他支持他的中共領導人，與某些從蘇俄返國的中國勞動者共產主義大學畢業生（博古、洛甫、王明與其他人）進行了長時間的權力鬥爭，後者受到布爾什維克黨當局的庇護。在這場鬥爭中，毛澤東對於中國革命分子在共產國際高等學府培訓的成果提出了相當負面的評價。他的主要論點是，中國共產黨員在蘇俄吸收了教條主義，他於一九三○年的論文〈反對本本主義〉（原標題為〈調查工作〉）一文中揭示了這種教條主義對中國革命的有害本質。 一九三八年九月至十一月，在粉碎了政敵之後，毛澤東開始對他們進行意識形態的再教育，宣稱「我們的戰鬥任務，就是以持續且有計畫的方式，培訓大量新幹部」。在一九四二至一九四四年的整風運動中，他勒令所有「教條主義者」（除了王明以外）在報告中承認他們在蘇俄什麼也沒學到。 舉例來說，以下是毛澤東之前一名主要政敵博古（本名秦邦憲，以化名波戈列洛夫〔Pogorelov〕於莫斯科中山大學／中國勞動者共產主義大學就讀）在他的「自白書」（一九三一年自蘇俄返回中國後，他領導中國共產主義青年團，並於一九三一至一九三五年二月擔任中共中央總書記）中寫道： 我在莫斯科接受……一種教條式的派系教育……在我個人生涯發展中，〔在蘇俄求學〕的這三年……是對我的意識有所毒害的一段時間……對於中國革命與中國共產黨而言，〔這所〕大學〔莫斯科中山大學／中國勞動者共產主義大學〕毫無用處；反之卻帶來無以計數的傷害……學生被灌輸對實踐的蔑視，盲目信仰學究式的教條，忽略了中國的現實，卻歌頌著外國「典範」……接受如此教育的翻譯幹部卻沾染對外國事物的浮誇愛好。對蘇俄與共產國際的尊重與景仰，被用來教育紅色買辦……這些學生，尤其是口譯員之中，逐漸形成了一群模範教條主義者，他們是外國走狗。 另一位中國勞動者共產主義大學畢業生楊尚昆（化名薩爾蒂科夫〔Saltykov〕）也在大約同一時間召開的某次中共中央政治局會期中說過同樣的話，周恩來也一樣，他對於共產國際執行委員會與這所大學的情況十分了解。 無論是毛澤東或任何一位中國領袖，都不敢公開對在莫斯科成立培訓中共黨員教育中心的布爾什維克黨人表達不滿。即便在一九四五年四月中共中央委員會通過權威性的〈關於若干歷史問題的決議〉中，也沒有將教條主義與蘇聯連結，但反對教條主義的鬥爭卻自然而然地組織起來，成為毛派領導階層的主要任務之一。 這也就是為什麼不僅在一九五○年代，也包括在之後，即便中共與蘇共一刀兩斷，當時的中國史學家不被准許說任何東方勞動者共產主義大學／民族與殖民地問題科學研究院、莫斯科中山大學／中國勞動者共產主義大學或國際列寧學校的任何好話，列寧與史達林主義時期的中蘇關係，都未曾在中國史學中留下悲傷的一頁。

title: China’s Communist Party elite gather for closed-door governance talks
zh_title: 中国共产党精英齐聚闭门谈治国理政
summary: 中国国家主席习近平和其他高层领导人周一在北京举行一次重要聚会，密切关注有关国家发展方向和未来领导力的线索。 2021年11月，中国共产党第十九届中央委员会第六次全体会议。资料图片：中国共产党。据官方媒体报道，大约有 300 名执政的共产党中央委员会成员出席了这次被称为五中全会的会议，他们将寻求加强内部纪律。其中包括减少腐败和提高干部效率的措施
content:
中国国家主席习近平和其他高层领导人周一在北京举行一次重要聚会，密切关注有关国家发展方向和未来领导力的线索。 2021年11月，中国共产党第十九届中央委员会第六次全体会议。资料图片：中国共产党。据官方媒体报道，大约有 300 名执政的共产党中央委员会成员出席了这次被称为五中全会的会议，他们将寻求加强内部纪律。其中包括减少腐败、提高干部效率和忠诚度的措施。这次在严密安保下举行的闭门会议在周四结束之前几乎不会公开，但会议的时机至关重要。另请参阅：关于中国共产党五中全会的信息五中全会在明年举行的一次重要党代会上召开，73岁的习近平几乎肯定会获得历史性的第四个任期并监督领导层改组。历次全会都是习近平巩固权威的关键时刻。这位中国领导人开展了长达14年的反腐败运动，清洗了数千名官员，其中包括数十名中央委员会官员。然而，他仍然对他认为干部没有执行他的命令感到沮丧。
官方媒体在全会前发表了一篇文章，内容是习近平一月份的一次讲话，其中他谴责了“两面派”官员，他们表面上遵守中央指令，但“内心抵制”，追求“个人主义”，而且是“政治机会主义”。 投票率低的分析人士告诉法新社，习近平正试图通过加强监督和规则来最大限度地提高干部的效率和忠诚度。但由于他的大规模清洗，预计今年的全会投票率将是前领导人毛泽东 1976 年去世以来的最低水平。中央委员会的 8 个席位空缺，另有 15 名成员正在接受调查并面临被替换的风险。习近平的反腐败运动还针对军队，推翻了党的最高武装部队机构中央军事委员会（CMC）七名委员中的五名。 2022年11月，习近平视察中央军委联合作战指挥中心。图片：中共新闻。据亚洲协会政策研究所称，2022 年任命的 44 名中央委员会军事成员中，只有两人没有被清洗或失踪。全会可能会任命新的中央军委委员；该党可以等到明年的代表大会来补充资金；或者习近平甚至可能重组党对其庞大军队的控制。
此次会谈也是在这个世界第二大经济体不稳定的时期举行的，该国一直在努力解决持续低迷的国内支出和关键房地产行业旷日持久的危机。与美国动荡的政治和经济关系也给中国领导人带来了压力。预计当局将在周四会议结束后发布结果摘要。

【原文 English Original】
China’s President Xi Jinping and other top leaders meet in Beijing on Monday at a key gathering watched closely for clues as to the country’s direction and future leadership. The sixth plenary session of the 19th Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party in November 2021. File photo: Communist Party of China. Roughly 300 members of the ruling Communist Party’s Central Committee in attendance at the meeting, called the fifth plenum, will be looking to tighten discipline within their ranks, according to state media. That includes measures to reduce corruption and make cadres more effective and loyal. Little of the closed-door gathering, held under tight security, will be made known until it concludes on Thursday, but the timing of the meeting is crucial. See also: What to know about the Chinese Communist Party’s Fifth Plenum The fifth plenum comes ahead of a major party congress next year, where 73-year-old Xi is almost certain to secure a historic fourth term and oversee a leadership reshuffle. Previous plenums have represented key moments for Xi to cement his authority. The Chinese leader has waged a 14-year campaign against corruption that has purged thousands of officials, including dozens of the Central Committee. Yet he remains frustrated with cadres he deems are not implementing his orders. State media published an article ahead of the plenum, based on a speech Xi gave in January in which he railed against “two-faced” officials who appear to comply with central directives but “inwardly resist”, pursue “individualism” and are “politically opportunistic”. Low turnout Analysts told AFP that Xi is trying to maximise efficiency and loyalty among cadres by imposing more supervision and rules. But as a result of his expansive purges, this year’s plenum is expected to have the lowest turnout since former leader Mao Zedong’s death in 1976. Eight of the Central Committee’s seats lie vacant, with another 15 members under investigation and at risk of being replaced. Xi’s anti-corruption drive has also targeted the military, toppling five of the seven members of the Central Military Commission (CMC), the party’s top armed forces body. Xi Jinping inspects the Central Military Commission Joint Operations Command Center in November 2022. Photo: CPC News. Of 44 military members appointed to the Central Committee in 2022, only two have not been purged or disappeared, according to the Asia Society Policy Institute. The plenum could see new members appointed to the CMC; the party could wait until next year’s congress to replenish it; or Xi might even restructure party control over its vast military. The talks also come at an unsteady time for the world’s second-largest economy, which has struggled to address persistently sluggish domestic spending and a protracted crisis in the crucial property sector. Turbulent political and economic ties with the United States are also weighing on China’s leaders. Authorities are expected to release a summary of the outcomes after the meeting concludes on Thursday.

title: Hong Kong athletes bag 41 medals at Asian Para Games with historic boccia run
zh_title: 香港运动员在亚洲残疾人运动会上凭借历史性的硬地滚球夺得41枚奖牌
summary: 香港运动员在亚洲残疾人运动会上夺得了 41 枚奖牌，夺得三块金牌，创造了香港硬地滚球的历史最好成绩。 2026 年 10 月 23 日，亚洲残疾人运动会的硬地滚球运动员。照片：中国香港残奥委员会，来自 Facebook。代表团于 10 月 18 日在日本名古屋和爱知县举行为期一周的比赛后于周日返回。来自该市的 80 名运动员参加了比赛，包括硬地滚球、游泳、乒乓球和击剑等 10 个项目。他们共获得3枚金牌、14枚银牌、24枚铜牌
content:
香港运动员在亚洲残疾人运动会上夺得了 41 枚奖牌，夺得三块金牌，创造了香港硬地滚球的历史最好成绩。 2026 年 10 月 23 日，亚洲残疾人运动会的硬地滚球运动员。照片：中国香港残奥委员会，来自 Facebook。代表团于 10 月 18 日在日本名古屋和爱知县举行为期一周的比赛后于周日返回。来自该市的 80 名运动员参加了比赛，包括硬地滚球、游泳、乒乓球和击剑等 10 个项目。他们总共获得了3枚金牌、14枚银牌和24枚铜牌。获得奖牌数量最多的是乒乓球项目，香港选手获得了 5 枚银牌和 10 枚铜牌。亚洲残疾人运动会的硬地滚球运动员梁玉荣和张源。照片：中国香港残奥委员会，来自 Facebook。在硬地滚球比赛中，运动员获得了八枚奖牌，其中包括两枚金牌、三枚银牌和三枚铜牌，创下了该队的历史最好成绩。据中国香港残奥委员会称，在比赛最后一天的混合双人项目中，老牌硬地滚球组合梁玉荣和张源以9比0击败中国国家队，为香港赢得了“至关重要的”金牌。在击剑比赛中，运动员们夺得了八枚奖牌，其中六枚奖牌由七届残奥会轮椅击剑冠军艾莉森·余 (Alison Yu) 获得。
“不屈不挠的决心” 在2023年于杭州举行的上届亚残运会上，香港赢得了47枚奖牌——8枚金牌、15枚银牌和24枚铜牌。击剑运动员余丽珊于2026年10月25日在香港国际机场。照片：中国香港残奥委员会，来自Facebook。行政长官李家超周六在一份声明中表示：“中国香港运动员在比赛中竭尽全力，展现了高超的技术和不屈不挠的决心。”他补充说：“他们的成就不仅为香港带来了荣誉，也以他们坚持不懈和永不放弃的体育精神激励了社会。”亚洲残疾人运动会紧接着亚运会，共有约 580 名香港运动员参加 38 个小项的比赛。香港代表团共夺得54枚奖牌，创奖牌总数纪录。其金牌总数为 11 枚，也是有史以来最高的。

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong athletes have brought home 41 medals from the Asian Para Games, winning three golds and achieving the city’s historic best in boccia. Boccia athletes at the Asian Para Games on October 23, 2026. Photo: China Hong Kong Paralympic Committee, via Facebook. The delegation returned on Sunday after the week-long games in Nagoya and the wider Aichi Prefecture in Japan, which began on October 18. Eighty athletes from the city competed in 10 sports at the games, including boccia, swimming, table tennis, and fencing. They won a total of three gold medals, 14 silver medals, and 24 bronze medals. The highest number of medals was won in table tennis, which saw Hong Kong competitors nab five silvers and 10 bronzes. Boccia players Leung Yuk-wing and Cheung Yuen at the Asian Para Games. Photo: China Hong Kong Paralympic Committee, via Facebook. In boccia, athletes won eight medals including two gold, three silver, and three bronze medals, marking the team’s best result in history. Veteran boccia duo Leung Yuk-wing and Cheung Yuen beat China’s national team 9-0 in a mixed pairs event on the final day of the games, securing a “crucial” gold for Hong Kong, according to the China Hong Kong Paralympic Committee. In fencing events, athletes brought home eight medals – six of which were won by Alison Yu, a seven-time Paralympic wheelchair fencing champion . ‘Indomitable determination’ During the last Asian Para Games, which were held in Hangzhou in 2023, Hong Kong won 47 medals – eight golds, 15 silvers and 24 bronze medals. Fencer Alison Yu at the Hong Kong International Airport on October 25, 2026. Photo: China Hong Kong Paralympic Committee, via Facebook. “Hong Kong, China athletes gave their utmost in the competition, demonstrating superb skills and indomitable determination,” Chief Executive John Lee said in a statement on Saturday. “Their achievements have not only brought honour to Hong Kong, but also inspired the community with their perseverance and never-give-up sportsmanship,” he added. The Asian Para Games followed the Asian Games , which saw around 580 athletes from Hong Kong competing in 38 events. The Hong Kong delegation took home 54 medals, a record for the total number of medals won. Its gold medal tally, at 11, was also the highest ever.

title: Hong Kong police arrest man allegedly caught lacing cat food with rat poison
zh_title: 香港警方逮捕一名涉嫌在猫粮中掺入老鼠药的男子
summary: 一名 34 岁男子在给流浪猫准备的食物碗中掺入老鼠药，被动物福利志愿者发现，警方以涉嫌虐待动物罪逮捕了他。何的监控录像发布在Threads上。照片：截图来自@sum_nicholas。警方在周六的一份声明中表示，当天凌晨 3.37 分左右接到举报，称这名何姓男子在猫粮碗中下了毒药。志愿者设置的摄像头录制的监控录像拍下了他的行为，并在社交媒体上疯传，还有志愿者后来对峙的视频。
content:
一名 34 岁男子在给流浪猫准备的食物碗中掺入老鼠药，被动物福利志愿者发现，警方以涉嫌虐待动物罪逮捕了他。何的监控录像发布在Threads上。照片：截图来自@sum_nicholas。警方在周六的一份声明中表示，当天凌晨 3.37 分左右接到举报，称这名何姓男子在猫粮碗中下了毒药。志愿者设置的摄像头录制的监控录像捕捉到了他的行为，并在社交媒体上疯传，还有志愿者后来与他对峙的视频。警方简报称，到达现场的警员在嫌疑人身上发现了一包老鼠诱饵和一把14厘米水果刀，并以涉嫌虐待动物和持有攻击性武器的罪名逮捕了他。受污染的猫粮的图像。照片：@hksaar.io，来自 Threads。何先生被扣留作进一步调查，案件由深水埗警区重案组接手。警方声明称，此案中没有猫受到伤害。 “请不要伤害它们” 在志愿者与何先生对峙的视频中，何先生否认试图伤害这些猫，并表示他只是想阻止流浪猫吃这些食物，以保持该地区的清洁。志愿者回应称，中毒的猫只会死在公共场所，造成更多卫生问题。
视频中可以看到何鸿燊穿着一件跑步背心，上面贴有“狼天使”或“狼钩”徽章——这一符号起源于中世纪德国纹章，后来在纳粹象征主义中广泛采用。截获34岁的香港涉嫌虐待动物报告（HKSAAR）的动物福利组织之一在Threads上表示，它已经监视何鸿燊一个多月了。 Ho 的跑步装备上有 Wolfsangel 补丁。照片：线程。香港特别行政区早在六月份就发布了有毒猫粮的照片，当时它是由与之合作的另一个志愿者组织首次发现的。照片显示，干粗粮上覆盖着一层厚厚的黑色糊状物，水碗里还有疑似老鼠诱饵的蓝色颗粒。根据香港法律，虐待动物的最高刑罚为罚款20万港元和监禁三年。其中一名志愿者尼古拉斯·萨姆(Nicholas Sum)周日在一篇帖子中表示：“你不必爱他们，但请不要伤害他们。” “我们埋伏了整整一个月，终于抓住了他。”萨姆说。 “非常感谢所有猫类救援志愿者、当地邻居和香港特别行政区管理局连续多个通宵追捕（嫌疑人）。”

【原文 English Original】
Police have arrested a 34-year-old man on suspicion of animal cruelty after animal welfare volunteers caught him lacing bowls of food left out for stray cats with rat poison. Surveillance footage of Ho posted on Threads. Photo: Screenshot via @sum_nicholas. In a Saturday statement, police said that a report was received at around 3.37am that day alleging that the man, surnamed Ho, had spiked bowls of cat food with poison. Surveillance footage recorded using cameras set up by the volunteers caught him in the act and went viral on social media, along with videos of the volunteers later confronting him. The police brief stated that officers who arrived on the scene found a packet of rat bait and a 14 cm fruit knife on the suspect and arrested him on suspicion of animal cruelty and possession of an offensive weapon. Images of the contaminated cat food. Photo: @hksaar.io via Threads. Ho was detained for further investigation, with his case taken over by the Sham Shui Po police district’s crime unit. No cats were harmed in the case, the police statement said. ‘Please do not harm them’ In the viral video of volunteers confronting Ho, he denied trying to harm the cats and said that he only wanted to deter the strays from eating the food to keep the area clean. The volunteers responded that the poisoned cats would only die in public areas, causing more hygiene issues. Ho can be seen in the video wearing a running vest with a patch bearing the Wolfsangel or “wolf’s hook” insignia – a symbol that originated in medieval German heraldry and was later adopted widely in Nazi symbolism. One of the animal welfare groups that intercepted the 34-year-old, Hong Kong Suspected Animal Abuse Report (HKSAAR), said on Threads that it had been monitoring Ho for more than a month. A Wolfsangel patch on Ho’s running gear. Photo: Threads. HKSAAR released photos of the poisoned cat food as far back as June, when it was first uncovered by another volunteer group it had been working with. The photos showed a thick black paste covering pieces of dry kibble, as well as blue granules of suspected rat bait in bowls of water. Under Hong Kong law, the maximum penalty for animal cruelty is a HK$200,000 fine and three years’ imprisonment. One of the volunteers, Nicholas Sum, said in a post on Sunday: “You don’t have to love them, but please do not harm them.” “After lying in wait for an entire month, we finally caught him,” Sum said. “Huge thanks to all the cat rescue volunteers, local neighbours, and HKSAAR for pulling multiple all-nighters in a row to track [the suspect] down.”

title: Lawmaker questions whether proposed HK$100,000 fines for private hospitals will deter hidden fees
zh_title: 立法会议员质疑对私家医院罚款10万港元是否能阻止隐性收费
summary: 一名香港立法会议员质疑政府提高香港私营医疗保健提供者价格透明度的提议所规定的罚款是否太低，无法起到有效的威慑作用。新民党议员何鸿燊对 2026 年 2 月 25 日的预算案作出回应。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。根据卫生部长罗仲茂周五向立法会提交的拟议法案，私人医疗服务提供者将被要求在接待处和收银台提供双语价目表。他们还必须在治疗前向患者提供预算估算
content:
一名香港立法会议员质疑政府提高香港私营医疗保健提供者价格透明度的提议所规定的罚款是否太低，无法起到有效的威慑作用。新民党议员何鸿燊对 2026 年 2 月 25 日的预算案作出回应。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。根据卫生部长罗仲茂周五向立法会提交的拟议法案，私人医疗服务提供者将被要求在接待处和收银台提供双语价目表。他们还必须在具体治疗和手术之前向患者提供预算估算，并在患者的账单比原始估算高出 20% 或更多时提供解释。新规定将适用于所有私人诊所、医院和保健中心。不遵守规定的私家医院每次违规最高可被罚款10万港元。对于日间手术中心和诊所，罚款最高可达 25,000 港元。建制派新民党议员何鸿燊向立法会部长表示，拟议的罚款可能太低，不足以对私立医院产生威慑作用。何说，一些私立医院，例如“跑马地一家”——可能是指养和医院——赚取“巨额利润”，10万港元对他们来说只是一笔小钱。卫生局局长罗仲茂。资料照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。
何先生用粤语说：“即使罚款10次，也只是100万港元，这对他们来说只是零钱。”对此，卫生局长表示，将根据具体情况开出罚单。 “如果一家大医院看诊人数较多，多次被罚款，累计罚款金额就相当可观了。”罗用粤语说。无价格上限 除了向患者提供价格信息和预算估算外，拟议的法案还将要求私立医院向卫生部提交与特定治疗和程序相关的账单统计数据和数据。持有执照的私立医院还必须公布历史账单统计数据，包括出院情况、住院时间中位数、住院费用和医生费用。罗告诉立法者，政府不会考虑限制私人医疗机构的收费，因为如果价格太高，患者可以去其他地方。香港中文大学医院是一家新私立医院，于 2021 年开业。照片：Wai Ki Wong/Google 地图。政府在提案中表示，新规定还将考虑医疗服务的性质——治疗过程中可能出现不可预见的临床因素，从而产生难以提前预测的医疗费用。
如果机构发现无法提供预算估算（例如，在需要立即护理的突发医疗紧急情况期间），则应在治疗后 48 小时内向患者或其代表提供固定的服务价格。

【原文 English Original】
A Hong Kong lawmaker has questioned whether fines under a government proposal to increase price transparency among the city’s private healthcare providers are too low to serve as an effective deterrent. Lawmaker Adrian Ho of the New People’s Party responds to the budget address on February 25, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Under the proposed bill introduced to the Legislative Council by health minister Lo Chung-mau on Friday, private healthcare providers will be required to provide a bilingual price list at reception desks and cashier counters. They must also give patients budget estimates before specific treatments and procedures and provide an explanation if patients’ bills are 20 per cent or more above the original estimate. The new rules will apply to all private clinics, hospitals, and health centres. Private hospitals that do not comply will see a maximum fine of HK$100,000 for each violation. For day procedure centres and clinics, this penalty falls to a maximum fine of HK$25,000. Adrian Ho, a lawmaker with the pro-establishment New People’s Party, told the minister in LegCo that the proposed fines might be too low to have a deterrent effect on private hospitals. Ho said some private hospitals, such as “one in Happy Valley” – likely a reference to the Hong Kong Sanatorium & Hospital – earn “massive profits” and HK$100,000 is a small sum for them. Secretary for Health Lo Chung-mau. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “Even if they are fined 10 times, that’s just HK$1 million, which is just loose change for them,” Ho said in Cantonese. In response, the health chief said penalty tickets would be issued on a per-case basis. “If a major hospital sees a high volume of patients and is fined repeatedly, the cumulative fines can add up to a substantial sum,” Lo said in Cantonese. No price cap Apart from providing price information and budget estimates to patients, the proposed bill will also require private hospitals to submit statistics on billing and figures related to specific treatments and procedures to the Department of Health. Licensed private hospitals will also have to publish historical billing statistics including discharges, median lengths of stay, hospital fees, and medical practitioners’ fees. Lo told legislators that the government is not considering capping the prices charged by private healthcare facilities, since patients can simply go elsewhere if prices are too high. CUHK Medical Centre, a new private hospital opened in 2021. Photo: Wai Ki Wong/Google Maps. The government said in its proposal that the new rules will also take into account the nature of healthcare services – unforeseeable clinical factors may arise during treatment and necessitate medical charges that are difficult to predict in advance. In cases where a facility finds it impractical to provide budget estimates – for example, during sudden medical emergencies that require immediate care – it should provide a fixed price for the service to the patient or their representative within 48 hours of treatment.

title: China condemns US designation of Confucius Institutes as threat
zh_title: 中国谴责美国将孔子学院视为威胁
summary: 中国周一指责美国“有针对性地抹黑”华盛顿将北京资助的孔子学院文化中心认定为国家安全威胁。塞内卡理工学院孔子学院。照片：维基共享资源。华盛顿将美国大学校园的这些中心视为中国共产党的宣传工具，并自 2025 年以来对这些机构实施了资金限制。美国国防部长皮特·赫格塞斯 (Pete Hegseth) 周五表示，他的部门在两个月内解散了数十个类似的组织，这些组织在两个月内重新出现，“利用这些组织的伪装”。
content:
中国周一指责美国“有针对性地抹黑”华盛顿将北京资助的孔子学院文化中心认定为国家安全威胁。塞内卡理工学院孔子学院。照片：维基共享资源。华盛顿将美国大学校园的这些中心视为中国共产党的宣传工具，并自 2025 年以来对这些机构实施了资金限制。美国国防部长皮特·赫格塞斯 (Pete Hegseth) 周五表示，他的部门在两个月内解散了数十个类似的组织，这些组织“使用不同的名称……但有着相同的使命”重新出现，并认为它们对国家安全构成威胁。中国外交部周一批评了此举。 “我们反对对孔子学院进行有针对性的抹黑和污名化，”外交部发言人郭家琨在新闻发布会上表示。他说：“中美教育交流与合作有利于增进两国人民之间的相互了解。”他补充说，这种关系“不应受到干扰和破坏”。美国国防部长皮特·赫格斯于 2026 年 5 月 30 日在新加坡举行的第 23 届香格里拉对话峰会上发表讲话。国际战略研究所，来自 Flickr。据孔子学院监管机构称，过去二十年来，中国已在 150 多个国家建立了数百所孔子学院。
这些文化中心被视为中国对德国歌德学院或英国文化协会等组织的回应，提供语言课程和文化交流项目。尽管中国领导人习近平称它们为“中国为世界和平与国际合作不懈努力的象征”，但这些文化中心在世界各地面临着越来越大的阻力。法国、瑞典、澳大利亚和加拿大等国的数十所孔子学院因类似的外国干涉指控而被关闭。

【原文 English Original】
China accused the United States on Monday of “targeted smearing” over Washington’s designation of Beijing-funded Confucius Institute cultural centres as national security threats . The Confucius Institute at Seneca Polytechnic. Photo: Wikicommons. Washington considers the centres on American university campuses as propaganda tools of the Chinese Communist Party and has imposed funding restrictions on the institutes since 2025. US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said on Friday his department had dismantled dozens of similar organisations over two months that had reappeared in disguise, “using different names… but with the same mission” and deemed them a threat to national security. China’s foreign ministry criticised the move on Monday. “We oppose the targeted smearing and stigmatisation of Confucius Institutes,” ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said at a news conference. “China-US educational exchanges and cooperation are beneficial to enhancing mutual understanding between the people of both countries,” he said, adding that such ties “should not be interfered with or undermined”. US Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth speaks during the 23rd Shangri-La Dialogue summit in Singapore on May 30, 2026. The International Institute for Strategic Studies, via Flickr. China has set up hundreds of Confucius Institutes in more than 150 countries over the last two decades, according to the body that oversees them. Presented as China’s answer to organisations such as Germany’s Goethe-Institut or the British Council, they offer language lessons and cultural exchange programmes. While Chinese leader Xi Jinping has called them a “symbol of China’s unremitting efforts for world peace and international cooperation”, the cultural centres have faced increasing resistance around the world. Dozens of Confucius Institutes have closed down in several countries following similar accusations of foreign interference including in France, Sweden, Australia and Canada.

【大紀元2026年10月26日訊】（大紀元記者林丹紐約報導）中國新時代人民黨（簡稱中國新民黨）10月24日在紐約法拉盛舉行集會，紀念第81個聯合國日，呼籲「把中共從聯合國趕出去」。與會者回顧中華民國參與創建聯合國的歷史，批評中共對民主國家及國際組織的滲透，並提出廢止聯大第2758號決議、推動聯合國改革等主張。

[![Image 6: 中國新民黨法拉盛集會紀念聯合國日，籲將中共逐出聯合國。](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14876704-195445-450x253.jpeg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14876704-195445-450x253.jpeg)

中國新民黨法拉盛集會紀念聯合國日，籲將中共逐出聯合國。（主辦方提供）

活動現場展示中華民國國旗，並拉起「紀念聯合國日，把中共從聯合國趕出去」及「抵抗才有希望，革命才是出路」等橫幅。

中國新民黨創辦人楊茂森表示，中華民國是聯合國創始會員國，也是首個簽署《聯合國憲章》的國家。中共取得中國在聯合國的代表權後，向民主國家，尤其是美國及聯合國各機構滲透，企圖以極權專制的價值觀改變二戰後建立的國際秩序，已對自由民主世界構成嚴重威脅。

他說，國際社會應重新審視中國在聯合國的代表權問題，並呼籲讓聯合國「回歸法律，回歸常識，回歸常態」。

中華民國海外公民委員會執行長曹勝華指出，1971年通過的聯大第2758號決議應該廢止廢止。他認為，這項決議使中共得以取代中華民國在聯合國的代表，國際社會應正視其後續影響。

曹勝華表示，蘇聯解體並不意味著民主與共產體制之間的對抗已經結束。他批評中共採取「韜光養晦」策略，利用民主國家提供的發展機會逐步壯大，最終試圖以專制價值觀改變世界秩序，呼籲美國及其他民主國家提高警覺。

他建議，由美國總統川普聯合烏克蘭及中華民國政府，推動召開聯合國創始會員國領袖會議，重申聯合國成立初衷，商討改革事宜。

中華民國國軍老兵關愛中心董事長胡福慶則關注俄羅斯入侵烏克蘭及台海安全。他表示，身為安理會常任理事國，俄羅斯發動侵略戰爭，中共則頻繁以軍事演習威脅台灣，這些情況與聯合國維護和平的宗旨背道而馳。

中國新民黨成員白祺帆回顧柏林圍牆倒塌、東歐民主化及蘇聯解體，指出蘇聯共產黨、東歐社會主義政權解體展現了人民追求自由、擺脫共產統治的力量。

聯合國日定於每年10月24日，紀念《聯合國憲章》於1945年當日生效。活動由中國新民黨創始人楊茂森組織，王建盾、張偉明、白祺帆、曹勝華、胡福慶、林學軍等人參加。

#香港设立药品监管机构，专家呼吁关注罕见病
香港将于 2026 年底建立药品和医疗器械监管机构。专家敦促新机构优先考虑罕见病药物审批、降低患者费用并招募国际人才加快审批速度。

# Hong Kong to set up drug regulator, experts call for rare disease focus

Hong Kong will establish a drug and medical devices regulator by end of 2026. Experts urge the new agency to prioritise rare disease drug approvals, reduce patient costs, and recruit international talent to speed up reviews.

[![Image 4: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

 By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

Hong Kong’s Drug and Medical Devices Regulatory Centre will be set up by the end of 2026, with Li Zili appointed as its director, the government announced.

Penny Peng of the Community Organisation for Social Development said Li’s connections in mainland China and overseas could help the city create an internationally recognised approval mechanism. She hopes the centre will introduce a “first-tier review” system to independently approve new drug registrations, bringing in more oncology and rare disease medicines to ease patients’ financial burden.

Lam Shun-chiu, founder of Hei Wah Pharmaceutical, recommended the centre first focus on approving new drugs for rare diseases. He also urged it to work with international drug regulators to set common standards for emerging fields such as gene therapy and cell therapy. Drug evaluation is a highly specialised field, Lam noted, and the centre should recruit talent from mainland China or abroad, including people who have worked at regulatory agencies or major pharmaceutical firms, to build a cross-disciplinary team and further shorten review times.

Chan Soo-kuen, senior executive director of the Hong Kong Research Pharmaceutical Manufacturers Association, said Hong Kong could act as a super-connector. If the centre can build an efficient and trustworthy evaluation system that serves both local and international markets, it could also help bring innovative drugs from overseas into Hong Kong.

当您负责确定团队奖金或贯穿整个季度的预算线的电子表格时，单个算术单可能会导致成本高昂的决策。香港的分析工作者——无论是运营、财务还是物流——通常都会处理图表、矩阵和多步骤计算。问题不在于是否使用人工智能数学工具，而在于如何在不外包判断的情况下使用它作为严格的第二次检查。 MathGPT.now 是一款免费的人工智能数学求解器，提供了一种结构化的方法来验证工作，但前提是您应用与同事评审相同的规则。

## MathGPT.now 为分析工作者提供什么
MathGPT.now 是一个基于浏览器的工具，它接受输入或拍照的数学问题并返回分步解决方案。其公开材料描述了一个将问题、方法、工作、答案和验证分开的结构。验证步骤是专业用途的关键：它可以包括替换、单元检查、域检查或通过替代方法求解。该工具还包括图形计算器、科学计算器以及练习题和公式参考库。基本使用无需注册，但付费套餐（每月 9.99 美元或通过学生电子邮件按年计费 4.99 美元）消除了使用限制。对于工作场所设置，免费套餐足以满足偶尔的验证任务，但大量用户应该意识到潜在的限制 - 该网站没有公开指定确切的免费套餐限制。

## 绘图作为操作中的目视检查
考虑香港仓库的一位运营分析师，他将拣货时间建模为订单大小的函数。假设模型为 _y = 0.4x + sin(x)_，其中 _x_ 是项目数，_y_ 是分钟。在 _x = 1.74_ 时，导数 _f'(x) = 0.91_ 表示曲线正在增加。经理可以将此函数输入 MathGPT.now 的图形计算器，并目视检查该点周围的斜率是否与声称的速率相符。该工具绘制曲线并可以显示交叉点和变化。这不是证明，而是一种快速的合理性检查：如果图表显示模型预测上升的情况下急剧下降，则说明有问题。协议很简单：输入函数，记下相关域的形状，然后与您自己的期望进行比较。如果视觉效果与您的计算相矛盾，请重新检查两者。

## 金融建模中的矩阵运算

香港的财务团队经常使用矩阵来衡量投资组合风险或多货币风险。例如，一个简单的二资产协方差矩阵可用于计算投资组合方差。 MathGPT.now 的线性代数主题涵盖向量、矩阵、变换、特征值和系统。工作人员可以输入矩阵乘法或求逆问题并收到逐步解决方案。要将其用作检查，请勿仅依赖最终数字。相反，请逐行遵循工作：验证

Workers and managers in Hong Kong can use MathGPT.now to verify analytical work through graphing, matrix operations, and second-method checks. This article provides a practical protocol for applying domain, units, substitution, and graph-based verification in operations and finance contexts.

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

26 Oct 2026 at 09:00 HKT · 6 min read

When you are responsible for a spreadsheet that determines a team’s bonus or a budget line that runs through the quarter, a single arithmetic slip can cascade into a costly decision. Analytical workers in Hong Kong—whether in operations, finance, or logistics—routinely handle graphs, matrices, and multi-step calculations. The question is not whether to use an AI math tool, but how to use one as a rigorous second check without outsourcing judgment. MathGPT.now, a free AI math solver, offers a structured way to verify work, but only if you apply the same discipline you would to a colleague’s review.

## What MathGPT.now offers the analytical worker

MathGPT.now is a browser-based tool that accepts typed or photographed math questions and returns a step-by-step solution. Its public materials describe a structure that separates the problem, method, working, answer, and verification. The verification step is the key for professional use: it can include substitution, unit checks, domain checks, or solving by an alternative method. The tool also includes a graphing calculator, a scientific calculator, and a library of practice questions and formula references. No signup is required for basic use, though a paid tier ($9.99/month or $4.99/month billed yearly with a student email) removes usage limits. For a workplace setting, the free tier is sufficient for occasional verification tasks, but heavy users should be aware of potential throttling—the site does not publicly specify exact free-tier limits.

## Graphing as a visual check in operations

Consider an operations analyst in a Hong Kong warehouse who models picking time as a function of order size. Suppose the model is _y = 0.4x + sin(x)_, where _x_ is the number of items and _y_ is minutes. At _x = 1.74_, the derivative _f'(x) = 0.91_ indicates the curve is increasing. A manager can enter this function into MathGPT.now’s graphing calculator and visually inspect whether the slope around that point matches the claimed rate. The tool plots the curve and can show intersections and change. This is not a proof, but it is a rapid plausibility check: if the graph shows a steep drop where the model predicts a rise, something is wrong. The protocol is simple: input the function, note the shape at the relevant domain, and compare with your own expectation. If the visual contradicts your calculation, re-examine both.

## Matrix operations in financial modelling

Finance teams in Hong Kong often use matrices for portfolio risk or multi-currency exposure. For example, a simple two-asset covariance matrix might be used to compute portfolio variance. MathGPT.now’s linear algebra topic coverage includes vectors, matrices, transformations, eigenvalues, and systems. A worker can type a matrix multiplication or inversion problem and receive a step-by-step solution. To use this as a check, do not rely on the final number alone. Instead, follow the working line by line: verify that the dimensions align, that each arithmetic step is correct, and that the final matrix has the expected shape. If the tool returns a 2x2 matrix where you expected 3x3, the error is likely in your input, not the tool. The public information does not specify whether MathGPT.now handles symbolic matrix entries or only numeric ones; a hands-on test would clarify this limitation.

## Domain, units, and substitution checks

MathGPT.now’s verification step explicitly includes checking the result by substitution, units, domain, or another method. For a Hong Kong logistics example: if you calculate the fuel cost for a delivery route as _cost = distance × rate_, and the answer is 500, ask: 500 what? The tool can check that units are consistent. If distance is in kilometres and rate is in dollars per litre, but fuel efficiency is missing, the number is meaningless. The domain check is equally important: if your model predicts a negative time for a positive input, the result is invalid. A worker can input the original equation and the proposed answer, and ask MathGPT.now to substitute and verify. The tool will show whether the left side equals the right side. This is a mechanical check, not a conceptual one, but it catches transcription errors and miskeyed numbers.

## Second-method checks: not a guarantee

The most powerful feature for professional use is the ability to solve the same problem by a different method. MathGPT.now’s interface allows you to ask for an alternative approach—for instance, solving a system of equations by substitution after you used elimination. If both methods yield the same answer, confidence increases. But this is not a guarantee. The tool may use the same underlying engine for both methods, meaning a systematic error could replicate. The UNESCO Guidance for generative AI in education and research (2023) warns that generative AI tools can produce plausible but incorrect outputs, and that human oversight remains essential. The OECD AI Principles (2019, updated 2024) emphasise transparency and accountability: you, the user, are accountable for the final decision. A second-method check in MathGPT.now is a useful cross-check, but it does not replace domain expertise or a manual sanity test.

## Privacy and security considerations for Hong Kong users

When you type or photograph a problem, the data is sent to MathGPT.now’s servers. The site states that payments are processed by Stripe and that progress stays in your browser, but it does not publicly specify data retention policies for problem inputs. For sensitive financial models or proprietary operational data, avoid entering actual numbers. Instead, anonymise the problem: change the values but keep the structure. For example, if your real covariance matrix contains confidential return data, replace the numbers with simple integers that preserve the mathematical relationship. The NIST AI Risk Management Framework resources (2023) recommend that organisations map risks related to data privacy and transparency. Hong Kong’s Personal Data Privacy Ordinance (PDPO) applies if any personal data is involved. For most analytical work, the risk is low if you use generic inputs, but be aware that the tool is not designed for confidential data.

## Practical checklist for using MathGPT.now at work

*   **Define the problem clearly** — Write down the equation or matrix exactly as you intend to check it.
*   **Run the tool once** — Input the problem and note the step-by-step working, not just the final answer.
*   **Verify units and domain** — Check that the answer has the right dimension and falls within a plausible range.
*   **Perform a substitution check** — Plug the answer back into the original equation manually or via the tool.
*   **Try a second method** — Ask MathGPT.now to solve using a different approach and compare results.
*   **Graph the function** — For any single-variable model, plot it and confirm the shape matches your expectation.
*   **Anonymise sensitive data** — Replace real numbers with structurally equivalent placeholders before input.
*   **Document the check** — Save or screenshot the steps as part of your audit trail.
*   **Apply human review** — Do not accept any output that contradicts your own understanding of the problem.

MathGPT.now is a free, accessible tool that can strengthen your analytical workflow when used with discipline. It does not replace judgment, but it can catch mistakes that a tired eye might miss. For Hong Kong workers juggling spreadsheets, models, and deadlines, that is a practical advantage.

## 中国市场放缓，英国传统精英私立学校纷纷进军印度

图像来源，Harrow School, Bengaluru

图像加注文字，在哈罗公学的班加罗尔（Bengaluru）校区，学生们穿着传统的哈罗帽子和制服。

*       *   Author, 尼基尔·伊南达尔（Nikhil Inamdar）
    *   Role, 印度孟买报道

*   Published 1 小时前

*   阅读时间: 3 分钟

位于印度西北部旁遮普邦（Punjab）昌迪加尔（Chandigarh）市郊，一间拥有473年历史的英国传统公学今年开设首个全女子国际校园。

与英格兰贝德福德郡（Bedfordshire）校园内标志性的哥德式中央建筑相比，印度校舍采用较现代化设计，设有专门兴建的教学大楼。但校园内一座醒目的红砖钟楼，仍保留着这所英国学校的传统印记。

位于莫哈利（Mohali）的贝德福德学校（Bedford School）是最新一所在印度设校的英国公学。至少已有六所英国公学（历史悠久的精英私立收费学校），包括三所在英国历史最悠久的学校，近年陆续在印度各地开设校园。

它们的扩张，正值中国市场环境趋紧，以及英国自2025年1月1日起对私立学校学费征收增值税（VAT）之际。

自2023年起，素有印度“矽谷”之称、汇聚大量软件和初创企业的班加罗尔（Bengaluru），已成为著名的哈罗公学（Harrow School）在印度的据点。印度首任总理尼赫鲁（Jawaharlal Nehru）便毕业于该校。

思贝礼学校（Shrewsbury School）则在印度中部城市博帕尔（Bhopal）设立校园；而威灵顿学院（Wellington College）选择落户浦那（Pune）。这座印度西部城市因拥有享负盛名的大学和学院而自称为“东方牛津”。

据报，米尔菲尔德学校（Millfield）、伊利沙伯女王学校（Queen Elizabeth's School）以及其他几所英国学校，未来数年亦将在印度开设分校。

数十年来，印度一直设有仿照英国殖民时期公学制度运作的寄宿学校，主要服务精英和贵族家庭。然而，随着新兴富裕阶层壮大，愈来愈多印度家庭希望让子女接触更国际化的教育，市场亦迅速扩展。

哈罗公学的班加罗尔分校校长卡洛琳·帕斯科（Caroline Pascoe）向BBC表示：“我们的国际课程对许多家长而言是一大吸引力。”

哈罗公学及贝德福德学校是印度少数提供完整剑桥课程（Cambridge curriculum）的学校之一，涵盖小学至高考（A-level）阶段。剑桥课程是一套全球教育体系，目前获全球约10,000所学校采用。

图像来源，Bedford School, Mohali

图像加注文字，至少六间英国公学进入印度，最新的一所是贝德福德学校。

哈尔西姆兰·辛格·科查尔（Harsimran Singh Kocchar）的大家族本身就在印度经营连锁学校，但他仍决定把五岁女儿帕丽妮特（Parineet）送入莫哈利的贝德福德学校。

他表示，原因在于学校“重视品格培养及自信，而不只是学业成绩”。

辛格又说，吸引他的另一个因素，是学校不像许多印度同类学校般存在“VIP文化”。

他说：“所有孩子都被一视同仁对待。部长和高级官员的子女不会享有较多特权。”

帕斯科表示，除了愈来愈多富裕的本地家庭外，海外印度人亦是这些学校的重要市场，包括长年在外国生活后回流印度的人士，以及仍居于英国或中东、希望子女保持与印度文化联系的家庭。

哈罗公学班加罗尔校区有60%的教职员来自海外。与其他英国公学一样，该校把自身独特传统带到印度校园。教师被称为“Beaks”，学生穿着传统哈罗帽和校服，并参加“The Long Ducker”跨国赛跑，该活动在哈罗全球各校同步举行。

校内亦设有英式教育标志性的“学院制度”。

这些充满英国传统色彩的校园文化，同时融入印度本地习俗，例如每天早上齐唱印度国歌，以及庆祝印度教重要节日象神节（Ganesh Chaturthi）。

图像来源，Harrow School, Bengaluru

图像加注文字，像班加罗尔的哈罗公学这样的学校会鼓励学生参加音乐和戏剧等课外活动。

印度不断增强的经济实力，以及迅速增加的新晋百万富翁人口，为英国公学扩张提供了有利条件，但这波增长部分亦是受到中国市场放缓所推动。

过去十年间，英国公学海外扩张很大程度上依赖中国和香港市场。目前由50所英国学校营运的151个海外分校校区中，有一半位于中国和香港。

不过，根据英国智库“私立教育政策论坛”（Private Education Policy Forum，PEPF）于2025年[发表的研究](https://www.pepf.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/SatelliteCampuses_PEPFReport_270525.pdf)，随着监管政策改变，以及各国政府加强审查甚至出现抗拒态度，相关增长已经放缓。

PEPF指出，中国于2024年实施的新法例要求学校将爱国主义教育融入所有学科，进一步增加海外学校在中国发展的挑战，甚至导致部分原定兴建的校园计划被取消。这促使有关学校开始考虑印度和越南等其他市场。

此外，英国在2024年秋季财政预算案中宣布对私立学校学费征收20%增值税（VAT）。莫哈利贝德福德学校（Bedford School Mohali）创校校长娜欧蜜·阿特金斯（Naomi Atkins）表示，这项措施迫使许多私立学校寻求海外发展机会。

她向BBC表示：“它们正处于非常艰难的处境。即使是过去从未考虑国际扩张的学校，如今也突然开始积极进入印度市场。”

图像来源，Harrow School, Bengaluru

图像加注文字，在印度，富裕的当地家庭和海外印度人是英国学校的主要目标市场。

不过，阿特金斯承认，印度并非一个容易开拓的市场。

这些学校大多透过与当地投资者或营运商合作设立分校。

阿特金斯表示，过去在其他国家，英国学校一般可从合作伙伴收取相当于收入10%的费用，但在印度，利润率在某些情况下可能低至仅1%。

她又表示，部分学校亦高估了印度市场的规模。

尽管印度有接近2.5亿名在学学生，但英语教育早已深深植根当地，来自本土学校的竞争远较中国、韩国或越南等非英语国家激烈得多。

此外，印度人均收入仍然较低，而英国学校的高昂学费亦限制了增长空间。部分学校的全寄宿学费可高达15,000英镑甚至更高。

阿特金斯说：“我曾在印尼、马来西亚和中国工作，但印度人对价格敏感得多，他们喜欢寻找划算的选择。”

正因如此，莫哈利贝德福德学校的学费约为其他英国学校的一半。

根据PEPF数据，2011/12学年至2022/23学年间，英国学校海外分校共录得1.524亿英镑利润，而且相关收益多年来显著增长。

不过，在印度，这些学校的发展看来更可能是缓慢而稳定，而非爆发式增长。

印度的殖民历史背景，以及新兴富裕阶层的崛起，确实为这些历史悠久的英国学校带来可观的商机，但至少在短期内，这个市场规模仍不足以弥补中国市场萎缩造成的损失。

我们使用了人工智慧协助翻译这篇文章，它的原文是英文。在发布之前，BBC记者检查了翻译的内容。

content:
**Gather monthly to explore where our Autism, Neurodiversity and Psychedelic experiences meet**, as well as how each plays out separately in our lives.

In many circles talking about autism, neurodiversity or psychedelics can be awkward or even taboo. **This is our space to explore and share, unmasked**. Come as you are, with your fidget toy, your quirks and special interests, and all that is uniquely you. This is an inclusive group where all are welcome, including allies.

We'll start each meeting with brief check-ins to help us get to know each other. Following will be time to chat about the topics anyone would like to discuss. **Our shared purpose is to allow us to come together, be our authentic selves, and connect with others who can relate to many of our own experiences.**

**Suggestion** - Bring some paper or a journal, and a pen, to jot down thoughts during the meeting while another person is speaking, so you remember all the brilliant thoughts you had on the topic when you get a chance to speak at the MeetUp! From experience the thoughts will spark. ;)

**Our meetings are monthly online, and we occaisonally have in person events maybe 1-2 times a year**, in addition to the monthly online MeetUps. In person events announced at the online meetings as they are planned.

(In person meetings - Please avoid fragranced products at our occasional in person meetings to support those with sensitivity to smells. We'll do our best to find in person meeting locations with decent lighting, and low levels of auditory distractions. Suggestions welcome on locations too!)

**About the host:**

**Be Friend** is an ordained minister in a non-denominational "church without walls" for over 16 years, a late diagnosed autistic woman, and an advocate who is steeped in the newly legal psilocybin ecosystem in Oregon. She's been involved since Nov. 2022 with grassroots advocacy, encouraging our state's legislators and the Oregon Health Authority to improve the rules for the Oregon Psilocybin Services Act (OPSA).

Be has also been part of the online psychedelic communities for quite a while now and has witnessed how coming together to chat about being on the spectrum and psychedelics, can be a powerful community building space.

************************
 This event is independently organized and is not hosted, supervised, or facilitated by the Portland Psychedelic Society, a donation-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization.

**To learn more about Portland Psychedelic Society programming, memberships, and more, please [visit our website](https://www.portlandpsychedelic.org/).**

[![Image 10: Photo of the user Christine - VSWW Volunteer](https://secure.meetupstatic.com/photos/member/7/a/2/6/thumb_325411270.jpeg?w=96) Hosted by Christine - VSWW V.](https://www.meetup.com/vedanta-society-of-western-washington-meetup/events/317139209/attendees/)

## Details

Join us for a weekly rhythm of meditation, teaching, and discussion led by Swami Avikarananda. The morning begins with meditation, followed by a teaching on spiritual life and Vedanta. After the talk, those attending in person are welcome to remain for coffee, tea, and continued discussion in our dining room. The bookstore will also be open. This reflects the new Sunday structure beginning May 3, 2026.

Because meditation is now the foundation of the morning, we ask everyone to **plan ahead to arrive and be settled before 10am**. Entering after meditation has begun is disruptive to the meditation period and to those already practicing. Upon arrival, you may choose to join Swami Avikarananda for Guided Meditation in the Chapel, or enter the Shrine upstairs for Silent Meditation.

This event is held in person at the Seattle Ashrama, and the 10:30 teaching is also [livestreamed on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@vedantasocietyofwesternwa/streams). Like all Vedanta Society activities, it is open to all and free of charge. Past talks may be selected from our [YouTube playlists](https://www.youtube.com/@vedantasocietyofwesternwa/playlists).

**Sunday Schedule**
**10am** Meditation (_Guided in the Chapel or Silent in the upstairs Shrine_)
**10:30am** Teaching (also available on [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@vedantasocietyofwesternwa/streams))
**11:30am** Discuss Vedanta over coffee and tea; [Bookstore](https://vedanta-seattle.org/media/bookshop/) available

_90-minute program, followed by discussion._

Read more

### Speaker

#### Swami Avikarananda

Swami Avikarananda is an ordained Hindu monk of the Ramakrishna Order and a resident minister at the Vedanta Society of Western Washington in Seattle. He conducts regular scriptural classes, meditation sessions, and public lectures focused on Advaita Vedanta, the Bhagavad Gita, and the lives of Sri Ramakrishna, Sri Sarada Devi, and Swami Vivekananda.

## Details

Whether you're carving groomers, exploring powder, racing gates, or simply wanting to enjoy longer days on the mountain, this class is designed to prepare your body for ski season. Join us in person or from anywhere on Zoom as we build the strength, balance, agility, flexibility, and stability that help you ski with greater confidence, control, and ease.

Each class combines yoga, functional movement, breathwork, and recovery techniques that improve leg endurance, core strength, hip mobility, and body awareness—all while reducing stiffness and helping lower the risk of injury. Every exercise can be modified, making this class welcoming for all abilities, whether you're preparing for your first season or your fiftieth.

At Healthy & Fun Choices®, we believe skiing starts long before you step into your boots. By training both your body and your mindset, you'll arrive on the mountain feeling stronger, more balanced, and ready to enjoy every run.
**Perfect for:** Skiers • Snowboarders • Nordic Skiers • Snowshoers • Winter Adventurers • All Ability Levels
**Join us in person or live on Zoom from anywhere!**

summary: Uyghur Cultural Preservation and Survival Through Education Funding goal: $10,000 The Uyghur people have been persecuted and subjected to repressive Chinese government policies in their Indigenous homeland of East Turkestan for many years.
content:
Uyghur Cultural Preservation and Survival Through Education

Funding goal: $10,000

The Uyghur people have been persecuted and subjected to repressive Chinese government policies in their Indigenous homeland of East Turkestan for many years. It is estimated that up to three million Uyghurs have been interned, imprisoned, and enslaved in detention centers, prisons, and forced labor facilities throughout China since 2017.

In 2021, the Uyghur Tribunal found that China was committing genocide and other crimes against humanity against Uyghurs. In 2022, the United Nations also concluded that China was committing human rights violations against Uyghurs amounting to crimes against humanity. Countries including the United States, Canada, the Netherlands, Czech Republic, United Kingdom, Lithuania, Belgium, and France have all declared a genocide in East Turkestan. Despite these declarations of genocide and related reports by various human rights organizations, atrocities against Uyghurs continue today with very limited international recognition and accountability.

During this time of ongoing genocide and cultural erasure in their Indigenous homeland, Uyghurs of the diaspora are working to preserve their culture and identity as a matter of survival. Uyghur education has been eradicated by the Chinese State, Uyghur texts are forbidden and in danger of being eliminated, and the Uyghur language itself is prohibited.

Uyghur scholars, linguists, and other specialists in the diaspora worldwide serve on the Uyghur Language and Education Committee of the Uyghur Academy to preserve the work of Uyghur intellectuals who have been persecuted and forcibly disappeared. This work has been ongoing since 2009 and is continuing to expand.

The Committee has created standards-aligned K-5 textbooks, which include classic and contemperory Uyghur literature, poetry, historical texts, and biographies for Uyghur children to learn about their own culture and identity in their native language. The Committee is seeking funding to expand and revise the existing K-5 textbooks, create teacher’s edition textbooks for educators, and design supplemental resources. They also hope to develop Middle and High School textbooks and related supplemental resources. To effectively implement these educational materials, they would also like to provide training for teachers.

Please consider supporting this urgent work of the Uyghur Academic Foundation as a matter of cultural survival for future generations of the Uyghur people.

References:

Thum, R. (2025, February). Eight years on, China’s repression of the Uyghurs remains dire.

United Nations Human Rights Office. (2022, August 31). OHCHR Assessment of human rights

**Craig De Meillon**

Donation protected

 My name is Craig De Meillon, and I am based in Miami, Florida. I work in safety and emergency management and am a trained firefighter and EMT with professional experience responding to disasters, emergencies, and humanitarian situations.

 I am raising these funds as an independent volunteer to support my deployment to the areas affected by the recent mudslides and flooding in Nepal near the China border. I am not a family member or representative of anyone affected by the disaster, nor am I collecting these funds on behalf of a government agency or other organization. I am responding independently based on my emergency-response experience and my ability to bring useful communications and search equipment into the field.

 The funds raised will be used primarily to cover the direct costs of my deployment and emergency-response work. This includes my airfare and ground transportation to and within the affected region, accommodation and essential field logistics, food and other necessary expenses while deployed, and emergency-response equipment and supplies.

 A significant part of the funding will also be used for search and communications capabilities. This may include purchasing or renting drones that can be used to conduct aerial searches, assess inaccessible areas, locate people who may be stranded or missing, and help response teams understand conditions on the ground. Funds will also be used for satellite communications equipment and associated Starlink service costs so that I can maintain reliable communications in areas where local telecommunications infrastructure may be damaged, unavailable, or overloaded.

 Where practical, I may purchase essential supplies locally rather than transporting them from the United States. This allows funds to be used more efficiently and can also support local businesses and responders.

 The primary beneficiary of this fundraiser is me, Craig De Meillon, because the funds are being raised to cover the actual expenses I incur while independently deploying and carrying out this emergency-response work. The money is not being raised for personal profit or general living expenses. It is intended to offset the costs directly associated with the mission, including travel, equipment, communications, transportation, and necessary field expenses.

 Once on the ground, I will coordinate as appropriate with local emergency responders, humanitarian organizations, community leaders, and other response personnel to determine where my skills, equipment, and communications capabilities can be most useful. My role and activities may change depending on the needs identified in the affected areas and the accessibility and safety of the region.

 I will keep records of mission-related expenses and provide updates throughout the deployment so donors can understand how the funds are being used and what work is being carried out on the ground.

 Thank you to everyone who contributes, shares this fundraiser, or supports the response in any way. Every contribution helps make it possible for me to get the equipment, communications, and resources needed to reach affected areas and assist where I can. Flood
