title: Cost barriers leave Hong Kong’s low-income elderly shut out of advance medical directives despite landmark law
zh_title: 尽管制定了具有里程碑意义的法律，但成本障碍使香港的低收入老年人无法获得预先医疗指示
summary: 78岁的冯浩珠自从得知新的预先医疗指令（AMD）法于7月下旬生效以来，一直希望将自己对临终治疗的愿望写成文字。但作为低收入深水埗靠政府福利生活的老年人，这一过程的成本迫使她重新考虑。 78岁的老人冯浩柱独居深水埗。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。冯认为该立法是一个重要的里程碑，因为它允许香港有能力的成年人拒绝不需要的维持生命的治疗或要求暂缓或与
content:
78岁的冯浩珠自从得知新的预先医疗指令（AMD）法于7月下旬生效以来，一直希望将自己对临终治疗的愿望写成文字。但作为低收入深水埗靠政府福利生活的老年人，这一过程的成本迫使她重新考虑。 78岁的老人冯浩柱独居深水埗。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。冯认为该立法是一个重要的里程碑，因为它允许香港有能力的成年人拒绝不需要的维持生命治疗或要求暂缓或撤回治疗。冯先生用粤语对《香港新闻社》表示：“我们过去从未与老年人谈论过死亡或临终之类的事情——人们认为这是一种禁忌。” “现在情况发生了变化。”虽然她总体上保持健康，但她认为现在制定一项指令是明智的，因为年近 80 岁的人的健康状况可能会迅速恶化。她不想在生命的最后时刻遭受疼痛或接受插管等侵入性干预。冯通过社工得知，请一位全科医生设立AMD需要约3,000港元。 “很多了……政府能给低收入人群提供补贴吗？”冯问道。当她意识到没有这样的津贴时，她犹豫了。预先医疗指示的示范表格。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。
外科医生、倡导积极规划临终旅程的非政府组织“勿忘我”的创始人范宁告诉《香港新闻社》，AMD对香港来说并不新鲜。公立医院自2008年左右开始根据普通法使用AMD，该法尊重个人在临终治疗方面的决策自主权，但此前这些服务主要针对被诊断为末期疾病的患者。 2024年底，香港通过了《生命维持治疗预先决定条例》，该成文法明确规定香港人有权拒绝积极的生命维持治疗，而医生有义务遵循AMD患者的决定。根据法律规定，精神正常的成年人可以在两名证人在场的情况下签署一份表格来建立 AMD，其中一名证人必须是注册医生。范说，他注意到，在这项具有里程碑意义的立法之后，一些老年人和患有慢性疾病的人希望尽快获得AMD，但对过程感到不确定。范宁是一名外科医生，也是当地慈善机构“勿忘我”的创始人。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。 “公立医院系统非常繁忙。现在，只有绝症患者才会得到协助进行AMD，通常是在接受姑息治疗时，”范用粤语说，指的是为患有致命疾病的人提供的专门支持。他建议其他人可以联系他们的家庭医生。
“不过，很多低收入人士没有家庭医生，这在香港仍然是中产阶级的事情，”范说，并补充说，并不是每个私营家庭医生都会帮助为新病人办理AMD。 流程不明 在预设医疗法生效一个月后，李淑卿和她的妹妹在私人诊所开设了AMD，每人支付3,000港元。 83 岁的李一直想留下指示，停止积极的维持生命治疗。她的丈夫几年前去世了，她现在独自住在公共住房里，靠政府的福利生活。 83岁李淑卿老人

【原文 English Original】
Seventy-eight-year-old Fung Ho-chu has been hoping to put her wishes on end-of-life treatment into writing ever since she learned that a new law on advance medical directives (AMD) came into effect in late July. But as a senior living on government welfare in low-income Sham Shui Po, the costs of the process have forced her to reconsider. 78-year-old senior Fung Ho-chu lives alone in Sham Shui Po. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Fung considered the legislation a major milestone, as it allows competent adults in Hong Kong to refuse unwanted life-sustaining treatment or request that it be withheld or withdrawn.  “We never talked about things like death or end-of-life with elderly people in the past – people believed it was a taboo,” Fung told HKFP in Cantonese. “Now things have changed.” While she remains generally healthy, she believes it wise to establish a directive now, given that individuals approaching 80 could see a rapid deterioration in health. She does not want to suffer from pain or undergo invasive interventions such as intubation in her final moments. Through social workers, Fung learned that it costs around HK$3,000 to have a general practitioner set up an AMD. “That is a lot… Could the government provide any subsidy for low-income people?” Fung asked. She hesitated when she realised there was no such allowance. The model form of advance medical directive. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Fan Ning, a surgeon and the founder of Forget Thee Not, an NGO advocating for proactive planning around end-of-life journeys, told HKFP that AMDs are not new to Hong Kong. Public hospitals have been using AMDs since around 2008 under common law, which respects individuals’ autonomy in decisions regarding end-of-life treatment, but previously the services were mainly for patients diagnosed with terminal illness. In late 2024, Hong Kong passed the Advance Decision on Life-sustaining Treatment Ordinance, a statute law that clearly states Hongkongers’ right to refuse aggressive life-sustaining treatment, and medics’ obligation to follow the decisions of patients with AMDs.  According to the law, a mentally competent adult can establish an AMD by signing a form in the presence of two witnesses, one of whom must be a registered medical practitioner.  Fan said he noticed, after the landmark legislation, that some seniors and people with chronic illnesses hoped to make AMDs as soon as possible, but were left uncertain about the process. Fan Ning, a surgeon and founder of local charity Forget Thee Not. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “The public hospital system is very busy. Now, only terminally ill patients will be assisted with making an AMD, usually when they are receiving palliative care,” Fan said in Cantonese, referring to specialised support for people living with a life-limiting illness. Others, he advised, can reach out to their family doctors. “However, many low-income people do not have a family doctor, which is still a middle-class thing in Hong Kong,” Fan said, adding that not every family physician in the private sector will help to make AMDs for new patients. Unclear p rocess One month after the advance directive law came into effect, Lee Suk Hing and her younger sister set up AMDs in a private clinic, paying HK$3,000 each.  Lee, 83, had always wanted to leave instructions to withhold aggressive life-sustaining treatment. Her husband passed away a few years ago and she now lives alone in public housing, relying on government welfare. 83-year-old senior Lee Suk Hing sets up advance medical directive soon after the law comes into effect. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “Life is unpredictable,” Lee said in Cantonese. “In my final moments, I do not want chest compressions or intubation. I am worried that, when the time comes, I will not be allowed to die.” Her children, she added, supported her decision. She recalled volunteering in senior care homes years ago and seeing patients lie in bed unconscious and attached to tubes for years. She was terrified of ending up the same way. Making an AMD takes time and communication. First, a nurse tested Lee and her sister to ensure they had the mental capacity to make the decision. Then a doctor explained the new law and form in detail before guiding them through end-of-life options. The process took two hours. Walking out of the clinic, Lee felt relieved that she had left instructions for her future care. However, she also felt the cost was too high for elderly people like her with little income. Elderly people in Hong Kong’s Mong Kok. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Lee called on the government to provide more support services, such as subsidies for low-income patients and seniors who want to implement a directive. “I think this would also be a good thing for the government,” Lee added. “By setting up an AMD, there may be fewer people lying unconscious in hospitals waiting for death, right? That would reduce the government’s financial burden.” Ivan Lin, a social worker serving seniors at local NGO the Society for Community Organization (SoCO), told HKFP that more and more elderly people are interested in setting up AMDs, but public awareness still lags behind, and it is not clear to many how to exercise their rights. According to Lin, patients diagnosed with terminal illness such as stage 4 cancer can get help making an AMD from medics in public hospital oncology departments. For those with other severe or long-term conditions, however, there is not a clear path. Recently, a senior with advanced diabetes who had to undergo regular haemodialysis told Lin that he was turned down when he asked for help making an AMD. Medical staff at a public hospital told him that the service was mainly for people with terminal illnesses. Ivan Lin, a social worker serving seniors at local NGO Society for Community Organization (SoCO). Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. For those in residential care, things are more difficult. A registered nurse who works closely with care homes told HKFP that many seniors in care want to make AMDs but struggle to find doctors to sign the form. Raising awareness Hong Kong’s government allowed an 18-month period for briefing and training of medics on the practice of AMD after the legislation was passed in late 2024. In a statement introducing the law in late July, the government said it had cooperated with different parties to provide seminars for healthcare professionals in the public and private sectors, including those in residential care homes.  HKFP reached out in October to 12 private clinics, including five general practitioners’ clinics and five geriatrics clinics, asking if they could assist a healthy senior to make an AMD. Most said they do not provide this service. At five clinics, the receptionists or nurses who answered the phone said they did not know what an AMD is. Elderly people walk out of a public hospital in Hong Kong in October 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Forget Thee Not founder Fan said that support services are necessary to promote a culture of planning in advance for care and treatment options near the end of life. The doctor also said there should be more education and communication before the setup of an AMD, making it clear that the directives do not entail either euthanasia or a blanket refusal of life-saving treatments. Under the new law, signatories can choose what kinds of medical care they want to refuse in different scenarios, such as if they are terminally ill or in a persistent vegetative state. They could refuse any form of life-sustaining treatment or only certain approaches, like CPR. The directive only becomes effective if the signer is unconscious and in one of these scenarios. The new legislation marks a milestone for end-of-life care in Hong Kong, according to Roger Chung, an associate professor at CUHK’s School of Public Health and Primary Care and co-director of the university’s Centre for Bioethics. “In Chinese culture, when someone reaches their final moments, it is usually family members who decide on treatments – and many family members will naturally insist on doing everything possible to save their beloved one,” Chung said in Cantonese. Roger Chung, Associate Professor of the School of Public Health and Primary Care (SPHPC) of CUHK and co-director of the CUHK Centre for Bioethics. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “Now people can say ‘no’ – we can decide not to be kept on life support at the end of life,” Chung said. “But passing the legislation is just the beginning.” Over the past few years, Chung has observed a growing willingness among Hongkongers to discuss death and how to prepare for it, noting that The Last Dance – a film that explores the death-care industry and challenges cultural taboos – broke box-office records last year . Over the long term, Chung hopes there will be a designated area in public hospitals to assist people in need to set up an advance directive, or even more comprehensive care plans. Advance care planning As a developed economy with a declining birth rate, Hong Kong has one of the most rapidly ageing populations in the world. In 2039, there will be around 2.52 million people aged above 65, accounting for 31 per cent of the population, according to government estimates. This has made the need for better preparation in handling chronic illnesses, end-of-life care and death increasingly urgent. Forget Thee Not’s Fan said Hong Kong has lagged in primary healthcare, with few people visiting family doctors regularly and a general lack of training among general practitioners. Hong Kong seniors and their caretakers leave a public hospital in October 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “Now [the government] is starting to develop the whole primary healthcare sector,” Fan said. In 2023, Hong Kong launched the Chronic Disease Co-Care Pilot Scheme, which aims to create a family doctor system and develop District Health Centres to meet the health needs of residents aged 45 and above. Under the scheme, patients diagnosed with high blood pressure or high blood glucose will be matched with a family doctor for follow-up under co-pay fees. Lin, the social worker, suggested authorities consider folding in services such as AMD assistance. Professor Chung at CUHK said AMDs should be seen as part of advance care planning (ACP), the process by which people make future care plans with caretakers and medical professionals. More NGOs like Forget Thee Not are now promoting the concept of ACP in Hong Kong. Apart from making AMDs, people can also consider drawing up a will and registering an Enduring Power of Attorney (EPA) – a legal document that allows an individual to appoint a trusted person to manage their financial and property affairs if they lose mental capacity. Fung Ho-chu struggles over setting up advance medical directive because of financial restraints. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. AMDs and EPAs, together with wills, are collectively known as the “three instruments of peace.” But while people can draft and sign wills on their own, doctors and lawyers are required to sign and witness EPAs, which usually adds up to more than the fees for AMDs. Fast approaching 80, Fung Ho-chu wanted to get all three done while she is healthy and has a clear mind. She has recently begun discussing her thoughts and preferences with her children. Due to financial constraints, she is weighing up which to prioritise and how much she can spend.

香港
香港赛马会捐款3,200万港元，与香港高尔夫球会慈善基金合作推出为期两年的社区高尔夫计划。该倡议旨在每年向超过 25,000 名学童、青少年和贫困居民介绍这项运动。

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

2026 年 10 月 25 日 23:16 香港时间 · 阅读 2 分钟

香港公开赛于10月25日在粉岭高尔夫球场落幕，吸引了数万名来自香港、中国内地及海外的观众。香港赛马会（HKJC）首次作为赛事官方社区合作伙伴参与其中，以新的社区举措支持M-Mark锦标赛。

在颁奖典礼上，香港赛马会企业事务执行董事谭志源颁发马会杯予赛事的低位香港业余选手林马强。财政司司长陈茂波、文化体育及旅游局局长罗淑佩也出席。
香港赛马会捐赠 3,200 万港元，与香港高尔夫球会慈善基金合作推出为期两年的赛马会社区高尔夫计划。该计划旨在向更广泛的受众介绍高尔夫运动，支持当地年轻的人才，并将锦标赛的好处扩展到球场之外。预计每年将有超过 25,000 名学童、青少年和贫困社区成员受益。

香港赛马会与香港高尔夫球会合作开展多项参与活动，包括校本活动、中学间比赛以及为各种水平的青少年举办的高尔夫球训练营。比赛之前，国际高尔夫球手参观了当地的一所小学，以激励学生，而俱乐部教练则通过实践高尔夫诊所来促进包容性。向贫困社区分发免费门票，以鼓励更广泛的参与。

赛事期间，赛马会球迷村的游客可享受推杆挑战等互动活动，而香港赛马会的义工团队则以气球人偶及其他景点招待大众。来访的高尔夫球手还可以参观香港的标志性景点，包括在跑马地赛马场观看欢乐星期三赛马之夜，这有助于向国际观众推广香港的赛马旅游业。

The Hong Kong Jockey Club has donated HK$32 million to launch a two-year community golf programme in partnership with the Hong Kong Golf Club Charitable Foundation. The initiative aims to introduce the sport to over 25,000 schoolchildren, teenagers and underprivileged residents annually.

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

25 Oct 2026 at 23:16 HKT · 2 min read

The Hong Kong Open concluded on 25 October at the Fanling Golf Course, drawing tens of thousands of spectators from Hong Kong, mainland China and overseas. For the first time, the Hong Kong Jockey Club (HKJC) participated as the event's official community partner, supporting the M-Mark tournament with new community initiatives.

At the awards ceremony, Raymond Tam Chi-yuen, HKJC's executive director for Corporate Affairs, presented the Club Cup to Markus Lam, the tournament's Low Hong Kong Amateur Player. Financial Secretary Paul Chan Mo-po and Secretary for Culture, Sports and Tourism Rosanna Law Shuk-pui also attended.

HKJC has donated HK$32 million to launch the Jockey Club Community Golf Programme, a two-year initiative in partnership with the Hong Kong Golf Club Charitable Foundation. The programme is designed to introduce golf to a broader audience, support young local talent, and extend the tournament's benefits beyond the course. It is expected that more than 25,000 schoolchildren, teenagers and underprivileged community members will benefit each year.

HKJC and the Hong Kong Golf Club collaborated on engagement activities, including school-based events, inter-secondary school competitions and golf clinics for young people of all abilities. Ahead of the tournament, international golfers visited a local primary school to inspire students, while club coaches promoted inclusion through hands-on golf clinics. Complimentary tickets were distributed to underprivileged communities to encourage wider participation.

During the tournament, visitors to the Jockey Club Fan Village enjoyed interactive activities such as a putting challenge, while a volunteer team from HKJC entertained crowds with balloon figures and other attractions. Visiting golfers were also treated to signature Hong Kong attractions, including a night at the Happy Wednesday races at Happy Valley Racecourse, helping to promote the city's horse racing tourism to an international audience.

title: Torture Tales from China’s Black Jails
zh_title: 中国黑监狱的酷刑故事

content:
_山姆·沃德插图_

中国秘密警察拘留了你。

这场磨难始于安全人员的突然袭击。他们指控你犯罪，限制你并将你推入车内。你被蒙上头巾或蒙住眼睛，戴上手铐，绑架到秘密地点，关在有软垫的牢房里，并以“危害中国”的罪名威胁要严惩。与此同时，你的家和办公室也会被搜查。

如果你是这个政权的批评者，长期担心它有一天可能会对你不利，那么这可能是一个奇怪的解脱时刻：你最坏的情况已经出现。如果你认为自己了解规则并且可以依靠官方联系或当局的合理性，那么你会经历幻想破灭和信任背叛的震惊。

您很难适应单独监禁和感官剥夺。房间里只有一张硬铺；你只有几件衣服和基本的洗漱用品。没有镜子——甚至无法保证看到自己的脸。最令人抓狂的是，你不能出去。你的宇宙现在以几平方英尺来衡量。
拘留你的便衣公安或国家安全人员不会告诉任何人你的位置或情况。法律赋予您聘请律师并咨询律师的权利。但在国家安全案件中，它还授权你的狱卒拒绝与律师接触，他们肯定会这样做，至少在他们完成对你的讯问和立案之前，这可能需要一年的时间。

与亲人和朋友、与世界、与自己的身份隔绝，你会体验到孤独的寒意和对联系的渴望。从现在开始，你唯一的人际关系就是与绑架者的关系。人权律师隋牧青回忆道，“思念家人的痛苦是最严重的痛苦”，这代表了许多人的心声。

> 电影中对酷刑的描述通过震撼和奇观实现，而指定居所监视居住则通过全面性和持续时间实现。根据法律，这种刑期最长可达六个月，随后通常会被判处数年拘留和监禁。它造成的伤疤持续时间更长。
这种令人心碎的经历是人权非政府组织保障卫士出版的最新一期《失踪者人民共和国》的主题。第三版收集了中国和外国公民被中国共产党安全机构绑架的新第一人称叙述，该程序被称为“指定居所监视居住”或简称“指居”。官方的英文翻译是“指定地点居住监视”（RSDL），这是一种平淡的官僚口气，故意掩盖逮捕前在秘密设施中的拘留，在那里，你的折磨者让你遭受骇人听闻的虐待，而你唯一的权利就是服从。

[![图2](https://www.thewirechina.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Cheng-Lei-On-Life-in-Chinese-Prison.png)](https://www.thewirechina.com/2026/01/04/heng-lei-on-life-in-chinese-prison/)
在撰写本书的前言时，我想反映他人的痛苦和生存，而不是讲述我自己在 2018 年至 2021 年期间作为[政治人质](https://www.strategicnarratives.org/p/ Five-years-of-freedom-and-the-prc)的经历。

我分析了其中的十篇文章和前两版中的几篇文章，以及中华人民共和国成立之初到现在的囚犯的故事。我还读了最近的[回忆录](https://www.harpercollins.com/products/ Cheng-lei- Cheng-lei?variant=4

【原文 English Original】
_Illustration by Sam Ward_

China’s secret police have detained you.

The ordeal begins with a surprise raid by security officers. They accuse you of crimes, restrain you and shove you into a vehicle. You are hooded or blindfolded, handcuffed, abducted to a secret location, locked in a padded cell, and threatened with severe punishment for “harming China”. Meanwhile, your home and office are searched.

If you are a critic of the regime who has lived with the perennial anxiety that it might one day move against you, this can be a moment of strange relief: your worst-case scenario has unfolded. If you thought you understood the rules and could count on official connections or the reasonableness of the authorities, you experience the shock of illusions dispelled and trust betrayed.

You struggle to adjust to solitary confinement and sensory deprivation. The room has only a hard bunk; you have only a few articles of clothing and basic toiletries. There are no mirrors — not even the reassurance of seeing your own face. Most maddeningly, you cannot go out. Your universe is now measured in a few square feet.

The plainclothes Public Security or State Security officers holding you won’t inform anyone of your location or conditions. The law entitles you to retain and consult a lawyer. But in state security cases, it also empowers your jailers to deny access to counsel, which they are sure to do, at least until they have finished questioning you and building their case, which could take a year.

Disconnected from loved ones and friends, from the world, from your own identity, you experience a chill of isolation and a longing for connection. From now on, your only human relationships are with your captors. Human rights lawyer Sui Muqing speaks for many when he recalls that “the pain of missing my family was the worst suffering.”

> What cinematic depictions of torture achieve through shock and spectacle, RSDL accomplishes through comprehensiveness and duration. By law it can last up to six months, usually followed by years of detention and prison. The scars it inflicts last much longer.

That soul-crushing experience is the subject of the latest edition of _People’s Republic of the Disappeared_, a new book published by the human rights NGO Safeguard Defenders. This third edition collects new first-person accounts of both PRC and foreign citizens abducted by the Chinese Communist Party’s security apparatus under a sinister procedure it calls _zhiding jusuo jianshi juzhu_ 指定居所监视居住 or _zhiju_ 指居 for short. The official English translation is “Residential Surveillance at a Designated Location” (RSDL), a bland bureaucratic mouthful that deliberately masks pre-arrest detention in a secret facility where your tormentors subject you to appalling abuse and your only right is to obey.

[![Image 2](https://www.thewirechina.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Cheng-Lei-On-Life-in-Chinese-Prison.png)](https://www.thewirechina.com/2026/01/04/cheng-lei-on-life-in-chinese-prison/)
In writing this book’s foreword I wanted to reflect the suffering and survival of others, rather than relating my own experience as a [political hostage](https://www.strategicnarratives.org/p/five-years-of-freedom-and-the-prc) from 2018–2021.

I analyzed its ten essays and several more from the two previous editions, as well as stories of prisoners from the PRC’s early decades to the present. I also read the recent [memoir](https://www.harpercollins.com/products/cheng-lei-cheng-lei?variant=46124399886370) of Cheng Lei, the Australian broadcast journalist whose stint as a CGTN news anchor was abruptly terminated by Ministry of State Security agents in 2020. They detained her in retaliation against Australian policies that had enraged their Communist Party masters. Together, these accounts reveal an enduring core curriculum of fear, coercive interrogation, thought remolding and forced submission to the power of the Party-state.

Through its control of all four dimensions in RSDL, especially time, the state becomes the sole point of reference. Blackout curtains cover the windows. With no clocks, no daylight and constant artificial light, circadian rhythms come unanchored. At least for the initial months, there will be nothing to read and no correspondence with the outside world beyond 30-minute consular meetings if you’re a foreign citizen. Monotony turns hours into eternity.

Footage from Canada’s CTV News of Michael Kovrig and Michael Spavor’s return to Canada, following their release from detention on September 24, 2021. _Credit: [CTV News](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vaNnjv24E6Y)_

Humans are wired to avoid uncertainty, but in RSDL the unpredictable becomes the only certainty. You don’t know where you are, how long you will be there, what they will do next, or whether you will survive with your sanity intact. What cinematic depictions of torture achieve through shock and spectacle, RSDL accomplishes through comprehensiveness and duration. By law it can last up to six months, usually followed by years of detention and prison. The scars it inflicts last much longer.

Solitary confinement feels like a kind of [social death](https://academic.oup.com/minnesota-scholarship-online/book/24160?login=false) that dissolves your identity and ability to make sense of a world that has apparently forgotten you. “If they just dug a hole and threw me into it, maybe no one would even know,” recalls women’s rights activist Li Qiaochu. With no social contact, anxiety overwhelms your ability to self-regulate. United Nations standards prohibit solitary confinement over more than fifteen consecutive days, beyond which it can amount to [torture](https://docs.un.org/en/A/66/268), according to the UN’s special rapporteur on the subject. Other UN experts deem RSDL an [enforced disappearance](https://ishr.ch/toolbox/resources/briefing-paper-un-experts-documentation-of-residential-surveillance-at-a-designated-location-rsdl-in-china/) and call for its end. Your jailers do not care.

An excerpt from the UN Special Rapporteur of the Human Rights Council’s interim [report](https://docs.un.org/en/A/66/268) on torture and other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment, 2011.

Surveillance and control are absolute. Escape and privacy are impossible. Cameras track your every gesture, as do the two guards who are always in the cell with you. They watch you sleep, shower and use the toilet. They may stand or sit beside you, encroaching on your personal space. They communicate only to give orders or fetch necessities. Adding to the humiliation, even your most basic acts and needs require their permission. Bathing is a privilege, not a right. You learn to handwash your clothes in a basin and wipe your cell clean.

The guards restrict your position and posture, forcing you to sit for hours in an interrogation chair, or on your bunk; to stand all day, or only sleep in certain positions, hands always visible. Your body stiffens, aches and grows weak from immobility and inadequate nutrition. Physical deterioration ensues. As muscles atrophy, the will follows.

If your case has drawn outside pressure and attention, they may not actively escalate your suffering further, instead counting on time to grind you down. For the less fortunate, more aggressive torture tactics can include vicious beatings and relentless verbal abuse. You might be forced, as Xie Yang was, to sit for hours at a time on a high stool, legs dangling, not reaching the ground, pressure swelling the legs and causing excruciating pain.

> A common tactic is to create a prisoner’s dilemma by warning (perhaps falsely) that others who know you have already confessed and incriminated you. Fear and shame become viruses you are exposed to daily, until your mental immune system collapses.

If that proves insufficient to force your compliance, officials may deprive you of sleep for days, as they did to several of these writers. Sleep deprivation is insidiously debilitating: it impairs reasoning, judgement, inhibition, memory and attention, and can induce hallucinations, delusions and paranoia. It also increases sensitivity to pain and disrupts hormones and the immune system. The world becomes incoherent, false memories arise, and you become compliant, emotionally dependent, easily suggestible, and unable to evaluate consequences. Like hunger and immobility, lack of sleep erodes your will to resist without leaving physical evidence.

A Cultural Revolution poster which says ‘Adhere to the truth, rectify mistakes; strengthen unity, forge ahead courageously!’. _Credit: [ChinesePosters.net](https://chineseposters.net/posters/d85-256)_

These stress and torture tactics soften you up for hundreds of hours of interrogation. Your case officers combine questioning methods from Chinese police procedures with thought reform and political loyalty techniques that date back to the Communist Party’s even more vicious early decades. Endless gaslighting narratives invert reality, casting you as the wrongdoer and these thugs as agents of righteous authority. They question not only your actions and motives, but your worldview, through relentless repetition compelling you to revise it to match their manufactured one. RSDL thus becomes a form of forced labor in which your daily toil is to answer your masters while they try to humiliate you into begging for mercy. From now on, as Li Qiaochu writes, “living is just being ceaselessly interrogated.”

In this war of psychological attrition, the officers meticulously go through the file they surely have on you for anything they might distort to incriminate you. A stray text message, your WeChat contacts, a business card, an email … anything they can access. Through hour after hour of circuitous questioning, they lie to you, twist your words, try to trick you into incriminating others, and incessantly harp on the slightest inconsistency. A common tactic is to create a prisoner’s dilemma by warning (perhaps falsely) that others who know you have already confessed and incriminated you. Fear and shame become viruses you are exposed to daily, until your mental immune system collapses.

[Safeguard Defenders](https://safeguarddefenders.com/en)’ book _The People’s Republic of the Disappeared_ (3rd edition)

Interrogations cycle between pressure and rapport, cruelty and kindness. They manipulate you with circular reasoning such as, “if you didn’t do anything against the law, then why are you here?” Through endless repetitions of this Kafkaesque logic, their premise justifies itself through familiarity, while your truth is rendered meaningless. RSDL authenticates itself within its own closed system.

The shifts from questioning to isolation and back are jarring. Loneliness makes you yearn for interaction and more willing to comply to maintain it — even with your tormentors. Cooperating may earn small privileges: books to read, movement, better food, and hints that you can hasten the process and lighten your sentence through compliance. By turning basic rights into special favors, they create feedback loops of learned helplessness that condition your brain’s reward centers to crave obedience as a means of survival.

Fail to comply and the interrogators could remind you of the pain your disappearance is causing your loved ones, stoke fears that defiance means never seeing them again, or even threaten to harm them as well. The mental anguish can break the strongest of wills. As Taiwanese human rights advocate Lee Ming-Che recounts, “the officers exploited my mental fragility with calculated threats and promises, preying on my desperation.”

Psychologically and biochemically, RSDL shakes the [three foundational conditions](https://psycnet.apa.org/doiLanding?doi=10.1037%2F0003-066X.55.1.68) of human wellbeing: agency (autonomous control over your own mind, body and actions); stability and predictability; and connection — the social ties through which we regulate our emotions.

Left: Lee Mi

title: How Taiwan’s November Local Elections Could Change the World
zh_title: 台湾 11 月地方选举将如何改变世界
summary: 从左到右：2026 年 10 月 10 日，李家芬、立法院院长韩国瑜、总统赖清德、第一夫人吴美如和副总统萧碧琴出席在台北举行的台湾双十国庆庆祝活动。_图片来源：总统府，来自 [Flickr](https://flic.kr/p/2sFrV8Y)_中期选举后，11 月举行的另一场选举也对全球安全至关重要。曾被《经济学人》称为“地球上最危险的地方”的台湾，将于11月28日举行市长和县长选举，为2028年总统大选奠定基础。
content:
从左到右：李家芬、立法院院长韩国瑜、总统赖清德、第一夫人吴美如和副总统萧碧琴于2026年10月10日在台北出席台湾双十国庆庆典。_图片来源：总统府 via [Flickr](https://flic.kr/p/2sFrV8Y)_

尽管许多人都关注美国中期选举，但 11 月的另一场选举也对全球安全至关重要。曾被《经济学人》称为“地球上最危险的地方”的台湾将于 11 月 28 日举行市长和地方法官选举。他们将为 2028 年总统竞选奠定基础，并带来华盛顿和北京之间爆发危机的风险。

台湾中央选举委员会于 2024 年 1 月 19 日正式认证赖清德和萧美琴当选总统和副总统。_图片来源： [DPP](https://www.facebook.com/photo.php?fbid=954044309418660&set=pb.100044392990655.-2207520000&type=3)_

凭借精明的竞选活动，台湾执政的民进党（DPP）有可能在反对派国民党（KMT）的据点中遭遇历史性的颠覆。民进党在 11 月的关键胜利将反过来推动台湾总统赖清德在 2028 年的连任竞选，但赖清德的胜利也预示着来自北京的更严厉的军事胁迫。
11月民进党的崛起意味着2028年的总统竞选很可能将由黎智英与台湾第二大城市台中市的温和国民党市长卢秀岩对决。现在这有可能成为一场势均力敌的竞争，增加了北京明年通过经济甚至军事压力介入的可能性。

中国海警和其他机构已经开始进行登船练习，使台湾以东的航行正常化，并对前往台湾港口的外国船只进行拦截。这些举动显然是对台湾实施经济隔离的准备。如果黎智英和民进党在 11 月的选举中占据优势，中国可能会在 2028 年投票前试图恐吓台湾选民，或许会实施软封锁。

###### **台湾2028年对阵已定**

习近平和国民党主席郑立文，北京，2026 年 4 月 10 日。_图片来源：发言人毛宁，来自 [X](https://x.com/SpoxCHN\_MaoNing/status/2042557566820196766/photo/1)_
国民党2028年的潜在候选人范围正在迅速缩小。饱受争议的国民党主席郑丽媛野心勃勃地获得提名，但她的毒性如此之大，以至于该党的候选人在今年 11 月的选举竞选活动中都彻底避开了她。她缺乏执政经验和亲中立场——在四月份与习近平的谄媚会面中表现得最为明显——意味着她几乎没有从台湾公众那里赢得[信任](https://www.setn.com/news/1864142)。

国民党在 11 月表现不佳将浇灭郑的总统野心，并迫使她辞去党主席职务。这也将使卢秀妍成为国民党2028年提名的最有力竞争者。卢在即将到来的选举中任期有限，因此将不得不辞去八年后的台中市长职务，从而腾出时间参加总统竞选。

卢是一个相对温和的人，主张增加军费开支，并[批评](https://www.hakkatv.org.tw/news-detail/1668400819682072)她自己的政党与中国结盟过于紧密。她还培养了一种协作[关系](https://www.cna.com.tw/news/aipl/2025072701

【原文 English Original】
From left to right: Lee Chia-fen, Legislative Yuan President Han Kuo-yu, President Lai Ching-te, First Lady Wu Mei-ju, and Vice President Hsiao Bi-khim attending Taiwan's Double Tenth National Day celebration in Taipei, October 10, 2026. _Credit: 總統府 via [Flickr](https://flic.kr/p/2sFrV8Y)_

While many eyes are on the U.S. midterms, another set of November elections also matters for global security. Taiwan, which _The Economist_ once called “the most dangerous place on Earth”, holds mayoral and magistrate elections on November 28. They will set the field for the 2028 presidential race, and with it the risk of a crisis between Washington and Beijing.

Taiwan’s Central Election Commission formally certify the election of Lai Ching-te and Hsiao Bi-khim as President and Vice President, January 19, 2024. _Credit: [DPP](https://www.facebook.com/photo.php?fbid=954044309418660&set=pb.100044392990655.-2207520000&type=3)_

Taiwan’s ruling Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) is within reach of historic upsets in strongholds of the opposition Kuomintang (KMT), thanks to shrewd campaigning. Key DPP wins in November would in turn turbocharge Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te’s reelection campaign in 2028 — but a Lai win would also portend harder military coercion from Beijing.

A DPP surge in November would mean the 2028 presidential field would most likely pit Lai against Lu Shiow-yen, the moderate KMT mayor of Taichung, Taiwan’s second-largest city. This now has the potential to be a close race, raising the chances that Beijing will get involved through economic or even military pressure next year.

The China Coast Guard (CCG) and other agencies have already been practicing ship boardings, normalizing movements east of Taiwan, and hailing foreign vessels heading to Taiwanese ports. These moves are clearly a form of preparation for imposing an economic quarantine on Taiwan. If Lai and the DPP emerge from November’s election in a position of strength, China will likely try to cow Taiwanese voters in the run-up to the 2028 vote, perhaps by operationalizing a soft blockade.

###### **Taiwan’s 2028 Matchup is Already Set**

Xi Jinping and KMT Chairwoman Cheng Li-wun, Beijing, April 10, 2026. _Credit: Spokesperson Mao Ning via [X](https://x.com/SpoxCHN\_MaoNing/status/2042557566820196766/photo/1)_

The KMT’s field of potential candidates for 2028 is shrinking fast. Controversial KMT chairwoman Cheng Li-wun, who has ambitions for the nomination, has become so toxic that the party’s candidates are outright avoiding her on the campaign trail for this November’s elections. Her lack of governing experience and pro-China stance — exhibited most clearly during her obsequious meeting with Xi Jinping in April — mean she has earned little [trust](https://www.setn.com/news/1864142) from Taiwan’s public.

A poor KMT showing in November would extinguish Cheng’s presidential ambitions and pressure her to resign as party chair. That would also leave Lu Shiow-yen as the strongest contender for the KMT’s 2028 nomination. Lu is term-limited for the upcoming elections and will thus have to leave her office as Taichung’s mayor after eight years, freeing her up for a presidential run.

Lu is a relative moderate who has advocated for higher military spending and [criticized](https://www.hakkatv.org.tw/news-detail/1668400819682072) her own party for aligning too closely with China. She has also cultivated a collaborative [relationship](https://www.cna.com.tw/news/aipl/202507270111.aspx) with Taiwan’s third-party, the Taiwan People’s Party (TPP), opening the door for an alliance in 2028 that would provide a stern test for Lai. (The KMT’s failure to work with the TPP the last time around cost it the 2024 presidential vote.)

The Western press has, though, largely overlooked Lai’s remarkable turnaround in fortunes. In July 2025, after a failed campaign to recall legislators and an aborted visit to the United States, Lai’s approval rating fell to just 31 percent. Today it’s at 51.4 percent, thanks in part to missteps by KMT chairwoman Cheng, and an economy surging on the back of the AI chips boom.

Taiwan’s GDP is now forecast to grow by 11 percent in 2026, a 39-year high. On August 17, Lai announced that the government would be handing out NT $10,000 (USD $313) to each citizen as a dividend from the AI boom, buying him and the DPP more love from voters.

Premier of Taiwan’s Executive Yuan, Cho Jung-tai (center), and officials announce the “AI Dividend, Shared by All” initiative, detailing plans for a universal NTD $10,000 cash distribution, August 20, 2026. _Credit: [Executive Yuan](https://www.ey.gov.tw/Page/9277F759E41CCD91/c9b62b00-c255-4c12-9eda-85409410beac)_

###### **Watch Taipei’s Local Elections**

The DPP is currently overperforming in two traditional KMT strongholds: Taipei City, and its surrounding municipality, New Taipei City. The last and only time the DPP won Taipei, Taiwan’s capital, was in 1994, and the last time it won New Taipei was in 2001. It could now win both in the same election, giving Lai’s re-election prospects a substantial boost. By contrast, it would be an unmitigated disaster for the KMT to lose one, let alone both races.

> A DPP breakthrough around the capital would give Lai momentum, all but finish Cheng Li-wun and clear Lu Shiow-yen’s path to the KMT nomination. It could also trigger Beijing to tighten the screws. Watch China’s coast guard as closely as Taiwan’s ballot box.

In Taipei City, the DPP is running Puma Shen Po-yang, a young, defense-minded legislator and founder of the civil defense group Kuma Academy. Shen is running an energetic and well-resourced campaign, swapping his proselytizing on national defense (which had made him one of Beijing’s least-favorite Taiwanese politicians) for an emphasis on quality of life and urban planning.

The DPP’s candidate for mayor of Taipei in the 2026 elections, Puma Shen. _Credit: [DPP](https://www.facebook.com/dpptw/posts/%EF%B8%8F%E5%8F%AA%E8%A6%81%E6%9C%89%E4%BA%BA%E9%96%8B%E5%A7%8B%E6%95%B4%E5%BA%A7%E5%9F%8E%E5%B8%82%E5%B0%B1%E8%83%BD%E4%B8%80%E8%B5%B7%E5%81%9A%E5%88%B0%E5%8F%B0%E5%8C%97%E5%B8%82%E9%95%B7%E5%80%99%E9%81%B8%E4%BA%BA-%E6%B2%88%E4%BC%AF%E6%B4%8B%E6%9C%80%E5%A5%BD%E7%9A%84%E5%9F%8E%E5%B8%82%E4%B8%8D%E8%A9%B2%E7%95%99%E4%B8%8D%E4%BD%8F%E4%BA%BA%E6%9C%80%E5%A4%9A%E7%9A%84%E9%A0%90%E7%AE%97%E4%B9%9F%E4%B8%8D%E8%A9%B2%E6%8F%9B%E4%B8%8D%E5%88%B0%E5%B8%82%E6%B0%91%E5%B0%8D%E6%9C%AA%E4%BE%86%E7%9A%84%E6%9C%9F%E5%BE%85-%E5%8F%B0%E5%8C%97-%E6%B2%88%E4%BC%AF%E6%B4%8B%E5%92%8C%E5%9C%98%E9%9A%8A%E6%95%B4%E7%90%86%E5%B8%82%E6%94%BF%E8%B3%87%E6%96%99%E7%A0%94%E7%A9%B6-199/1614841823338902/)_

The DPP has given Shen a successful makeover, swapping the scruffy hair and hoodies he donned as a legislator for a neater haircut, a suit and tie. In the streets of Taipei, images of Shen’s face outnumber those of his opponent, incumbent mayor Chiang Wan-an, ten to one. His team has given his campaign a clever, orange-coloured theme — providing a thematic distance from the green-themed DPP in the minds of KMT-leaning Taipei voters.

Despite earlier being projected to lose in a landslide, Shen has narrowed his deficit in the [polls](https://tw.news.yahoo.com/%E6%B4%8B%E6%B5%81-%E8%BF%BD%E5%88%B0%E5%8F%AA%E5%B7%AE1-2%E5%80%8B%E7%99%BE%E5%88%86%E9%BB%9E-%E6%9E%97%E4%BF%AE%E6%B0%91-%E6%B2%88%E4%BC%AF%E6%B4%8B%E6%95%A2%E8%AE%93%E6%B0%91%E7%9C%BE%E9%9A%A8%E6%A9%9F%E5%87%BA%E9%A1%8C-030900469.html) to just 1.2 percent behind Chiang as of September 22. And while Chiang may still win, Shen is establishing himself as a next-generation powerhouse for the DPP.

###### **Beijing’s Response**

China will almost certainly try to scare Taiwanese voters in the run-up to the 2028 elections. Beijing has already [branded](https://web.archive.org/web/20260922163359/https:/www.gwytb.gov.cn/xwdt/xwfb/wyly/202607/t20260722_12778251.htm) Lai Ching-te a “destroyer of peace” and [termed](https://web.archive.org/web/20260813090907/https:/www.gwytb.gov.cn/xwdt/xwfb/wyly/202410/t20241014_12656119.htm) Puma Shen a “diehard Taiwan independence separatist”, a label which can carry the death penalty in China.

[![Image 6](https://www.thewirechina.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/J-Michael-Cole-QA.png)](https://www.thewirechina.com/2026/01/18/j-michael-cole-on-the-best-and-worse-cases-for-taiwans-future/)

If the November elections strengthen Lai’s hand, expect PRC pressure to intensify through to 2028. Yet Beijing’s attempts to bend the outcome of the vote could backfire as they have in the past.

The China Coast Guard and the Maritime Safety Administration are already setting the groundwork for coercive moves. Since June, the Coast Guard has expanded “law enforcement patrols” to the waters off Taiwan’s east coast and has begun radioing foreign vessels bound for Taiwanese ports. These signal Beijing’s preparations for a potential economic blockade — one whose timeline could move up if Beijing’s preferred partners, the KMT, falters.

November’s vote will not pick Taiwan’s next president, but it will shape the race to do so. A DPP breakthrough around the capital would give Lai momentum, all but finish Cheng Li-wun and clear Lu Shiow-yen’s path to the KMT nomination. It could also trigger Beijing to tighten the screws. Watch China’s coast guard as closely as Taiwan’s ballot box.

* * *

John Pomfret was the _Washington Post_’s Beijing bureau chief from 1996 to 2003.

Seamus Boyle is a senior associate at Garnaut Global LLC, a global strategic consultancy.

## Details

[Blood on the Clocktower (BotC)](https://boardgamegeek.com/boardgame/240980/blood-on-the-clocktower)is currently the #1 rated party game on [Boardgamegeek.com!](http://boardgamegeek.com!/) We are so pleased that the local community playing BotC at Spielbound has grown such that multiple simultaneous games are being run at each of our BotC meet ups!

In November, the BotC meetup is scheduled for Monday, November 2 from 5:30 - 10:30 PM ... and Spielbound is reserving the *entire* Annex (up to 50 attendees~) for this event! Halloween weekend just passed; you are welcome to attend in costume! Dress up as your favorite BotC character!!!!

* A day pass is required to join this special event ($6 per person on Mondays or current Spielbound member); please check in with the front cafe staff when you arrive.
 * Those who have never played 'Blood on the Clocktower' at Spielbound are welcome to attend this event for free to try it out!
 * Storytellers will be on hand to explain the game rules to novice players, starting at 5:30 PM~

_More on the game:_
 Blood on the Clocktower is a game of murder and mystery, lies and logic, deduction and deception for five-to-twenty courageous players and one devious storyteller.

A social game played in person, seated in a circle, each player receives either a ‘good’ or ‘evil’ token with their unique character on it. Good players share information to solve the mystery whilst evil players lie about who they are and what they know. The good team wins if they can piece together their knowledge, trust each other, and execute the demon. The evil team wins if the demon can sow distrust, evade detection, and wipe out the village.

## Details

**✨ An Hour of Sketching, With Feedback on Your Drawing**

Always wanted to draw? This beginner class starts at the time of this event and takes you from blank page to finished sketch in an hour. No art supplies to buy: any pencil and plain paper will do.

Today's class: **Landscapes**, trees, hills, paths and skies, and how to give a view depth.

Every class ends with personal written feedback: upload a photo of your drawing and get specific tips on how to improve it.

No experience needed. If you've ever said "I can't draw", this is for you.

**Register through the link below** to book your place in this class.

✅ **What you get:**

*   Just a pencil and paper, nothing to buy
*   A chat shared with the people booked into your session
*   A full hour of guided drawing, step by step
*   Feedback on your drawing included, no subscription
*   Personal written feedback on the drawing you make

Sit down, sharpen up, sketch along. 🖼️

**Free monthly real estate investor networking in Omaha.** Bring a deal, find capital, JV partners, agents, lenders and developers.

👉 **Grab your FREE ticket here (required for entry):**[https://www.eventbrite.co.uk/e/real-estate-investor-networking-omaha-property-deal-network-pdn-tickets-1999158473811](https://www.eventbrite.co.uk/e/real-estate-investor-networking-omaha-property-deal-network-pdn-tickets-1999158473811)

Property Deal Network (PDN) is a relaxed monthly meetup for real estate investors, developers and professionals who want to do business face-to-face.

**What happens at PDN Omaha?**
 People bring deals. Others bring capital. Some are sourcing their next project, others are looking for JV partners or professional services. The format is simple: arrive, grab a drink and start conversations. No presentations, no pitches from the front – just direct networking with people who are actively working in real estate.

**Who attends?**
 Investors (from first-timers to portfolio owners), developers, sourcing agents, brokers, attorneys, architects, lenders and accountants. If you're involved in real estate – or want to be – you'll find relevant people here.

**Practical details**
 • **When:** Tuesday 27 October, from 7pm local time
 • **Venue:** Moe & Curly's Pub, 1011 Capitol Avenue, Omaha, NE, 68102
 • **Cost:** Free to attend. The venue asks that everyone buys a drink at full price
 • **Dress:** Smart casual (no sportswear). Over 25s only; ID may be requested

This is an established event that runs every month (except December) – if this date doesn't work, there's always next month. All Omaha dates: [https://www.propertydealnetwork.com/locations/north-america-networking-events/usa-networking-events/omaha-nebraska-usa-property-networking-event/](https://www.propertydealnetwork.com/locations/north-america-networking-events/usa-networking-events/omaha-nebraska-usa-property-networking-event/)

**Industry professional?** Paid promotion tickets (max 2 per event) are available on the ticket page for architects, accountants, builders, mortgage brokers, insurance brokers, interior designers, lenders, realtors and surveyors.

_Property Deal Network – real estate investor networking in 190+ cities worldwide. Join this group to hear about PDN events everywhere._

## Details

Lois S. is graciously hosting us at her church. We'll have our very own whole-foods, plant-based, no-oil SOUPFEST.

Any plant-based soup is great, but you're free to bring anything that goes with soup--breads, corn bread, dessert. Bring dishes containing NO oil or animal products. Bring your own take-home containers, and we'll share our leftovers. Plates, eating utensils, and napkins provided. It might be helpful to bring your own serving utensils. We will provide coffee, tea, water, and maybe lemonade.
 If you'd like to help set up, come a bit early.

If you're unfamiliar with our way of eating, check our discussion board. You'll find plenty of recipe websites that comply with the Forks Over Knives program. (I promise, it's easy!) A couple of websites with easy, compliant recipes: [happyherbivore.com,](http://happyherbivore.com,/)[drmcdougall.com/recipes.](http://drmcdougall.com/recipes.) Can't cook? Think fruit salad, fruit plate, vegetable platter.

The church was kind enough to offer their space free of charge. We'll clean up after ourselves and wash the dishes after dinner. We'll have an optional free-will donation plate to give them as a thank-you.

(No need to RSVP if you can't make it.)

Omaha Forks Over Knives is a lively group celebrating the health benefits of a whole-foods, plant-based, no-oil diet. Each of us is in a different place with foods we do and do not consume; we're not The Food Police. We're here to support and learn from each other. (While we're at it, we entertain each other as well.) If you're new to this, we ask that, at a minimum, you limit your food selection to plant-based items.

content:
We are 100 families taking on the CCP - and we need your help.

我們是「皇家鑄幣廠居民協會」，由約一百戶職工家庭組成。我們懇請你伸出援手。

In 2018, our homes-key-worker flats in Tower Hamlets were sold in a secretive deal to the People's Republic of China. We had no say. No warning. And now, we face living under the shadow of a hostile superpower.

2018年，我們居住的Tower Hamlets地段，在未經通知、無任何諮詢下，被秘密售予中國政府。我們無從置喙，如今更面對一個敵對政權的威脅。

The UK Government is expected to approve plans to build the largest embassy in Europe - right here, at Royal Mint Court, next to the Tower of London… and directly on top of our homes.

英國政府即將批准於倫敦塔旁的皇家鑄幣廠（Royal Mint Court）興建歐洲最大規模的中國大使館，預定地點正正位於我們所居之上。

This is not just a planning dispute.

我們擔憂的不僅是一項城市規劃決策，而是一場關乎國家安全、人身安全與基本權利的危機。

China has never shown any regard for our safety - and now the Government and the Metropolitan Police have abandoned us too.

自2018年起，中國政府從未就此提供明確回應，我們甚至不知道會否被驅逐、是否仍能繼續安居於此。而如今，政府與執法機關也對我們置之不理。

We are the Royal Mint Court Residents Association. People backed our previous Crowdfunder campaign that helped pay for a barrister to present our evidence including an independent security assessment showing the serious risks to us from a terror attack on the mega-embassy.

我們是「皇家鑄幣廠居民協會」。我們之前的眾籌活動獲得許多人的支持，資助我們聘請資深大律師提交證據，包括一份獨立的安全評估報告，指出超級大使館可能帶來的恐襲風險。

We are now launching an urgent legal challenge - a Judicial Review - to change the law and stop this injustice.

我們現在正展開一項緊急法律挑戰 — 即司法覆核 — 希望改變現行法律，阻止這場不公。

We need your help to protect our community from the mighty Chinese Communist Party.

我們需要你的幫助，去保護我們的社區，免受強大的中國共產黨威脅。

Whatever you can spare us, will help David stand-up to Goliath.

無論你能捐出多少，都能幫助大衛對抗歌利亞。

We are seeking to pursue a Judicial Review because we have believed all along that the planning process has been flawed. Here are some of the reasons we think are likely to be relevant:

我們決定提起司法覆核，是因為我們始終認為整個規劃程序存在問題。以下是我們認為可能相關的一些原因：

“Closed mind”: Ministers may have signalled early approval to China, before formal procedures were followed, breaking the law and abusing planning powers. In a similar vein, objections disappeared after UK ministers returned from Beijing. Residents have felt like pawns in a geopolitical game since the start.

預設立場：部長們可能在正式程序開始前就向中方表示支持，違反法律並濫用規劃權力。在部長們從北京回來之後，原有的反對聲音突然消失。居民們從一開始就覺得自己成了地緣政治博弈中的棋子。

Security concerns: Building a fortified embassy with homes on site and critical infrastructure nearby, ignoring espionage concerns and the real human risk to dissidents, is indefensible.

安全隱患：在住宅區內及重要基礎設施附近建設高度防禦的大使館，無視間諜活動與對異見人士的人身威脅，完全不能接受。

Procedural unfairness: We were shut out of the process. No consultation. No transparency. No respect for the people who live here.

程序不公：我們被完全排除在決策過程之外。無諮詢、無透明、無對居民的尊重。

Legitimate expectation: We were promised due process and protection. We got silence.

合理期望落空：我們被承諾將獲程序保障與保護，實際卻是得不到任何保障。

What’s wrong with the embassy plan?

We still live here. 100 families. Nurses, teachers, pensioners. Our 100 homes are on land now owned by the Chinese government. That means the Chinese ambassador is our landlord - with rights to enter our homes.

我們仍然住在這裡 ，足足一百戶家庭，包括護士、教師、退休人士。我們的一百個住所現已位於中國政府擁有的土地上。這代表中國大使成為我們的業主，有權進入我們的住所。

China refuses to answer us. Since 2018, we’ve begged for assurances: will we be evicted? Will we be safe? Can we stay? Beijing’s answer: not until we get planning permission. This refusal, and the proposal to install a temporary style wooden boundary fence as a dividing line, raises fears that the Chinese Government intends to take back the entire 100 apartments at St Mary Graces Court once they secure diplomatic status for the site, leaving us homeless.

中國拒絕回應我們的訴求。自2018年起，我們不斷尋求保證：我們會被驅逐嗎？我們是否安全？我們能否繼續居住？北京的答覆是：等規劃許可下來再說。這種拒絕，以及擬議中以臨時木欄分隔的做法，讓我們擔心中國政府一旦取得外交地位，將會收回整個St Mary Graces Court的100個單位，使我們流離失所。

This embassy is a fortress. It’s not a normal diplomatic building. It will have secret communications centres, fortified walls, and surveillance technology that can monitor our entire estate, even our bedrooms. It will also stand on top of critical UK cables that MI5 warn are a security risk to the UK.

這座大使館是一個堡壘，並非普通的外交建築。它將設有秘密通訊設施、加固圍牆、監控技術，可監視整個屋苑，甚至包括我們的睡房。而它的地基下方，更有英國重要電纜 ，MI5曾警告這是對國家安全的威脅。

The UK Government knows the risk - and ignored it. Our independent security report warns that this site puts families and national security at risk. Even the UK’s Head of Counter-Terrorism originally objected - citing threats to residents and dissidents. But since ministers returned from Beijing, objections have mysteriously vanished.

英國政府明知有風險，卻選擇無視。我們的獨立安全報告指出，該地點將危害居民與國家安全。甚至連英國反恐部門首長最初也曾反對 ， 指出對居民與異見人士的威脅。但自從部長從北京回來後，這些反對聲音神秘地消失。

Ministers made no mention of the 100 families living here. We are alarmed that the letters from Home Secretary Yvette Cooper and Foreign Secretary David Lammy have ignored the fact that UK families live in 100 apartments on the land that is actually part of Royal Mint court - and is owned by the Chinese government. Our Resident’s Chairman has personally appealed to ministers, submitted the full Crilly Consultants security report, and our plight has appeared in The Times, FT, BBC, CNN, and more. What is happening to democratic accountability in this country?

部長們從未提及這裡有一百戶居民。我們對內政大臣Yvette Cooper及外交大臣David Lammy的信件感到震驚，因為他們完全忽略了皇家鑄幣廠的土地上住有英國公民、100個家庭。我們的居民協會主席曾親自致函部長、提交完整的Crilly安全報告，而我們的處境亦已被《泰晤士報》、《金融時報》、BBC、CNN等多間媒體報導。英國民主問責制度何在？

The first duty of the UK government is to protect its citizens. We understand the UK’s diplomatic obligations - but not at the expense of its own people. The refusal to acknowledge the basic risks of housing a high-security foreign embassy on top of a residential block is deeply troubling. It appears the government is prioritising relations with Beijing over the safety of its own citizens.

英國政府的首要職責是保護其國民。我們明白外交義務，但不能以犧牲本國人民為代價。將一個高安全級別的外國大使館設於住宅區上方，而拒絕承認基本風險，是極度令人不安的。

It’s not just about us. Dissidents, including Hong Kongers, Uyghurs, Tibetans, Taiwanese and Chinese exile communities are terrified. They’ve told us they no longer feel safe protesting outside the site, and on British soil. Their presence, and ours, will be met with constant surveillance and intimidation by a regime known to harass and threaten activists - even abroad.

這件事不僅關係到我們。流亡港人、維吾爾人、西藏人、台灣人及中國異見社群皆感到恐懼。他們表示不再敢在該地點或英國土地上公開抗議。他們與我們一樣，將面對來自這個以恐嚇異見者聞名的政權的持續監控與威嚇。

The people have spoken, and they support us.

人民已經發聲，並支持我們。

On 8 February 2025, thousands of British citizens - including Hong Kongers, Uyghurs, Tibetans, Taiwanese and Chinese pro-democracy activists, and human rights campaigners - gathered outside Royal Mint Court in protest against this embassy.

2025年2月8日，數以千計的英國公民 ，包括港人、維吾爾人、西藏人、台灣人、中國民主人士與人權倡議者， 齊集皇家鑄幣廠，抗議中國大使館計劃。

They were joined by cross-party MPs, journalists, and allies. Together, they said NO to the Chinese embassy, and YES to democratic values, safety, and justice.

他們與跨黨派議員、記者及盟友並肩站立，一同說出明確立場：反對中國大使館，支持民主、安全與公義。

Further mass protests followed on 15 March, 3 May, and 14 June - showing growing national resistance to the plan.

3月15日、5月3日及6月14日亦舉行後續大型集會，反對聲浪日益壯大。

They continue to protest, and have made it clear: they won’t stop until this mega-embassy deal is over.

抗議仍在持續，並清楚表示：他們不會停止，直至該項目取消為止。

But the Government is not listening.

但政府並未聆聽我們的訴求。

So now, we go to court.

所以現在，我們只有訴諸法庭。

But we need your help - fast.

但我們需要您的協助 - 迅速的協助。

The legal fees for a Judicial Review are beyond the reach of ordinary families. But with your help, we can stand up to both Beijing and Whitehall.

司法覆核的法律費用遠超普通家庭的負擔。但在您的幫助下，我們能夠與北京和英國政府對抗。

This case is about more than one building. It’s about:

這宗案件關乎的遠不止一座建築。它關乎：

Protecting British citizens from state overreach

保護英國公民免受國家權力的侵害

Defending UK democracy from foreign influence

捍衛英國的民主，抵抗外國影響

Challenging backroom deals that put power over people

挑戰那些將權力凌駕於人民之上的秘密交易

If we succeed, we won’t just protect our homes. We’ll set a precedent that no foreign government can build on British soil without respecting British citizens and British values.

如若成功，我們不僅能保護我們的家園，我們更是創下先例：任何外國政府不得在罔顧英國公民和英國價值的前提下在英國土地上建造任何建築。

Will you stand with us?

您願意與我們並肩作戰嗎？

Please chip in whatever you can. £10. £100. £1,000. Every penny goes to legal costs to take this to court. We are a group of teachers, nurses, shop workers and pensioners. We don’t have the Chinese Communist Party’s millions - but with your help, we do have people power.

請您捐出任何您能負擔的金額 — 不論是 £10，£100 還是 £1,000。每一分錢都將用於支付法律費用，讓我們將此案帶上法庭。我們只是一群教師、護士、店員和退休人士。雖然我們沒有中國共產黨的龐大資金 — 但在您的幫助下，我們擁有的是人民的力量。

Share this far and wide.

請廣傳此訊息。

Donate if you can.

如有行力，請捐款。

Stand up for democracy.

為民主發聲。

Because if they can do this to us, they can do it to anyone.

唇亡齒寒。

PLEASE NOTE

請注意：

This is a secure UK-based platform, fully registered and subject to UK law.

這是一個安全的英國平台，註冊並受英國法律管轄。

It is widely used to support political and legal campaigns, including by MPs, NGOs, and grassroots movements - some of which are openly critical of the Chinese government.

該平台廣泛用於支持政治和法律活動，包括國會議員、非政府組織和基層運動 — 包括曾公開批評中國政府的政治活動。

The platform offers full transparency, with public donation records and payment processing via Stripe or PayPal.

該平台提供完全透明的捐款記錄，並通過 Stripe 或 PayPal 處理支付。

There is no history of censorship or compliance with pressure from the Chinese state.

台以往並無自我審查紀錄，也未曾屈從於中國的壓力。

It adheres strictly to GDPR regulations, ensuring donor and campaigner data is protected.

平台嚴格遵守 GDPR 規範，確保捐款者和活動者的數據安全。

About your donations

關於您的捐款

2.95% + 0.25 of each donation goes to the platform; 100% of the remaining funds will be used to cover legal costs.

每筆捐款將扣除 2.95% 加 £0.25 之平台手續費，其餘款項將全數用以支付法律相關費用。

If the legal case is dismissed, your donation will be directed to charity unless you request a refund. If you would like your donation returned, please email us. We will calculate and refund your contribution (with platform fee deducted).

如法律訴訟最終被駁回，捐款將撥捐予慈善機構，除非閣下主動申請退款。如欲索回捐款，請電郵至，我們將在扣除平台手續費後，計算並退還閣下之捐款。

About campaign updates

關於活動更新

We will post updates every two weeks, which you can follow directly on this page.

我們每兩週更新一次進展，您可以直接於此頁面查看。

**Pie Formosa**

*   ![Image 11: Profile photo of Pie Formosa](https://images.gofundme.com/oDQ7stGTWGmhdF5F-1lcSzcnM08=/128x128/https://gofundme.com/person/profiles/bf38dced-b4fe-46c1-8b1f-7dadeaaa0f66/bf38dced-b4fe-46c1-8b1f-7dadeaaa0f66.png)

Pie Formosa is organizing this fundraiser.

**Pie Formosa**

Donation protected

 I sometimes describe myself as a refugee from WeChat to Instagram — but I am also, quite literally, a refugee from China.

 I am a political dissident, human rights activist, non-binary person and independent writer living with invisible disabilities, now continuing my work in Europe.

 I write and create public work about censorship, authoritarianism, political memory, democracy, queer and trans freedom, refugee experiences, neurodiversity, and the cultural spaces where resistance survives.

 For years, WeChat was one of the places where I published my work. Readers could easily support independent creators with small tips. Then the Chinese Communist Party shut down my account. I lost not only a platform, but also an audience, an archive, and a simple way for people to support my work.

 This fundraiser is part of rebuilding that independence.

 Living with invisible disabilities also means that conventional employment structures and constant high-intensity workloads are not always accessible or sustainable for me. I need a modest and stable income to make independent research, writing and human-rights work sustainable.

 Your support will help cover:

 * research, writing and documentation

 * travel to human-rights, democracy and civil-society events

 * digital tools and publishing costs

 * accessibility-related working needs

 * basic living costs that allow me to continue this work independently

 My first goal is €3,500.

 If something I have written, documented or created has informed, helped or inspired you, even €1, €5 or €10 helps me keep this work alive. If donating is not possible, sharing this fundraiser also makes a real difference.

 Authoritarianism depends on silence and forgetting. Independent voices survive because people choose to keep them alive.

 Thank you for supporting my work.

 Pie Formosa (they/them)

Dear Friends,

My name is Alan, and I am writing this with a sincere and humble heart.

I am a Chinese political dissident living in Houston, Texas. Because of my beliefs and my willingness to speak openly about freedom, human rights, and justice, I have faced serious threats and intimidation from the Chinese government. These pressures have made it impossible for me to safely return to China, where my family still lives. Every day, I carry the pain of being separated from my loved ones, uncertain when—or if—I will ever be able to reunite with them again.

Beyond the emotional suffering, I am now facing severe financial hardship. Due to restrictions and complications surrounding the transfer of my personal funds from abroad, I have been unable to access resources that I once depended on for survival. My savings are rapidly disappearing, and I am now struggling simply to cover basic daily necessities such as food, housing, transportation, and medical care.

This situation has left me feeling isolated and vulnerable. I never imagined that standing by my principles would lead to such profound personal sacrifice, but I continue to hold onto hope.

Today, I am reaching out with deep humility to ask for your support. Any assistance—whether financial help, practical resources, or connections to organizations that aid individuals in political exile—would mean more than words can express. Your kindness could help me maintain stability during this incredibly difficult chapter of my life and allow me to continue moving forward with dignity.

I am not asking for luxury, only for the chance to live safely and meet my most basic needs while I navigate these extraordinary challenges.

Thank you for taking the time to read my story. Your compassion, understanding, and support would be a lifeline during one of the hardest periods of my life.

With deepest gratitude,

Alan

据法国内政部周日发布的全国初步统计，周六在法国爆发的抗议活动导致1314人被拘留，消防部门出动75次扑救火灾；此外，53名执法人员受伤，24家商铺遭抢劫。

法国内政部在声明中指出，周六共“统计到289起公共道路活动”，包括示威和集会，参与者达41万；而10月17日则发生了441起活动，示威者人数达55万人。

该声明继续写道：“游行队伍按照事先规划并经与地方当局协商确定的路线在公共道路上游行，并在国内安全部队的监管下顺利进行”。

**极左翼风险群体**

然而，在多个城市，“由激进左翼和极左翼活动分子等组成的风险群体，在大部分游行队伍的前方、内部或边缘聚集”，从而引发了冲突。

在包括巴黎、马赛、波尔多、图卢兹和图尔在内的多个城市，游行尾声时爆发了示威者与治安部队的冲突，后者使用催泪瓦斯进行反击。

Hong Kong hosted its first-ever palanquin race inspired by the legendary folk deity Ji Gong at Victoria Park on Sunday, drawing crowds eager to witness a revival of a storied plague-banishing ritual from the 19th century.

The tradition is rooted in the long-held Chinese folk belief that parading deities in palanquins can dispel evil and purify the community.

The event, organised by the Tung Cheng Yuen Buddhist Association and supported by the Chinese Temples Committee along with over 20 cultural and educational organisations, formed the centrepiece of the three-day 2026 International Ji Gong Cultural Festival.

The competing teams carried palanquins from Tik Lung Lane to Wan Chai Pier, then crossed the harbour by boat to Hung Hom, in a nod to Ji Gong’s epidemic-dispelling journey. Along the route, participants tackled various obstacle challenges that tested their teamwork, patience, and problem-solving skills.

Beyond the race, the festival featured Cantonese opera performances for seniors, blessing ceremonies, interactive booth games, and a Ji Gong plague-expelling ritual procession. Attendees also enjoyed hands-on activities such as fan-shaped soap workshops, compression art sessions, and lacquer fan crafts to immerse themselves in Chinese cultural practices.

Organisers noted that the event serves as a reminder for the public to remain vigilant against epidemics and to safeguard traditional religious rituals.

# 以色列将在大选日关闭所有约旦河西岸口岸

3 小时前 3 小时前
在周五发生一起造成两名以色列士兵死亡的袭击后，以色列军方宣布，将在下周二大选期间关闭与约旦河西岸之间的所有陆路口岸。

在以色列对希伯伦市展开军事行动期间，被疏散的巴勒斯坦人的房屋上挂起以色列国旗 图像来源: Mahmoud Illean/AP Photo/picture alliance

广告

（德国之声中文网）[以色列](https://dw.com/zh/%E4%BB%A5%E8%89%B2%E5%88%97/t-40363274)军方周日（10月25日）宣布，从当天起，巴勒斯坦人不得进入西岸的以色列社区工作；下周二的大选日全天关闭所有陆路口岸，禁止巴勒斯坦工人进出整个约旦河西岸地区。以色列将在下周二（10月27日）举行议会选举。

上周五，[巴勒斯坦](https://dw.com/zh/%E5%B7%B4%E5%8B%92%E6%96%AF%E5%9D%A6/t-40889933)武装人员在希伯伦市（Hebron）附近发动袭击，造成两名以色列士兵丧生，另有三人受伤。两名袭击嫌疑人被击毙。以色列军方随后在约旦河西岸展开了军事行动。巴勒斯坦激进组织哈马斯对此次袭击表示赞赏，但并未宣称对此负责。以色列军队表示，已“逮捕了约40名嫌疑人，其中包括隶属于[哈马斯](https://dw.com/zh/%E4%BB%A5%E8%89%B2%E5%88%97-%E5%93%88%E9%A9%AC%E6%96%AF%E6%88%98%E4%BA%89/t-68961301)和伊斯兰圣战组织（Islamic Jihad）的恐怖分子。”

希伯伦市长优素福·贾巴里（Yousef al-Jabari）向半岛电视台表示，自周五以色列发动突袭以来，已有约2200人流离失所。以色列国防部长伊斯雷尔·卡茨（Israel Katz）证实了这一数字。他在接受以色列公共广播公司（Kan）采访时称，在“我们彻底解决希伯伦境内所有与哈马斯相关的问题之前”，巴勒斯坦人“将不被允许返回”。

以色列总理内坦尼亚胡强调要让袭击者付出沉重代价，并称正计划开展一场以色列1967年首次占领约旦河西岸以来最大规模的行动。

（法新社、路透社）

# Eastern Taiwan may see heavy rain as Champi heads to Japan: CWA

10/25/2026 02:49 PM

[](jsvscript:)[](jsvscript:)[](javascript:void(0))[Listen](javascript:)

CNA photo Oct. 24, 2026

Taipei, Oct. 25 (CNA) Eastern Taiwan could still see localized showers, with heavy rain possible in Hualien and Taitung counties, as Tropical Storm Champi weakens and moves farther away from Taiwan and toward Japan, the Central Weather Administration (CWA) said Sunday.

Northern Taiwan will see cloudy skies after brief showers on Sunday, while central and southern Taiwan will be mostly cloudy to sunny, with a chance of afternoon showers in mountainous areas and heavy rain possible in mountainous parts of southern Taiwan, the CWA said.

Daytime temperatures will range from 27 to 30 degrees Celsius in northern Taiwan and from 30 to 32 degrees in central and southern Taiwan, while nighttime lows will fall to 22-25 degrees, the agency said.

Localized showers are expected to persist in eastern Taiwan on Monday, while areas north of Taoyuan may see scattered showers, the CWA forecast.

The rest of the country will be mostly cloudy to sunny, with brief, scattered showers possible in mountainous parts of southern Taiwan, the CWA said.

On Tuesday and Wednesday, strengthening seasonal northeasterly winds will bring cooler temperatures to northern Taiwan, along with showers in eastern Taiwan, areas north of Taoyuan and the Hengchun Peninsula in the south.

Other parts of the island will see mostly cloudy to sunny skies, although brief afternoon showers are possible in mountainous parts of central and southern Taiwan, the CWA said.

As the seasonal winds weaken on Thursday and Friday, mostly cloudy to sunny conditions are expected to return across Taiwan, the CWA said.

As of 8 a.m. Sunday, Champi was located east-northeast of Taiwan and moving northeast toward Japan at 24 kilometers per hour, according to the CWA. Tropical Storm In-Fa was about 5,000 kilometers from Taiwan and was not expected to have a direct impact on the island.

title: Book Club: On Courage by Julia Angwin and Ami Fields-Meyer, Sun, Oct 25, 2026, 4:00 PM   | Meetup
summary: We are reading _On Courage: How to Be a Dissident in an Age of Fear_ by Julia Angwin and Ami Fields-Meyer for our October book club meeting. The meeting will be held at the We Are Family Community Center located on the second floor at 3265
content:
We are reading _On Courage: How to Be a Dissident in an Age of Fear_ by Julia Angwin and Ami Fields-Meyer for our October book club meeting.

The meeting will be held at the We Are Family Community Center located on the second floor at 3265 N. Carolina Ave in North Charleston. [Click here for directions](https://lowcountryhumanists.org/waf-directions/).

After the discussion, participants will have an opportunity to continue the conversation informally at Rebel Taqueria.
_Thanks to the generosity of our donors, SHL has funds available to ensure everyone feels welcome and able to participate. If you would like to participate in dining with us after book club but the cost presents a challenge, please email us at [shl@lowcountryhumanists.org,](http://shl@lowcountryhumanists.org,/) and we can discreetly arrange to cover your costs._

**About the Book:**
 The United States is only the latest country to face a leader who wields fear as a weapon, punishes political enemies, disappears people off the street, and undermines free and fair elections. Today nearly three out of four people on earth live under authoritarianism, the highest rate since the late 1970s.

But even under repressive conditions, each of us holds the power to help defeat autocrats. Based on their acclaimed The New Yorker essay “So You Want to Be a Dissident?,” veteran reporter Julia Angwin and political strategist Ami Fields-Meyer give us a captivating – and profoundly hopeful – guide to courage in an age of fear.

Meet a student from Hong Kong who risked everything for democracy. A mom in a working-class neighborhood of Caracas who broke with the political movement that raised her. Cairo twentysomethings who staged a gutsy stunt to help bring down a dictator. A mild-mannered immigrant fighting to save a landmark U.S. civil rights law. People throughout the United States and across five continents who faced serious risks for dissenting in their workplace, their community, or their country. _On Courage_ is the story of how they did it anyway – and how you can do it, too.

Blending rich, previously untold narratives with history, spirituality, and movement research, Angwin and Fields-Meyer deliver a highly accessible book full of practical lessons – an inspiring resource for anyone, anywhere, who feel the walls of history closing in on them. _On Courage_ is a roadmap to political courage and a powerful case for how taking personal risks can help save the free world.

## Details

Join your humanist friends at the **Holiday Festival of Lights Fun Walk** at James Island County Park. This is an event put on by Charleston County Parks as a preview for their popular Festival of Lights. [We have done this the last two years](https://lowcountryhumanists.org/2025-festival-of-lights-fun-walk/) and had a great time!

Tickets are $38 per vehicle, and **expected to sell out fast**, so buy tickets now!

There are two different events on consecutive days. **Be sure to buy tickets for Wednesday, November 11th!** Buy tickets and find additional information on the event page:
[https://www.ccprc.com/event/holiday-festival-of-lights-fun-run-%26-walk/516/](https://www.ccprc.com/event/holiday-festival-of-lights-fun-run-%26-walk/516/)

This event is part of a sneak preview of the annual Festival of Lights at James Island County Park. The walk is 2 miles on a paved course through over 200 light displays. After the walk, participants are invited to enjoy the festival's amenities.

**Plan to arrive by 6 pm**. The gate closes to additional entrants at 6:30 pm. The walk will start once all cars are parked. See the park's event site linked above for all the additional details.

Tickets are per vehicle, not per person. We will try to plan a rally point outside the park to meetup before the event to carpool.
_If you would like to participate in the event, but the cost presents a challenge, please email us at [shl@lowcountryhumanists.org.](http://shl@lowcountryhumanists.org./) We expect that some of our ticketed participants will have room in their vehicles to bring additional people._

# Recovering from Religion Support Group Meeting - South Carolina Chapter

[![Image 7: Photo of the user Charles Hammond](https://secure.meetupstatic.com/photos/member/c/b/8/6/thumb_325252102.jpeg?w=96) Hosted by Charles H. and 2 others Recovering from R. is a Super Organizer](https://www.meetup.com/rfr-south-carolina-chapter/events/316772548/attendees/)

## Details

The South Carolina Chapter Recovering from Religion support group will meet the fourth Wednesday or each month at 6pm Eastern. **This meeting will be held in-person at the We Are Family community room located at 3265 North Carolina Avenue, Suite 202 in North Charleston.** Attendees are welcome to share, but may also decide to remain anonymous if they so choose.

Light refreshments will be provided. Please contact one of the event hosts if you have any questions or concerns ahead of the meeting.

The primary focus of a Recovering from Religion support group is to provide ongoing support to individuals as they let go of their religious beliefs. This transitional period is an ongoing process that can result in a range of emotions, as well as a ripple effect of consequences throughout an individual’s life. As such, the support meetings are safe and anonymous places to express these doubts, fears, and experiences without biased feedback or proselytizing.
 We are here to help each other through this journey.

There is no cost to attend this support group but, if you feel so inclined, donations can be made at [www.recoveringfromreligion.org/donate](http://www.recoveringfromreligion.org/donate)

If you'd like to provide confidential feedback for this meeting, click here [https://forms.gle/yhC7frShmyrRS56G7](https://forms.gle/yhC7frShmyrRS56G7)

If you find you need to talk with someone before the next support meeting, RfR has a hotline and online chat for that express purpose. Call [844-368-2848](http://tel:+18443682848/) to speak with someone. To chat online, go to [www.recoveringfromreligion.org](http://www.recoveringfromreligion.org/) and click on the green chat bubble in the lower left corner of the site.

If you are in need of professional help, we can recommend the Secular Therapy Project to provide options to connect with a professional therapist. All therapists have been thoroughly vetted by our organization and offer only evidence-based and non-religious treatment. Connect with them at [www.seculartherapy.org.](http://www.seculartherapy.org./)

Like what RfR does? Why not volunteer! There are quite a few options. Head over to [RfR Volunteer Form](https://www.recoveringfromreligion.org/volunteer) for more info.

content:
## Details

**Thursday, November 5, 7 pm (Doors open at 6:45 for socializing)**
**Sierra Club presents: Designing and Building for a Sustainable Future**
**April Magill, Principal Architect and Executive Director, Root Down Designs**
**College of Charleston Rita Hollings Science Center Auditorium, 58 Coming Street (corner of George)**
**Free and open to the public. Also on Zoom, please register here:**
[https://us02web.zoom.us/meeting/register/5tI7iy7tTe-6P0SPlsU_mA](https://us02web.zoom.us/meeting/register/5tI7iy7tTe-6P0SPlsU_mA)
 The latest research makes one thing clear: addressing climate change on a global scale requires us to rethink the built environment. Buildings contribute significantly to global warming—not only through how we heat and cool them, but through the materials we use to construct them.
 Healthy, breathable buildings made from bio-based, plant-derived materials offer a powerful path toward a carbon-negative future—one that supports the health of both our planet and the people who inhabit it.
 Come learn how April and the Root Down team are pioneering this movement across the Southeast and beyond through progressive architecture, hands-on building workshops, and educational classes that are transforming the way we think about—and build—the places we call home.
 April Magill is a leading voice and pioneer in climate-smart, healthy, and sustainable building. She is the founder and owner of Charleston-based Root Down Designs, as well as the founder and executive director of a nonprofit advancing healthy, affordable housing for disadvantaged communities. As an educator and adjunct professor at the American College of the Building Arts, April teaches sustainable building practices and materials and has led numerous community workshops. She is also a sought-after national speaker on bio-based, carbon-negative building materials.
 Sierra Club mission statement: To explore, enjoy, and protect the wild places of the earth

**Reiki** is a Japanese energy healing technique developed in the early 1900’s by Mikao Usui to stimulate health and vitality through channeling life force energy. While promoting a deep state of relaxation, Reiki therapy may reduce stress, anxiety, and pain through gentle touch and transferring of energy. The practitioner delivers this energy through their hands to assist in improving the recipients biofield flow and balance on the physical, emotional, mental, and spiritual levels. By having a tranquil effect on the mind and body, Reiki promotes healing and restoration while having a favorable influence on the parasympathetic and autonomic nervous systems.

**Access Bars** was developed by Gary Douglas as a set of tools and processes applied to facilitate more consciousness. As a restorative modality, Access Bars involves the practitioner connecting with 32 points on participants head through gentle touch. This contact facilitates the release of negative energetic thought forms, ideas, beliefs, emotions, and considerations that create barriers. As energetic blockages are discharged, a rebalancing occurs making room for improved thought patterns. Results may include a more peaceful mind, relaxed body, improved outlook, stress relief, more energy, and feeling replenished. Measurements of electrical activity of the brain conducted after an Access Bars treatment were shown to have literally calmed brain activity down.

**Facilitator: Lisa Ann Helmly,MS,RDN,LDN, [lisa@lisahelmly.com**](http://lisa@lisahelmly.com**/)

*   Holy Fire III/Karuna Reiki Master
*   Certified Kundalini Reiki Practitioner
*   Certified Access Bars Practitioner
*   Passionate about inspiring people to optimize their health and wellbeing.
*   Small changes yield big results.

As a Low Country Native, Lisa is enthused to share complimentary integrated healing and restorative modalities to promote optimal health and well-being. Holding a Bachelor of Arts in Business Administration equipped Lisa to gain experience in the corporate environment, flip residential housing properties, and continue managing her rental property business. Completing a Master of Science in Nutrition as a Registered Dietitian Nutritionist prepared Lisa for working in the medical sector assisting patients with a variety of illnesses, disease states, and conditions. During this time to the present, Lisa pursued further studies in alternative and integrative health practices attaining multiple credentials. While working in these areas, Lisa continued serving in her roles as a mother, daughter, sister, and friend.

**Sounds Productive Right? Does Being More Productive Support Health and Well-Being?**

“Getting busier does not necessarily make you better…affectively managing your stress does!”

You really didn’t think all of that activity was done perfectly with complete ease and grace, did you? Of course not. As Lisa was stressed out creating elevated levels of cortisol and adrenaline, this lack of balance was in opposition to a positive state of health and well-being. How ironic is that behavior? Lisa more fully understands how stress and being out of balance can have a negative impact on the mind and body. Sometimes the vehicle that drives a person to do, may eventually run them over. Hypothetically speaking, imagine being in a hit and run accident driven by yourself in your very own car. Can you relate now? The coping mechanism of burning the candle at both ends is comfortable because it is familiar. However, the candle may eventually burn out.
 If there is one commonality that we all have in this human experience, it’s managing our own life stressors. Add a dose or two of trauma along the way and what do you get…**Amplified Stress with Triggers.** The well-being sessions are offered here for interested participants to explore complementary and integrative approaches on processing and managing stress to ultimately feel and function better. You are invited to take this peaceful exploration on optimizing your own health and happiness.
