content:
官方媒体援引地方当局的消息称，中国偏远的西藏地区发生强烈地震，造成至少 16 人死亡、46 人受伤。布达拉宫，西藏拉萨。资料照片：维基共享资源。周四晚上 10:33（格林威治标准时间 1433）发生的 7.0 级地震中，超过 300 栋房屋倒塌。官方通讯社新华社称，官员们仍在评估损失情况，救灾工作正在进行中。中国中央电视台（CCTV）援引当地官员的话说，受伤人数为 46 人，其中 11 人伤势严重，339 间房屋倒塌或受损。中央电视台发布的视频显示，地震发生时，餐厅里的工作人员纷纷逃离，超市货架上的物品纷纷掉落。美国地质调查局称，震中位于那曲地区东北偏东约190公里、自治区首府拉萨东北390公里的山区。撞击深度约为10公里。美国地质勘探局绘制的 2026 年 10 月 22 日西藏地震地震震动图。照片：美国地质调查局。据央视报道，该地区已启动三级地震灾害应急响应。震中位于巴庆县马如乡。据新华社报道，镇副镇长拉旺达波表示，镇政府明显有震感，办公室墙壁出现裂缝。该机构表示，县城的电力和电信服务中断。
据新华社报道，已派出300多名警察参与救援工作，地区消防救援总队已调集347名人员前往受灾地区。闭路电视画面显示，救援人员爬过受损的建筑物，其中一些建筑物的屋顶已经倒塌，并载着一名人员。它还显示救援人员用手电筒照射其他受损的建筑物，士兵们排队准备部署。中国的地震比较常见。 2025年1月，西藏定日县发生地震，造成至少126人死亡。据官方媒体报道，2023 年 12 月，中国西北部偏远的甘肃省发生地震，造成至少 127 人死亡。那次地震是中国自 2014 年以来最严重的一次地震，当时西南部的云南省有 600 多人死亡。 2008年四川省发生大地震，造成约9万人死亡或失踪，其中包括约5,000名学童。

【原文 English Original】
A strong earthquake killed at least 16 people and injured 46 in China’s remote Tibet region, state media said, citing local authorities. Potala Palace, Lhasa, Tibet. File photo: Wikicommons. More than 300 houses collapsed in the 7.0 magnitude quake, which struck on Thursday at 10:33 pm (1433 GMT). Officials were still evaluating the damage, and disaster relief work was ongoing, state news agency Xinhua said. China Central Television (CCTV) put the number of injured at 46, 11 of them seriously, with 339 houses collapsed or damaged, citing local officials. Videos posted by CCTV showed workers running out of restaurants and objects falling off shelves at supermarkets when the quake struck. The epicentre was located in a mountainous area about 190 kilometres east-northeast of Nagqu, and 390 kilometres northeast of the regional capital Lhasa, the US Geological Survey said. It struck at a shallow depth of around 10 kilometres. USGS Shakemap of the earthquake that struck Tibet on October 22, 2026. Photo: US Geological Survey. A level-III earthquake disaster emergency response was activated in the area, CCTV reported. The epicentre was in Maru township in Baqen county. Township deputy head Lhawang Dagpo said the quake was clearly felt at the township office, which sustained cracks in the walls, according to Xinhua. Power and telecoms services were disrupted in the county seat, the agency said. More than 300 police officers have been dispatched for relief work while the regional fire and rescue corps has mobilised 347 personnel to the affected areas, Xinhua reported. Rescue workers clambered through damaged buildings, some with collapsed roofs, and carrying one person, footage on CCTV showed. It also showed rescue workers shining flashlights on other damaged buildings and soldiers lining up ready to be deployed. Earthquakes in China are relatively common. In January 2025, at least 126 people were killed in an earthquake in Tibet’s rural Tingri county. In December 2023, a quake in remote Gansu province in northwest China killed at least 127 people, according to state media. That quake was China’s deadliest since 2014, when more than 600 people died in the southwestern province of Yunnan. A huge tremor in 2008 in Sichuan province left some 90,000 people dead or missing, including around 5,000 schoolchildren.

title: 警方突袭 Box Hill 地下赌场，多名涉案华人落网
source: 澳洲唐人街 – Australia ChinaTown News 中文华人新闻
summary: 澳洲广播公司 10 月 23 日报道，维州警方在调查墨尔本北区、东区涉毒案件期间，一举捣毁两处地下赌场，多名中国籍嫌疑人落网。 警方查明，两处地下赌场分别设在 Carnegie 以及华人聚居区 Box Hill 的物业内。行动中，探员还在周边多个地点查获毒品、武器、非法烟草以及大额现金。 本次行动被拘留的外籍人员包含 3 名中国籍、2 名马来西亚籍人士。警方后续还计划传唤其他涉案人员，追究毒品相关罪责。 本周早些时候，警方就在 Box Hill 一处非法赌场抓获一名男子 探员
content: 澳洲广播公司 10 月 23 日报道，维州警方在调查墨尔本北区、东区涉毒案件期间，一举捣毁两处地下赌场，多名中国籍嫌疑人落网。 警方查明，两处地下赌场分别设在 Carnegie 以及华人聚居区 Box Hill 的物业内。行动中，探员还在周边多个地点查获毒品、武器、非法烟草以及大额现金。 本次行动被拘留的外籍人员包含 3 名中国籍、2 名马来西亚籍人士。警方后续还计划传唤其他涉案人员，追究毒品相关罪责。 本周早些时候，警方就在 Box Hill 一处非法赌场抓获一名男子 探员持搜查令，对 Carnegie、Box Hill、Balwyn North 以及 South Melbourne 多处地点展开搜查，起获枪支、砍刀、长剑、匕首等各类武器，同时查获 60 万澳元现金、非法烟草与电子烟、7 公斤冰毒以及 5 公斤氯胺酮。 这项调查最早始于 7 月，警方当时在墨尔本北区 Bundoora 的一处物业拘捕 9 名涉嫌关联某犯罪集团的人员。 被捕人员当中有两名马来西亚籍男子、一名中国籍男子以及一名泰国女子。 一名 38 岁马来西亚籍男子被控持有用于毒品贩运的物质、设备或材料，以及处理赃物；另一名 29 岁马来西亚籍男子被控贩运冰毒、持有仿制枪支、疏于处置犯罪所得、使用虚假文件。 一名 27 岁中国籍男子被控持有冰毒、违禁武器，以及非法贩运烟草和电子烟；一名 25 岁泰国女子被控持有冰毒，并且持有一套被盗警用制服。 上述四人目前仍处于羁押状态，同址被捕的另外五人，警方拟通过传票形式，以多项毒品罪名对其提起诉讼。 进入 8 月，调查人员在 Carnegie 排查时，发现一处正在运营的非法赌场。 警方称该场所内设多个赌间，事发时有 15 人在场参与赌博，其中两人为赌场工作人员。警方现场问询后释放这 15 人，后续计划发传票，以处置犯罪所得、在未经许可的赌博场所逗留等罪名起诉他们。 10 月 15 日，专案组继续开展联动搜查，对 South Melbourne 一处物业执行搜查令。一名 40 岁的 South Melbourne 女子被捕，面临多项指控，包括商业规模大宗冰毒贩运、持有可卡因以及持有违禁武器。 时隔五天，警方搜查 Box Hill 另一处物业，查获第二家地下赌场，当场抓获两名涉嫌经营赌场的人员。 一名 43 岁中国籍男子被控处置疑似犯罪所得财产、在未经许可的赌博场所逗留，该男子现已被拘留。 警方在墨尔本东区 Box Hill 非法赌场内查封赌桌 另一名 49 岁、居住在 Balwyn North 的男子，警方将以同类罪名传票起诉。 同日，探员还搜查了 Box Hill Whitehorse Road 的一处地址，现场搜出现金与手写账本，证据显示这里曾开展大规模赌博活动。警方拘捕一名 59 岁 Box Hill 女子，其被指为赌场工作人员。 在 Balwyn North 一处住宅的搜查中，警员找到更多现金、赌场筹码，还起获 4 支枪支、其余武器、大批烟草以及制毒设备，并抓获一名 45 岁 Balwyn North 女子。警方拟通过传票，以处置疑似犯罪所得财产、涉枪相关罪名对其追责。 维州警方调查组侦缉督察 Carlie Kohler 在通报中表示，系列抓捕行动将有力打击扎根本地的贩毒集团。 她称：“查处这些赌场、取缔场内非法活动，能够减少流入街头的毒品与武器。本次一系列拘捕，是我们多层次打击有组织犯罪的关键举措。我们呼吁掌握毒品进口、生产或贩运线索的民众主动向警方举报。”

# 中共五中全會前瞻：會前為何密集「打虎」？未來怎樣「從嚴治黨」？

圖像來源，Getty Images

Published 1 小時前

閱讀時間: 3 分鐘

中共第二十屆中央委員會第五次全體會議（五中全會）將於10月26日至29日在北京召開，主題為「全面從嚴治黨」。這是二十一大前一年舉行的全會，在反腐持續升溫、高級官員接連落馬的背景下，外界關注中共如何總結過去的反腐成果，以及是否為明年換屆鋪路。

會前數月，反腐行動再度密集。8月27日，江西省長葉建春被查；10月13日，已退休的前重慶市長黃奇帆也被宣布接受調查。近年落馬的中管幹部人數持續攀升。

美國喬治亞州立大學政治學教授安德魯·魏德曼（Andrew Wedeman）長期研究中國政治與反腐運動。他對BBC中文表示，近幾年被查的「老虎」數量屢創新高，反腐的力度和速度遠超以往任何時期。「這意味著兩件事：第一，反腐運動確實抓到了很多人；第二，它並沒有成功發揮威懾作用。」

分析人士認為，北京正透過會前的反腐行動，進一步整頓官僚體系，並處理二十一大前的人事問題。但十三年反腐之後，仍有三個關鍵問題沒有答案：習近平能否讓官僚體系真正按他的意志運作？十三年反腐後，腐敗是否減少、威懾是否有效？退休官員是否仍有安全空間？

## 「黨建」主題：從制定政策到落實政策

按照慣例，五中全會本應聚焦下一個五年規劃。但本屆三中全會延遲，四中、五中全會的議題依次順延。四中全會已審議通過「十五五」規劃建議，五中全會因此承接通常屬於六中全會的黨建議題。官方已明確，會議將審議《中共中央關於持之以恆推進全面從嚴治黨若干重大問題的決定》。

魏德曼認為，這反映習近平當前最關注的已不只是制定新政策，而是如何確保政策得以落實。習近平近年多次批評地方官員「陽奉陰違」、「自行其是」。在魏德曼看來，北京真正希望解決的不只是腐敗，更是官僚體系的執行力。

亞洲協會政策研究所中國政治研究員牛犇（Neil Thomas）在發給BBC中文的電郵中預測，全會後可能出現幾項變化：重大項目和財政支出的監管加強，黨委書記的問責機制強化，更多利用大數據查處腐敗，地方官員面對更嚴格的監管，紀檢部門的權力進一步擴大。

不過他也提醒，如此嚴厲的問責制度，可能令基層官員更不願承擔風險。

## 十三年反腐，如何繼續「從嚴治黨」

中共反腐在習近平2012年底上台之後，開啟「風暴」模式，「打虎拍蠅」成為中國人耳熟能詳的政治語碼。「老虎」通常指中央管理的副部級以上官員；「蒼蠅」指查處基層腐敗官員。

落馬的中管官員人數近年持續攀升，根據中紀委披露，2025 年立案審查調查的中管幹部181人，比2024年的92人增加近一倍。同期立案縣處級幹部4.1萬人，立案鄉科級幹部13.7萬人。

魏德曼說：「過去十幾年裡，習近平的反腐運動累積了驚人的戰果，但他並沒有贏得這場戰爭。」他指出，反腐的目的不只是查處，更在形成威懾，讓涉腐者收手，讓未涉腐者不敢越界，但高官落馬數量長期居高不下，說明這一效果沒有達到預期。他說，許多今天落馬的「老虎」，在中層任上就已涉腐，有的持續十年、十五年，期間不僅逃過查處，還一路升遷。

對於外界所說的「越反越腐」，他並不認為是反腐催生了更多腐敗。更準確的說法是，十三年高壓反腐，仍未完全改變官員的行為模式。

## 被污染的池子中，如何選人？

魏德曼認為，習近平如今面對的，已不再主要是前任時期提拔的官員。「現在他真正不得不面對的，是那些在他任內被提拔上來的人當中的腐敗問題。」他形容，習近平把落馬的「老虎」清除，再提拔新人接替，卻發現自己是在一個已被污染的池子裡挑人。在他看來，問題未必只存在於個別官員或特定派系，而可能與整個幹部選拔機制有關。

他還留意到，許多落馬官員近年公開發表的懺悔錄，敘事高度相似：從懷抱理想、服務人民開始，進入體制後逐步受環境影響，最終走向腐敗，落馬後完成悔悟。他認為，這種公式化的自白，反映官方傾向把腐敗歸因於個人道德失守。但如果大量官員講述幾乎相同的故事，問題是否僅在個人道德？

他分析，改革開放後的經濟高速增長和市場化，改變了官員的激勵方式。相比毛澤東時代強調的集體主義和奉獻精神，如今許多官員更傾向於把個人、家庭和未來發展納入考量。習近平透過意識形態教育和黨建工作，試圖重建官員的服從意識與使命感，但魏德曼認為效果並不明顯。

牛犇同樣認為，反腐如今已是持續性的組織整頓機制，而不再是派系鬥爭。於是，五中全會再次強調「全面從嚴治黨」，一個難以迴避的問題是：中共能否改變滋生腐敗的制度環境和官僚文化，還是只能繼續靠更嚴格的監督與懲罰維持運轉？

## 「安全著陸」不再存在？

會前，葉建春、曾與薄熙來共事的黃奇帆相繼被查，外界討論「安全著陸」是否已不復存在。

香港大學政治與公共行政學系副教授朱江南表示，目前這一輪密集的反腐傳遞出即使退休、離任也沒有所謂安全著陸的訊號，表達中央反腐沒有放鬆的意圖。

魏德曼說，他從不相信中共官場存在真正的安全著陸，1995年的陳希同、2006年的陳良宇，以及後來的周永康、薄熙來都是例證。

至於黃奇帆為何落馬，他認為目前很難判斷：可能與重慶任期有關，可能與上海時期有關，可能與退休後的金融圈人脈有關，也可能純粹是「政治祭旗」。

牛犇則認為，黃奇帆是專業技術官僚，他的落馬顯示當下的反腐已超越傳統派系劃分，更聚焦政治忠誠、風險控制和組織紀律。

五中全會也是觀察二十一大前人事布局的重要窗口。近年多名中央委員落馬，部分政治局職位出現空缺，這些位置是否會有新安排，是外界關注的焦點。

此外，中國政壇至今沒有明確的接班人。魏德曼和牛犇都認為，這反映習近平面臨兩難：不指定接班人有助維持權威，指定接班人則可能提前形成新的權力中心。

Tightening Credit Conditions Put Pressure on Asian Investments in US bbert@hudson.org Fri, 10/23/2026 - 15:02 SVG Commentary Oct 23, 2026 Nikkei Asia Tightening Credit Conditions Put Pressure on Asian Investments in US Japan, South Korea, and Taiwan must turn pledges into return-delivering projects.   Riley Walters Senior Fellow Riley Walters Commentary Caption Construction of the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Arizona semiconductor manufacturing complex in Phoenix, Arizona, on February 1, 2026. (Getty Images) Toggle Table of Contents Contents Contents Share to Twitter Twitter Share to Facebook Facebook Share to LinkedIn LinkedIn Share to E-mail E-mail Print Print There are great political expectations for the combined $1.4 trillion in direct investment and credit commitments that Japan, South Korea and Taiwan have made as a part of their investment deals with the administration of President Donald Trump. Recent updates on these deals should come as no surprise as the U.S. quickly approaches its midterm elections. But progress toward each deal's total investment value has been seen over the last year, with some moving faster than others. The terms of each deal differ and, now ,tightening credit conditions in the U.S. are putting additional pressure on all three as investors expect to see interest rates rise and stay elevated for longer. Taiwan has made the greatest progress toward its direct investment goal of $250 billion thanks to Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. exceeding that amount with its own commitments of $265 billion. Taiwan's companies are paramount for America's insatiable demand for artificial intelligence. Taiwan still has an additional goal of $250 billion in credit commitments to make. Recent announcements of $55 billion in technology-related projects, and $4.4 billion in Alaskan liquefied natural gas (LNG), are positive developments but bridging the remaining $190 billion gap will become harder. Finance for these projects is expected to be denominated in U.S. dollars and using U.S. interest rates. Of the three Asian economies , Taiwan is more vulnerable to a currency shock. U.S. tariffs on semiconductor imports could further weaken the Taiwan dollar at a moment's notice. When President Donald Trump announced his global tariffs in April 2025, the Taiwan dollar depreciated 7% against the U.S. dollar, while the Japanese yen and South Korean won both fell just 3%. Meanwhile, U.S. rates are already roughly double what's offered in Taiwan. This difference could widen further as U.S. rates are expected to move closer to 5% over the next year. Meanwhile, Japan is about one-quarter of its way toward satisfying its $550 billion investment in strategic sectors, with approximately $130 billion announced toward nuclear and gas-powered energy projects and an investment into Global Foundries for semiconductor manufacturing. Like Taiwan, Japan's investments are heavily influenced by short-term U.S. interest rates as its investment deal links to a six-month Secured Overnight Financing Rate. Given the remaining $420 billion will likely be spread across different projects over the next two years, and not all announced overnight, this will affect the profitability of future projects. Finally, it was recently announced that South Korea will put upwards of $142 billion toward eight nuclear projects and a natural gas power plant , with an additional $54 billion potentially going to the same Alaska LNG project. Combined, these would nearly satisfy the $200 billion in direct investments it has previously agreed to, with only an additional $150 billion for shipbuilding remaining. The problem for South Korea, and another reason why securing these deals sooner than later has been important, is that the terms of their investment deal link the base rate for their projects to the U.S.'s 20-year Constant Maturity Treasury (CMT) rate. The yield for 20-year Treasury securities, and subsequently the CMT, is quickly approaching a 25-year-high of 6%. Announcing multi-billion-dollar investments and successfully financing them are two different challenges. It's safe to assume that the projects that have been announced so far, most of which are in the energy sector, have the largest sticker value with the greatest project lifespan. Future projects will likely be smaller in total value with greater short-term exposure to issues such as technology developments and capital upgrades. As a part of their respective deals, both Japan and South Korea have agreed to a profit-sharing mechanism with the U.S. South Korea's agreement includes more specific language that deals need to be commercially viable. This is why there has been some hesitancy on its part to commit to the Alaska LNG project. But also why Trump announced the new Taiwan investment will include a 20-year off-take agreement from that project worth $70 billion to $80 billion. Higher rates and yields will ultimately slow the rate of returns for future investments. South Korea's deal allows it to at least discuss with U.S. officials alternative solutions if they believe a project won't recoup its investments within 20 years. But all deals also maintain that the U.S. can still impose tariffs if countries refuse to fully or partially fund a project. The U.S. is seeing an investment boom unlike ever before with equity and portfolio flows at record highs. As U.S. credit conditions tighten, investors will become more selective, increasing competition among projects seeking financing. Finding investors for these government-linked projects has already been difficult. And higher rates will raise the expected returns investors want from new projects. At the end of the day, the Trump administration will get the $1.4 trillion worth of new investments it's been promised. The question now is whether these governments can secure their deals under attractive enough terms that allow them to recover their investments sooner rather than later. title: 西藏那曲发生7.0级地震，十余人死亡
source: 纽约时报中文网 国际纵览

content:
](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/10/23/multimedia/23int-china-tibet-quake-pvlf/23int-china-tibet-quake-pvlf-master1050.jpg)

周五，救援人员在西藏那曲市一个受地震影响的村庄展开救援。该地区海拔较高，预计未来几天将有降雪。 Xinhua, via Associated Press

据中国官方媒体报道，周四，一场7.0级地震袭击了中国西南部的西藏地区，造成至少16人死亡，许多人被迫逃到户外。

根据美国地质调查局的数据，地震发生在当地时间晚上10点33分，震中距离西藏北部城市那曲约190公里。据报道，该地区随后发生了多次余震。据官方媒体报道，地震造成至少54人受伤，300多栋房屋被毁。

中国国家电视台发布的视频画面显示，地震引发地面晃动，数十人纷纷从商店、餐厅和公寓楼中奔跑出来。画面还显示，士兵和救援人员正将水和食物等物资装上军用卡车，沿着狭窄的公路驱车前往受灾地区。

地震导致震中玛如乡周边村庄居民的供水和供电中断。根据2020年的人口普查数据，玛如乡约有7605名居民。

据中国官方通讯社新华社报道，已有1600多名搜救人员被派往那曲市。伤者中有11人受重伤。至少有一名被困在废墟下的被救者已被成功救出。

中国领导人习近平呼吁“全力开展”救援工作，并敦促官员们继续监测该地区的局势和天气。该地区海拔较高，气候寒冷，预计未来几天会有降雪。

那曲距离西藏首府拉萨约480公里。西藏于20世纪50年代被北京吞并，受到严格监控，长期以来一直是藏人抗议活动的发生地，包括自焚事件。长期以来，藏人一直在争取维护独立于占人口多数的汉族的宗教自由和文化身份。

西藏也是中国最欠发达的地区之一，许多地方难以抵达。今年9月，席卷西藏另一地区的[致命洪流](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/26/world/asia/nepal-tibet-floods-wtk.html)在西藏造成至少数十人死亡，在尼泊尔造成1300人死亡。

喜马拉雅地区在不久的过去曾录得强震。2015年尼泊尔发生的7.8级地震造成近9000人死亡。

title: Army Activates Air Defense Guam Battalion Focused on Chinese, North Korean Threats - USNI News
zh_title: 陆军启动关岛防空营重点应对中国和朝鲜威胁 - 美国海军学院新闻
source: 美国海军学会新闻 USNI（军事/海上）（Google新闻聚合）
summary: 美国陆军下士。 2019 年 2 月 6 日，在关岛安德森空军基地的末段高空区域防御 (THAAD) 系统教练机上进行导弹装卸演习时，第 94 陆军防空与导弹防御司令部鹰爪特遣队的爱国者发射站增强型操作员兼维护员罗赫利奥·阿尔格塔 (Rogelio Argueta) 下达命令。 美国陆军照片 美国陆军最近启动了一个驻关岛防空营，旨在保护该岛免受中国和朝鲜日益严重的空中和导弹威胁。第43防空炮兵团第3营，活跃
content:
美国陆军下士。 2019 年 2 月 6 日，关岛安德森空军基地，第 94 陆军防空与导弹防御司令部“爪子”特遣部队的爱国者发射站增强型操作员兼维护员罗赫利奥·阿格塔 (Rogelio Argueta) 在末段高空区域防御 (THAAD) 系统教练机上进行导弹装卸演习时发出命令。美国陆军照片

美国陆军最近在关岛部署了一个防空营，旨在保护该岛免受中国和朝鲜日益先进的空中和导弹威胁。

10月16日组建的第43防空炮兵团第3营将继承“黑爪”特遣部队的关岛防御职责。上一次陆军轮换任务始于 2013 年，旨在应对潜在的朝鲜弹道导弹威胁。

近年来，随着中国人民解放军火箭军的崛起，该任务的重点已扩大到在潜在冲突中抵御中国导弹的攻击。 [五角大楼于 2023 年启动关岛防御系统计划](https://news.usni.org/2023/05/10/pentagon-starts-work-to-build-ballistic-missile-defense-capability-in-guam)满足击败北京的弹道、巡航和高超音速武器所需的要求罢工[.](https://news.usni.org/2023/05/10/pentagon-starts-work-to-build-ballistic-missile-defense-capability-in-guam)
陆军在该营启动的新闻稿中写道：“关岛的战略位置使其成为美国在整个地区军事行动的重要组成部分，支持联合部队行动，同时使防空和导弹防御成为保护支持这些任务所需的部队和基础设施的关键部分。”

2026 年 10 月 16 日，隶属第 94 陆军防空与导弹防御司令部第 43 防空炮兵团、第 38 防空炮兵旅第 3 营的美国陆军士兵参加在关岛安德森空军基地举行的启动仪式。美国陆军照片

随着印太对手远程精确打击能力的增强，地面部队着眼于在关岛加强态势。 3-43 ADA 将运行爱国者、末段高空区域防御和新的中级火力防护能力系统，[_星条旗报_于 8 月报道_。](https://www.stripes.com/theaters/asia_pacific/2026-08-21/guam-defense-patriot-ifpc-systems-22615488.html) 与传统的爱国者和萨德系统相比，IFPC 将提供针对飞机、导弹和无人机的中短程防御。

组合后，这些系统提供了一个分层网络，可以应对潜在的西太平洋冲突中可能出现的各种空中和导弹威胁。
“士兵们开发了连接传感器、指挥和控制系统、发射器和拦截器所需的新程序、关系和集成，以促进统一的防御架构。3-43 ADA 现在支持陆军对关岛战略防御系统的贡献是再合适不过了，”3-43 ADA BN 指挥官约书亚·乌内斯中校在新闻稿中说。

据陆军称，从特遣部队到营的过渡标志着国防部“在印度-太平洋地区建立永久防空能力”的承诺。

2025 年 12 月 16 日，在关岛安德森空军基地举行的指挥变更仪式上，分配到“利爪”特遣部队的美国陆军士兵列队。美国陆军照片

关岛目前的防空系统由六座陆军“萨德”发射装置和美国海军“宙斯盾梳”组成

【原文 English Original】
U.S. Army Cpl. Rogelio Argueta, Patriot Launching Station Enhanced Operator-Maintainer, assigned with Task Force Talon, 94th Army Air and Missile Defense Command gives commands, during a practice missile reload and unload drills on a Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) system trainer at Andersen Air Force Base, Guam, Feb. 6, 2019. US Army photo

The U.S. Army’s recently activated a Guam-based air defense battalion meant to protect the island from increasingly advanced air and missile threats fielded by China and North Korea.

The 3rd Battalion, 43rd Air Defense Artillery Regiment, activated on Oct. 16, will inherit the defense of Guam responsibilities of Task Force Talon. The previous Army rotational mission began in 2013 to counter potential North Korean ballistic missile threats.

With the rise of the People’s Liberation Army Rocket Force in recent years, the mission has expanded its focus to defend against a barrage of Chinese missiles in a potential conflict. T[he Pentagon initiated plans for the Guam Defense System in 2023 t](https://news.usni.org/2023/05/10/pentagon-starts-work-to-build-ballistic-missile-defense-capability-in-guam)o meet the requirements needed to defeat Beijing’s ballistic, cruise and hypersonic strikes[.](https://news.usni.org/2023/05/10/pentagon-starts-work-to-build-ballistic-missile-defense-capability-in-guam)

“Guam’s strategic location makes it an important part of U.S. military operations throughout the region by supporting joint force operations while making air and missile defense a critical part of protecting the forces and infrastructure needed to support those missions,” reads the Army release on the battalion’s activation.

U.S. Army soldiers assigned to 3rd Battalion, 43rd Air Defense Artillery Regiment, 38th Air Defense Artillery Brigade, 94th Army Air and Missile Defense Command, participate in an activation ceremony on Andersen Air Force Base, Guam, Oct. 16, 2026. US Army photo

The ground branch has eyed a reinforced posture on Guam with the increase of Indo-Pacific adversaries’ long-range precision strike capabilities. The 3-43 ADA will operate Patriot, Terminal High Altitude Area Defense and new Intermediate Fires Protection Capability systems, [_Stars and Stripes reported_ in August.](https://www.stripes.com/theaters/asia_pacific/2026-08-21/guam-defense-patriot-ifpc-systems-22615488.html) Compared to the legacy Patriot and THAAD systems, IFPC will provide medium- to short-range defense against aircraft, missiles and drones.

When combined, the systems provide a layered network to engage a variety of air and missile threats that could be fielded in a potential Western Pacific conflict.

“The soldiers developed new procedures, relationships and integration required to connect sensors, command and control systems, launchers and interceptors to promote a unified defensive architecture. It’s only fitting that 3-43 ADA now stands up the Army’s contribution to the strategic Guam Defense System,” Lt. Col. Joshua Urness, 3-43 ADA BN commander, said in the release.

According to the Army, the transition from task force to battalion signals the Defense Department’s commitment “toward permanent air defense capabilities in the Indo-Pacific.”

U.S. Army soldiers assigned to Task Force Talon stand in formation during a change of command ceremony at Andersen Air Force Base, Guam, Dec. 16, 2025. US Army photo

Guam’s current air defenses are composed of six Army THAAD launchers and U.S. Navy Aegis Combat System warships assigned to its defense on an as-need basis. Future plans aim to integrate a networked system capable of conducting 360-degree detection and interception of air and missile threats.

Since Task Force Talon’s original mission over a decade ago, the complexity and quantity of Indo-Pacific missile threats has only increased. Today, the People’s Liberation Army Navy is in the [process of fielding](https://news.usni.org/2026/03/05/chinese-navy-expanding-nuclear-attack-boat-fleet-and-missile-strike-capabilities-oni-commander-says) more nuclear attack boats equipped with vertical launching systems. [The Pentagon has also said it expects the PLAN to have a nine carrier strike group force by 2035,](https://news.usni.org/2025/12/24/china-wants-nine-aircraft-carriers-by-2035-says-new-pentagon-report) which will expand Beijing’s blue water projection capabilities.

title: Rwanda: Kagame Defends Strict Dress Codes Amid Rwanda's Dressing Controversy
summary: Rwandan President Paul Kagame has defended cultural expectations on dressing, arguing that societies have their own standards of acceptable behaviour which should not be abandoned simply because other countries embrace different ways of lif
content:
Rwandan President Paul Kagame has defended cultural expectations on dressing, arguing that societies have their own standards of acceptable behaviour which should not be abandoned simply because other countries embrace different ways of life.

Speaking on Thursday while addressing more than 10,000 young Rwandans at BK Arena in Kigali during the "Meet The President" session, Kagame said dress codes should be understood within the context of the places people visit and the values of the society in which they live.

"If you are going to the beach, by the water, where people go to relax, there is a certain way you can dress and behave that may be different from other places. That is perfectly acceptable. But imagine someone coming here dressed as though they were at the beach. Would that work? Wouldn't you all turn around and wonder, what happened to this person?" Kagame asked.

His remarks come amid a growing debate in Rwanda over restrictions on women's dressing, following incidents in which women have faced scrutiny over their clothing in public spaces.

The debate intensified after a video circulated showing police officers forcefully handcuffing a young woman wearing a miniskirt at a bus park in Rubavu.

The Rwanda National Police subsequently cleared the woman of wrongdoing and detained the officers involved pending disciplinary review.

The incident also drew criticism from human rights advocates and public commentators, who argued that cultural values should not be used to justify police intimidation, harassment or arbitrary enforcement of dress standards against women.

Addressing the wider debate, Kagame said the expectations should apply to men as well, arguing that discussions about dressing are often unfairly directed at women.

"By the way, this is not just about women. Most of the time, these things are made to be about women, but the same applies to men. Even now, imagine we are sitting here, and a man suddenly walks in, as though he has just come from the gym, wearing shorts, with nothing on his upper body, and comes to sit among us. People would ask, what happened to this person? Did he forget where he was going?" he said.

Kagame argued that societies should be allowed to maintain their own social standards rather than adopt practices from other countries without considering whether they fit local values.

He said people's willingness to participate in a particular social setting could also depend on the expectations established by those organising it.

"Now, if we had all agreed to come dressed that way, then perhaps that is how it would be. But some people would not come. Isn't that so? Some would simply decide not to attend, saying, we are not going to be part of that," he said.

The Rwandan leader said communities have ways of regulating behaviour through shared expectations and self-regulation, adding that practices accepted elsewhere should not automatically be embraced by Rwandans.

"There is a way society regulates itself, including through self-regulation. But when you simply say, we have seen this elsewhere, so let us do the same here, and you bring it into our society, society may tell you, we have not reached that point yet. Perhaps we were moving in that direction, but we are not there yet," Kagame said.

He called for disagreements over cultural values to be handled through dialogue rather than hostility, saying people should be able to reach an understanding when differences emerge.

"That should not create any hostility. There should be a way of regulating these things so that people can come to an understanding," he said.

Kagame compared society's response to unfamiliar practices to the body's reaction to a foreign object, which it gradually attempts to remove.

"It is like a foreign body. I think those of you in the medical profession know this. When a foreign object, a fragment of something, enters the body, the body tends to reject it. It keeps pushing it out. Even when a thorn gets stuck in your skin, if you leave it there for some time, it begins to work its way out. Eventually, you find it near the surface and remove it. Society works in much the same way," he said.

He added that tensions can arise when individuals seek to introduce practices that conflict with the established values of a community, while other members of that society resist the changes.

"A healthy society, with its own way of functioning, when something unfamiliar is introduced into it, gradually, little by little, that society begins to push it away. There is then a struggle between someone trying to change society to fit something they have brought from elsewhere, and society itself saying, do not bring these things here, and pushing that person away. But there should be no conflict. That is how these things should work," Kagame said.

He urged young people to reflect on the values they want for themselves and the direction in which they want their society to develop.

"Young people like you should keep these things in mind. Think about them. Understand what it is that you want for yourselves," he said.

Kagame also called for open discussions about changing social norms, urging young Rwandans to question practices that are becoming more common but which they consider inconsistent with their culture or harmful to society.

"Even here, in our discussions, people should be able to raise these questions and say, there are things we have seen becoming increasingly accepted in our society, yet they are not part of our culture. They do not even bring us any benefit. Why should we accept them, especially when they are things that harm people? Why?" he asked.

title: Nigeria Vs North Korea - Five Players Who Could Decide World Cup Showdown
summary: With North Korea's attacking firepower posing a serious threat, Nigeria will have to be disciplined at the back while making their own opportunities count. Nigeria's Flamingos face a major test of their ambitions at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women
content:
With North Korea's attacking firepower posing a serious threat, Nigeria will have to be disciplined at the back while making their own opportunities count.

Nigeria's Flamingos face a major test of their ambitions at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup when they meet defending champions North Korea in their final Group B fixture on Friday, with a place in the knockout stage at stake.

Head coach Akeem Busari's side must find a way to contain an opponent that has scored 12 goals in its opening two matches, dismantling Puerto Rico 6-0 before producing an even more emphatic 6-1 victory over Poland.

Nigeria, meanwhile, bounced back from their opening 2-1 defeat to Poland with a 2-0 win over Puerto Rico, courtesy of goals from Oluwakemi Adegbuyi and Precious Oscar. That victory has kept the Flamingos in contention, but they will need another strong performance to overcome one of the tournament's most dangerous teams.

With North Korea's attacking firepower posing a serious threat, Nigeria will have to be disciplined at the back while making their own opportunities count. Individual brilliance could prove decisive, making the contributions of these five players particularly important when the teams meet at the Mohammed VI Football Complex in Rabat.

**Yu Jong-hyang - North Korea**

If Nigeria need a reminder of the threat posed by North Korea's attack, Yu Jong-hyang's performances in the opening two fixtures provide it.

Like Kim, Yu has scored four goals, registering two against Puerto Rico and another brace against Poland. Her ability to find the net in consecutive matches makes her one of the leading attacking threats the Flamingos must contain.

Yu also enters the contest with an impressive reputation from the previous edition of the competition, where she won the Golden Ball and Golden Boot at the 2025 FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup.

That pedigree, combined with her current form, makes her a player Nigeria cannot afford to overlook. She has demonstrated the ability to convert opportunities and influence matches, while her movement and composure in front of goal make her particularly dangerous when opponents allow her time to turn or attack space.

For Busari's side, the challenge will be to deny Yu the service she needs and ensure that North Korea's attacking players do not repeatedly find themselves in one-on-one situations around the Nigerian penalty area.

With four goals already to her name, Yu will be eager to continue her scoring run, and Nigeria's defensive organisation could determine how much influence she has on the contest.

**Oluwakemi Adegbuyi - Nigeria**

For Nigeria, Oluwakemi Adegbuyi is one of the players who could make a significant difference as the Flamingos attempt to upset the defending champions and strengthen their chances of reaching the knockout stage.

The Robo Queens forward provided an important response to Nigeria's opening defeat to Poland, scoring the first goal in the 2-0 victory over Puerto Rico on 20 October.

Adegbuyi struck in the 25th minute to give the Flamingos the lead before Precious Oscar sealed the result in stoppage time. Her performance earned her the Player of the Match award, recognising her contribution to a victory that restored confidence within the Nigerian camp.

Her goal was important not only because it put Nigeria ahead but also because it helped ease the pressure on a team that needed a positive result to keep its qualification hopes alive.

Against North Korea, Adegbuyi's ability to take chances will be particularly important. The Asian champions have conceded just once in their first two matches, meaning Nigeria may not enjoy the same number of clear opportunities they had against Puerto Rico.

The Flamingos will need their forwards to be sharp when openings emerge, and Adegbuyi could be central to that effort. Her confidence after scoring in the previous match should provide encouragement as Nigeria prepare for a much more demanding defensive challenge.

If the Nigerian attack can find ways to exploit spaces behind North Korea's defence, Adegbuyi's movement and finishing could offer Busari's side a route to goal.

**Kim Won-sim - North Korea**

With four goals in the team's opening two matches, Kim Won-sim has emerged as one of North Korea's most dangerous attacking weapons at the tournament.

The forward announced herself with a brace in the 6-0 demolition of Puerto Rico before repeating the feat against Poland, underlining her ability to deliver consistently against different opponents.

Her finishing has been a major part of North Korea's impressive start, and the Flamingos cannot afford to give her the freedom to operate in dangerous areas around the penalty box.

Kim's movement and eye for goal will demand constant attention from Nigeria's defenders, who must remain compact and prevent the forward from receiving possession in positions where she can punish even the smallest defensive lapse.

For the Flamingos, limiting Kim's influence could be one of the most important assignments of the evening. Allowing her to settle into the game would give North Korea another avenue to extend their remarkable scoring run.

**Precious Oscar - Nigeria**

Precious Oscar completes the list after delivering a crucial contribution off the bench in Nigeria's victory over Puerto Rico.

The forward scored the Flamingos' second goal in stoppage time, putting the result beyond doubt and ensuring Nigeria collected their first three points of the tournament.

Her late strike demonstrated the importance of maintaining attacking intensity until the final whistle, particularly in a competition where goal difference and qualification permutations could become decisive.

Oscar's contribution also gives Nigeria another attacking option to consider against North Korea. Whether she starts or is introduced during the match, her ability to make an impact in the final third could be valuable in a fixture where the Flamingos may need to take advantage of limited opportunities.

The challenge for Nigeria will be to create enough openings to bring their attacking players into dangerous positions. Against a North Korean side that has scored freely and conceded only once, the Flamingos cannot afford to waste chances.

Oscar will be hoping to build on her goal against Puerto Rico and provide another important contribution as Nigeria pursue a place in the knockout rounds.

Her previous impact also offers Busari an option if the game requires fresh attacking energy in the second half, particularly if Nigeria are chasing a goal or need to change the rhythm of the contest.

**Ri Ye-rim - North Korea**

While much of the attention has centred on Kim and Yu, Ri Ye-rim is another North Korean attacker who deserves close monitoring after her performances in the group stage.

Ri scored in the 6-0 victory over Puerto Rico and found the net again against Poland, demonstrating that North Korea's threat extends well beyond their two leading scorers.

Her contribution is particularly significant for Nigeria because it highlights the difficulty of preparing to face an attack with several players capable of delivering goals. Concentrating exclusively on Kim and Yu could leave other members of the North Korean forward line with the space to make the difference.

Ri's involvement in the scoring against both opponents also reflects the attacking depth that has helped the defending champions record 12 goals in two games.

Nigeria's defenders and midfielders must therefore remain alert to runners arriving from different areas of the pitch rather than allowing their attention to become fixed on the most prominent names.

If Ri receives the freedom to attack the penalty area, she could become another major problem for the Flamingos. Her performances so far make her a genuine threat as North Korea look to complete the group stage with another victory.

**A defining test for the Flamingos**

Friday's meeting is more than just another group-stage fixture for Nigeria. With qualification at stake, the Flamingos must produce a disciplined performance against a North Korean side that has looked formidable in front of goal.

Kim Won-sim and Yu Jong-hyang headline the defending champions' attacking threat, while Ri Ye-rim's contribution underlines the depth of their forward line. Nigeria will need to be alert across the pitch to prevent North Korea from dictating the contest.

At the other end, Adegbuyi and Oscar have already shown that they can make decisive contributions, and the Flamingos will need their attacking players to deliver again if they are to challenge the champions.

Busari's team have demonstrated resilience by recovering from their defeat to Poland, but the next step is to prove they can compete with the strongest sides in the tournament.

For Nigeria, the formula is clear: defend with discipline, remain composed under pressure and take the chances that come their way. If the Flamingos can execute that plan, they have an opportunity to turn a difficult assignment into a defining moment in their World Cup campaign.

title: Africa: All of Africa Today - October 23, 2026
summary: **Tanzania Opposition Official Charged With Treason** A senior official of Tanzania's main opposition party, Chadema, John Pambalu, has been charged with[treason](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-22/tanzanian-opposition-leade
content:
**Tanzania Opposition Official Charged With Treason**

A senior official of Tanzania's main opposition party, Chadema, John Pambalu, has been charged with[treason](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-22/tanzanian-opposition-leader-charged-with-treason-over-protests "https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-22/tanzanian-opposition-leader-charged-with-treason-over-protests"), an offence that carries a potential death penalty. Pambalu, a member of the party's national council and former youth wing leader, is accused of seeking to disrupt the 2025 general election through protests intended to intimidate the government. He is the second senior Chadema figure to face treason charges after party leader Tundu Lissu. The charges come amid a wider crackdown on government critics following the October 2025 elections, which President Samia Suluhu Hassan officially won with 98% of the vote. Opposition groups and rights organisations say about 2,000 people were killed during the subsequent protests. A government-initiated inquiry put the death toll at 518. Chadema was excluded from the election, and party officials have vowed to continue challenging the government.

**Immigrant Beaten to Death in Durban, South Africa**

Follow us on [WhatsApp](https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K "https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K") | [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/ "https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/") for the latest headlines

A foreign national has been beaten to[death](https://allafrica.com/stories/202610230062.html)by a crowd of about 50 people in Durban, prompting a police investigation amid growing anti-immigrant tensions in South Africa. Police said the unidentified man was believed to be in his late 30s or early 40s. He was first approached by two men by the roadside before being assaulted by a larger group. He was pronounced dead at the scene. The motive remains unclear. The killing follows a series of anti-immigrant protests that have turned violent in parts of the country, with shops and vehicles set alight in Durban and Soweto. Several African countries, including Nigeria, Ghana and Zimbabwe, have expressed concern over attacks on their citizens, with some arranging repatriations. South Africa has experienced xenophobic violence for nearly two decades, including deadly attacks in 2008 that killed more than 60 people. The unrest is unfolding amid widespread unemployment, poverty and inequality. Researchers said broad claims that migrants cause crime and job losses are not supported by evidence.

**Malawi Opposition Demands Answers Over President's Absence**

Malawi's opposition Malawi Congress Party has demanded[answers](https://allafrica.com/stories/202610230090.html)over President Peter Mutharika's prolonged absence from the country while the nation faces fuel shortages, medicine scarcity and rising living costs. Campaign director Moses Kunkuyu said the concern was not the president's private trip abroad but the government's failure to communicate clearly about who was leading the country and responding to the crises. Motorists are spending hours waiting for fuel, while patients struggle to access essential medicines. The opposition also criticised Vice-President Jane Ansah for remaining silent, urging her to reassure citizens that the government is functioning and has a plan to address the shortages. The criticism comes as economic hardship deepens and public frustration grows over the lack of clear communication and action from the authorities.

**Ruto Urges Africa to Finance Its Own Growth**

Kenyan President William Ruto has[urged](https://allafrica.com/stories/202610230092.html)African governments to strengthen and rely more on the continent's financial institutions to fund development. He said that Africa must take greater responsibility for its economic future. Speaking at the 25th Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) summit in Harare, Zimbabwe, Ruto said Africa holds more than US$4 trillion in domestic financial assets, much of which remains in foreign accounts while local projects struggle to secure funding. He called on governments to invest their reserves in African institutions, support their bonds and guarantees, and channel more development projects through them. Ruto also urged countries to deepen regional trade, remove trade barriers and build stronger value chains as global protectionism increases. He cited Kenya's investment in African financial institutions and said a planned US$16 billion East African refinery in Kenya would be financed almost entirely by African institutions. Ruto handed over COMESA's chairmanship to Zimbabwean President Emmerson Mnangagwa, stressing that regional integration must deliver tangible benefits for citizens.

**Africa CDC Warns No Country Is Safe as Ebola Spreads to Nigeria**

The Ebola outbreak[caused](https://allafrica.com/stories/202610230018.html)by the Bundibugyo virus has killed 4,690 people and remains uncontrolled, with Nigeria reporting its first case in more than a decade, according to Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention director-general Jean Kaseya. The outbreak, which began in the Democratic Republic of Congo in May, has recorded 9,735 confirmed cases, with eight provinces in the country affected and an estimated 65 to 70 new cases reported daily. The Nigerian patient, a woman who arrived in Abuja on October 3, was diagnosed 16 days later, raising concerns about possible exposure to numerous contacts. The World Health Organization said 44 contacts had been identified and were being monitored, while authorities investigate where she contracted the virus. Kaseya stressed the need for stronger surveillance in hospitals, health facilities and across borders, amid conflicting accounts from Nigerian and Ugandan officials about the woman's travel history. There is currently no approved vaccine or specific treatment for the Bundibugyo virus. Kaseya also defended calls for greater transparency in the management of international Ebola response funding, saying governments need clear information about resources entering their countries.

#### Sign up for free AllAfrica Newsletters

Get the latest in African news delivered straight to your inbox

**Mali Army, Russian-Linked Forces Accused of Civilian Abuses**

Human Rights Watch has [accused](https://allafrica.com/stories/202610230063.html)Mali's armed forces and Russia-controlled Africa Corps of committing serious abuses against civilians in the central Mopti region during renewed fighting. The organisation said an apparent military drone strike on September 16 killed eight civilians and injured at least six others in Guélédié village. Witnesses reported that the strike hit an area where residents had gathered to access satellite internet, although armed fighters linked to al-Qaeda were reportedly present in the village. Human Rights Watch also documented alleged torture and inhumane detention at a military base in Sévaré between May and August, where civilians were reportedly held in overcrowded shipping containers without adequate food, water, sanitation or medical care. Former detainees described severe beatings, electric shocks and waterboarding, and alleged that several prisoners died while in custody. The Malian military said its September operation targeted suspected militants and destroyed their equipment. Human Rights Watch called for credible investigations and accountability, warning that attacks on civilians, torture and denial of medical care may constitute violations of international humanitarian law and, in some cases, war crimes.

title: East Africa: Ruto Hands Comesa Chairmanship to Mnangagwa
summary: Nairobi — Africa must take greater responsibility for financing its development by strengthening its own financial institutions, President William Ruto has said. The President urged African States to show confidence in African institutions,
content:
Nairobi — Africa must take greater responsibility for financing its development by strengthening its own financial institutions, President William Ruto has said.

The President urged African States to show confidence in African institutions, saying they have already demonstrated their capacity by financing Africa's trade, insuring the continent's risks and standing with African States when others stepped back.

He called on African governments to place more of their reserves with African institutions, channel development projects through them and back their bonds and guarantees.

Through the Alliance of African Multilateral Financial Institutions, he explained, African institutions can now pool their strength and act on a continental scale.

Follow us on [WhatsApp](https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K "https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K") | [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/ "https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/") for the latest headlines

"We cannot ask the world to trust African institutions if we do not trust them ourselves. Africa holds more than $4 trillion in domestic financial assets. Yet much of these sit in foreign accounts, earning little while our own projects wait for capital," he said.

President Ruto made the remarks on Thursday during the 25th Summit of the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) Heads of State and Government held at the New Parliament Building in Harare, Zimbabwe.

Zambian President Hakainde Hichilema, COMESA Secretary-General Chileshe Mpundu Kapwepwe and AfCFTA Secretary-General Wamkele Mene were among those present.

Kenya, President Ruto pointed out, has increased shareholding in Afreximbank, the Africa Finance Corporation and African Trade and Investment Development Insurance (ATIDI).

"Just for your information, the $16 billion East Africa refinery that will be built in Kenya will be almost wholly funded by African financial institutions. That is the scale of the resources that we have," he said.

He noted that Africa cannot be ambitious in its plans and timid in financing them.

"Every programme we agree upon must be matched by the resources to deliver it. Otherwise, our communiqués will promise what our budgets cannot pay for," he said.

At the summit, President Ruto handed over the chairmanship of COMESA to Zimbabwean President Emmerson Mnangagwa.

He expressed confidence in President Mnangagwa's leadership to take COMESA forward.

"Under his stewardship, and with the support of every Member State, I trust that we will turn the ambition of One Market, One Future into progress our people can see and feel," he said.

The President said he was proud of the progress made during Kenya's chairmanship, including stronger economic growth, increased intra-regional trade and deeper digital integration.

"When we assumed the Chair, we set one priority: Leveraging digitalisation to deepen regional value chains for sustainable and inclusive growth. Today, that priority is a programme, not a slogan," he said.

As the outgoing chairperson, President Ruto also presented and launched the COMESA 2026-2030 Medium-Term Strategic Plan and the 2025 Annual Report.

The report, he said, outlines the need to accelerate intra-African trade, eliminate non-tariff barriers, improve connectivity and ensure the benefits of integration reach every segment of society.

He noted that as the global order shifts and protectionism rises, Africa's response must be deeper regional integration, stronger value chains and increased trade among African States.

He pointed out that the greatest market for Africa's goods is Africa.

"Regional integration is no longer a dream we discuss. It is an economic and strategic necessity. We must trade more among ourselves, build resilient regional value chains and deepen our productive capacity so that we can withstand the next shock and seize the next opportunity," he said.

The President, therefore, called on the COMESA Secretariat to fast-track the COMESA Market Levy to secure sustainable and predictable financing for regional priorities.

He explained that integration should be measured not by the volume of trade or the strength of institutions alone but by the opportunities created for citizens of the continent.

The President also said Africa seeks a new engagement with its partners, rooted in sovereign equality, built on mutual benefit and measured by shared prosperity.

President Ruto reiterated that the era of extracting Africa's natural resources without corresponding benefits for the continent must give way to mutually beneficial partnerships.

"To every partner who seeks our minerals, our markets and our young workforce, our offer is clear: Invest with us, process with us, build with us. We will be fair in our partnerships, firm in our interests, open in our markets, and reliable in our word," he said.

#### Sign up for free AllAfrica Newsletters

Get the latest in African news delivered straight to your inbox

He added: "Africa does not come asking for a seat at the edge of the table. We come to help set it."

On his part, President Mnangagwa commended President Ruto for his steadfast leadership during his tenure, steering COMESA with purpose and clarity, particularly in digitalisation and regional value chains.

He called on the summit to advance practical and sustainable solutions that will strengthen resilience, reposition the region to better navigate global shocks and promote the prosperity of the continent.

"With unity of purpose, let us deliver on the promise of shared prosperity, a better life and a better future for the people of Africa," he said.

President Hichilema called on African nations to walk the talk on integration by unlocking the continent's resources for the benefit of its people and the vast African market.

He said that Africans are responsible for developing Africa, noting that others will follow if citizens take the lead.

"We are all saying the right things. We must now take the extra steps to realise this vision. And nobody will do it other than ourselves," he said.
