On the surface, these are routine Party meetings. Yet the appointments also offer a glimpse of shifts within the CCP’s political establishment ahead of its 21st National Congress in 2027.

## Aging trend emerges among CCP officials

Provincial reshuffles are widely seen as an early stage in determining the personnel lineup for the next CCP Central Committee. An [analysis](https://x.com/cnpoliwatch?utm_source=chatgpt.com) posted on X on Oct. 19 by the account “China Personnel Watch” suggests that younger generations are making up a smaller share of provincial Party standing committees.

The account cited 117 officials born in the 1960s, or 29.1 percent of provincial standing committee appointments, after the 2011–2012 reshuffle. By comparison, 68 officials born in the 1970s accounted for 17.3 percent following the 2021–2022 reshuffle. The figures were attributed to [Caixin reports published](https://china.caixin.com/2022-07-01/101907145.html) on [July 4, 2012](https://opinion.caixin.com/2012-07-04/100407151.html), and July 1, 2022.

“This is the clearest manifestation of the aging of leading officials in provincial-level personnel appointments,” China Personnel Watch argued, predicting that officials born after 1975 could be even less represented in the 2026–2027 round. Because the comparison examines different birth cohorts at different points in time, however, it does not by itself establish an increase in the overall average age.

The account said the previous reshuffle produced 392 provincial standing committee appointments. Of these, 68 involved officials born in the 1970s, averaging about 2.2 per province. Two became provincial Party deputy secretaries: Zhuge Yujie and Shi Guanghui. Four other standing committee members were born in or after 1975: Ren Wei, Zhang Hongwen, Zhang Xiaoqiang and Yilizati Ahmaitijiang.

Ren Wei, born in May 1976, was the youngest member of a provincial Party standing committee following that reshuffle. He served in Tibet’s regional leadership and turned 50 this year.

A new appointment in Anhui has now changed that distinction. He Chunkuan, the province’s vice governor and Xuancheng Party secretary, was [elected to Anhui’s provincial Party standing committee on Oct. 23](https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_34316372). Born in October 1977, He is 49 and is now the youngest provincial standing committee member, [according to Caixin](https://china.caixin.com/2026-10-23/102496587.html).

China Personnel Watch calculated that the previous round’s 392 appointments involved officials born, on average, in August 1966, with an average age of 55.6 at the time. Qinghai had the youngest provincial standing committee, averaging 53.9 years, and Henan the oldest, at 56.7.

All 31 provincial-level regions had at least one standing committee member born in the 1970s. Beijing and Shanghai had five each, while Tibet had four, the account said. Whether the current reshuffle brings more officials born after 1975—or any born in the 1980s—into those ranks remains an open question.

## Xinjiang’s leadership raises questions about retirement conventions

[Xinjiang’s regional Party congress](https://www.xinjiang.gov.cn/xinjiang/xjyw/202610/1680f492076a4df1bbd99af31c7ee73b.shtml) opened in Urumqi on Oct. 19, with Party Secretary Chen Xiaojiang delivering the work report and regional Chairman Erkin Tuniyaz presiding. The meeting was scheduled to conclude on Oct. 23.

China Personnel Watch noted that Chen and Erkin, both 64, are older than the 63-year threshold the account described as a customary benchmark for nomination to provincial Party secretary or governor. Under earlier conventions, officials of their ages might have been expected to retire during the transition. Whether those conventions will be applied in Xinjiang remains unclear.

The account suggested that Chen’s continued service could strengthen his chances of entering the Politburo after the 21st National Congress. That assessment is speculative; no such appointment has been announced.

The post also discussed Erkin’s potential future role in the National People’s Congress (NPC) and the possible retirement of Shohrat Zakir, the Uyghur vice chairman of the NPC Standing Committee. Zakir, born in August 1953, stepped down as Xinjiang’s regional chairman before the 2021 reshuffle and became an NPC Standing Committee vice chairman in March 2023.

One X user criticized the flexibility of retirement norms: “The ‘age limit’ has become a stretchable rubber band.” The user argued that without predictable rules for leaving office, officials’ careers remain subject to the distribution of power rather than transparent succession.

Xi himself turned 73 this year. In 2018, China removed the two-term constitutional limit on the presidency; in 2022, Xi secured a third term as CCP general secretary. His continued tenure, along with repeated anti-corruption campaigns, has fueled debate among analysts about leadership succession and divisions within the Party.

## State media calls for closer scrutiny of younger officials

CCP state media have meanwhile raised concerns about the conduct of younger cadres. A Sept. 2 [People’s Daily commentary](https://paper.people.com.cn/rmrb/pc/content/202609/02/content_30178539.html) criticized some for seeking quick results, avoiding difficult assignments and pursuing conspicuous achievements. It described the underlying problem as a distorted view of political performance.

On Oct. 15, the Party’s theoretical journal [Qiushi published Xi’s article](https://www.moe.gov.cn/jyb_xwfb/moe_176/202610/t20261015_1454274.html), “Advancing Full and Rigorous Party Self-Governance with Higher Standards and More Substantive Measures,” drawn from his Jan. 12 address to the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection.

“Regardless of who they are, how high their position is, or how great their contributions have been, anyone who engages in corruption will be shown no leniency,” Xi said in the published remarks. He called for intensified investigations of corruption involving senior leaders and younger cadres, among others.

Xi also warned against “two-faced” officials who profess loyalty while acting otherwise. During leadership transitions, he said, such officials must not be allowed to pass the vetting process.

Political commentator Yu Ming argued that an aging CCP leadership could generate dissatisfaction among younger officials. He interpreted the warnings issued amid provincial reshuffles as a sign of intensifying factional struggles within the Party. That interpretation remains an assessment rather than an established account of internal events.

Independent commentator Du Zheng, writing for Taiwan’s [Up Media](https://www.upmedia.mg/tw/commentary/china-hong-kong-insights/257600?utm_source=chatgpt.com), offered a related argument. He said relatively young senior officials had grown up outside the Cultural Revolution, lived through the reform era and had access to information beyond official Party channels, including material about the 1989 Tiananmen crackdown.

Du pointed to disciplinary accusations that officials had “improperly discussed the central leadership” as evidence, in his view, that Xi does not command unquestioning loyalty throughout the Party. He argued that some officials privately consult publications the CCP considers politically unacceptable, despite restrictions on such material.

Du concluded that a future leader would have to dismantle what he characterized as the CCP’s “evil and corrupt” system. He also suggested that Xi could preside over the Party’s final generation.

title: Xiplomacy: Reading Xi's vision for global governance through metaphors
summary: BEIJING, Oct. 23 (Xinhua) -- The 2026 Global Governance Forum (Xiong'an) is set to open on Friday in the Xiong'an New Area, north China's Hebei Province, bringing into world focus a pressing question: How can countries work together to addr
content:
BEIJING, Oct. 23 (Xinhua) -- The 2026 Global Governance Forum (Xiong'an) is set to open on Friday in the Xiong'an New Area, north China's Hebei Province, bringing into world focus a pressing question: How can countries work together to address shared challenges in an interconnected world amid growing protectionism and unilateralism?

In speeches and meetings on multiple occasions, Chinese President Xi Jinping has used vivid metaphors to articulate his vision for global governance. These metaphors offer insights into his approach to building a more just, equitable and inclusive global governance system.

IN SAME BOAT

"I was looking at the vast ocean when I boarded the ship, and it struck me that we are all indeed fellow passengers in the same boat," Xi said while addressing the 2018 APEC CEO Summit hosted at a unique setting -- onboard the giant cruise Pacific Explorer in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea.

The metaphor embodies the essence of Xi's vision of building a community with a shared future for humanity, highlighting the interconnectedness of countries and the need for solidarity and cooperation in addressing common challenges.

Today, the interconnected world is grappling with four mounting deficits: a peace deficit that exacerbates geopolitical conflicts, a development deficit that widens the North-South divide, a security deficit that erodes mutual trust, and a governance deficit that undermines the effectiveness of multilateralism.

In 2019, at the China-France Global Governance Forum held in Paris, Xi proposed a four-pronged approach to addressing the four deficits. First and foremost, he called for fairness and reasonableness to address the governance deficit.

"It is advisable to uphold a vision of global governance featuring extensive consultation and joint contribution for shared benefits," Xi said, calling for actively advancing the democratization of global governance rules.

As the world has found itself in a new period of turbulence and transformation, global governance has come to a new crossroads. Against this backdrop, Xi put forward the Global Governance Initiative (GGI) at the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) summit in September 2025 in China's coastal city of Tianjin.

"I look forward to working with all countries for a more just and equitable global governance system and advancing toward a community with a shared future for humanity," Xi said, stressing sovereign equality and genuine multilateralism.

TRAFFIC LIGHTS

"A world without rules is like a crossroads without traffic lights, where chaos and disorder are all but guaranteed," Xi said at the 2026 BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India.

This metaphor highlights the importance of rules in maintaining the international order. While having rules in place matters, how they are made and who gets to make them matter even more.

International rules must be written and upheld jointly by all countries based on the purposes and principles of the UN Charter, rather than dictated by those with the strongest muscles or the loudest voice, Xi once stressed.

He has also called for the purposes and principles of the UN Charter and other universally recognized basic norms of international relations to be observed comprehensively, fully and in their entirety.

"There should be no double standards, and the house rules of a few countries must not be imposed upon others," he said.

The GGI proposed by President Xi reflects the objective transformation of the world system and responds to the aspirations of most countries for a fairer and more representative system of global governance, said Rahmon Ulmasov, a professor at the Russian-Tajik (Slavonic) University.

MAKING THE PIE BIGGER

Xi has repeatedly used the metaphor of a pie to describe the gains of international cooperation. "We should make the pie of win-win cooperation bigger, and ensure that more development gains will be shared more fairly by people across the world," he said at the 23rd meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization in 2023.

The pie metaphor reflects the people-centered and action-oriented vision of the GGI: making the gains of cooperation bigger while ensuring that they are shared more widely and fairly. When proposing the GGI, Xi emphasized the importance of "ensuring that the people of every nation are the actors in and beneficiaries of global governance."

The SCO, the platform where Xi proposed the GGI, provides an example. Within the grouping, China has announced the establishment of cooperation platforms in energy, green industries and the digital economy, as well as centers for scientific and technological innovation, higher education, and vocational and technical education.

The expanding scope of cooperation shows how the "pie" can be made bigger in practice: by opening up new areas of cooperation, creating more opportunities for development and ensuring that the benefits reach more people.

Beyond making the pie bigger, Xi has also called for sharing the pie fairly to ensure justice and equity. For him, the ultimate purpose of better global governance is to promote common development and improve people's well-being across the globe.

At the G20 summit held in Brazil in 2024, Xi called for building a just world of common development, saying "prosperity and stability would not be possible in a world where the rich become richer while the poor are made poorer, and countries should make global development more inclusive, beneficial to all, and more resilient."

To build such a world, Xi said, there should be more bridges of cooperation, and less "small yard, high fences," so that more and more developing countries will be better off and achieve modernization. ■

title: China & Taiwan Update, October 23, 2026
summary: ## Toplines **Taiwanese national security and policy officials are drawing attention to expanded People’s Republic of China (PRC) influence operations ahead of Taiwan’s November local elections, likely to increase polarization among Taiwane
content:
## Toplines

**Taiwanese national security and policy officials are drawing attention to expanded People’s Republic of China (PRC) influence operations ahead of Taiwan’s November local elections, likely to increase polarization among Taiwanese people and reduce public trust in Taiwanese officials.**The Taiwan National Security Bureau (NSB) stated in a report submitted for a meeting on October 22 that likely PRC-origin cyberattacks against the Government Services Network (GSN), an independent digital network created specifically for Taiwanese government agencies, rose to 185.6 million attacks in July, and that cyberattacks against the GSN have risen to an average of 2.58 million attacks per day.[1] The NSB stated that it could not discount the possibility that the attacks may be PRC attempts to interfere in Taiwan’s November local elections.[2] The NSB report further stated that the PRC is likely using artificial intelligence (AI)-generated content and fake polls to attempt to influence the November local elections. The NSB uncovered 2.5 million suspect social media posts from January to August, a 48 percent increase from the same period in 2025.[3] An anonymous national security official stated on October 20 that the PRC’s United Front (UF) is using AI to influence public opinion by analyzing different sectors of the Taiwanese public and creating tailored accounts and messages to attempt to fuel polarization and discourage voter participation.[4] Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) Secretary-General Hsu Kuo-yung additionally stated at an October 19 Taipei forum on PRC election interference that the PRC uses religious exchanges, targeted messaging, and AI to influence Taiwanese voters ahead of the November local elections.[5] NSB Director-General Tsai Ming-yen added on October 22 that the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) may be coordinating cheap airfare for Taiwanese citizens residing in the PRC to return to Taiwan to vote in November’s local elections, likely assuming that those voters hold comparatively PRC-favorable views.[6]

The PRC has conducted wide-ranging election interference operations against Taiwan in previous elections and has been conducting increasingly indirect and decentralized influence operations, in line with the operations highlighted by the NSB, with the goal of exacerbating divisions in Taiwanese society and sowing distrust in Taiwan’s democracy.[7] Influence operations uncovered during the 2024 Taiwan presidential election included a significant amount of polarizing online content surrounding the ruling DPP and former President Tsai Ing-wen and fake news about Taiwan’s ties to the United States.[8] Taiwanese think tank Doublethink Lab published a report on March 4 that found that a PRC state-affiliated firm had aggregated information on 170 politicians and tens of thousands of notable Taiwanese individuals, likely in preparation for election interference efforts adjacent to those observed by the NSB and GSN.[9] Online election interference and influence operations will only increase as the November 28 elections draw closer.

**The People’s Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) deployed four Type 071 Landing Platform Deck ships in an unusual combat training formation in the South China Sea, possibly to support PRC efforts to intimidate the Philippines into reducing its activity around disputed maritime features.**PRC state media reported that a formation made up of the PLAN Type 071 Landing Platform Deck (LPD) ships _Kunlunshan_, _Changbaishan_, _Qilianshan,_ and _Wuzhishan_ carried out live-fire combat training drills, including simulated air defense, target practice, and replenishment drills on October 14.[10] The Type 071 is designed to carry out and support amphibious operations and can carry air-cushion landing craft (LCAC), helicopters, amphibious assault vehicles, and combat infantry.[11] PRC state media also highlighted the Type 071 LPD’s importance in potential “island-reef assault, transportation and sovereignty defense missions in locations such as the South China Sea and the Taiwan Strait.”[12]

PRC media stated that the Type 071 will likely serve to temporarily support People’s Liberation Army (PLA) amphibious forces conducting amphibious landings.[13] The Type 071 likely seeks to improve its survivability for these operations by drilling air defense and receiving supplies at sea.[14] PLAN amphibious assault ships like the Type 071 would likely play a key role in a potential amphibious invasion of Taiwan.[15] Type 071s would likely operate alongside other types of amphibious assault ships and surface combatant vessels in a large-scale combat landing operation, however.[16] This marks the first instance of four PLAN Type 071 LPDs training together in a single formation since August 2025, and the first time that PRC media has reported four Type 071s operating together without other PLAN vessel types accompanying them.[17]

The PRC may intend for this unusual training activity to signal to the Philippines the PLAN’s ability to seize and hold disputed maritime features in the South China Sea, and to intimidate the Philippines into reducing or stopping cooperative maritime activities with the US Navy near disputed maritime features.[18] PLAN Type 071 ships trained alongside other PLAN surface combatants in joint air-sea drills around Scarborough Shoal in August and September.[19] These drills included launching LCAC and helicopters from onboard the Type 071.[20] The PRC deployed an increased number of PLAN and China Coast Guard (CCG) ships, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), and a maritime patrol aircraft to Scarborough Shoal on October 16 after the Philippine Navy conducted a maritime patrol near Scarborough Shoal as part of a cooperative maritime activity with the US Navy on October 15.[21] The PLAN also deployed ships to shadow the USS _Charleston_ as it conducted a freedom of navigation operation (FONOP) near the disputed Sabina Shoal on October 20.[22] The PRC likely seeks to coerce the Philippines into reducing its presence in the South China Sea and tacitly, or explicitly, accepting PRC territorial claims over disputed maritime features there.[23]

## Key Takeaways

1.   **PRC Election Interference in Taiwan:** Taiwanese national security and policy officials are reporting increased People’s Republic of China (PRC) influence operations using AI-generated content and cyberattacks to increase polarization, reduce public trust in the Taiwanese government, and reduce voter turnout. These influence operations will likely continue to increase in the lead-up to Taiwan’s November 28 local elections.
2.   **PLAN Modernization:** The People’s Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) conducted live-fire combat training drills using four Type 071 Landing Platform Deck ships designed to support amphibious landing operations on October 14. PRC state media highlighted the use of these vessels in operations in the South China Sea and Taiwan Strait. This unusual exercise formation and training activity was likely intended to intimidate the Philippines into reducing or stopping its maritime activities near disputed South China Sea features.

## Cross-Strait Relations

### Taiwan

**The PRC may be hiring criminals to injure and intimidate Taiwanese individuals who speak against the CCP.**Taiwanese prosecutors indicted five Taiwanese men on October 21 for allegedly trying to seriously injure a Taiwanese comedian, Huang Yi-hao, who mocked the CCP and CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping.[24] The prosecutors alleged that the five men accepted $14,000 from an individual in the PRC to collect Huang’s personal information and severely injure him. One of the men installed a global positioning system (GPS) tracker on Huang’s scooter and uncovered his home address and daily routines. Three of the men staged a car accident at Huang’s home, hitting Huang with a car. Huang suffered bruising but was not seriously injured.

Taiwanese authorities have publicized several recent instances of Taiwanese critics of the PRC being attacked or intimidated by PRC-linked individuals. Vandals allegedly under instruction from the PRC threw paint and feces at Taipei’s Comedy Club on May 29 before Huang was scheduled to perform there.[25] A Hong Kong triad leader allegedly paid a Hong Kong man to travel to Taiwan to assault the chief executive officer (CEO) of the Indo-Pacific Strategy Think Tank Akio Yaito in Taichung in July.[26] Taiwanese authorities indicted four Taiwanese private investigators who took money from Hong Kong-based individuals to surveil DPP legislator Puma Shen’s home.[27] Taiwanese prosecutors and government officials have characterized these cases as “transnational repression.”[28]

The PRC may be co-opting criminals in Hong Kong and Taiwan to intimidate individuals the PRC deems to be “Taiwanese separatists” or vocal critics of the CCP. The CCP often cooperates with criminal gangs to pursue its policy aims in the PRC and abroad.[29] The PRC pays criminals to carry out transnational repression to suppress critics while maintaining plausible deniability, as no clear paper trail links the criminal acts to the PRC government.

### China

**The PRC likely built a second “drone mothership,” a surface vessel that could work in tandem with other naval vessels to transport unmanned underwater vehicles (UUVs). PRC UUVs could play a key role in undersea warfare in a Taiwan contingency.**Naval News reported on October 18 that two videos circulating on the PRC social media platform Weibo likely show the second “drone mothership.”[30] The footage showed tugboats pulling the vessel through the PRC’s Pearl River.[31] The second mothership resembles the first in structure, containing likely hangar spaces and a large opening, but is slightly smaller at approximately 150 meters long.[32] The original mothership contained twelve masts, possibly meant as devices to lift UUVs out of the water, and the second mothership contains six.[33] The mothership was first sighted near a shipyard known for producing PLA support vessels, including amphibious barges.[34] Neither mothership has been observed in action at the time of writing, however.[35]

The PRC has increasingly tested UUVs in recent years and could seek to deploy them in a Taiwan contingency or other maritime conflict. The PRC debuted a “hunt and kill” UUV in 2025, the same year the Philippines found a PRC UUV operating in the South China Sea.[36] The PRC is already building and testing extra-extra-large UUVs (XXLUUVs) to act as uncrewed submarines.[37] Satellite imagery shows that the PRC is likely constructing at least two UUVs between 35 and 45 meters long.[38] ISW-CDOT previously assessed that the PRC could use a drone mothership to extend the XXLUUVs’ deployment range or allow its XXLUUVs to coordinate with a naval task force.[39] The mothership could serve as a command-and-control hub for multiple XXLUUVs traveling with the task force, while the other ships in the group could protect the mothership from missile strikes.[40] Sophisticated PRC UUVs could conduct minelaying or disrupt submarine activity, key capabilities in a possible Taiwan contingency.[41]

## Southeast Asia

### Philippines

**The PLAN shadowed the US littoral combat ship USS****_Charleston_****while it conducted a FONOP near Sabina Shoal. The PRC may view the FONOP as indicative of a renewed US effort to challenge PRC territorial claims in the South China Sea in support of the Philippines.**A PLA Southern Theater Command (STC) spokesperson stated that the PLA dispatched naval forces to track and monitor the USS _Charleston_ on October 20 near Sabina Shoal in the disputed Spratly Islands.[42] The STC spokesperson claimed that the USS _Charleston_ illegally entered PRC waters around Sabina Shoal without PRC authorization and demanded the United States immediately cease its actions. # 中共五中全会将登场：习近平再掌权六年？

广告

（德国之声中文网）中共五中全会下礼拜即将拉开帷幕，主题为“全面从严治党”。分析人士指出，这场会议可能是明年中央领导层换届前最后一次重要的党内会议。路透社报道，尽管外界普遍预期，中国国家主席习近平将在明年召开的中共第二十一次全国代表大会上，开启第四个党总书记任期，但这次五中全会，仍为他提供了进一步巩固权力、强化思想统一，以及加深个人对中共影响力的机会。

五中全会将于10月26日至29日在北京召开。路透社指出，[习近平](https://dw.com/zh/%E4%B9%A0%E8%BF%91%E5%B9%B3/t-17452142)上台后发起的[反腐运动](https://dw.com/zh/%E6%B2%A1%E6%9C%89%E4%B8%8D%E5%80%92%E7%BF%81%E9%BB%84%E5%A5%87%E5%B8%86%E4%B8%8E%E5%80%92%E6%9F%A5%E4%BA%8C%E5%8D%81%E5%B9%B4/a-79682475)，已对中国庞大的官僚体系中的数百万人展开不同程度的调查。数百名高官和将领遭到整肃，其中甚至包括习近平昔日的亲信。批评者认为，这些整肃行动，尤其是针对军方最高层的调查，可能破坏体制稳定，并削弱军队的作战准备能力。但中共将这场运动描述为必要且具有重塑作用的行动，并表示铁腕正风反腐，迎来浴火重生。

托尼·布莱尔全球挑战研究所中国政策研究员奥斯曼（Ruby Osman）表示：“中共日益强化党内整肃，并非因为官员的行为变得更糟，而是因为相关政治利害关系越来越重大。“。她还补充指出，习近平的许多亲信可能在2027年领导层换届时退休。分析人士并不预期五中全会会出现重大人事变动，也不认为，会议将透露潜在的接班安排。

中国研究学者、时事评论作家林和立认为，中共中央总书记、中央军事委员会主席、中华人民共和国国家主席三个职位仍都将由习近平担任。他在台湾外国记者会的活动上说：“我的判断是，习近平有能力继续保住这三个最高职位，并再掌权六年，直到中共第二十二次全国代表大会。”

在反腐风暴中，数十名高级官员和高级将领遭到调查、免职和清洗。总部位于纽约的亚洲协会政策研究所估计，2022年产生的中央委员会成员中，只有大约77.4%仍具备出席下周会议的条件。这意味着，在中共的纪律整顿行动中，近四分之一的成员已遭到撤换。

路透社指出，随着整肃行动持续推进，中央委员会成员人数不断减少。苏黎世大学现代中国研究的教授米特尔施泰特（Jean Christopher Mittelstaedt）对路透社表示，这次五中全会的出席人数“很可能将创下后毛时代以来的最低纪录，人数少于去年10月会议的168名中央委员和147名候补中央委员”。

今年5月，[两名前国防部长魏凤和与李尚福被判处死缓](https://dw.com/zh/%E4%B8%A4%E4%BD%8D%E5%89%8D%E9%98%B2%E9%95%BF%E5%90%8C%E6%97%A5%E5%AE%A3%E5%88%A4-%E6%9D%8E%E5%B0%9A%E7%A6%8F%E5%92%8C%E9%AD%8F%E5%87%A4%E5%92%8C%E4%B8%80%E5%AE%A1%E8%A2%AB%E5%88%A4%E5%A4%84%E6%AD%BB%E7%BC%93/a-77078748)。林和立指出，目前中国军方只剩下四名上将。他认为，对台湾而言，这可能是个好消息：“由于多名高级将领接连遭到整肃。尽管负责台海军事行动的东部战区仍由一名上将指挥，但军方高层的混乱局面，意味着解放军目前尚不具备发动对台军事行动的条件。“

# 微软：网络攻击背后有与中国有关的黑客

19 小时前

* [复制链接](javascript:void(0);) [![图片 11：分享](https://www3.nhk.or.jp/nhkworld/common/svg/ic_share.svg)](javascript:void(0);)
* [![图片12：facebook](https://www3.nhk.or.jp/nhkworld/common/svg/ic_facebook.svg)](javascript:void(0);)
* [![图片 13: X](https://www3.nhk.or.jp/nhkworld/common/images/x.png)](javascript:void(0);)
* [![图片 14: LINE](https://www3.nhk.or.jp/nhkworld/common/svg/ic_line.svg)](javascript:void(0);)

微软表示，一群与中国政府有联系的黑客使用人工智能工具对全球数百个组织发起网络攻击。

这家美国科技巨头表示，这个与中国结盟的组织使用了一个名为 ARTEX 的框架来实施攻击，目标包括公共和私人组织。它表示通过对系统日志和其他记录的分析证实了网络攻击。

这些目标涵盖广泛的行业，包括航空航天、国防、能源和金融服务。

微软表示，其中几次攻击使黑客能够在三个小时内获得对组织云基础设施的特权访问。

据称，登录尝试次数峰值达到每分钟 2,900 次，这样的速度让防御者几乎没有时间检测入侵并做出响应。

目前尚不清楚 ARTEX 是否也被用于最近针对日本公司的一系列网络攻击，但据报道，在上个月末的一系列事件中，它被用来针对韩国金融机构。

# Microsoft: China-linked hackers behind cyberattacks

19 hours ago

*   [Copy link](javascript:void(0);) [![Image 11: Share](https://www3.nhk.or.jp/nhkworld/common/svg/ic_share.svg)](javascript:void(0);)
*   [![Image 12: facebook](https://www3.nhk.or.jp/nhkworld/common/svg/ic_facebook.svg)](javascript:void(0);)
*   [![Image 13: X](https://www3.nhk.or.jp/nhkworld/common/images/x.png)](javascript:void(0);)
*   [![Image 14: LINE](https://www3.nhk.or.jp/nhkworld/common/svg/ic_line.svg)](javascript:void(0);)

Microsoft says a group of hackers linked to the Chinese government used an AI tool to launch cyberattacks on hundreds of organizations worldwide.

The US tech giant says the China-aligned group used a framework called ARTEX to carry out the attacks, which targeted both public and private organizations. It says it confirmed the cyber-offensive through an analysis of system logs and other records.

The targets span a broad range of industries, including aerospace, defense, energy and financial services.

Microsoft says several of the attacks allowed the hackers to gain privileged access to an organization's cloud infrastructure in under three hours.

It says the number of sign-in attempts peaked at 2,900 per minute, a pace that leaves defenders with little time to detect an intrusion and respond.

It's not clear whether ARTEX was also used in a series of recent cyberattacks on Japanese firms, but it was reportedly used to target South Korean financial institutions in a series of incidents from late last month.

content:
_以下是上周西太平洋主要舰船活动和演习的摘要。_

## **在菲律宾海**

2026 年 10 月 21 日，美国海军、日本海上自卫队、澳大利亚皇家海军、加拿大皇家海军和法国海军舰艇在菲律宾海举行的“锐剑 27”(KS27) 演习中齐头并进。美国海军照片

作为美日“利剑 27”演习的一部分，西奥多·罗斯福号航母打击群周三在菲律宾海。

航空母舰西奥多·罗斯福号 (CVN-71) 搭载第 11 舰载机联队 (CVW) 和巡洋舰 USS_Chosin_(CG-65) 领先日本海上自卫队直升机驱逐舰 JS _Ise_(DDH-182)、驱逐舰 JS _Kongo_ (DDG-173) 和 JS _Asahi_(DD-119)、澳大利亚皇家海军护卫舰 HMAS _Stuart_ (FFH153)、加拿大皇家海军护卫舰 HMCS _Regina_ (FFH334) 和一艘法国护卫舰在进行海军演习。

## 在西里伯斯海

中国人民解放军海军辽宁舰舰艇 [周五被发现](https://x.com/bncdotph/status/2113486033795068415?s=46&t=E74_DbuPOhFRAs5RyI-Miw) 正在穿越位于菲律宾巴西兰市和三宝颜市之间的巴西兰海峡。该打击群包括航空母舰辽宁号 (16)、巡洋舰鞍山号 (103) 和无锡号巡洋舰 (104) 以及驱逐舰怀宁号 (123)。

## **在日本**
2026 年 10 月 21 日，日本岩国海军陆战队航空站举行的“锐剑 27”（KS27）演习中，一艘台风无人水面舰艇展示了海军拦截技术。美国海军陆战队照片

美日双边“锐剑27”演习将于周一至10月29日在日本举行。大部分活动将在日本西南部地区进行。

大约 45,000 名日本自卫队、11,000 名美国军人以及来自澳大利亚、加拿大、法国、德国、荷兰、新西兰和菲律宾的部队以及来自韩国和英国的观察员参加了此次活动。

包括西奥多·罗斯福号航母战斗群在内的总共 260 架飞机和 40 艘舰艇正在部署参加演习，演习于周一在石垣岛举行[正式仪式](https://www.dvidshub.net/image/10031703/keen-sword-27-opening-ceremony)。

与海上[演习](https://www.dvidshub.net/image/10038745/uss-theodore-roosevelt-cvn-71-participates-keen-sword-27)、海军陆战队和日本陆上自卫队一起(日本陆上自卫队)[反舰](https://www.dvidshub.net/image/10034230/ks-27-us-marines-with-12th-lct-embark-jltv-and-nmesis)和防空导弹部队将部署到先岛群岛进行岛屿防御演习。[](https://www.dvidshub.net/image/10042298/mcas-iwakuni-drone-demo)

_The following is a summary of major ship movements and exercises in the Western Pacific over the last week._

## **In the Philippine Sea**

U.S. Navy, Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force, Royal Australian Navy, Royal Canadian Navy, and French Navy ships steam together during Exercise Keen Sword 27 (KS27), Oct. 21, 2026, in the Philippine Sea. US Navy photo

The Theodore Roosevelt Carrier Strike Group was in the Philippine Sea as of Wednesday as part of U.S.-Japan Exercise Keen Sword 27.

Aircraft carrier USS _Theodore Roosevelt_ (CVN-71) with embarked Carrier Air Wing (CVW) 11 and cruiser USS _Chosin_(CG-65) is leading Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force helicopter destroyer JS _Ise_(DDH-182),destroyers JS _Kongo_ (DDG-173) and JS _Asahi_(DD-119), Royal Australian Navy frigate HMAS _Stuart_ (FFH153), Royal Canadian frigate HMCS _Regina_ (FFH334) and a French frigate in the naval drills.

## In the Celebes Sea

The People’s Liberation Army Navy Liaoning CSG [was spotted Friday](https://x.com/bncdotph/status/2113486033795068415?s=46&t=E74_DbuPOhFRAs5RyI-Miw) transiting the Basilan Strait, which is between Basilan and Zamboanga City, Philippines. The strike group includes aircraft carrier CNS _Liaoning_ (16), cruisers CNS _Anshan_ (103) and CNS _Wuxi_ (104) and destroyer CNS _Huainen_ (123).

## **In Japan**

A Typhoon unmanned surface vessel demonstrates naval interception techniques during Exercise Keen Sword 27 (KS27), at Marine Corps Air Station Iwakuni, Japan, Oct. 21, 2026. US Marine Corps photo

The U.S.-Japan bilateral Exercise Keen Sword 27 is being carried out in Japan from Monday to Oct. 29. The majority of activities will take place in Japan’s southwest region.

Approximately 45,000 Japan Self-Defense Force, 11,000 U.S. service members and forces from Australia, Canada, France, Germany, the Netherlands, New Zealand and the Philippines are participating alongside observers from the Republic of Korea and the United Kingdom.

A total of 260 aircraft and 40 ships, including the Theodore Roosevelt Carrier Strike Group are being deployed for the drills, which opened Monday with a[formal ceremony](https://www.dvidshub.net/image/10031703/keen-sword-27-opening-ceremony) on Ishigaki Island.

Along with at-sea[drills](https://www.dvidshub.net/image/10038745/uss-theodore-roosevelt-cvn-71-participates-keen-sword-27), Marine Corps and Japan Ground Self-Defense Force (JGSDF)[anti-ship](https://www.dvidshub.net/image/10034230/ks-27-us-marines-with-12th-lct-embark-jltv-and-nmesis) and anti-air missile units will be deployed to the Sakishima Islands for island defense drills.[](https://www.dvidshub.net/image/10042298/mcas-iwakuni-drone-demo)

[Drone demonstrations](https://www.dvidshub.net/image/10042298/mcas-iwakuni-drone-demo) will occur at Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Iwakuni,and U.S. Air Force F-22 Raptor fighters will deploy to Japan Air Self-Defense Force Tsuiki Air Base. A[irfield repair training](https://www.dvidshub.net/image/10038599/us-marines-airmen-train-airfield-damage-repair-during-keen-sword-27) will take place at Kadena Air Base,[cyber exercises](https://www.dvidshub.net/image/10041549/us-japan-and-partners-strengthen-cyber-readiness-during-keen-sword-27) at Sagami Depot, [joint fighter aircraft flights](https://www.dvidshub.net/image/10042468/us-marines-us-air-force-jasdf-conduct-photo-exercise-during-keen-sword-27) and an[“elephant walk”](https://www.dvidshub.net/video/1027108/1st-maw-japan-ground-self-defense-force-aircraft-stage-elephant-walk-during-keen-sword-27) of Marine Corps and JGSDF rotary wing and tiltrotor aircraft will be at MCAS Futenma.

复合能源技术 (CET) Hadalus-XL 亮相 401 Tech Bridge，2025 年 BlueTIDE 活动。CET 照片

加利福尼亚州圣地亚哥——乍一看，Hadalus-XL 无人水下航行器及其深色平板可能不会像快艇或时尚战斗机那样吸引好奇的目光。

但它的价值在于它所做的事情，总部位于罗德岛州的复合能源技术公司的首席技术官本·罗森塔尔 (Ben Rosenthal) 表示。 34英尺长的水下航行器可以拖运数吨货物。其面板和组件可折叠平放，以便在 20 英尺集装箱中运输，包装后可使用简单工具快速组装或拆卸。

周三，罗森塔尔站在停泊在洛马角海军基地潜艇码头上的超大型 UUV 变体旁边，对 USNI 新闻表示：“我们有点像海上的皮卡。我们可以将又大又重的东西运送到位。” “它比现有的任何其他车辆都更大、更重。”

Hadalus-XL 可能不是最性感的技术，但这种自动驾驶车辆的实用性对于需要补给部队、跟踪敌方潜艇、反击或呼叫火力支援的海上指挥官来说是很清楚的。

“赢得战争的是后勤，”罗森塔尔说。
后勤是美国军方官员通过澳大利亚、英国和美国之间的三边 AUKUS 安全协议关注的日益增长的威胁之一。小型无人机和攻击舰等廉价高科技系统的扩散威胁着从黑海、波斯湾到北大西洋的力量。其他地方的补给部队和支援部队也很容易受到影响。

虽然三边协议最初侧重于核动力潜艇和工业基地，但 AUKUS 第二支柱的军事官员已将重点扩大到用于水下作战的新兴机器人和自主技术。

Hadalus 和其他几艘由私营企业开发的 UUV 参加了周三在南加州举行的[AUKUS Pillar II“Maritime Big Play-Pacific”](https://www.cpf.navy.mil/Newsroom/News/Article/4621543/us-navy-aukus-partners-launch-landmark-maritime-big-play-pacific-demonstration/)演示。 Hadalus 在海上度过了为期五天的活动，其中包括 40 多个行业和政府海事多域系统。

据美国海军称，演示和实弹作战片段的重点是打击行动、有争议的补给和水下作战。总部位于圣地亚哥的太平洋海军信息战中心、美国太平洋舰队和海军陆战队在圣地亚哥的圣克莱门特岛和海军陆战队基地彭德尔顿营主办了此次活动。
官员们周三在媒体圆桌会议上表示，这三个国家的行业和政府之间的合作是 AUKUS 开发和应用新兴技术的核心。

五角大楼负责研究和工程的副部长办公室负责关键技术的助理部长迈克尔·多德表示：“目标很简单。确定哪些领域可以通过合作提供任何一个国家单独有效地实现的作战优势。”

多德的办公室赞助了 MBP-Pacific 活动，他表示，通过海事大活动，五角大楼正在尽早将运营商、技术专家和行业聚集在一起。

【原文 English Original】
Composite Energy Technologies (CET) Hadalus-XL at the 401 Tech Bridge, BlueTIDE event in 2025. CET photo

SAN DIEGO, Calif. — At first glance, the Hadalus-XL unmanned underwater vehicle and its dark flat panels might not catch the curious eye like a go-fast boat or sleek fighter jet.

But its value is in what it does, said Ben Rosenthal, chief technology officer with Composite Energy Technologies, a Rhode Island-based company. The 34-foot underwater vehicle can haul several tons of cargo. Its panels and components fold flat for transport in a 20-foot container, packaged for quick assembly or disassembly with simple tools.

“We’re kind of a pickup truck of the ocean. We can bring big, heavy things into position,” Rosenthal told USNI News on Wednesday while standing next to the extra-large, UUV variant parked on a submarine pier at Naval Base Point Loma. “It’s much bigger and much heavier than any other vehicle that’s out there.”

Hadalus-XL might not be the sexiest tech, but the utility of such an autonomous vehicle is meant to be clear to maritime commanders needing to resupply forces, track an enemy submarine, counter-attack or call for fire support.

“What wins wars is logistics,” Rosenthal said.

Logistics is among the growing threats U.S. military officials are focused on through the trilateral AUKUS security agreement between Australia, the United Kingdom and the United States. The proliferation of cheap, high-tech systems like small aerial drones and attack vessels threaten forces from the Black Sea and the Persian Gulf to the North Atlantic. Resupplying units and supporting troops elsewhere are also vulnerable.

While the trilateral agreement initially focused on nuclear-powered submarines and the industrial base, military officials in AUKUS Pillar II have expanded the focus to new and emerging robotics and autonomous technologies for undersea warfare.

Hadalus and several other UUVs developed by private industry participated in the[AUKUS Pillar II “Maritime Big Play-Pacific”](https://www.cpf.navy.mil/Newsroom/News/Article/4621543/us-navy-aukus-partners-launch-landmark-maritime-big-play-pacific-demonstration/)demonstration on Wednesday in Southern California. Hadalus spent five days at sea for the event, which included more than 40 industry and government maritime multi-domain systems.

The demonstration and live-fire operational vignettes focused on strike operations, contested resupply and undersea warfare, according to the U.S. Navy. San Diego-based Naval Information Warfare Center Pacific, U.S. Pacific Fleet and the Marine Corps hosted the event, held in San Diego, at San Clemente Island and Camp Pendleton Marine Corps Base.

Collaboration among industry and governments from all three countries is central to AUKUS to develop and field emerging technologies, officials said Wednesday during a media roundtable.

“The objective is straightforward. Identify areas where working together delivers an operational advantage that no one nation could achieve as efficiently on its own,” said Michael Dodd, assistant secretary for critical technologies in the Office of the Undersecretary for Research and Engineering at the Pentagon.

Through Maritime Big Play events, the Pentagon is bringing operators, technical experts and industry together earlier in the process, said Dodd, whose office sponsored the MBP-Pacific event.

“That ensures operational relevance and interoperability are built in from the outset of these sprints, not added after a system’s already been developed,” said Dodd. “The work is practical. It’s about evaluating systems under demanding conditions, improving interoperability in real time and identifying force multipliers that can strengthen the combined force.”

## **AUKUS is Making ‘Real Progress’**

A U.S. Mk 48 Heavyweight Torpedo is loaded onto the Royal Navy’s experimental XLUUV XV Excalibur on Sept. 13, 2026. U.S. Navy image

[This year’s priorities under Pillar II](https://www.defence.gov.au/news-events/news/2026-06-02/aukus-partners-launch-pillar-ii-project)are focused on[torpedoes](https://news.usni.org/2026/09/22/u-s-u-k-launch-torpedo-from-royal-navy-unmanned-submarine), unmanned vehicles, mines and undersea communications, Dodd said. Autonomous undersea vehicles – with the ability to deploy and employ a range of payloads in a contested logistics environment from sensors to drones and torpedoes – was the focus of MBP-Pacific. The delivery of systems and payloads is slated to start next year.

But Pillar II goes beyond demonstration, said Sir Stephen Lovegrove, the U.K.’s Special Representative for AUKUS. Pillar II is seeing experimentation and capability building, as well as improved interoperability among industry and governments.

“This is not about looking at the best of each other’s kit and systems and seeing which one to choose,” Lovegrove said. “This is about making sure that the whole thing works together, and that 1+1+1 equals considerably more than three.”

David Nockels, Australia’s first assistant secretary for Defense Trade, Regulation and Industrial Collaboration, said he’s seeing “real progress” across Pillar II.The government is developing the [Royal Australian Navy’s Ghost Shark](https://news.usni.org/2026/10/21/royal-australian-navys-ghost-shark-uuvs-will-have-minelaying-uav-payloads)fleet in partnership with Anduril Australia. This week, military and government officials announced investments in UUV payloads, including the ability to lay sea mines and deploy drones, small and towed sonar.

“As the strategic environment becomes far more complex, the need to accelerate our delivery of military capability and strengthen interoperability is only increasing,” Nockels said. “[Lessons learned] will inform future experimentation, future capability development and the operational integration of our militaries and… help ensure AUKUS continues to deliver practical capability outcomes for our warfighters.”

The Royal Australian Navy’s Ghost Shark are being equipped with sea mine, aerial drone swarms and supply payloads for use in the coming years, according to a video shared Oct. 21, 2026. Anduril Industries image

In the overall scenario for the latest demonstration MBP-Pacific Pillar II, joint forces moving across island chains faced off against an adversary that impacted logistical support and resupply, said Gerry Tighe, Maritime Big Play director and former naval aviator. Enemy threats came from drones in the air, on the surface and undersea. The scenario represented “a whole new world” where using lethal systems or sensors like acoustic sonar arrays demonstrated during Pillar II can provide a warfighting advantage, Tighe said.

While this latest Pillar II scenario was set with the Indo-Pacific in mind, Pillar II’s focus on maritime capabilities is “theater agnostic,” Lovegrove said.

“We clearly are committed to playing our part in the Indo-Pacific, but our main focus is the North Atlantic, Mediterranean and High North. These are obviously areas where the principal threat is Russia,” he said.

U.K. military officials have deemed Russia the greatest threat to U.K. security, most recently[in September during a speech](https://news.usni.org/2026/09/21/russia-is-greatest-threat-to-u-k-security-says-first-sea-lord) at the Department of Naval Research in London. First Sea Lord Gen. Sir Gwyn Jenkins said Russia has increased its activities in the North Atlantic and is probing the U.K. for weaknesses. The Royal Navy is spending more time and resources monitoring Russian vessels and the shadow fleet. An average of two Royal Navy warships deploy each week to conduct such tasks, Jenkins said.

“Our approach is to monitor, track and then call out the bad behavior,” Second Sea Lord Vice Adm. Paul Beattie, told reporters on Wednesday. “I think we know how important undersea cables and pipelines are to any nation, but particularly to an island nation.”

## **Maritime Solutions**

Hadalus XL fit in a 20-foot container for easy transport. CET image

AUKUS Pillar II provides tech companies a way to collaborate with other vendors and products, and MBP-Pacific served as a realistic venue to show their capabilities and utility to the military.

“You’ve got to be able to work together and collaborate and make a system of systems that solves the mission, rather than the one thing you’re looking at,” Rosenthal said.

CET’s fully autonomous Hadalus UUV has everything it needs to swim, navigation sensors – “everything it needs to know where it is in the world to avoid hitting anything,” Rosenthal said.

Additionally, it can be equipped with additional systems as needed. On Wednesday, the battery-operated vehicle was outfitted with a launcher system to deploy six drums.

Hadalus’ carbon-fiber composite hull “is acoustically invisible,” Rosenthal said, its dark hue helping it blend into the sea. Over the five days Hadalus was in the water, data showed it is undetectable, according to Rosenthal.

“It’s surprising how hard it is to spot when it’s bobbing around in the waves,” Rosenthal said. “We suspected that it would be hard to find in the water, but we didn’t have hard data to show that. Getting that data saying we truly can’t be detected was super, super beneficial.”

CET is currently capable of building 110 UUVs per month at its Rhode Island factory with the possibility of expanding to accommodate a higher production rate, Rosenthal said. The company and its partners are working through a contract with the Marine Corps for a smaller UUV.

Anduril Australia’s extra-large autonomous undersea vehicle Dive-XL participated in MBP-Pacific in California in October of 2026. Anduril image

Among UUVs in play at MBP-Pacific was[Dive-XL](https://www.anduril.com/dive-xl), Anduril Australia’s extra-large autonomous undersea vehicle that fits into a standard 40-foot container. It can carry multiple payloads, including[Ultra Maritime’s Sea Spear deployable acoustic array](https://umaritime.com/sonar-solutions/deployable-sonar-arrays/).

“You could leave this behind on the bottom and then it can detect contacts that swim by and then communicate between the different nodes,” said Tim Rochholz, Anduril Maritime’s director of fleet integration and U.S. XL programs.

Dive-XL’s configurable bays support various payloads, including Copperhead UUVs, Mark 48 torpedo equivalents and[Seabed Sentry](https://www.anduril.com/news/anduril-introduces-seabed-sentry), he said.

“The challenging part is the data,” Rochholz said. “You can collect all this data you want on the bottom of the ocean. You’ve got to get it somewhere off the ocean floor and then do something with that information.”

One U.K vendor’s system played a key role during MBP-Pacific.[Seaber’s RECALL,](https://seaber.fr/applications#asw-training)a small orange recoverable UUV, served as the enemy in the anti-submarine warfare scenarios.

“It’s pretending to be a submarine. We were the target,” said John Peters, ocean systems technician with RS Aqua, a Portsmouth, U.K.-based company that distributes the French-made device.

The UUV has a wide range of frequencies that it can emit to mimic a range of undersea threats.

The underwater drone can reach a depth up to 300 meters. Because it is recoverable, the UUV can reduce costs with repeated use.

Feedback from the ASW demonstrations were positive, Peters said.

“Systems were detecting us, which is good,” he said.

## **Easing Barriers**

Existing U.S. regulations – specifically International Traffic in Arms Regulations, or ITAR – control the sale, transfer and export of defense and military technologies that can stymie innovation and limit interoperability among industry and nations.

Easing ITAR restrictions will smooth those acquisition pathways and get systems produced and into the hands of operators more quickly, officials said.

zh_title: 陆军启动关岛防空营重点应对中国和朝鲜威胁 - 美国海军学院新闻
summary: 美国陆军下士。 2019 年 2 月 6 日，在关岛安德森空军基地的末段高空区域防御 (THAAD) 系统教练机上进行导弹装卸演习时，第 94 陆军防空与导弹防御司令部鹰爪特遣队的爱国者发射站增强型操作员兼维护员罗赫利奥·阿尔格塔 (Rogelio Argueta) 下达命令。 美国陆军照片 美国陆军最近启动了一个驻关岛防空营，旨在保护该岛免受中国和朝鲜日益严重的空中和导弹威胁。第43防空炮兵团第3营，活跃
content:
美国陆军下士。 2019 年 2 月 6 日，关岛安德森空军基地，第 94 陆军防空与导弹防御司令部“爪子”特遣部队的爱国者发射站增强型操作员兼维护员罗赫利奥·阿格塔 (Rogelio Argueta) 在末段高空区域防御 (THAAD) 系统教练机上进行导弹装卸演习时发出命令。美国陆军照片

美国陆军最近在关岛部署了一个防空营，旨在保护该岛免受中国和朝鲜日益先进的空中和导弹威胁。

10月16日组建的第43防空炮兵团第3营将继承“黑爪”特遣部队的关岛防御职责。上一次陆军轮换任务始于 2013 年，旨在应对潜在的朝鲜弹道导弹威胁。

近年来，随着中国人民解放军火箭军的崛起，该任务的重点已扩大到在潜在冲突中抵御中国导弹的攻击。 [五角大楼于 2023 年启动关岛防御系统计划](https://news.usni.org/2023/05/10/pentagon-starts-work-to-build-ballistic-missile-defense-capability-in-guam)满足击败北京的弹道、巡航和高超音速武器所需的要求罢工[.](https://news.usni.org/2023/05/10/pentagon-starts-work-to-build-ballistic-missile-defense-capability-in-guam)
陆军在该营启动的新闻稿中写道：“关岛的战略位置使其成为美国在整个地区军事行动的重要组成部分，支持联合部队行动，同时使防空和导弹防御成为保护支持这些任务所需的部队和基础设施的关键部分。”

2026 年 10 月 16 日，隶属第 94 陆军防空与导弹防御司令部第 43 防空炮兵团、第 38 防空炮兵旅第 3 营的美国陆军士兵参加在关岛安德森空军基地举行的启动仪式。美国陆军照片

随着印太对手远程精确打击能力的增强，地面部队着眼于在关岛加强态势。 3-43 ADA 将运行爱国者、末段高空区域防御和新的中级火力防护能力系统，[_星条旗报_于 8 月报道_。](https://www.stripes.com/theaters/asia_pacific/2026-08-21/guam-defense-patriot-ifpc-systems-22615488.html) 与传统的爱国者和萨德系统相比，IFPC 将提供针对飞机、导弹和无人机的中短程防御。

组合后，这些系统提供了一个分层网络，可以应对潜在的西太平洋冲突中可能出现的各种空中和导弹威胁。
“士兵们开发了连接传感器、指挥和控制系统、发射器和拦截器所需的新程序、关系和集成，以促进统一的防御架构。3-43 ADA 现在支持陆军对关岛战略防御系统的贡献是再合适不过了，”3-43 ADA BN 指挥官约书亚·乌内斯中校在新闻稿中说。

据陆军称，从特遣部队到营的过渡标志着国防部“在印度-太平洋地区建立永久防空能力”的承诺。

2025 年 12 月 16 日，在关岛安德森空军基地举行的指挥变更仪式上，分配到“利爪”特遣部队的美国陆军士兵列队。美国陆军照片

关岛目前的防空系统由六座陆军“萨德”发射装置和美国海军“宙斯盾梳”组成

【原文 English Original】
U.S. Army Cpl. Rogelio Argueta, Patriot Launching Station Enhanced Operator-Maintainer, assigned with Task Force Talon, 94th Army Air and Missile Defense Command gives commands, during a practice missile reload and unload drills on a Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) system trainer at Andersen Air Force Base, Guam, Feb. 6, 2019. US Army photo

The U.S. Army’s recently activated a Guam-based air defense battalion meant to protect the island from increasingly advanced air and missile threats fielded by China and North Korea.

The 3rd Battalion, 43rd Air Defense Artillery Regiment, activated on Oct. 16, will inherit the defense of Guam responsibilities of Task Force Talon. The previous Army rotational mission began in 2013 to counter potential North Korean ballistic missile threats.

With the rise of the People’s Liberation Army Rocket Force in recent years, the mission has expanded its focus to defend against a barrage of Chinese missiles in a potential conflict. T[he Pentagon initiated plans for the Guam Defense System in 2023 t](https://news.usni.org/2023/05/10/pentagon-starts-work-to-build-ballistic-missile-defense-capability-in-guam)o meet the requirements needed to defeat Beijing’s ballistic, cruise and hypersonic strikes[.](https://news.usni.org/2023/05/10/pentagon-starts-work-to-build-ballistic-missile-defense-capability-in-guam)

“Guam’s strategic location makes it an important part of U.S. military operations throughout the region by supporting joint force operations while making air and missile defense a critical part of protecting the forces and infrastructure needed to support those missions,” reads the Army release on the battalion’s activation.

U.S. Army soldiers assigned to 3rd Battalion, 43rd Air Defense Artillery Regiment, 38th Air Defense Artillery Brigade, 94th Army Air and Missile Defense Command, participate in an activation ceremony on Andersen Air Force Base, Guam, Oct. 16, 2026. US Army photo

The ground branch has eyed a reinforced posture on Guam with the increase of Indo-Pacific adversaries’ long-range precision strike capabilities. The 3-43 ADA will operate Patriot, Terminal High Altitude Area Defense and new Intermediate Fires Protection Capability systems, [_Stars and Stripes reported_ in August.](https://www.stripes.com/theaters/asia_pacific/2026-08-21/guam-defense-patriot-ifpc-systems-22615488.html) Compared to the legacy Patriot and THAAD systems, IFPC will provide medium- to short-range defense against aircraft, missiles and drones.

When combined, the systems provide a layered network to engage a variety of air and missile threats that could be fielded in a potential Western Pacific conflict.

“The soldiers developed new procedures, relationships and integration required to connect sensors, command and control systems, launchers and interceptors to promote a unified defensive architecture. It’s only fitting that 3-43 ADA now stands up the Army’s contribution to the strategic Guam Defense System,” Lt. Col. Joshua Urness, 3-43 ADA BN commander, said in the release.

According to the Army, the transition from task force to battalion signals the Defense Department’s commitment “toward permanent air defense capabilities in the Indo-Pacific.”

U.S. Army soldiers assigned to Task Force Talon stand in formation during a change of command ceremony at Andersen Air Force Base, Guam, Dec. 16, 2025. US Army photo

Guam’s current air defenses are composed of six Army THAAD launchers and U.S. Navy Aegis Combat System warships assigned to its defense on an as-need basis. Future plans aim to integrate a networked system capable of conducting 360-degree detection and interception of air and missile threats.

Since Task Force Talon’s original mission over a decade ago, the complexity and quantity of Indo-Pacific missile threats has only increased. Today, the People’s Liberation Army Navy is in the [process of fielding](https://news.usni.org/2026/03/05/chinese-navy-expanding-nuclear-attack-boat-fleet-and-missile-strike-capabilities-oni-commander-says) more nuclear attack boats equipped with vertical launching systems. [The Pentagon has also said it expects the PLAN to have a nine carrier strike group force by 2035,](https://news.usni.org/2025/12/24/china-wants-nine-aircraft-carriers-by-2035-says-new-pentagon-report) which will expand Beijing’s blue water projection capabilities.

Taishin International Bank (Taishin Bank) opened its flagship private banking branch in Kaohsiung's Asia New Bay Area on October 23, the latest step in its push to serve southern Taiwan's growing ranks of wealthy clients and connect the island's wealth management market with the rest of Asia. The branch reflects Taishin Bank's broader response to the government's initiative to establish Taiwan as an Asian asset management hub. Sam Lin, Chief Executive Officer of Private Banking and Strategic Wealth Clients Group of Taishin Bank, hosted the opening ceremony. Taishin Bank also signed a memorandum of understanding to establish a strategic alliance with Union Bancaire Privée (UBP), one of Switzerland's largest family-owned private banks, to draw on UBP's expertise in wealth management for high-net-worth clients and international investment, strengthening Taishin Private Banking's international reach and service capabilities.

Taishin International Bank (Taishin Bank) opened its flagship private banking branch in Kaohsiung's Asia New Bay Area on October 23, the latest step in its push to serve southern Taiwan's growing ranks of wealthy clients and connect the island's wealth management market with the rest of Asia. The branch reflects Taishin Bank's broader response to the government's initiative to establish Taiwan as an Asian asset management hub. Sam Lin, Chief Executive Officer of Private Banking and Strategic Wealth Clients Group of Taishin Bank, hosted the opening ceremony. Taishin Bank also signed a memorandum of understanding to establish a strategic alliance with Union Bancaire Privée (UBP), one of Switzerland's largest family-owned private banks, to draw on UBP's expertise in wealth management for high-net-worth clients and international investment, strengthening Taishin Private Banking's international reach and service capabilities.

"As the merger of Taishin FHC and Shin Kong FHC begins to deliver the benefits of greater scale, our customer base has grown to over 11 million," Sam Lin said. To meet fast-growing demand from wealthy clients, Taishin Bank established its Private Banking and High-End Wealth Management business in 2026, bringing together wealth planning advisers with more than 20 years of experience in financial services and Certified Financial Planner (CFP) or Associate Financial Planner (AFP) credentials, alongside experienced lawyers and accountants, to strengthen wealth planning services for high-net-worth clients. As global tax rules evolve and family businesses pass from one generation to the next, Taishin Private Banking's family office offers comprehensive advisory services across five core areas: family investment management, wealth transfer, tax services, family governance and lifestyle management.

Michael Blake, UBP's chief executive for Asia, expressed confidence in the partnership, pointing to the combined group's substantial resources and deep experience in serving local clients. He said the partnership is built on shared corporate values, a client-first approach and complementary strengths: Taishin Bank brings an intimate understanding of the needs of high-net-worth clients in Taiwan, while UBP contributes a global investment perspective and extensive international wealth management experience. Looking ahead, Blake said UBP will share global market insights and expertise in asset allocation and investment management, helping Taishin's private banking team broaden its international perspective and strengthen its professional capabilities through talent development and knowledge sharing. Both banks expect the partnership to help raise the standard of private banking services in Taiwan.

With over 35 years of experience in wealth management and a sustained commitment to serving high-net-worth clients, Taishin Bank has built a comprehensive private banking platform encompassing specialist teams, a broad range of financial products and operations in Taiwan, Hong Kong and Singapore. At the heart of the partnership with UBP is a shared ambition: to translate international expertise into tangible benefits for clients. Going forward, Taishin Bank will combine its deep understanding of the Taiwanese market and the needs of high-net-worth clients with UBP's global market insights and investment expertise to further refine its approach to asset allocation, expand its product offerings and strengthen its wealth management capabilities, delivering a more comprehensive and internationally connected private banking experience.

Taishin Private Banking will remain rooted in Taiwan, strengthen its connections across Asia and extend its reach to global markets, guided by a commitment to professional excellence and the preservation of wealth across generations. True to its promise, "We are committed to safeguarding what you entrust to us," the bank aims to be a trusted, long-term "asset and liability management partner" for high-net-worth clients and families — helping them manage their wealth with confidence, create long-term value and preserve their legacy for generations to come.

# Typhoon Champi damages roads, knocks out power across Taiwan

10/23/2026 03:41 PM

[](jsvscript:)[](jsvscript:)[](javascript:void(0))[Listen](javascript:)

[Link](javascript:)[Whatsapp](javascript:)[Reddit](javascript:)[Line](javascript:)[Email](javascript:)

A huge crane was battered by waves brought by Typhoon Champi and toppled into the ocean at Fugang Fishing Port in Taitung County on Friday. CNA photo Oct. 23, 2026

Taipei, Oct. 23 (CNA) Typhoon Champi caused damage and disruptions across Taiwan on Friday, including road closures and injuries, and prompted evacuations in several places as powerful winds and waves pounded the island's eastern coast.

At around 9:40 a.m. Friday, waves as high as 6 meters swept a large crane into the sea at Fugang Harbor in Taitung County, an incident captured in an online video that captured bystanders exclaiming as the waves hit.

In Hualien, two National Dong Hwa University students riding a scooter hit a fallen tree near the campus Thursday night because heavy rain had reduced visibility. Both suffered minor injuries and were discharged from the hospital after treatment.

Focus Taiwan Video

At Changbin Harbor in northern Taitung, waves as high as 8 meters battered the coast, sending seawater onto roads and overturning three bamboo rafts.

A section of the southbound lane of Provincial Highway 9 near the entrance to Duoliang Village in Taitung County, at the 401-kilometer mark, was closed after part of the roadbed on the outer side of the northbound lane was washed away.

Chiu Min-feng (邱民豐), head of the Highway Bureau's Dawu Maintenance Office, said the damage had not disrupted traffic, but the bureau was concerned that continued erosion could further damage the embankment.

The office will place concrete breakwater blocks as an emergency measure, and the outer northbound lane will close temporarily, Chiu said.

Passengers brave the windy rainpour in streets of New Taipei on Friday. CNA photo Oct. 23, 2026

Heavy rain also prompted evacuations. In New Taipei City, 1,397 people in landslide-prone areas of Yingge, Xindian, Pingxi and Shulin districts were expected to be evacuated, Mayor Hou Yu-ih (侯友宜) said.

Preventive evacuations involving 350 people were also carried out in Datong and Nan'ao townships in Yilan County, according to local authorities.

An engineering truck arrives as a Taipower worker repairs power lines in Yunlin County on Friday. Photo courtesy of a private contributor

As of 2 p.m., 77,498 households across Taiwan had lost power, with power restored to 75 percent of them and 19,029 households still without electricity, Taiwan Power Co. said.

Earlier Friday, the Central Emergency Operations Center reported that the typhoon had left one person dead and 94 injured as of 6 a.m.

title: 菲律宾就第二托马斯浅滩军舰警告中国：拖走“马德雷山”号将被视为“战争行为”
summary: 菲律宾国防部长特吉尔伯托·特奥多罗(Gilberto Teodoro)警告中国，任何试图拖走坐滩在第二托马斯浅滩的“马德雷山”号(BRP Sierra Madre)军舰的行动，都将被菲律宾视为“战争行为”。 特奥多罗是在星期五(10月23日)的一次线上采访中做出该表述的。他表示，对“马德雷山”号登陆舰的任何威胁都将被非常严肃对待，因为这等于针对菲律宾共和国军舰采取行动。 菲律宾媒体报道，当被问到中国海警或军人若试图强登“马德雷山”号，菲律宾能否援引美菲《共同防御条约》共同应对
content:
菲律宾国防部长特吉尔伯托·特奥多罗(Gilberto Teodoro)警告中国，任何试图拖走坐滩在第二托马斯浅滩的“马德雷山”号(BRP Sierra Madre)军舰的行动，都将被菲律宾视为“战争行为”。

特奥多罗是在星期五(10月23日)的一次线上采访中做出该表述的。他表示，对“马德雷山”号登陆舰的任何威胁都将被非常严肃对待，因为这等于针对菲律宾共和国军舰采取行动。

菲律宾媒体报道，当被问到中国海警或军人若试图强登“马德雷山”号，菲律宾能否援引美菲《共同防御条约》共同应对时，特奥多罗说：“这种可能性是存在的。”

但特奥多罗也强调，是否援引防御条约作出回应，最终须由菲律宾总统小费迪南德·马科斯（Ferdinand Marcos Jr.)决定。

根据美菲1951年签订的《共同防御条约》，两国若在太平洋海域遭到武装攻击，均被视为危及自身的和平与安全，两国将依照各自的宪法程序采取行动应对共同危机。

美国多次重申，《美菲共同防御条约》适用于在南中国海任何地点针对菲律宾武装部队、公务船只和飞机发动的武装袭击。

就菲律宾国防部长的说法，美国之音向美国战争部发出问询电邮，但截至美国之音发稿时为止，还没有收到战争部的回应。

**菲华文报刊爆：中国拟推十项反制措施**

10月22日，一家总部位于马尼拉的华文报刊《菲律宾商报》援引消息人士的话披露，由于中方对菲方近期涉华行动和相关言论逐渐失去耐心，正考虑推出[十项反制措施](https://www.shangbao.com.ph/pdf/2026/10-22/U205P5038T1D207070F103DT20261022011508.pdf)，其中包括将坐滩第二托马斯浅滩(Second Thomas Shoal，中国称仁爱礁，菲律宾称阿云津礁) 破旧的“马德雷山”号拖走，以彻底解决该问题。

十项反制措施还包括制裁一批被中国视为反华的菲律宾政客、公布部分菲律宾政客于中国的利益往来、不再允许菲律宾对“马德雷山”号运补、切断中国对菲的成品油及化肥供应等等。

“马德雷山号”是一艘二战时期的老旧军舰，菲律宾1999年将其搁浅在第二托马斯浅滩，以强化其主权主张。军舰上驻有一支小规模部队，菲律宾船只定期向舰上驻军运送食品和其他物资，并轮换人员。第二托马斯浅滩是该地区主要的冲突热点之一。

截至目前，中方官方尚未证实十项反制措施的消息，但相关传闻在菲律宾引发高度关注。

**中菲外交争议持续**

菲律宾外交部星期四(10月22日)发表声明，重申马尼拉坚持“一个中国”政策，但是抨击中国驻菲大使馆近期“升级且有违外交礼仪”的言论。

中国驻菲大使井泉10月15日在接受记者采访时表示，如果北京动用武力，可能轻易就能获胜。

井泉当时说：“如果我们想动用武力，可能很容易就能获胜。但我们不会这样做，我们不会动用武力。要知道，我们热爱和平。”

菲律宾外交部当天发表声明，对井泉的发言表达不满和强烈反对的立场，指责他“用词不当”，向马尼拉传递出一种“隐晦”的武力威胁。

菲律宾外交部随后召见井泉，就其言论表达了菲方的强烈反对。菲律宾外交部副部长玛丽亚·特蕾莎·拉扎罗(Maria Theresa Lazaro)以“具有挑衅性”且“不可接受”描述井泉的言论。

10月21日，菲律宾十位跨党派众议院议员提出一项决议案，敦促马科斯总统宣布井泉为“不受欢迎的人”。

**中菲南中国海上冲突不断**

自9月份以来，中菲除了外交争议外，在南中国海上的冲突也不间断。

10月初，中菲双方就发生在第二托马斯浅滩附近的一次医疗救助行动相互指责。据菲律宾军方说，10月8日，菲律宾军方需要从 “马德雷山”号军舰上撤离一名生病的菲律宾军人。

菲律宾海岸警卫队指责中国海警船阻挠紧急撤离行动，其中包括使用高压水炮，显然意在阻止菲律宾巡逻船抵达该浅滩，以接回生病的执勤人员。

此外，菲律宾军方报告称，9月份出现在南中国海有争议岛礁周边的中国军舰和海警船数量几乎翻了一番。

另外，9月8日，在韩国首尔举行的2026年首尔安全对话(SDD)上，菲律宾国防部长特奥多罗对他认为的中方现场递上的一张纸条当场做出强势回应，抨击中国此举践踏《联合国海洋法公约》(UNCLOS)，并称纸条是“赤裸裸的胁迫、霸凌和侵略”。

中方对于上述事件的菲方表述均予以否认和反驳。在撤离生病的菲方军人事件中，外交部发言人毛宁指责菲方“对中方倒打一耙”，属“挑事生非、哗众取宠”。

content:
中共即将召开以加强党内治理为主题的二十届五中全会。分析人士说，在一系列高层官员遭到清洗、习近平为继续执政布局之际，这次会议不仅将提供观察人事变化的窗口，也将显示他准备如何解决一个持续困扰其执政的问题：如何让官员既服从中央，又能有效落实政策。

这次全会定于10月26日至29日在北京举行，将审议《中共中央关于持之以恒推进全面从严治党若干重大问题的决定》。

两位研究中国政治的学者在接受美国之音采访时表示，他们将重点关注哪些官员出席、哪些处分获得正式确认，以及中央委员会的空缺是否得到填补。这些变化可能为预计于2027年召开的中共二十一大提供人事线索。

与此同时，亚洲协会政策研究所(ASPI)发表的一篇分析指出，习近平能够主导北京高层政治，却未必能确保庞大的党政体系按照他的要求运转。加强政治控制能否带来更好的治理，将是此次会议的重要观察点。

**人事变动：谁出席，谁递补？**

“我在这次全会上最关注、也认为影响最大的，是人事变动，”布鲁金斯学会约翰·桑顿中国中心研究员秦江南(Jon Czin)告诉美国之音。

秦江南说，习近平正在为下一个任期铺路，但近年来的清洗也大幅改变了党内高层的构成，军队尤其如此。全会将帮助外界判断，这轮震荡究竟波及了多大范围。

长期研究中国政治的加州大学圣迭戈分校政治学教授史宗瀚(Victor Shih)认为，另一个重要看点是，中央候补委员是否会递补进入中央委员会。

“过去几年，很多中央委员和中央候补委员因为反腐清洗而被撤职，”他说，“其中许多人的空缺一直没有填补。”

史宗瀚说，在下一次党代会筹备工作成为主要任务之前，这次全会是处理人事空缺的重要机会。他表示，中共二十一大前还会召开一次全会，但届时工作将主要围绕二十一大的安排展开。

亚洲协会政策研究所中国分析中心高级研究员牛犇(Neil Thomas)及共同作者在文章《习近平控制力的局限：中共五中全会观察重点》中指出，除了观察谁获得递补，还应关注哪些符合递补顺序的候补委员被跳过，因为这可能提供有关其政治处境的线索。

不过，文章也提醒，官员没有出席会议，并不能单独证明其已经遭到清洗。

秦江南说，军方人事值得特别关注，因为变化不仅涉及掌握军队指挥权的中央军事委员会，也波及更广泛的军方中央委员。

“受到冲击最严重的确实是军队。”他说。秦江南表示，多名军方中央委员长期未公开露面，使外界难以确认他们的状况。全会的出席名单和人事决定，将有助于判断清洗的范围。

牛犇等人的文章同样将军队领导层列为重点。他们认为，全会可能提供补充中央军委成员的机会，但习近平也可能选择到下一次党代会时再重组军委。

**严格纪律能否解决执行难题？**

北京将全面从严治党视为增强执政能力的重要条件。中共中央政治局在讨论全会筹备工作时强调，要维护党中央集中统一领导，并增强党的长期执政能力。

牛犇等人的分析认为，习近平当前面对的难题，不只是官员是否表态忠诚，而是他们能否将中央要求转化为实际成果。

文章指出，基层官员面对不断增加的任务和紧张的财政资源，可能更倾向于避免犯错、展示合规，而不是尝试新办法。因此，政策执行不力既可能来自推诿，也可能反映现有考核机制和资源约束。

作者认为，判断全会成效的一个关键，是新规定能否为官员提供更清楚的工作重点，并保护合理探索，还是主要增加新的处罚依据。

史宗瀚说，他将关注习近平在已经强化国家监察体系、巡视地方和国有企业等机制之后，还会提出哪些制度措施，使党内纪律成为持久安排。

他同时认为，高压反腐也可能给治理稳定带来问题。官员之间仍然存在激烈的晋升竞争，腐败指控可能成为相互举报的工具，而接连撤换官员又会造成较高的人事流动。

“他对反腐败的高度强调，在某种程度上也已经成为中国稳定治理的一个问题。”史宗瀚说。

史宗瀚还指出，对公务支出的严格限制可能产生经济代价，尤其影响依赖政府会议、差旅及其他相关需求的服务业企业。

他认为，公务支出收紧，加上房地产市场疲弱和外资减少，已经给服务业经营和就业带来压力。他强调，解决办法不是放弃反腐，而是区分违法行为与合法的行政支出。

这些判断也意味着，全会提出的纪律要求如何落实，可能影响地方政府的支出和经济活动，而不只是党内管理。

**为2027年布局，接班信号仍不明朗**

尽管人事安排受到关注，史宗瀚并不预期此次全会将明确习近平的潜在接班人。

“至少从公开信息来看，我们确实还不知道这些人可能是谁。”他说。

牛犇等人的文章也认为，习近平很可能在下一次党代会上寻求第四个任期，但不太可能在这次全会上释放明确的接班信号。作者指出，推迟选择有助于维持习近平眼下的权威，却也让长期权力交接问题继续悬而未决。

**对美中关系的影响**

秦江南认为，习近平对党代会和国内政治的关注，也可能影响外交安排。他说，随着习近平将更多精力投入新任期的准备工作，未来与美国总统唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)会面的时间安排可能变得更不确定，而领导人会面一直被认为为美中关系提供一定程度的稳定。

9月25日，美中峰会结束，习近平在携夫人彭丽媛离开华盛顿时曾确认，他与特朗普总统在年底前还有两次会晤的机会。“我们预期接下来今年和总统先生还有两次的会面。 一次就是在中国举行的APEC会，再一次呢，就是在美国举行的G20会，我们欢迎总统先生和夫人到中国去访问。”

对观察人士而言，五中全会的看点因此不仅在于对习近平权威的再次确认，也在于具体的人事和制度安排：哪些空缺得到填补，哪些官员仍然缺席，以及新的纪律要求能否改善政策执行。这些将为判断习近平如何准备下一阶段的执政提供线索。

title: Bannerman pulls trigger on $353M uranium mine
zh_title: 班纳曼启动价值 3.53 亿美元的铀矿开采
summary: Bannerman Energy（ASX、NSX：BMN；US-OTC：BNNLF）及其中国合作伙伴 CNNC Overseas 已批准在纳米比亚建设 Etango 铀项目，该项目的资金没有项目债务，预计将于 2028 年首次生产。该开发项目预计投产前成本为 3.53 亿美元，平均每年产出 350 万磅氧化铀。班纳曼在周五的声明中表示，早期作品已投入约 6400 万美元，剩下约 2.89 亿美元用于前期制作支出。经过多年的努力，这一决定使 Etango 进入全面建设阶段。
content:
Bannerman Energy（ASX、NSX：BMN；US-OTC：BNNLF）及其中国合作伙伴 CNNC Overseas 已批准在纳米比亚建设 Etango 铀项目，该项目的资金没有项目债务，预计将于 2028 年首次生产。该开发项目预计投产前成本为 3.53 亿美元，平均每年产出 350 万磅氧化铀。班纳曼在周五的声明中表示，早期作品已投入约 6400 万美元，剩下约 2.89 亿美元用于前期制作支出。经过多年的研究和准备工作，这一决定使 Etango 进入全面建设阶段。张伯伦在一份新闻稿中表示：“[最终投资决定]是二十多年来勘探、研究和严格降低风险的结晶，它正式承诺合资公司将全面建设世界级的 Etango 铀矿项目。” “在全球公用事业日益需要安全、多元化供应之际，Etango 将成为纳米比亚埃龙戈地区的一家长期大型生产商，埃龙戈地区是一个成熟的铀矿省份。”此次批准是在 9 月份与中国核工业集团公司旗下的中核海外达成融资协议之后获得的，该协议不仅获得了建设资金，还为 Etango 的大部分产品找到了买家。班纳曼持有该合资公司55%的股份，中核海外持有45%的股份。该合资企业拥有 Etango 95% 的股份。周五，Bannerman 股价在悉尼下跌 4.2%，至每股 3 澳元，该公司估值约为 7.48 亿澳元。
据 FNArena 报道，在做出建设决定之前，瑞银集团保留了买入评级，但将目标价下调 17% 至 4.39 澳元，以反映近期股权融资的稀释作用。该银行认为 Etango 资金充足。中核集团主要买家 根据融资安排，中方合作伙伴投资3.204亿美元，其中合资企业投资2.945亿美元。它将按照基于市场的条件购买 Etango 60% 的终生产量，没有价格下限或上限。 Bannerman 保留剩余 40% 的独立营销权。截至 9 月 30 日，该合资企业持有约 2.95 亿美元现金，用于支付剩余的预制作支出。 Bannerman 单独持有约 1.75 亿澳元，该公司表示，该资金通过建设、产能扩张和有针对性的商业生产来充分为其剩余的营运资金份额提供资金。资本估算的范围为正负 10%。 Etango 经批准的设计要求采用露天开采和堆浸作业，年处理量为 800 万吨。纳米比亚于 2023 年 12 月颁发采矿许可证，环境审批涵盖拟建矿山及配套基础设施。班纳曼 9 月份的施工更新显示，大宗土方工程已完成 99%。前两个合同包的混凝土已浇筑约 86%，永久供水管道第一阶段已完成约 90%。

【原文 English Original】
Bannerman Energy (ASX, NSX: BMN; US-OTC: BNNLF) and its Chinese partner CNNC Overseas have approved construction of the Etango uranium project in Namibia, with funding secured without project debt and first production targeted for 2028. The development is expected to cost $353 million before production and deliver an average of 3.5 million lb. of uranium oxide annually. About $64 million has already been spent on early works, leaving roughly $289 million in pre-production spending, Bannerman said in its announcement Friday. The decision moves Etango into full-scale construction after years of studies and preparatory work. “[The FID] is the culmination of more than two decades of exploration, study and disciplined de-risking, and it formally commits the JV to full-scale construction of the world-class Etango Uranium project,” Chamberlain said in a release. “Etango is set to be a long-life, large-scale producer in Namibia’s Erongo region, a highly established uranium province, at a time when the world’s utilities increasingly need secure, diversified supply.” The approval follows a September financing deal with CNNC Overseas, part of China National Nuclear Corp., that secured both construction capital and a buyer for most of Etango’s output. Bannerman owns 55% of the joint venture and CNNC Overseas holds 45%. The venture owns 95% of Etango. Bannerman shares fell 4.2% to A$3 apiece in Sydney on Friday, valuing the company at roughly A$748 million. Ahead of the construction decision, UBS retained its Buy rating but cut its price target 17% to A$4.39 to reflect dilution from recent equity raisings, FNArena reported . The bank considered Etango fully funded. CNNC main buyer Under the financing arrangement , the Chinese partner invested $320.4 million, including $294.5 million in the joint venture. It will buy 60% of Etango’s lifetime production on market-based terms without price floors or ceilings. Bannerman retains independent marketing rights over the remaining 40%. The venture held about $295 million in cash at Sept. 30 to cover remaining pre-production spending. Bannerman separately held about A$175 million, which it said fully funds its remaining share of working capital through construction, ramp-up and targeted commercial production. The capital estimate carries a range of plus or minus 10%. Etango’s approved design calls for an open pit and heap-leach operation processing 8 million tonnes annually. Namibia awarded the mining licence in December 2023 , and environmental approvals cover the proposed mine and supporting infrastructure. Bannerman’s September construction update put bulk earthworks at 99% complete. About 86% of concrete for the first two contracted packages had been poured, while the first stage of the permanent water pipeline was about 90% complete.
